title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
廣西鄕試錄序
聖天子御㝢紀元是爲萬曆癸酉
天下士當大比于鄕
上採言官議
詔下郡國諸所登進皆崇本實毋
爲浮夸骫骳習海內人士亦
旣仰承
===
德意斌斌嚮風矣維時廣西巡按
監察御史唐鍊職司監臨𢋫
飭百度先期走幣延諸文學
至則以洛及敎授蔡存省爲
考試敎諭劉起鵬李子象爲
同考試而提調則屬之左布
政使楊成左參議高則益監
punctuated:
廣西鄕試錄序

聖天子御㝢紀元，是爲萬曆癸酉，天下士當大比于鄕。上採言官議，詔下郡國：諸所登進，皆崇本實，毋爲浮夸骫骳習。海內人士，亦旣仰承德意，斌斌嚮風矣。維時，廣西巡按監察御史唐鍊職司監臨，𢋫飭百度，先期走幣延諸文學。至，則以洛及敎授蔡存省爲考試，敎諭劉起鵬、李子象爲同考試；而提調則屬之左布政使楊成、左參議高則益，監
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Guangxi Provincial Examination

In the first year of the reign of the Sacred Son of Heaven, which is the guiyou year of the Wanli era [1573], the scholars of the realm were due for the great triennial competition in the provinces. His Majesty adopted the deliberations of the speaking officials and issued an edict to the prefectures and principalities stating that all those selected for advancement should esteem substance and reality, and must not indulge in the habits of superficial ostentation or tortuousness. Scholars and gentlemen throughout the empire have already reverently received His virtuous intentions and in refined manner turned toward this wind of reform. At this time, Regional Inspector and Investigating Censor of Guangxi Tang Lian 唐鍊 held the office of Supervising Official. With solemn diligence he regulated all measures and, in advance of the date, sent out gifts to invite various men of letters. When they arrived, he appointed me, [Sun] Luo 洛, along with Prefectural Instructor Cai Cunxing 蔡存省 as Examiners, and County Instructors Liu Qipeng 劉起鵬 and Li Zixiang 李子象 as Associate Examiners; the post of Proctor was assigned to Left Administration Commissioner Yang Cheng 楊成 and Left Assistant Administration Commissioner Gao Zeyi 高則益, while that of Censor-in-Charge of the…

title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
試則屬之按察使高察僉事
夏道南諸執事皆慎簡以充
先是府江諸夷弗靖提督兩
廣軍務都察院右都御史兼
兵部右侍郎殷正茂巡撫廣
西都察院右副都御史郭應
聘與御史會疏
===
請討一舉蕩平故士得益脩絃誦
之業即洛等祗役而來也亦
夷猶即次無復曩時震駭之
警矣既鎖闈合提學僉事江
圻所簡士一千四百有奇試
之遵
制拔其雋五十五人復梓其文為
punctuated: 試則屬之按察使高察、僉事夏道南，諸執事皆慎簡以充。先是，府江諸夷弗靖，提督兩廣軍務、都察院右都御史兼兵部右侍郎殷正茂，巡撫廣西、都察院右副都御史郭應聘，與御史會疏請討，一舉蕩平。故士得益脩絃誦之業，即洛等祗役而來也，亦夷猶即次，無復曩時震駭之警矣。既鎖闈，合提學僉事江圻所簡士一千四百有奇試之。遵制拔其雋五十五人，復梓其文為
translation_en: … the surveillance of the examination was assigned to Surveillance Commissioner Gao Cha 高察 and Assistant Surveillance Commissioner Xia Daonan 夏道南, while all the various functionaries were carefully selected to fill their posts. Earlier, the various non-Chinese tribes along the Fu River (Fujiang 府江) had been unruly. Supreme Commander of Military Affairs in Liangguang, Right Censor-in-Chief of the Censorate concurrently serving as Right Vice Minister of War Yin Zhengmao 殷正茂, and Grand Coordinator of Guangxi, Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief of the Censorate Guo Yingpin 郭應聘, submitted a joint memorial with the Regional Inspector requesting permission to launch a punitive expedition, and swept them away in a single stroke. Consequently, the scholars were able to further cultivate their studies of music and recitation; even as I, Luo 洛, and my colleagues came respectfully to perform our duties, we traveled at ease and lodged in peace, no longer experiencing the alarming alerts of former times. Once the examination compound was locked, we gathered the more than one thousand four hundred scholars selected by Education Intendant Assistant Surveillance Commissioner Jiang Qi 江圻 and examined them. In compliance with the imperial system, we selected fifty-five of the most outstanding talents, and furthermore printed their essays onto woodblocks to form…

title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
錄以
獻洛宜敘諸簡端洛惟賢喆之
生雖乾坤鍾秀川嶽孕靈其
所涵濡造就于
聖人之化者良不淺尠載昔姬周
文武迭興道化隆洽至成王
以緝熈宥密荷厥仔肩于時
===
周公居左召公居右同德恊
心廑吐握之謀廣延攬之策
故其所布列於常伯常任準
人及執贄而見者濟濟多俊
乂士然大都皆岐酆西土之
産此固成周氣運之盛昌謂
非聖世作人之明徵不可也
punctuated: 錄以獻，洛宜敘諸簡端。洛惟賢喆之生，雖乾坤鍾秀、川嶽孕靈，其所涵濡造就于聖人之化者，良不淺尠。載昔姬周，文、武迭興，道化隆洽。至成王以緝熈宥密荷厥仔肩，于時周公居左，召公居右，同德恊心，廑吐握之謀，廣延攬之策，故其所布列於常伯、常任、準人，及執贄而見者，濟濟多俊乂士，然大都皆岐、酆西土之産。此固成周氣運之盛昌，謂非聖世作人之明徵不可也。
translation_en: …a record to present to the throne, and it is fitting that I, Luo, write a preface at the beginning of the volume. I reflect that in the birth of worthy and wise men, although Heaven and Earth concentrate their finest essence and the rivers and mountains conceive their spiritual energy, the extent to which they are steeped in and molded by the transforming influence of the Sage is truly neither shallow nor slight. Looking back to the Zhou dynasty of the Ji clan, when Kings Wen and Wu arose in succession, moral transformation was flourishing and pervasive. By the time King Cheng shouldered his heavy responsibilities with radiant brightness and serene profundity, at that time the Duke of Zhou stood to his left and the Duke of Shao to his right. Sharing the same virtue and uniting their hearts, they were diligent in plans that made them spit out their food and grasp their hair to welcome worthies, and they broadened their policies for recruiting talent. Therefore, those who were arrayed in office as regular senior advisors (changbo), regular administrative officials (changren), and law-enforcement officials (zhunren), as well as those who presented ceremonial gifts to have an audience, were a multitude of outstanding and capable men; yet for the most part they were all natives of Qi, Feng, and the western lands. While this was certainly due to the flourishing vitality of the Zhou at its height, one cannot say that it was not also a clear proof of a sacred age cultivating men of talent.

title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
今顯庸矣顧卑卑然不自振
燿至偭規矩而改錯斯何以
故素絲之染易緇百鍊之鋼
難淬自昔嘅之矣爾諸士在
膠庠中亦聞
主上之董正百官乎蓋嘗莊誦
勅詞首欲正人心湔宿垢共襄王
===
道與海內更始其有依阿淟
涊噂沓潏訛者國有常憲大
哉
王言與周官三事大夫之訓先後
同符焉夫周官者成王致太
平之書而周召所與共篤棐
者也其言曰功崇惟志業廣
punctuated: 今顯庸矣，顧卑卑然不自振燿，至偭規矩而改錯，斯何以故？素絲之染易緇，百鍊之鋼難淬，自昔嘅之矣。爾諸士在膠庠中，亦聞主上之董正百官乎？蓋嘗莊誦勅詞，首欲正人心、湔宿垢，共襄王道，與海內更始；其有依阿淟涊、噂沓潏訛者，國有常憲。大哉王言！與《周官》三事大夫之訓先後同符焉。夫《周官》者，成王致太平之書，而周、召所與共篤棐者也。其言曰：「功崇惟志，業廣
translation_en: …now that they are prominently employed, they instead act basely and fail to rouse themselves to distinction, even turning their backs on rules and measures and altering their course—for what reason is this? That plain silk when dyed easily turns black, and steel forged a hundred times is hard to temper, has been lamented since antiquity. While you scholars were in the state schools, did you also hear of how His Majesty supervises and rectifies the hundred officials? Indeed, I have reverently recited the words of the imperial edict: first and foremost, he wishes to rectify men's minds and wash away old filth, so that all may together assist in the Kingly Way and make a fresh start with all within the seas; as for those who are obsequious and impure, or who engage in sycophantic chatter and deceitful falsehoods, the state has its constant penal laws. Great are the King's words! Though separated in time, they tally completely with the instructions to the three categories of high officials in the "Officers of Zhou" (Zhou guan). Now, the "Officers of Zhou" is the text by which King Cheng brought about Great Peace, and that in which the Dukes of Zhou and Shao joined in offering devoted assistance. Its words say: "High merit depends on aspiration; broad achievement…

title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
惟勤爾諸士旣隨計吏以上
異日布列有位展采錯事則
將何以辨志而貞業哉亦惟
皇極之敷言是訓是迪其庶幾永
底于休以無負爾山川之靈
乃或澤鞭以倖售抱腊以爲
璞使人得而姍訾其後洛不
===
敢知也洛不敢知也是舉也
詰兵鎮遠則總兵署都督同
知李錫綜理防範于內外則
右參政鄭茂副使金柱沈子
木莊國楨徐作右參議李文
續僉事高克謙參將錢鳳翔
王世科王承恩都司署都指
punctuated:
惟勤。爾諸士旣隨計吏以上，異日布列有位，展采錯事，則將何以辨志而貞業哉？亦惟皇極之敷言，是訓是迪，其庶幾永底于休，以無負爾山川之靈。乃或澤鞭以倖售，抱腊以爲璞，使人得而姍訾其後，洛不敢知也，洛不敢知也。
是舉也，詰兵鎮遠，則總兵、署都督同知李錫；綜理防範于內外，則右參政鄭茂，副使金柱、沈子木、莊國楨、徐作，右參議李文續，僉事高克謙，參將錢鳳翔、王世科、王承恩，都司署都指
translation_en:
… only through diligence.” Now that you gentlemen are to accompany the reporting officials up to the capital, and in the future will be arrayed in official positions to display your talents and manage affairs, how then will you discern your aims and keep your undertakings upright? Only by taking the widely promulgated words of the Imperial Perfection as your instruction and your guide may you perhaps forever attain excellence, so as not to fail the numinous spirit of your mountains and rivers. If, however, anyone should oil his whip to seek lucky advancement by trickery, or clutch dried rat-meat while pretending it is uncarved jade, thereby giving others cause to ridicule and disparage him afterward—of that, I, Luo, dare not know; of that, I, Luo, dare not know!

In this undertaking, inspecting the troops and pacifying the distant regions was the work of Regional Commander and Acting Vice Commissioner-in-Chief Li Xi 李錫; comprehensively managing and maintaining security inside and outside the compound were Right Administration Vice Commissioner Zheng Mao 鄭茂, Surveillance Vice Commissioners Jin Zhu 金柱, Shen Zimu 沈子木, Zhuang Guozhen 莊國楨, and Xu Zuo 徐作, Right Assistant Administration Commissioner Li Wenxu 李文續, Assistant Surveillance Commissioner Gao Keqian 高克謙, Assistant Regional Commanders Qian Fengxiang 錢鳳翔, Wang Shike 王世科, and Wang Cheng'en 王承恩, and Regional Military Commission Acting Assistant Regional Military…

title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
揮僉事汪可大許文楊照以
入
賀行者右參政李鳳副使劉廷
舉以遷秩行者左參政胡直
咸先後與勞以使節戾止者
成安伯郭應乾大理寺評事
杜詩中書舍人王蕋蔣務稼
===
行人司行人彭應時咸有事
玆土法得並書
湖廣承天府儒學教授朱洛
謹序
punctuated:
揮僉事汪可大、許文、楊照。以入賀行者：右參政李鳳，副使劉廷舉；以遷秩行者：左參政胡直，咸先後與勞。以使節戾止者：成安伯郭應乾，大理寺評事杜詩，中書舍人王蕋、蔣務稼，行人司行人彭應時，咸有事玆土，法得並書。
湖廣承天府儒學教授朱洛謹序。
translation_en:
…Acting Assistant Regional Military Commissioners Wang Keda 汪可大, Xu Wen 許文, and Yang Zhao 楊照. Those who departed on missions to offer congratulations at court—Administration Vice Commissioner of the Right Li Feng 李鳳 and Surveillance Vice Commissioner Liu Tingju 劉廷舉—and he who departed upon promotion in rank—Administration Vice Commissioner of the Left Hu Zhi 胡直—all contributed their efforts at various stages. Those who arrived here bearing imperial credentials—Earl of Cheng'an 成安伯 Guo Yingqian 郭應乾; Case Reviewer of the Court of Judicial Review Du Shi 杜詩; Drafters Wang Rui 王蕋 and Jiang Wujia 蔣務稼; and Messenger of the Messenger Office Peng Yingshi 彭應時—all had official business in this territory, and by rule are entitled to be recorded together.
Respectfully prefaced by Zhu Luo 朱洛, Instructor of the Confucian School of Chengtian Prefecture 承天府 in Huguang 湖廣.

title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
萬曆元年廣西鄉試
監臨官
巡按廣西監察御史唐鍊〔純之湖廣常德衛官籍浙江仁和縣人壬戌進士〕
提調官
廣西等處承宣布政使司左布政使楊成〔汝大直隸長洲縣籍無錫縣人丙辰進士〕
廣西等處承宣布政使司左參議高則益〔汝謙江西南昌縣人壬戌進士〕
監試官
廣西等處提刑按察司按察使高察〔汝哲四川內江縣人丙辰進士〕
廣西等處提刑按察司僉事夏道南〔宗時浙江餘姚縣人己未進士〕
===
考試官
湖廣承天府儒學教授朱洛〔周卿江西新淦縣人丁卯貢士〕
浙江杭州府儒學教授蔡存省〔宣懋福建晉江縣人戊午貢士〕
同考試官
福建福州府連江縣儒學教諭劉起鵬〔舒卿江西泰和縣人己酉貢士〕
福建汀州府武平縣儒學教諭李子象〔汝賢廣東揭陽縣人戊午貢士〕
印卷官
廣西等處承宣布政使司經歷司都事梅一元〔子仁直隸宣城縣人監生〕
廣西等處提刑按察司經歷司經歷朱士先〔養志江西萬安縣人吏員〕
punctuated:
萬曆元年廣西鄉試。
監臨官：
巡按廣西監察御史唐鍊〔純之，湖廣常德衛官籍，浙江仁和縣人，壬戌進士〕。
提調官：
廣西等處承宣布政使司左布政使楊成〔汝大，直隸長洲縣籍，無錫縣人，丙辰進士〕；
廣西等處承宣布政使司左參議高則益〔汝謙，江西南昌縣人，壬戌進士〕。
監試官：
廣西等處提刑按察司按察使高察〔汝哲，四川內江縣人，丙辰進士〕；
廣西等處提刑按察司僉事夏道南〔宗時，浙江餘姚縣人，己未進士〕。
考試官：
湖廣承天府儒學教授朱洛〔周卿，江西新淦縣人，丁卯貢士〕；
浙江杭州府儒學教授蔡存省〔宣懋，福建晉江縣人，戊午貢士〕。
同考試官：
福建福州府連江縣儒學教諭劉起鵬〔舒卿，江西泰和縣人，己酉貢士〕；
福建汀州府武平縣儒學教諭李子象〔汝賢，廣東揭陽縣人，戊午貢士〕。
印卷官：
廣西等處承宣布政使司經歷司都事梅一元〔子仁，直隸宣城縣人，監生〕；
廣西等處提刑按察司經歷司經歷朱士先〔養志，江西萬安縣人，吏員〕。
translation_en:
The Guangxi Provincial Examination of the First Year of the Wanli Era (1573).

Supervising Official:
Tang Lian 唐鍊, Regional Inspector of Guangxi and Investigating Censor [courtesy name Chunzhi 純之; registered in an official household of Changde Guard, Huguang, and a native of Renhe County, Zhejiang; metropolitan graduate (jinshi) of the renxu year (1562)].

Proctors:
Yang Cheng 楊成, Left Administration Commissioner of the Provincial Administration Commission of Guangxi and Other Places [courtesy name Ruda 汝大; registered in Changzhou County, Zhili, and a native of Wuxi County; metropolitan graduate (jinshi) of the bingchen year (1556)].
Gao Zeyi 高則益, Left Assistant Administration Commissioner of the Provincial Administration Commission of Guangxi and Other Places [courtesy name Ruqian 汝謙; native of Nanchang County, Jiangxi; metropolitan graduate (jinshi) of the renxu year (1562)].

Monitoring Officials:
Gao Cha 高察, Surveillance Commissioner of the Provincial Surveillance Commission of Guangxi and Other Places [courtesy name Ruzhe 汝哲; native of Neijiang County, Sichuan; metropolitan graduate (jinshi) of the bingchen year (1556)].
Xia Daonan 夏道南, Assistant Surveillance Commissioner of the Provincial Surveillance Commission of Guangxi and Other Places [courtesy name Zongshi 宗時; native of Yuyao County, Zhejiang; metropolitan graduate (jinshi) of the jiwei year (1559)].

Examiners:
Zhu Luo 朱洛, Instructor of the Confucian School of Chengtian Prefecture, Huguang [courtesy name Zhouqing 周卿; native of Xingan County, Jiangxi; tribute scholar (gongshi) of the dingmao year (1567)].
Cai Cunxing 蔡存省, Instructor of the Confucian School of Hangzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang [courtesy name Xuanmao 宣懋; native of Jinjiang County, Fujian; tribute scholar (gongshi) of the wuwu year (1558)].

Associate Examiners:
Liu Qipeng 劉起鵬, Instructor of the Confucian School of Lianjiang County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian [courtesy name Shuqing 舒卿; native of Taihe County, Jiangxi; tribute scholar (gongshi) of the jiyou year (1549)].
Li Zixiang 李子象, Instructor of the Confucian School of Wuping County, Tingzhou Prefecture, Fujian [courtesy name Ruxian 汝賢; native of Jieyang County, Guangdong; tribute scholar (gongshi) of the wuwu year (1558)].

Officials for Stamping Examination Papers:
Mei Yiyuan 梅一元, Assistant Registrar in the Registry of the Provincial Administration Commission of Guangxi and Other Places [courtesy name Ziren 子仁; native of Xuancheng County, Zhili; National University Student (jiansheng)].
Zhu Shixian 朱士先, Registrar in the Registry of the Provincial Surveillance Commission of Guangxi and Other Places [courtesy name Yangzhi 養志; native of Wan'an County, Jiangxi; Subofficial Functionary (liyuan)].

title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
收掌試卷官
桂林府知府彭文質〔在份福建莆田縣人己未進士〕
南寧府知府杜思〔子睿浙江鄞縣人丙辰進士〕
受卷官
平樂府知府陳子佐〔道謙福建惠安縣人丙辰進士〕
梧州府知府許嶽〔子峻浙江錢塘縣人庚戌進士〕
潯州府知府楊珂〔士佩福建晉江縣人乙丑進士〕
太平府知府林廷顯〔斯德福建福清縣人壬子貢士〕
彌封官
===
桂林府同知陳所學〔在行廣東番禺縣人壬子貢士〕

title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
爲聖本由學而成
詔誥表內科一道
擬漢却千里馬詔文帝元年
擬唐以張九齡爲中書令誥開元二十二
年
擬以薛瑄爲禮部侍郎兼翰林院學士直
文淵閣謝表天順元年
判語五條
官吏給由
===
功臣田土
服舍違式
飛報軍情
脩理倉庫
第叁塲
策五道
問自古明良相遇不偶然也喜起賡歌都
俞吁咈三代以還不可尚矣漢唐而下
雖治不歫古然英主賢臣亦時相與規
punctuated:
「爲聖本由學而成。」

詔、誥、表內科一道：
擬漢《却千里馬詔》（文帝元年）。
擬唐《以張九齡爲中書令誥》（開元二十二年）。
擬《以薛瑄爲禮部侍郎兼翰林院學士直文淵閣謝表》（天順元年）。

判語五條：
官吏給由。
功臣田土。
服舍違式。
飛報軍情。
脩理倉庫。

第叁塲：
策五道：
問：自古明良相遇，不偶然也。喜起賡歌，都俞吁咈，三代以還，不可尚矣。漢、唐而下，雖治不歫古，然英主賢臣，亦時相與規……
translation_en:
"Becoming a sage essentially comes through learning."

One composition chosen from Imperial Edicts (zhao), Patents (gao), or Memorials (biao):
Imitation of the Han Dynasty "Imperial Edict Rejecting the Thousand-Li Horse" (first year of Emperor Wen [179 BCE]).
Imitation of the Tang Dynasty "Patent Appointing Zhang Jiuling 張九齡 as Secretariat Director" (twenty-second year of the Kaiyuan era [734 CE]).
Imitation of the "Memorial of Thanks for Appointing Xue Xuan 薛瑄 as Vice Minister of Rites Concurrently Serving as Hanlin Academician on Duty in the Hall of Literary Profundity (Wenyuan ge)" (first year of the Tianshun era [1457]).

Five Legal Judgments (panyu):
Issuance of service-record certificates for officials and subofficial functionaries;
Landed estates of meritorious statesmen;
Clothing and housing in violation of regulations;
Express reporting of military intelligence;
Repair and maintenance of granaries and treasuries.

Third Session

Five Policy Questions (ce):
Question: Since antiquity, the meeting of an enlightened ruler and worthy ministers has never been by chance. Joyously rising to exchange songs in continuation, and expressing agreement and disagreement in court deliberations ("du, yu, xu, fu")—since the Three Dynasties, such heights could no longer be surpassed. From the Han and Tang dynasties onward, although governance did not reach [?] antiquity, heroic rulers and worthy ministers nevertheless from time to time joined together to plan…

title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
公私交困何策以善其終歟營堡分兵
列戍所以保境安民也乃戍守之卒既
寡且疲田主里排與賊勾結甚者豪勢
包食其田議者欲專意招安量輸煙竈
俾歲時羈縻似矣然夷性喜攻殺者十
九而奉漢法者十一巨奸大猾鼓煽出
沒何計以消其黨歟量地制賦則壤之
遺也曩戶口稅畝半爲夷侵疆理紊矣
邇者兵威稍振有司方議平均乃影射
成風清之未幾而告訐踵至豈丈量之
法卒不可行歟分屯給軍養兵之遺也
今屯田子粒半爲官占行伍耗矣邇者
地方多故部檄日行清理乃詭冒成習
督之愈急而玩愒如故豈屯種之制獨
不可講歟夫計兵食以固根本嚴交通
以杜釁端清田賦以厚民生復屯種以
資軍實皆粵西所宜急講而有司掣肘
難任者諸生桑梓之慮必有慨于中矣
punctuated: 公私交困，何策以善其終歟？營堡分兵列戍，所以保境安民也。乃戍守之卒既寡且疲，田主里排與賊勾結，甚者豪勢包食其田。議者欲專意招安，量輸煙竈，俾歲時羈縻，似矣。然夷性喜攻殺者十九，而奉漢法者十一；巨奸大猾鼓煽出沒，何計以消其黨歟？量地制賦，則壤之遺也。曩戶口稅畝半爲夷侵，疆理紊矣。邇者兵威稍振，有司方議平均；乃影射成風，清之未幾而告訐踵至，豈丈量之法卒不可行歟？分屯給軍，養兵之遺也。今屯田子粒半爲官占，行伍耗矣。邇者地方多故，部檄日行清理；乃詭冒成習，督之愈急而玩愒如故，豈屯種之制獨不可講歟？夫計兵食以固根本，嚴交通以杜釁端，清田賦以厚民生，復屯種以資軍實，皆粵西所宜急講，而有司掣肘難任者。諸生桑梓之慮，必有慨于中矣…
translation_en:
…when both public finances and private livelihoods are exhausted, by what policy can we bring this to a sound conclusion?

Dividing troops among camps and forts to form a chain of garrisons is the means to protect the borders and pacify the people. Yet the garrison soldiers are both few and exhausted, while landowners and community heads (lipai) collude with the bandits; in extreme cases, powerful magnates engross and live off their lands. Those who deliberate on policy wish to focus exclusively on offering amnesty and pacification, having them pay a modest hearth tax so as to keep them under loose rein (jimi) from year to year—this seems plausible enough. Yet by nature nine out of ten of the native tribesmen delight in raiding and killing, while only one in ten obeys Chinese law; great villains and arch-knaves stir them up and come and go at will. By what plan can their factions be dissolved?

Measuring the land to fix the tax assessment is the legacy of grading the soil. In the past, half of the registered households and taxable acreage were encroached upon by the tribesmen, throwing land boundaries and administration into disorder. Recently, as military prestige has been somewhat restored, the authorities are just now deliberating on equalizing assessments; yet fraudulent evasion (yingshe) has become a pervasive custom, so that no sooner is a clearance begun than accusations and counter-charges follow on one another's heels. Can it be that the method of land surveying is ultimately impossible to carry out?

Allotting state farms (tun) to supply the military is the legacy of maintaining troops on the land. Today, half of the grain yield from the military farms is seized by officers, and the ranks are depleted. Recently, because the region has suffered many disturbances, dispatches from the Ministry daily order a clearance and audit; yet fraudulent registration has become an entrenched habit, and the more urgently it is supervised, the more negligence and procrastination continue as before. Can it be that the system of military agricultural colonies alone cannot be profitably discussed?

To calculate troop strength and provisions so as to secure the foundation, to strictly prohibit illicit collusion so as to stop the sources of conflict, to clear up land taxes so as to enrich the people's livelihood, and to restore military farming so as to supply army provisions—all these are matters that demand urgent discussion in Guangxi, yet in which the authorities find their hands tied and the burden difficult to bear. In your concern for your native region, you students must surely have felt deep emotion within…

title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
者湛然德性之常用焉此則永肩一心而無所
事志矣自德之全於心而為仁仁之難成以違
仁者衆也必操存罔間于須臾虛明不雜以私
欲其所造次於是顛沛於是者渾乎天理之周
流焉此則中心安仁而無所事守矣學而至此
庶可與語純心已乎至若藝者道德仁之散見
亦養心者所不廢也是必會而通之以繹其趣
優而游之以適其情斯則應務因以不匱而此
心庶其有養矣豈曰藝成而下非君子之所貴
===
也而可無游歟要之由道德仁以及于藝而吾
心之理盡之矣自志道據德依仁以及游藝而
事心之功盡之矣兼内外該本末其斯以為善
學乎抑論古者小學教以六藝而夫子論學乃
以游藝終焉何也記有之不興其藝不能樂學
故操縵安弦施于正業之後此大學之教也然
非其要也夫子天縱之聖自謂不在多能而三
月不違一貫授受惟回之愚參之魯得之藝如
求達如賜不與焉噫聖學傳心之要端可識矣
punctuated: 者，湛然德性之常用焉。此則永肩一心，而無所事志矣。自德之全於心而為仁，仁之難成，以違仁者衆也。必操存罔間于須臾，虛明不雜以私欲，其所造次於是、顛沛於是者，渾乎天理之周流焉。此則中心安仁，而無所事守矣。學而至此，庶可與語純心已乎！至若藝者，道德仁之散見，亦養心者所不廢也。是必會而通之以繹其趣，優而游之以適其情，斯則應務因以不匱，而此心庶其有養矣。豈曰「藝成而下」，非君子之所貴也，而可無游歟？要之，由道德仁以及于藝，而吾心之理盡之矣；自志道、據德、依仁以及游藝，而事心之功盡之矣。兼内外、該本末，其斯以為善學乎！抑論古者小學教以六藝，而夫子論學乃以游藝終焉，何也？《記》有之：「不興其藝，不能樂學。」故操縵安弦，施于正業之後，此大學之教也，然非其要也。夫子天縱之聖，自謂不在多能，而「三月不違」、「一貫」授受，惟回之愚、參之魯得之，藝如求、達如賜不與焉。噫！聖學傳心之要，端可識矣。
translation_en: … is clear and tranquil, the constant functioning of one's moral nature. This is to forever uphold a single mind without needing to labor at setting the will. As for virtue being complete in the mind and becoming humaneness, humaneness is difficult to achieve because the ways of departing from humaneness are many. One must hold fast and preserve it without interruption even for an instant, keeping it empty and bright, unmixed with selfish desires; in moments of haste Cleaving to this, and in moments of danger cleaving to this, it becomes wholly the all-pervading flow of Heavenly Principle. This is to be at peace in humaneness in the center of one's mind, without needing to labor at guarding it. When learning reaches this point, one can perhaps speak of a pure mind! As for the arts, they are the scattered manifestations of the Way, virtue, and humaneness, and are also not neglected by those who nourish the mind. Therefore, one must synthesize and master them to draw out their meaning, and leisurely roam in them to suit one's feelings; thus in responding to affairs one will not be deficient, and this mind will perhaps be nourished. How could one say that "what is completed in the arts is inferior" and not valued by the gentleman, and that one may dispense with roaming in them? In sum, from the Way, virtue, and humaneness extending to the arts, the principles of our mind are exhausted; from setting the will on the Way, holding fast to virtue, and relying on humaneness extending to roaming in the arts, the effort of serving the mind is exhausted. Combining inner and outer, encompassing root and branch—is this not what it means to be good at learning? Yet if we consider that in antiquity the lesser learning taught the Six Arts, whereas the Master in discussing learning concluded with roaming in the arts, why is this? The Record of Rites (Liji) has it: "If one does not take pleasure in the arts, one cannot delight in learning." Therefore practicing the unstrung琴 and tuning the strings were applied after the regular studies; this was the teaching of the greater learning, yet it was not its essential point. The Master, a sage endowed by Heaven, said of himself that his sagehood did not lie in having many abilities; and as for "not departing from humaneness for three months" and the transmission and reception of the "one thread binding all," only the "foolish" Yan Hui 顏回 and the "dull" Zeng Shen 曾參 attained it, while someone accomplished in the arts like Ran Qiu 冉求 or discerning like端木賜 Duanmu Ci (Zigong) had no part in it. Alas! The essential point of the sage's learning in transmitting the mind can truly be recognized here.

title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
效乎君德貴明有惑其何以辨幾微也今惟尊
賢則啓心沃心之餘必多聞見而藻鑑於是乎
彰焉涵育深而聰明亶大賢明其大者不惑于
其大也論思久而智慮融次賢明其小者不惑
于其小也所謂察乎人倫明乎庶物斯理庶乎
其無疑矣非尊賢之效乎有是道立之身則賢
益知所尊有是不惑之心則身益知所脩以是
身以是賢而立政政其有不舉乎經常之道其
益如此抑論九經之目雖繁而脩身尊賢已思
===
過半然其始則在立志故文之敬止武之敬勝
皆志以率氣也志立則誠誠則道德九經一以
貫之矣哀公曰寡人不能進於是也惡在其爲
志也夫子未言脩身尊賢之事而先及其效亦
懼哀公之畏難也夫後之有志於文武之政者
自立志始
孟子曰禹惡旨酒而好善言湯執中立賢
無方文王視民如傷望道而未之見武
王不泄邇不忘遠周公思兼三王以施
punctuated:
效乎？君德貴明，有惑其何以辨幾微也？今惟尊賢，則啓心沃心之餘，必多聞見，而藻鑑於是乎彰焉。涵育深而聰明亶，大賢明其大者，不惑于其大也；論思久而智慮融，次賢明其小者，不惑于其小也。所謂察乎人倫，明乎庶物，斯理庶乎其無疑矣，非尊賢之效乎？有是道立之身，則賢益知所尊；有是不惑之心，則身益知所脩。以是身，以是賢，而立政，政其有不舉乎？經常之道，其益如此。抑論九經之目雖繁，而脩身、尊賢已思過半，然其始則在立志。故文之敬止，武之敬勝，皆志以率氣也。志立則誠，誠則道德、九經一以貫之矣。哀公曰：「寡人不能進於是也。」惡在其爲志也？夫子未言脩身、尊賢之事，而先及其效，亦懼哀公之畏難也夫！後之有志於文、武之政者，自立志始。

孟子曰：「禹惡旨酒而好善言。湯執中，立賢無方。文王視民如傷，望道而未之見。武王不泄邇，不忘遠。周公思兼三王，以施
translation_en:
…effect? The virtue of a ruler prizes clarity; if he suffers from confusion, how can he discern subtle incipiencies? Now, if only he honors the worthy, then beyond opening and enriching his mind, he will surely broaden his hearing and seeing, and his discerning judgment will thereby shine forth. When nurturing is deep and intelligence becomes genuine, great worthies clarify what is great, so he is not confused about great matters; when deliberation is sustained and wisdom becomes thorough, lesser worthies clarify what is small, so he is not confused about small matters. What is meant by "discerning human relationships and understanding the multitude of things"—this principle will then be nearly free from doubt. Is this not the effect of honoring the worthy? When one possesses a person established in the Way, one knows all the better how to honor the worthy; when one possesses a mind free from confusion, one knows all the better how to cultivate the person. With such a person and with such worthies to establish governance, how could governance fail to be upheld? Such are the benefits of the constant andinvariant Way.

Moreover, if we discuss the items of the Nine Standards (jiujing), although they are numerous, cultivating the person and honoring the worthy already account for more than half of the understanding. Yet their beginning lies in establishing the will. Thus King Wen's "reverent resting" and King Wu's "reverence prevailing" were both cases of the will leading the vital energy (qi). When the will is established, there is sincerity; when there is sincerity, moral virtue and the Nine Standards are penetrated by a single thread. Duke Ai said, "I, the lonely one, am unable to advance to this." Wherein, then, lay his will? Before the Master spoke of the tasks of cultivating the person and honoring the worthy, he first touched upon their effects, fearing indeed that Duke Ai would recoil from the difficulty! Those in later times who aspire to the governance of Kings Wen and Wu must begin by establishing their will.

Mencius said: "Yu hated fine wine and loved good words. Tang held fast to the Mean and established the worthy without regard to bounds. King Wen looked upon the people as if they were wounded, and gazed toward the Way as though he had not yet seen it. King Wu did not treat the near with familiarity, nor did he forget the distant. The Duke of Zhou sought to combine theThree Kings, so as to implement…

title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
四事其有不合者仰而思之夜以繼日
幸而得之坐以待旦
同考試官教諭劉批此題重羣聖憂勤惕勵之心上
而道統意于言外見之是作發揮明爽不事纏擾宜錄以式
考試官教授蔡批理明詞雅
考試官教授朱批俊潔
大賢於羣聖而各舉其任道之心焉蓋聖人以
斯道爲己任也任之切則其心之憂勤惕勵也
===
寧容已乎且聖人之經世以道而其任道以心
心之不息道之所以常存也吾嘗仰稽羣聖而
觀其憂勤惕勵之心豈惟堯舜爲然哉于夏而
得禹焉禹之心何心也旨酒是惡善言是好危
微之戒禹之祗承於舜者也于商而得湯焉湯
之心何心也惟中是執惟賢是用日躋之敬湯
之纘服于禹者也于周而得文武焉文作于前
而加意于斯道斯民視之如傷也望之未見也
文其純臨保之心者乎武承于後而致謹于易
punctuated:
四事；其有不合者，仰而思之，夜以繼日；幸而得之，坐以待旦。」

同考試官教諭劉批：此題重羣聖憂勤惕勵之心上，而道統意于言外見之。是作發揮明爽，不事纏擾，宜錄以式。
考試官教授蔡批：理明詞雅。
考試官教授朱批：俊潔。

大賢於羣聖，而各舉其任道之心焉。蓋聖人以斯道爲己任也，任之切，則其心之憂勤惕勵也，寧容已乎？且聖人之經世以道，而其任道以心。心之不息，道之所以常存也。吾嘗仰稽羣聖，而觀其憂勤惕勵之心，豈惟堯、舜爲然哉！于夏而得禹焉。禹之心，何心也？旨酒是惡，善言是好，危微之戒，禹之祗承於舜者也。于商而得湯焉。湯之心，何心也？惟中是執，惟賢是用，日躋之敬，湯之纘服于禹者也。于周而得文、武焉。文作于前，而加意于斯道斯民，視之如傷也，望之未見也，文其純臨保之心者乎！武承于後，而致謹于易…
translation_en:
…these four matters. Whenever there was anything that did not suit the times, he looked up and thought about it, from day into night; and when he was fortunate enough to grasp it, he sat waiting for the dawn."

Associate Examiner County Director of Studies Liu comments: This topic places weight on the anxious diligence and vigilant exertion in the minds of the various sages, while the meaning of the transmission of the Way is seen beyond the words. This composition develops the theme with clarity and briskness, without indulging in convoluted entanglement; it ought to be recorded as a model.
Examiner Prefectural Director of Studies Cai comments: The principles are clear and the diction is elegant.
Examiner Prefectural Director of Studies Zhu comments: Refined and concise.

The great worthy speaks of the various sages and brings forth for each the mind with which he took up the burden of the Way. Indeed, the sages took this Way as their personal responsibility; since they shouldered it so earnestly, how could the anxious diligence and vigilant exertion of their minds ever be allowed to cease?

Moreover, the sages ordered the world through the Way, and they shouldered the Way through their minds. That the mind never ceases is why the Way perpetually endures. I have looked up to examine the various sages and observed their minds of anxious diligence and vigilant exertion—how could this be true only of Yao and Shun! In the Xia dynasty, we find Yu. What sort of mind was Yu's mind? He despised fine wine and loved good words; the admonition regarding the precariousness of the human mind and the subtlety of the moral mind was what Yu reverently received from Shun. In the Shang dynasty, we find Tang. What sort of mind was Tang's mind? He held fast only to the Mean and employed only the worthy; the reverence that ascended daily was how Tang continued the work of Yu. In the Zhou dynasty, we find Kings Wen and Wu. Wen arose before, devoting his attention to this Way and this people—looking upon them as if they were wounded, and gazing toward the Way as if he had not yet seen it; did not Wen possess a mind of pure oversight and protection! Wu succeeded him afterward, exercising utmost caution over what is easily…

title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
忽易忘邇之不泄也遠之不忘也武其秉執兢
之心者乎夫得禹湯之心者文武也成文武之
德者周公也公則以三王之道雖各行于當時
而三王之事當變通于今日故因其時與勢之
所值思欲兼而施之方其未合則反覆以思不
知繼日之為勤也及其既得則黽勉于行不知
待旦之為勞也周公之善繼善述而敷求哲王
者又何如其為心也哉吁此道統之所由傳也
繼周公者又豈無以周公之心為心而繩斯道
===
于不墜者乎此孔孟之心所以不容已也大抵
聖賢以心相傳而究其所以為心亦惟致謹于
幾希之間耳蓋理欲之幾甚微而心之存亡甚
易衆人惟肆而失之故愈危而愈微聖人惟敬
而存之故既聖而益聖此一中之所由傳而萬
世心學之原也孔子之作春秋孟子之闢楊墨
無非欲人存此心而已有斯道之責者念之
易
厥孚交如信以發志也
punctuated:
忽易忘，邇之不泄也，遠之不忘也，武其秉執兢之心者乎！夫得禹、湯之心者，文、武也；成文、武之德者，周公也。公則以三王之道雖各行于當時，而三王之事當變通于今日。故因其時與勢之所值，思欲兼而施之。方其未合，則反覆以思，不知繼日之為勤也；及其既得，則黽勉于行，不知待旦之為勞也。周公之善繼善述，而敷求哲王者，又何如其為心也哉！吁！此道統之所由傳也。繼周公者，又豈無以周公之心為心，而繩斯道于不墜者乎？此孔、孟之心所以不容已也。大抵聖賢以心相傳，而究其所以為心，亦惟致謹于幾希之間耳。蓋理欲之幾甚微，而心之存亡甚易。衆人惟肆而失之，故愈危而愈微；聖人惟敬而存之，故既聖而益聖。此一中之所由傳，而萬世心學之原也。孔子之作《春秋》，孟子之闢楊、墨，無非欲人存此心而已。有斯道之責者，念之。

《易》
厥孚交如，信以發志也。
translation_en:
… easily neglected and easily forgotten: he did not treat the near with familiarity, nor did he forget the distant. Did not King Wu hold fast to a mind of cautious reverence! Now, those who grasped the minds of Yu and Tang were Kings Wen and Wu; he who brought the virtue of Wen and Wu to completion was the Duke of Zhou. The Duke considered that although the Ways of the Three Kings had each been practiced in their own times, the affairs of the Three Kings ought to be adapted to the present day. Therefore, according to the juncture of time and circumstance he encountered, he pondered with the desire to combine those three ways and put them into practice. While they were not yet harmonized, he turned them over and over in his thoughts, not counting it arduous to make night a continuation of the day; and once he had grasped them, he strove earnestly to put them into action, not counting it toilsome to sit waiting for the dawn. How great indeed was the mind of the Duke of Zhou in skillfully continuing their wills, skillfully carrying forward their affairs, and widely seeking out the former wise kings!

Ah! This is how the transmission of the Way (daotong) was handed down. Among those who came after the Duke of Zhou, how could there be none who took the mind of the Duke of Zhou as their own mind, and carried on this Way so that it would not fall to the ground? This is why the minds of Confucius and Mencius could not stop themselves. In general, sages and worthies transmitted the Way from mind to mind, and if we examine what constituted their mind, it was simply exercising the utmost caution over that slight distinction. For the incipient stirrings of Heavenly principle and human desire are most subtle, and the preservation or loss of the mind is most easy. The multitude indulge themselves and lose it, and thus the human mind becomes ever more precarious and the moral mind ever more subtle; the sages are reverent and preserve it, and thus having already become sages, they become ever more sagely. This is how the single Mean was transmitted, and it is the source of the learning of the mind (xinxue) for ten thousand generations. Confucius's composition of the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu) and Mencius's refutation of Yang Zhu and Mo Di were desired solely to make people preserve this mind and nothing more. Let those who bear responsibility for this Way take heed of it!

Book of Changes (Yi)
"His sincerity is reciprocated": his trustworthiness inspires the wills of others.

考試官敎授蔡批講下交孚宛然盛世氣象
考試官敎授朱批清雅脫塵
爻有同心之化由其誠能動物也蓋至誠而不
動者未之有也信以發志其交孚也固宜夫子
象傳之意以爲人君之治有也保大定功莫尚
乎賢養賢致民莫先乎信一信立而君道其庶
===
幾矣大有六五柔順虛中信之質也虛己以應
九二之賢而上下歸之周公之辭曰厥孚交如
蓋言其始也純心以任賢其繼也因賢以得衆
誼之相維分不得而間之觀心于朝君臣其一
體也情之相繫跡不得而疎之觀心于野天下
猶一家也若是者非强之也亦非私也乃信以
發志耳蓋人臣之媚玆其君孰無是志也惟上
無以發之則雖其義不可逃求其感奮而興未
必然也天下之歸向其君孰無是志也惟上無
punctuated:
同考試官敎諭李批：「發志處發揮殆盡，一結尤見忠愛，取之。」
考試官敎授蔡批：「講下交孚，宛然盛世氣象。」
考試官敎授朱批：「清雅脫塵。」
爻有同心之化，由其誠能動物也。蓋至誠而不動者，未之有也。信以發志，其交孚也固宜。夫子《象傳》之意，以爲人君之治有也，保大定功，莫尚乎賢；養賢致民，莫先乎信。一信立，而君道其庶幾矣。《大有》六五，柔順虛中，信之質也；虛己以應九二之賢，而上下歸之。周公之辭曰：「厥孚交如。」蓋言其始也，純心以任賢；其繼也，因賢以得衆。誼之相維，分不得而間之，觀心于朝，君臣其一體也；情之相繫，跡不得而疎之，觀心于野，天下猶一家也。若是者，非强之也，亦非私也，乃信以發志耳。蓋人臣之媚玆其君，孰無是志也？惟上無以發之，則雖其義不可逃，求其感奮而興，未必然也。天下之歸向其君，孰無是志也？惟上無
translation_en:
Associate Examiner and Instructor Li 李 comments: "The passage on 'inspiring the will' is expounded almost exhaustively, and the conclusion especially shows loyalty and affection. Selected."
Examiner and Confucian School Director Cai 蔡 comments: "The exposition of mutual trust vividly evokes the atmosphere of a flourishing age."
Examiner and Confucian School Director Zhu 朱 comments: "Pure, refined, and free from vulgarity."

That the line possesses the transforming power of uniting hearts in harmony is because its sincerity can move others. Indeed, there has never been one of utmost sincerity who failed to move others. When trustworthiness inspires the wills of others, it is only natural that there is mutual confidence. The meaning of the Master's Commentary on the Images (Xiangzhuan) is that in a ruler's governance of abundance, for preserving greatness and establishing merit, nothing surpasses the worthy; for nourishing the worthy and winning over the people, nothing comes before trustworthiness. Once trustworthiness is established, the Way of the ruler is nearly complete. The Six in the Fifth place of the hexagram Possession in Great Measure (Dayou), gentle, compliant, and receptive in the center, embodies the substance of trustworthiness; humbling himself to respond to the worthy of the Nine in the Second place, both those above and those below turn to him in allegiance. The Duke of Zhou's line statement says: "His sincerity is reciprocated." This means that at the outset, he employs the worthy with a pure heart; subsequently, through the worthy he wins the multitude. Bound together by righteousness, differences in rank cannot divide them; observing their hearts at court, ruler and minister are as one body. Linked together by affection, physical distance cannot estrange them; observing their hearts in the countryside, all under Heaven is like a single family. That it is so is neither forced nor born of partiality; it is simply that trustworthiness inspires their wills. For among ministers who love their ruler, who does not have this will? Only if the one above has nothing with which to inspire it, then although they cannot escape their duty, to expect them to be moved and roused to action is not necessarily assured. Among all under Heaven who turn in allegiance toward their ruler, who does not have this will? Only if the one above has nothing…

title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
考試官敎授蔡批發出大舜命岳之意宛然
考試官敎授朱批詞理俱到
聖君謀治於大臣欲其廣視聽于天下焉夫視
聽以天下則民情無不達矣此道盡而民焉有
不得其所者哉宜帝舜首詢于四岳也意曰人
君通天下以為一身則必公天下以為視聽四
岳者作朕耳目而民情之通塞繫焉者也將何
以輔我哉誠以今日紹堯致治固嘗見時雍之
化矣然四海至大而民情之伏也無窮則遺于
===
吾明之外者尚多也爾其為我明四目焉倡率
作之權以廓吾大觀之哲太和景象吾固得而
快覩也而四海困窮吾亦得而兼照焉合四方
之明為一人之明固有不下堂階而視周於萬
里矣昔之時雍者庶其再見矣乎亦嘗聞擊壤
之歌矣然四方至廣而民情之隱也無盡則遺
于吾聰之外者何限也爾其為我達四聰焉任
率先之責以大吾兼聽之公九敘惟歌固得而
聞其休也而下民其咨亦得而聞其戚焉合四
punctuated:
考試官敎授蔡批：發出大舜命岳之意宛然。
考試官敎授朱批：詞理俱到。

聖君謀治於大臣，欲其廣視聽于天下焉。夫視聽以天下，則民情無不達矣。此道盡而民焉有不得其所者哉？宜帝舜首詢于四岳也。意曰：人君通天下以為一身，則必公天下以為視聽。四岳者，作朕耳目，而民情之通塞繫焉者也，將何以輔我哉？誠以今日紹堯致治，固嘗見時雍之化矣。然四海至大，而民情之伏也無窮，則遺于吾明之外者尚多也。爾其為我明四目焉，倡率作之權，以廓吾大觀之哲。太和景象，吾固得而快覩也；而四海困窮，吾亦得而兼照焉。合四方之明為一人之明，固有不下堂階，而視周於萬里矣。昔之時雍者，庶其再見矣乎！亦嘗聞擊壤之歌矣。然四方至廣，而民情之隱也無盡，則遺于吾聰之外者何限也。爾其為我達四聰焉，任率先之責，以大吾兼聽之公。九敘惟歌，固得而聞其休也；而下民其咨，亦得而聞其戚焉。合四
translation_en:
Comment by Examiner and Instructor Cai: It vividly brings out the intent of the great Shun's charge to the Chiefs of the Four Mountains.
Comment by Examiner and Instructor Zhu: Both diction and principle hit the mark.

When the sage ruler takes counsel on governance with his great ministers, he wishes them to broaden his sight and hearing across all under heaven. Now, when one sees and hears through all under heaven, there is nothing in the conditions of the people that fails to reach above. When this way is fulfilled, how could any of the people fail to find their proper place? Rightly did Emperor Shun begin by consulting the Chiefs of the Four Mountains. His meaning was as follows: Since a ruler unites all under heaven into a single body, he must make all under heaven the public medium of his sight and hearing. The Chiefs of the Four Mountains act as my ears and eyes, and upon them depends whether the conditions of the people are communicated or obstructed—how, then, will you assist me? Truly, as I today succeed Yao in bringing about order, I have indeed already witnessed the transformative influence of general harmony. Yet the Four Seas are vast in the extreme, and the hidden conditions of the people are inexhaustible; thus what remains beyond the reach of my own clear sight is still great. You must clarify the four eyes for me, taking the initiative to lead and inspire, so as to enlarge the wisdom of my comprehensive view. The scenes of supreme harmony I shall of course be able to behold with delight; yet the distress and poverty within the Four Seas I shall also be able to illuminate together. By combining the clear sight of the four quarters into the clear sight of the One Man, without descending from the hall steps my vision will indeed reach everywhere across ten thousand li. May that general harmony of the past perhaps be seen once more! I have also heard the song of tapping on the earth. Yet the four quarters are broad in the extreme, and the unvoiced feelings of the people are endless; how boundless, then, is what remains beyond the reach of my own acute hearing! You must open the four ears for me, bearing the responsibility of leading the way, so as to magnify the impartiality of my comprehensive listening. When the Nine Offices are in order and celebrated in song, I shall of course be able to hear of their blessings; yet when the common people sigh and murmur, I shall also be able to hear of their griefs. By combining the four…

title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
者于是爲無負矣是蓋履其位思盡其實有其
實斯稱其名夏臣之忠愛至矣禹之籲俊尊帝
以此吾王其知法哉抑此大禹得之皐陶而見
知于虞廷者也堯舜禹以一中照臨於上而孔
壬之畏猶兢兢焉則當時君臣致謹于迪知忱
恂有道矣蓋惟中則好惡不偏而官人斯當此
當時所以庶明勵翼而野無遺賢也不然用舍
偏而匪人進所謂九德者皆非矣然則君相用
人其有本哉故曰取人以身
===
詩
鶴鳴于九皐聲聞于天魚在于渚或潛在
淵樂彼之園爰有樹檀其下維穀他山
之石可以攻玉
同考試官教諭李批〔體認含蓄是得詩人言外之意者錄之〕
考試官教授蔡批〔詠物處清奇可觀〕
考試官教授朱批〔擺脫宿塵宜式多士〕
punctuated:
者，于是爲無負矣。是蓋履其位，思盡其實，有其實，斯稱其名。夏臣之忠愛至矣！禹之籲俊尊帝以此，吾王其知法哉！抑此大禹得之皐陶，而見知于虞廷者也。堯、舜、禹以一中照臨於上，而孔壬之畏猶兢兢焉，則當時君臣致謹于迪知忱恂有道矣。蓋惟中則好惡不偏，而官人斯當，此當時所以庶明勵翼，而野無遺賢也。不然，用舍偏而匪人進，所謂九德者皆非矣。然則君相用人，其有本哉！故曰：「取人以身。」

詩
鶴鳴于九皐，聲聞于天。魚在于渚，或潛在淵。樂彼之園，爰有樹檀，其下維穀。他山之石，可以攻玉。
同考試官教諭李批：〔體認含蓄，是得詩人言外之意者，錄之。〕
考試官教授蔡批：〔詠物處清奇可觀。〕
考試官教授朱批：〔擺脫宿塵，宜式多士。〕
translation_en:
… [those] would thereby not fail in their duties. This is because in occupying their positions, they think of fulfilling their substance; having the substance, they thus match their titles. The loyalty and devotion of the ministers of Xia were utmost indeed! It was by this means that Yu called forth men of excellence to honor the Lord; may our King know to take this as his model!

Moreover, this was what Great Yu obtained from Gao Yao and knew from witnessing it in the court of Yu [Shun]. Yao, Shun, and Yu shone down from above with a single centrality, yet in their dread of artful flatterers they remained ever cautious and wary; thus the ruler and ministers of that time had a way of exercising utmost care in advancing and knowing those who were sincere and trustworthy. For only when there is centrality are likes and dislikes unbiased, and the appointment of men to office is consequently fitting. This is why at that time the numerous enlightened ones strove to assist like wings, and no worthy men were left neglected in the wilds. Otherwise, if employment and dismissal are biased and unworthy men advance, what are called the Nine Virtues will all be falsified. This being so, when ruler and chief minister employ men, does it not have a fundamental root? Therefore it is said: "One selects men by means of one's own person."

Classic of Poetry (Shijing):
"The crane cries in the nine marshes, and its voice is heard in the sky. The fish lies by the islet, or plunges into the deep. Pleasant is that garden, where there are sandalwood trees, and beneath them the paper-mulberry. The stones of those other hills may be used to polish jade."

Associate Examiner, Instructor Li's comment: [Its comprehension is subtle and reserved; this is one who has grasped the meaning beyond the poet's words. Record it.]
Examiner, Professor Cai's comment: [The passages depicting things are pure, extraordinary, and worthy of appreciation.]
Examiner, Professor Zhu's comment: [It shakes off stale dust and is fitting to serve as a model for the many scholars.]

title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
也縱有睦魯之心則不執兵于邊鄙亦已幸矣
今隨感而化是聖人一言重於三軍也綏之斯
來動之斯和吾于是知禮之可以爲國矣爭伯
業者景也縱有歸地之心則待請而後與固其
常也今誠服而歸是聖人功化神於俄頃也期
月而可三年有成吾于是知聖人用世之績矣
然則斯歸也其諸異乎濟西謹闡之歸歟斯來
也其亦猶夫屈完之來歟春秋特書齊人來歸
鄆讙龜陰田所以見齊人心服而歸田孔子以
===
禮化强之績也聖人以天自處何自序之爲嫌
哉抑聞之晏嬰知矣而不知仲尼乃導其君以
謝過獨何歟蓋孔子之聖夫人能知之豈晏子
果不知乎其託爲詞說以沮之或亦歸女樂之
意與雖然三田歸而齊景服義之美著矣其獻
替之功不可誣也故曰晏子以其君顯
禮記
天子布德行惠
punctuated:
也。縱有睦魯之心，則不執兵于邊鄙，亦已幸矣；今隨感而化，是聖人一言重於三軍也。「綏之斯來，動之斯和」，吾于是知禮之可以爲國矣。爭伯業者，景也。縱有歸地之心，則待請而後與，固其常也；今誠服而歸，是聖人功化神於俄頃也。「期月而可，三年有成」，吾于是知聖人用世之績矣。然則斯歸也，其諸異乎濟西、謹、闡之歸歟？斯來也，其亦猶夫屈完之來歟？《春秋》特書「齊人來歸鄆、讙、龜陰田」，所以見齊人心服而歸田，孔子以禮化强之績也。聖人以天自處，何自序之爲嫌哉？抑聞之：晏嬰知矣，而不知仲尼，乃導其君以謝過，獨何歟？蓋孔子之聖，夫人能知之，豈晏子果不知乎？其託爲詞說以沮之，或亦歸女樂之意與？雖然，三田歸而齊景服義之美著矣，其獻替之功不可誣也。故曰：「晏子以其君顯。」

禮記
天子布德行惠
translation_en:
… Even if he had intended to maintain friendly relations with Lu, merely refraining from taking up arms along the borderlands would already have been fortunate enough. Now, however, he was immediately moved and transformed—showing that a single word from the sage carries more weight than three armies. "When he comforts them, they come; when he moves them, they are harmonious"—from this I know that ritual propriety can indeed be used to govern a state!

He who contended for hegemony was Duke Jing [of Qi 齊景公]. Even if he had intended to return the lands, waiting for a formal request before granting them would normally have been his custom. Now, however, he submitted in sincere admiration and returned them—showing that the transformative achievement of the sage works its marvel in an instant. "In a year's cycle it would be acceptable, and in three years there would be accomplishment"—from this I know the efficacy of the sage's service to the world!

That being so, is not this return of land different from the return of the lands west of the Ji River 濟西, or of Huan 讙 [printed as 謹] and Chan 闡? And is not this coming [of Qi] comparable to the coming of Qu Wan 屈完? The Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu 春秋) specially records that "the men of Qi came to return the fields of Yun 鄆, Huan 讙, and Guiyin 龜陰" in order to show that the men of Qi submitted in their hearts and returned the fields—the achievement of Confucius (Kongzi 孔子) in transforming the strong through ritual propriety. Since the sage Comported himself as Heaven, why would he shy away from recording his own deeds?

Yet I have also heard it said: Yan Ying 晏嬰 was wise, yet he did not truly know Zhongni 仲尼 [Confucius]; why then did he alone guide his ruler to apologize for his fault? Indeed, anyone could recognize the sageliness of Confucius—could Master Yan (Yanzi 晏子) really have been ignorant of it? When he contrived arguments to thwart him [from being enfeoffed in Qi], was that not perhaps the same sort of calculation as when [Qi later] sent the female musicians? Even so, with the return of the three tracts of land, the admirable virtue of Duke Jing of Qi in submitting to righteousness was made manifest, and Yan Ying's merit in offering counsel on what to promote and what to discard cannot be denied. Therefore it is said: "Master Yan became illustrious through his ruler."

Record of Rites (Liji 禮記)
"The Son of Heaven disseminates virtue and practices benevolence…"

title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
而達之下者莫非人君之至愛矣其猶天載無
聲而品彙均荷其並育之化乎要之德與惠非
二也自仁之存諸心爲德自仁之及于物爲惠
德者惠之本惠行而德斯布矣王者憲天之政
固如此則其參天地而贊化育也有由然哉抑
論賑乏周困是爲德惠固矣而繼之以聘賢禮
士者何也蓋天生物不能自遂而付之君君繼
天不能獨理而寄之臣則任賢圖治尤帝王要
務而爲天下得人所以爲仁之大也堯之舉舜
===
舜之舉禹臯陶率是道爾不然春和議賑一代
賢主也而胡以未遑少之故曰堯舜之仁不徧
愛人急親賢也
禮者殊事合敬者也樂者異文合愛者也
同考試官教諭劉批敬愛即在事文之中特不因事
文而有殊異耳是作足以發之
考試官教授蔡批講合敬合愛處精透
考試官教授朱批詞氣雅暢
punctuated:
而達之下者，莫非人君之至愛矣。其猶天載無聲，而品彙均荷其並育之化乎！要之，德與惠非二也。自仁之存諸心爲德，自仁之及于物爲惠。德者，惠之本；惠行而德斯布矣。王者憲天之政固如此，則其參天地而贊化育也，有由然哉！抑論賑乏周困是爲德惠固矣，而繼之以聘賢禮士者，何也？蓋天生物不能自遂而付之君，君繼天不能獨理而寄之臣。則任賢圖治，尤帝王要務，而爲天下得人，所以爲仁之大也。堯之舉舜，舜之舉禹、臯陶，率是道爾。不然，春和議賑，一代賢主也，而胡以未遑少之？故曰：「堯、舜之仁，不徧愛人，急親賢也。」
「禮者，殊事合敬者也；樂者，異文合愛者也。」
同考試官教諭劉批：敬愛即在事文之中，特不因事文而有殊異耳。是作足以發之。
考試官教授蔡批：講合敬合愛處精透。
考試官教授朱批：詞氣雅暢。
translation_en:
…and what reaches those below is nothing other than the ruler's utmost love. Is this not like the workings of Heaven, which are without sound, yet all things equally receive its transformation that nurtures them together? In sum, virtue (de) and kindness (hui) are not two separate things. From the standpoint of benevolence preserved in the mind, it is called virtue; from the standpoint of benevolence extended to creatures, it is called kindness. Virtue is the root of kindness; when kindness is practiced, virtue is thereby spread abroad. The government of a true king in modeling himself on Heaven is truly like this; thus, his forming a triad with Heaven and Earth and assisting in their transforming and nourishing work surely has its basis!

Yet if we consider that relieving the needy and aiding the distressed indeed constitute virtue and kindness, why is this then followed by inviting the worthy and showing ritual courtesy to scholars? It is because Heaven gives birth to things but cannot bring them to fulfillment by itself, and so entrusts them to the ruler; the ruler succeeds Heaven but cannot govern alone, and so entrusts the task to his ministers. Therefore, employing the worthy to plan for good governance is an especially vital duty of emperors and kings, and obtaining men of talent for the world is what constitutes the greatness of benevolence. Yao's elevation of Shun, and Shun's elevation of Yu and Gao Yao, all followed this path. Otherwise, deliberating on famine relief in the mildness of spring was the act of a worthy ruler of an era—why then was he faulted for not yet having time for what was most urgent? Hence it is said: "The benevolence of Yao and Shun did not extend its love to all men alike; it considered attachments to the worthy urgent."

"Ritual is that which unites reverence across differing affairs; music is that which unites affection across differing patterns."

Comment by Associate Examiner, County Director of Studies Liu: Reverence and affection reside right within the affairs and patterns; they simply do not differ on account of the affairs and patterns. This composition is sufficient to elucidate this point.
Comment by Examiner, Prefectural Director of Studies Cai: The explanation of uniting reverence and uniting affection is precise and penetrating.
Comment by Examiner, Prefectural Director of Studies Zhu: The diction and tone are elegant and fluent.

title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
記者于禮樂而著其情之出於一焉甚矣禮樂
有自然之情也事文異而敬愛一是可見其情
之同矣此禮樂感化之由而記者著之意謂禮
樂之道合乎造化而感夫人心然人心之所由
感亦以禮樂本無異情耳自聖人防民僞以敎
之中而禮制焉禮自外作有其事必有其敬者
也人皆以事殊則敬與之俱殊矣而不知至賾
不齊者其燦然之迹至敬無文者其秩然之原
經禮固惟三百矣而所以綱紀乎人道一中正
===
以爲之質也曲禮固惟三千矣而所以品節乎
人情一恭順以爲之制也善觀大禮者不求諸
事求諸敬斯其悉禮之精乎自聖人防民情以
敎之和而樂作焉樂由中出有其文必有其愛
者也人皆以文異則愛與之俱異矣而不知治
其飾無非英華之發動其本悉出和順之休五
聲雖異其音而聲之所以成文爲音者皆欣喜
之發越也六律雖異其數而律之所以得數有
常者皆歡愛之流形也善觀大樂者不求諸文
punctuated: 記者于禮樂，而著其情之出於一焉。甚矣，禮樂有自然之情也！事文異而敬愛一，是可見其情之同矣。此禮樂感化之由，而記者著之。意謂：禮樂之道，合乎造化而感夫人心，然人心之所由感，亦以禮樂本無異情耳。自聖人防民僞以敎之中，而禮制焉。禮自外作，有其事必有其敬者也。人皆以事殊則敬與之俱殊矣，而不知至賾不齊者，其燦然之迹；至敬無文者，其秩然之原。經禮固惟三百矣，而所以綱紀乎人道，一中正以爲之質也；曲禮固惟三千矣，而所以品節乎人情，一恭順以爲之制也。善觀大禮者，不求諸事，求諸敬，斯其悉禮之精乎！自聖人防民情以敎之和，而樂作焉。樂由中出，有其文必有其愛者也。人皆以文異則愛與之俱異矣，而不知治其飾，無非英華之發；動其本，悉出和順之休。五聲雖異其音，而聲之所以成文爲音者，皆欣喜之發越也；六律雖異其數，而律之所以得數有常者，皆歡愛之流形也。善觀大樂者，不求諸文，
translation_en:
With regard to ritual and music, the recorder of the Record of Rites (Liji) makes manifest how their inner sentiments issue from a single source. Truly great indeed is the spontaneous sentiment inherent in ritual and music! Though their affairs and patterned expressions differ, their reverence and affection are one; from this one can see that their underlying sentiments are the same. This is the means by which ritual and music move and transform people, and so the recorder sets it forth.

The meaning is that the Way of ritual and music accords with the creative transformations of nature and moves the human heart; yet the reason the human heart is moved is simply that ritual and music originally have no differing sentiments. Ever since the sages guarded against the hypocrisy of the people so as to teach them centrality, ritual was instituted. Ritual is enacted from the outside; wherever there is a ceremonial affair, there is necessarily its accompanying reverence. People all suppose that because the affairs differ, the reverence differs along with them. Yet they do not know that what is most intricate and varied are its resplendent outward traces, whereas utmost reverence without embellishment is its orderly source. The major rules of ritual (jingli) are indeed three hundred in number, yet that by which they give structure to the human Way takes a single impartiality and uprightness as its substance; the minor rules of demeanor (quli) are indeed three thousand in number, yet that by which they grade and regulate human feelings takes a single respectful compliance as its rule. One who is skilled at observing great ritual does not seek it in the outward affairs, but seeks it in reverence—is this not to comprehend the essence of ritual fully?

Ever since the sages guarded against the unruly passions of the people so as to teach them harmony, music was created. Music issues from within; wherever there is a patterned expression, there is necessarily its accompanying affection. People all suppose that because the patterned expressions differ, the affection differs along with them. Yet they do not know that ordering its outward ornaments is nothing other than the burgeoning of its efflorescence, while stirring its root comes entirely from the beauty of harmonious compliance. Although the five notes differ in their tones, that by which the notes form patterns and become music is in every case the outward expression of joy and delight; although the six pitch-pipes differ in their numerical proportions, that by which the pitch-pipes attain their constant numbers is in every case the flowing manifestation of joyful affection. One who is skilled at observing great music does not seek it in the patterned expressions, …

title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
求諸愛斯其知樂之深乎吁禮樂有敬愛之情
如此情同而四海之內合敬同愛也固其所哉
雖然聖人之禮樂通天地而感四海固也君子
于此有致禮樂之功焉誠能以禮治躬以樂治
心則莊敬嚴威易直子諒愛敬備于一身而中
和之極建矣舉而措之天下民莫不承聽承順
參賛位育之化亦繇是致焉然則禮樂可斯須
去身哉圖治者盍審諸
第貳塲
===
論
爲聖本由學而成
同考試官教諭　批以盡人合天立意得聖學要領
至發揮大禹作聖工夫無餘蘊高薦允宜
考試官教授蔡　批議論根柢造語高古佳士
考試官教授朱　批典實莊重
論曰聖人不以其得之天者自恃而以其脩之
人者事天故其成聖也不以天而以人夫聖人
punctuated:
求諸愛，斯其知樂之深乎？吁！禮樂有敬愛之情如此，情同而四海之內合敬同愛也，固其所哉！雖然，聖人之禮樂通天地而感四海，固也；君子于此，有致禮樂之功焉。誠能以禮治躬，以樂治心，則莊敬嚴威、易直子諒，愛敬備于一身，而中和之極建矣。舉而措之天下，民莫不承聽承順，參賛位育之化，亦繇是致焉。然則禮樂可斯須去身哉？圖治者盍審諸！

第貳塲

論

爲聖本由學而成

同考試官教諭　批：以盡人合天立意，得聖學要領；至發揮大禹作聖工夫，無餘蘊，高薦允宜。
考試官教授蔡　批：議論根柢，造語高古，佳士。
考試官教授朱　批：典實莊重。

論曰：聖人不以其得之天者自恃，而以其脩之人者事天，故其成聖也，不以天而以人。夫聖人
translation_en:
… look for it in affection—is this not to understand music deeply? Ah! Since rites and music embody the feelings of reverence and affection in this way, the feelings are the same, and it is only natural that within the四海 (Four Seas) all unite in reverence and share in affection! Even so, while the rites and music of the sages penetrate heaven and earth and move all within the Four Seas as a matter of course, the noble man has work to do here in bringing rites and music to realization. If he can truly govern his person through rites and govern his mind through music, then with solemn reverence and stern majesty, and an easy, upright, filial, and sincere heart, affection and reverence will be complete within his own person, and the ultimate standard of equilibrium and harmony will be established. When he takes this and applies it to the world, none among the people will fail to heed and obey, and the transformative work of participating in the cosmic order to establish heaven and earth and nourish the myriad things will also be achieved through this. That being so, may rites and music be separated from one's person even for a moment? Why do those who plan for governance not examine this closely!

Second Session

Discourse

"Becoming a Sage Basically Comes About Through Learning"

Associate Examiner, Instructor [blank], comments: Establishing its thesis on fulfilling the human to accord with Heaven, this grasps the essential point of sage learning; as for its elaboration of the Great Yu's (Da Yu 大禹) effort in becoming a sage, nothing is left unexpressed. High recommendation is truly fitting.
Examiner, Instructor Cai 蔡, comments: The argumentation is well-grounded and the phrasing lofty and archaic; a fine scholar.
Examiner, Instructor Zhu 朱, comments: Classical, substantive, and dignified.

title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
者天之所生以寄斯道之統者也生之也不偶
故其畀之也獨厚畀之也獨厚故其望之也獨
隆使聖人自恃其厚於天也而不思學以成之
則天下萬事萬物之理寧能會之於至精至一
以無失其中而當天之意乎是故其憂勤惕勵
之心不能自釋而盡人合天之學不容已也張
敬夫曰禹之爲聖本由學而成意其知禹者乎
其善言天人之際者乎且夫學之名何始乎伏
羲神農黃帝各以其道而爲君仰觀俯察制器
===
尚象天下稱聖焉不聞其所謂學也孔子刪書
斷自唐虞而下其言堯舜之聖一則曰放勳格
天一則曰重華協帝不聞其所謂學也是數聖
人者皆繼天立極之君也豈其得之天也至厚
而無俟於學與抑禹之聖不及三皇二帝而必
待於學與曰是不然洪荒之世吾無得而論矣
堯之克明非學以明之乎舜之大智非學以知
之乎是故都俞吁咈皆學之事百揆岳牧皆學
之人總章衢室皆學之地耄老倦勤皆學之時
punctuated:
者，天之所生以寄斯道之統者也。生之也不偶，故其畀之也獨厚；畀之也獨厚，故其望之也獨隆。使聖人自恃其厚於天也，而不思學以成之，則天下萬事萬物之理，寧能會之於至精至一，以無失其中而當天之意乎？是故其憂勤惕勵之心不能自釋，而盡人合天之學不容已也。張敬夫曰：「禹之爲聖，本由學而成。」意其知禹者乎？其善言天人之際者乎？

且夫學之名何始乎？伏羲、神農、黃帝，各以其道而爲君，仰觀俯察，制器尚象，天下稱聖焉，不聞其所謂學也。孔子刪《書》，斷自唐、虞而下，其言堯、舜之聖，一則曰「放勳格天」，一則曰「重華協帝」，不聞其所謂學也。是數聖人者，皆繼天立極之君也，豈其得之天也至厚，而無俟於學與？抑禹之聖不及三皇、二帝，而必待於學與？曰：是不然。洪荒之世，吾無得而論矣。堯之克明，非學以明之乎？舜之大智，非學以知之乎？是故都俞吁咈，皆學之事；百揆岳牧，皆學之人；總章衢室，皆學之地；耄老倦勤，皆學之時。
translation_en:
… is one whom Heaven brings forth in order to entrust with the transmission of this Way. Since bringing him forth is no mere coincidence, what Heaven bestows upon him is uniquely generous; and since what it bestows upon him is uniquely generous, what it expects of him is uniquely grand. Suppose a sage were to rely arrogantly upon the generosity he received from Heaven and not think of bringing it to completion through learning: how then could he comprehend the principles of the myriad affairs and myriad things in the world in their utmost refinement and utmost unity, so as never to lose hold of the Mean and thereby fulfill the intention of Heaven? Therefore, his mind of anxious diligence and vigilant exertion cannot be set aside, and his learning—which exhausts human effort in order to accord with Heaven—cannot cease. Zhang Jingfu 張敬夫 [Zhang Shi 張栻] said: "Yu's 禹 becoming a sage was fundamentally achieved through learning." Might we not suppose that he truly understood Yu, and that he was skilled at speaking of the relation between Heaven and man?

Moreover, when did the term "learning" first arise? Fuxi 伏羲, Shennong 神農, and the Yellow Emperor 黃帝 each ruled by means of his own Way; looking up to observe the heavens and looking down to examine the earth, they fashioned implements and revered symbolic images, so that the world acclaimed them as sages—yet one does not hear of what they called "learning." When Confucius 孔子 edited the Book of Documents (Shu), he began from the eras of Tang 唐 and Yu 虞 onward. In speaking of the sageliness of Yao 堯 and Shun 舜, of the one it says "of vast merit, reaching to Heaven," and of the other it says "ofsplendid brilliance, in harmony with the former sovereign"—yet one does not hear of what they called "learning." These several sages were all sovereigns who succeeded Heaven and established the supreme standard. Was it that what they received from Heaven was so supremely generous that they had no need to wait upon learning? Or was it that Yu's sageliness did not equal that of the Three Sovereigns and Two Emperors, so that he necessarily had to depend upon learning? I say: It is not so. Of the era of primordial antiquity, we have no way to speak. Yet as for Yao's ability to make bright his virtue, was it not made bright through learning? As for Shun's great wisdom, was it not known through learning? Therefore, the cries of approval and sighs of dissent at court were all the business of learning; the General Regulator, the Four Peaks, and the Twelve Pastors were all companions in learning; the Bright Hall (Zongzhang) and theAudience Chamber (Qushi) were all places of learning; and even the years of advanced old age and weariness from toil were all times of learning. …

title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
堯與舜焉不學特無學之名耳無學之名而有
學之實此聖人之心學均之爲善事其天也何
獨於禹而疑之禹得統於舜者也堯之命舜曰
允執厥中中之一言帝王心學之傳盡之矣舜
之命禹則益之以三言蓋至於禹之時沕穆之
氣恐其漸漓也故人心不得不戒其危道心不
得不戒其微非精非一何以守中禹之聞斯言
也曰曆數在我矣民心屬我矣天之厚而望我
何以副之於是有所默然長思焉有所惕然深
===
省焉有所汲汲不能自已焉不以有天下爲樂
而以任天下是懼民生未遂何以上追夫標枝
野鹿之世民心不古何以遠紹夫協和於變之
風九載弗績幹蠱蓋愆何以近傚乎克諧蒸乂
之孝危者如何而安微者如何而著精者何以
不雜一者何以不二任之重故憂之深憂之深
故學之篤是故一饋十起一沐三握無時非學
也克勤于邦克儉于家無地非學也昌言拜益
底績俞皐無人非學也飲食菲之宮室卑之衣
punctuated: 堯與舜焉不學？特無學之名耳。無學之名而有學之實，此聖人之心學，均之爲善事其天也，何獨於禹而疑之？禹得統於舜者也。堯之命舜，曰「允執厥中」。中之一言，帝王心學之傳盡之矣。舜之命禹，則益之以三言。蓋至於禹之時，沕穆之氣恐其漸漓也，故人心不得不戒其危，道心不得不戒其微，非精非一，何以守中？禹之聞斯言也，曰：「曆數在我矣，民心屬我矣，天之厚而望我，何以副之？」於是有所默然長思焉，有所惕然深省焉，有所汲汲不能自已焉。不以有天下爲樂，而以任天下是懼。民生未遂，何以上追夫標枝野鹿之世？民心不古，何以遠紹夫協和於變之風？九載弗績，幹蠱蓋愆，何以近傚乎克諧蒸乂之孝？危者如何而安？微者如何而著？精者何以不雜？一者何以不二？任之重，故憂之深；憂之深，故學之篤。是故一饋十起，一沐三握，無時非學也；克勤于邦，克儉于家，無地非學也；昌言拜益，底績俞皐，無人非學也；飲食菲之，宮室卑之，衣
translation_en: How could Yao and Shun not have engaged in learning? It is merely that they lacked the word "learning." Lacking the word "learning" while possessing the reality of learning—this was the learning of the mind-and-heart of the sages, through which all alike served their Heaven well. Why then should one doubt this only in the case of Yu? Yu was the one who received the succession from Shun. When Yao charged Shun, he said, "Sincerely hold fast the Mean." With that single word, "the Mean," the transmission of the emperors' and kings' learning of the mind-and-heart was expressed in full. When Shun charged Yu, however, he added three more phrases to it. For by the time of Yu, it was feared that the profound and pure ethos might gradually thin out; therefore, with the human mind one could not but guard against its precariousness, and with the mind of the Way one could not but guard against its subtlety. Without being discerning and without being undivided, how could one hold fast the Mean? When Yu heard these words, he said to himself: "The heavenly succession now rests with me; the hearts of the people are now entrusted to me. Heaven has been generous to me and places its hopes in me—how shall I live up to them?" Thereupon he fell into silent and prolonged reflection, into fearful and deep self-examination, and into an urgent, unceasing striving. He did not take joy in possessing the realm, but rather feared the burden of taking responsibility for it. "If the people's livelihood is not yet fulfilled, how can I match the ancient age when rulers were like high branches and the people like wild deer? If the people's hearts are no longer as in antiquity, how can I carry on from afar the ethos of harmony and transformation? After nine years without success in the flood control, as I rectify my father's failure and cover his faults, how can I emulate near at hand Shun's filial piety in bringing harmony and ordering things so that his parents did not proceed to wickedness? How is what is precarious to be made secure? How is what is subtle to be made manifest? How is what is discerning to be kept free from admixture? How is what is undivided to be kept free from duality?" Because his burden was heavy, his anxiety was deep; because his anxiety was deep, his learning was earnest. Therefore, rising ten times during a single meal and grasping his hair three times during a single wash—there was no time that was not learning. Being diligent in the state and frugal in the family—there was no place that was not learning. Bowing to Yi for his splendid words and assenting to Gao Yao regarding the achievement of results—there was no person from whom he was not learning. Making his food and drink frugal, making his palaces and chambers low, and making his clothing…

title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
服惡之無事非學也猶未也克艱之謨幾康之
迪其祗承于帝者皆學也鼓鐘之設鼛鐸之陳
其下詢于人者皆學也九功之叙九叙之歌其
錫之天下者皆學也典則之貽疇範之列其垂
之後世者皆學也夫以尊居九重富有四海之
身而勞心焦思胼手胝足不自暇逸以學如此
豈聖人誠有所不足哉不以天之厚我者是恃
而以天之望我者是憂耳聰目明天之厚我也
而必以視聽明威之學廣之聲律身度天之厚
===
我也而必以準繩規矩之學約之天無外聖人
之心亦無外天不息聖人之心亦不息心不息
故學不已學不已故聖必成九州攸同四隩旣
宅人皆曰禹其輔相天地之聖人乎而不知其
成允成功之學成之也六府孔脩三事允治人
皆曰禹其左右生民之聖人乎而不知其祗台
德先之學成之也危者安而微者著精者不雜
而一者不二以紹執中之傳人皆曰禹其繼往
開來之聖人乎而不知其寸陰必惜思日孜孜
punctuated: 服惡之，無事非學也。猶未也。克艱之謨，幾康之迪，其祗承于帝者，皆學也；鼓鐘之設，鼛鐸之陳，其下詢于人者，皆學也；九功之叙，九叙之歌，其錫之天下者，皆學也；典則之貽，疇範之列，其垂之後世者，皆學也。夫以尊居九重、富有四海之身，而勞心焦思，胼手胝足，不自暇逸以學如此，豈聖人誠有所不足哉？不以天之厚我者是恃，而以天之望我者是憂。耳聰目明，天之厚我也，而必以視聽明威之學廣之；聲律身度，天之厚我也，而必以準繩規矩之學約之。天無外，聖人之心亦無外；天不息，聖人之心亦不息。心不息故學不已，學不已故聖必成。九州攸同，四隩旣宅，人皆曰：「禹其輔相天地之聖人乎！」而不知其成允成功之學成之也。六府孔脩，三事允治，人皆曰：「禹其左右生民之聖人乎！」而不知其祗台德先之學成之也。危者安而微者著，精者不雜而一者不二，以紹執中之傳，人皆曰：「禹其繼往開來之聖人乎！」而不知其寸陰必惜、思日孜孜
translation_en: …wearing coarse clothing—there was no affair that was not learning. And even that was not all. The counsels on overcoming difficulties and the guidance on attending to the subtle springs of peace—that whereby he reverently received instruction from the Emperor Shun—was all learning; the setting up of drums and bells and the displaying of large drums and wooden-clapper bells—that whereby he inquired of the people below—was all learning; the ordering of the nine achievements and the singing of the nine orderings—that which he bestowed upon the empire—was all learning; the bequeathing of canons and rules and the arrangement of the categories of the Great Plan—that which he handed down to posterity—was all learning. Now, for one whose person dwelt in the exalted ninefold palace and possessed the wealth of everything within the Four Seas to labor his mind and rack his thoughts, with calloused hands and chapped feet, allowing himself no leisure or ease in order to learn like this—was it truly because the sage had some deficiency? He did not rely upon that with which Heaven had generously endowed him, but rather worried about that which Heaven expected of him. Acute hearing and clear sight were Heaven's generous endowment to him, yet he обязательно broadened them through the learning of seeing, hearing, discernment, and majesty; a voice that was a standard of pitch and a person that was a standard of measure were Heaven's generous endowment to him, yet he обязательно restrained them through the learning of the plumb-line, the compass, and the square. Heaven has nothing outside it, and the mind of the sage likewise has nothing outside it; Heaven never ceases, and the mind of the sage likewise never ceases. Because his mind never ceased, his learning never stopped; because his learning never stopped, his sagehood was निश्चितly accomplished. When the Nine Provinces were harmonized and the four quarters made habitable, everyone said, "Is not Yu a sage who assists and complements Heaven and Earth?"—not knowing that it was accomplished by his learning of fulfilling his trustworthiness and completing his achievements. When the six treasuries of nature were greatly ordered and the three affairs of governance truly regulated, everyone said, "Is not Yu a sage who aids and supports the living people?"—not knowing that it was accomplished by his learning of reverently putting his own virtue first. When the precarious was made secure and the subtle made manifest, when the refined was kept unmixed and the unified kept undivided, so as to carry on the transmission of holding fast to the Mean, everyone said, "Is not Yu a sage who continues the past and opens up the future?"—not knowing that it was accomplished by his learning of cherishing every fraction of time and thinking tirelessly day by day…

title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
之學成之也雖其得之天者不同而其脩之人
者實力譬之百尺之臺雖由丘陵而增築之功
不可誣也九仞之淵雖由川澤而疏浚之勞不
可誣也孰謂禹之爲聖而不由學以成之乎噫
殷湯聖也而制事制心文武聖也而緝熈敬勝
周公聖也而繼日待旦孔子聖也而忘食忘憂
千聖授受共此學也而又何疑於禹也雖然學
一也而後之學者何其多岐矣乎卑之以功利
左之以刑名陷溺之以詞章訓詁而精一執中
===
之旨晦矣彼功利刑名無論也而詞章訓詁亦
豈希聖者所事哉朱子曰帝王之學與韋布不
同誠以帝王之所重者此心此中之外無餘事
也故經傳雖博取其足以裨益身心而已矣史
籍雖繁取其足以監戒興亡而已矣不此之務
而誇多涉獵樂此不疲於心學乎何有也此又
有志於聖者所當知
表
擬以薛瑄爲禮部侍郎兼翰林院學士直
punctuated:
之學成之也。雖其得之天者不同，而其脩之人者實力。譬之百尺之臺，雖由丘陵，而增築之功不可誣也；九仞之淵，雖由川澤，而疏浚之勞不可誣也。孰謂禹之爲聖，而不由學以成之乎？噫！殷湯聖也，而制事制心；文武聖也，而緝熈敬勝；周公聖也，而繼日待旦；孔子聖也，而忘食忘憂。千聖授受，共此學也，而又何疑於禹也？雖然，學一也，而後之學者何其多岐矣乎！卑之以功利，左之以刑名，陷溺之以詞章訓詁，而精一執中之旨晦矣。彼功利、刑名無論也，而詞章、訓詁亦豈希聖者所事哉？朱子曰：「帝王之學，與韋布不同。」誠以帝王之所重者，此心、此中之外無餘事也。故經傳雖博，取其足以裨益身心而已矣；史籍雖繁，取其足以監戒興亡而已矣。不此之務，而誇多涉獵，樂此不疲，於心學乎何有也？此又有志於聖者所當知。
表
擬以薛瑄爲禮部侍郎兼翰林院學士直
translation_en:
…learning. Although what he received from Heaven was extraordinary, what he cultivated through human effort was genuinely strenuous. To use an analogy: even if a hundred-foot terrace is built upon a natural hill, the merit of adding to and constructing it cannot be denied; even if a nine-fathom abyss originates from a natural stream or marsh, the labor of dredging and deepening it cannot be denied. Who could say that Yu's attainment of sagehood was not accomplished through learning?

Alas! Tang of Yin was a sage, yet he regulated affairs and regulated his mind; Kings Wen and Wu were sages, yet they practiced continuous illumination and let reverence prevail; the Duke of Zhou was a sage, yet he joined night to day and sat waiting for the dawn; Confucius was a sage, yet he forgot to eat and forgot his sorrows. A thousand sages passed down and received this same learning—so why harbor any doubt regarding Yu?

Nevertheless, learning is one, yet how numerous are the diverging paths taken by later learners! They debase it with utilitarianism and profit, lead it astray with legalism and nominalism, and drown it in belles-lettres and philological exegesis, so that the essential meaning of "refinement and singleness" and "holding fast to the Mean" is obscured. Never mind utilitarianism and legalism—how could belles-lettres and philological exegesis ever be the proper business of one who aspires to sagehood? Master Zhu [Zhu Xi] said: "The learning of emperors and kings is different from that of commoners in coarse cloth." Truly, this is because what emperors and kings value lies solely in this mind and this Mean, beyond which there is nothing else. Therefore, although the Classics and commentaries are vast, one selects from them only what suffices to benefit body and mind; although the historical records are voluminous, one selects from them only what suffices to serve as a mirror and warning of rise and fall. If one does not attend to this, but instead boasts of wide-ranging browsing and delights in it tirelessly, what does that have to do with the learning of the mind (xinxue)? This, too, is what those who set their will on sagehood ought to know.

Memorial (biao)

A draft memorial of thanks on behalf of Xue Xuan 薛瑄 upon his appointment as Vice Minister of Rites concurrently serving as Hanlin Academician in attendance at…

title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
文淵閣謝表天順元年
同考試官教諭批詞藻典麗才思悠長陳
謝中不忘獻替非徒四六之工已也宜錄以式
考試官教授蔡批文非雕繪語極渾成讀之想見
忠愛佳士佳士
考試官教授朱批駢麗典則
天順元年某月某日大理寺卿臣薛瑄伏
蒙
===
聖恩以臣為禮部侍郎兼翰林院學士
文淵閣辦事謹奉
表稱
謝者秩佐寅清備論思而聯
紫禁任隆調燮叅
帷幄而覲
丹霄
殊恩下逮于儒臣
特簡首塵于
punctuated:
文淵閣，謝表。天順元年。

考試官教授朱批：駢麗典則。
天順元年某月某日，大理寺卿臣薛瑄，伏蒙聖恩，以臣為禮部侍郎兼翰林院學士，文淵閣辦事，謹奉表稱謝者。秩佐寅清，備論思而聯紫禁；任隆調燮，叅帷幄而覲丹霄。殊恩下逮于儒臣，特簡首塵于
translation_en:
… in the Hall of Literary Profundity (Wenyuange), a Memorial of Thanks. First year of the Tianshun era (1457).

Comment by Associate Examiner, Instructor (jiaoyu): The diction is classical and elegant, the talent and thought far-reaching. Amidst expressing gratitude, he does not forget to offer counsel on what to adopt and what to reject; this is not merely skill in four-six parallel prose. It should be recorded as a model.

Comment by Examiner, Prefectural Director of Studies (jiaoshou) Cai: The writing is not merely carved and painted ornament; the language is utterly natural and complete. Reading it, one can envision his loyalty and devotion. A fine scholar! A fine scholar!

Comment by Examiner, Prefectural Director of Studies Zhu: Parallel beauty and classical norms.

On a certain day of a certain month in the first year of the Tianshun era, Your Servant Xue Xuan 薛瑄, Chief Minister of the Court of Judicial Review (Dali si qing), having humbly received Sacred Grace appointing Your Servant as Vice Minister of Rites (Libu shilang) concurrently Hanlin Academician (Hanlinyuan xueshi) to attend to affairs in the Hall of Literary Profundity, reverently presents this memorial to express thanks:

My rank assists in the reverent and pure administration of rites, providing deliberation and reflection while linked to the Purple Forbidden City; my responsibility is exalted in harmonizing and blending governance, participating in the tent of strategy and having audience in the Cinnabar Firmament. Extraordinary grace reaches down to a Confucian minister; special selection first graces [by the]…

title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
明聖翰史當清華之選春卿兼
密勿之司彌切氷兢深慙蚊負臣瑄誠惶誠
恐稽首頓首竊惟昊帝載分龍紀名五官
而順四時軒皇肇啟鴻圖奠三辰而任六
相虞廷典禮咨伯寔惟秩宗周室建官姬
公時兼太宰春曹居貳卿之亞隋代以侍
郎名銜學士擅兩制之榮唐宗以翰林視
草坐而論道股肱心膂以相資入則宣猷
舟楫鹽梅之是賴十載掌絲綸于紫殿寵
===
深雉尾之陪廿年握樞軸于黃扉恩厚龍
津之讌自兩漢而下咸崇敷瓊摛藻之英
由三代以還皆重論道經邦之彥故事雖
沿于往昔得人莫盛於
明時
高祖開基朱宋陶吳惟平文章而詳
奏啟
文皇膺曆黃胡金解始參軍國而預機謨如燌
如綸如時勉之賢名高一代惟溥惟榮惟
punctuated: 明聖。翰史當清華之選，春卿兼密勿之司，彌切氷兢，深慙蚊負。臣瑄誠惶誠恐，稽首頓首。竊惟昊帝載分龍紀，名五官而順四時；軒皇肇啟鴻圖，奠三辰而任六相。虞廷典禮，咨伯寔惟秩宗；周室建官，姬公時兼太宰。春曹居貳卿之亞，隋代以侍郎名銜；學士擅兩制之榮，唐宗以翰林視草。坐而論道，股肱心膂以相資；入則宣猷，舟楫鹽梅之是賴。十載掌絲綸于紫殿，寵深雉尾之陪；廿年握樞軸于黃扉，恩厚龍津之讌。自兩漢而下，咸崇敷瓊摛藻之英；由三代以還，皆重論道經邦之彥。故事雖沿于往昔，得人莫盛於明時。高祖開基，朱、宋、陶、吳惟平文章而詳奏啟；文皇膺曆，黃、胡、金、解始參軍國而預機謨。如燌、如綸、如時勉之賢，名高一代；惟溥、惟榮、惟
translation_en:
…the enlightened sage. The post of Academician-Historian is a prestigious and pure selection, while the sub-ministerial office in the Ministry of Rites is joined with confidential state duties; I am ever more filled with trepidation, as if walking on thin ice, and deeply ashamed, like a mosquito trying to bear a mountain. Your servant [Xue] Xuan 薛瑄 is truly fearful and truly apprehensive, bowing his head to the ground again and again.

I humbly reflect that when Taihao 太皞 divided the dragon-named offices, he designated the five officials to accord with the four seasons; when the Yellow Emperor initiated his grand design, he ordered the sun, moon, and stars and employed the six prime ministers. At the court of Yu [Shun], when appointing someone to take charge of the rites, he consulted Bo [Yi] 伯夷 to serve as Regulator of the Sacred Rites (zhizong); when the House of Zhou established its offices, the Duke of Zhou at times concurrently served as Grand Counselor (taizai). In the Ministry of Rites, ranked just below the Minister, the Sui dynasty instituted the title of Vice Minister (shilang); the Academicians (xueshi) enjoyed the glory of drafting both outer and inner decrees, and the Tang emperors assigned the Hanlin Academy to review draft edicts. Sitting to discourse on the Way, rulers and ministers rely on one another like limbs and heart and spine; entering court to proclaim grand counsels, the sovereign depends on them like boats and oars or salt and plum. Holding charge of imperial decrees in the Purple Palace for ten years, one receives deep favor attending behind the pheasant-tail fans; grasping the pivot of state in the Yellow Gate [Chancellery] for twenty years, one enjoys generous grace at the Dragon Ford banquets. From the Two Han dynasties downward, all have esteemed brilliant talents who spread forth jade-like prose and literary splendor; from the Three Dynasties onward, all have valued worthies who discourse on the Way and order the state. Although the precedents have been passed down from antiquity, the attainment of capable men has never been more flourishing than in the Ming era. When the High Ancestor (Gaozu, Emperor Taizu) founded the dynasty, Zhu [Sheng] 朱升, Song [Lian] 宋濂, Tao [An] 陶安, and Wu [Chen] 吳沉 solely deliberated on literary compositions and carefully reviewed memorials and communications; when the Cultured Emperor (Wenhuang, Emperor Chengzu) received the mandate, Huang [Huai] 黃淮, Hu [Guang] 胡廣, Jin [Youzi] 金幼孜, and Xie [Jin] 解縉 first participated in military and state affairs and took part in confidential counsels. Worthies such as [Zeng] Qi 曾棨, [Wang] Lun 王綸 [or Li Shimian's contemporaries], and [Li] Shimian 李時勉 held renown that towered over their generation; [Yang] Pu 楊溥, [Yang] Rong 楊榮, and…

title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
士奇之業望著
三朝蓋惇典代言必才行擅長者方稱其選而
調元補袞非謀斷兼資者莫充其員如臣
戇愚驟蒙顯錄一朝殊遘千載榮施恭惟
皇帝陛下
玄德神凝
英資天授
重輝日月繫四夷萬國之懽心
再斡乾坤纘
===
二祖
一宗之丕緒
留神問學
孝養久達于
重闈
注念老成敬恭克謹于羣祀飭風憲以開薦
舉敦節儉而謹灾祥省役蠲租惓惓民間之
疾苦進賢去惡孜孜吏治之勸懲屬當
帝命之維新特軫
punctuated: 士奇之業，望著三朝。蓋惇典代言，必才行擅長者方稱其選；而調元補袞，非謀斷兼資者莫充其員。如臣戇愚，驟蒙顯錄，一朝殊遘，千載榮施。恭惟皇帝陛下，玄德神凝，英資天授。重輝日月，繫四夷萬國之懽心；再斡乾坤，纘二祖、一宗之丕緒。留神問學，孝養久達于重闈；注念老成，敬恭克謹于羣祀。飭風憲以開薦舉，敦節儉而謹灾祥。省役蠲租，惓惓民間之疾苦；進賢去惡，孜孜吏治之勸懲。屬當帝命之維新，特軫
translation_en:
… and the achievements of Yang Shiqi (楊士奇), their renown was illustrious across Three Reigns. Indeed, to uphold the canons and draft imperial pronouncements, only those who excel in both talent and conduct are equal to the selection; and to harmonize the primordial forces and mend the imperial robes, none who lack both strategic counsel and decisive judgment can fill the post. As for one as simple and foolish as your servant, to suddenly receive such prominent appointment is an extraordinary encounter of a single morning and a glorious bestowal of a thousand years.

Reverently I reflect that Your Majesty the Emperor possesses profound virtue spiritually concentrated and heroic endowments bestowed by Heaven. Adding radiance to the sun and moon, You bind the joyful hearts of the four border tribes and myriad states; turning anew the cosmos of Qian and Kun, You carry on the grand enterprise of the Two Founders and One Ancestor. Devoting Your mind to inquiry and learning, Your filial nourishment has long reached the Two Empresses Dowager in the inner palace; fixing Your thoughts on seasoned elders, Your reverent devotion is unfailingly meticulous across all the sacrifices. You rectify the Censorate to open the path of recommendation, and cultivate frugality while heeding portents and omens. Lightening corvée labor and remitting taxes, You are earnestly concerned with the hardships of the common people; advancing the worthy and removing the wicked, You are tirelessly diligent in the encouragement and punishment of official administration. Just at this time when the Imperial Mandate is renewed, You especially take to heart…

title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
宸衷之求舊惟爰立賢于夢卜乃
眷倚下及芻蕘晉貳南宮併乘藝苑瞻依
北斗侍直
文淵蘭省綴次于文昌已高曳履薇垣映躔
于
華蓋尚媿覆甌𨗳羽
彤墀班隨八座凝輝
黼扆位接
三台可是迂儒濫承
===
異數伏念臣瑄河汾末品志學欲宗洙泗之
源澤絳庸流傳心切求關閩之派飭躬礪
節以明道不在多言復性教人謂工文無
裨實用夙承師訓長竊賢科攬轡湖湘未
能肅官常而懲貪墨校文齊魯亦頗正士
習而抑浮夸繼以虛名謬蒙拔擢旋因法
守幸遂投閒
優召偶及蓬門孤踪再登棘寺詎意
上天開泰
punctuated:
宸衷之求舊。惟爰立賢于夢卜，乃眷倚下及芻蕘。晉貳南宮，併乘藝苑；瞻依北斗，侍直文淵。蘭省綴次于文昌，已高曳履；薇垣映躔于華蓋，尚媿覆甌。𨗳羽彤墀，班隨八座；凝輝黼扆，位接三台。可是迂儒，濫承異數。

伏念臣瑄，河汾末品，志學欲宗洙泗之源；澤絳庸流，傳心切求關閩之派。飭躬礪節，以明道不在多言；復性教人，謂工文無裨實用。夙承師訓，長竊賢科。攬轡湖湘，未能肅官常而懲貪墨；校文齊魯，亦頗正士習而抑浮夸。繼以虛名，謬蒙拔擢；旋因法守，幸遂投閒。優召偶及蓬門，孤踪再登棘寺。詎意上天開泰，
translation_en:
… the imperial mind's search for experienced ministers. Wishing to establish the worthy as through dreams and divination, Your favored reliance extends down even to humble grass- and wood-gatherers. Promoted to Vice Minister in the Ministry of Rites and concurrently presiding over the Hanlin Academy, I gaze upon the Northern Dipper and attend on duty in the Hall of Literary Profundity (Wenyuan ge). In the Orchid Department, ranked beside the Wenchang constellation, I already trail my shoes in high station; in the Crape-Myrtle Enclosure, shining in the orbit of the Canopy constellation, I am still ashamed lest my name be covered under the golden bowl as unworthy. With heron-feather insignia at the vermilion steps, my rank follows the Eight Executives; bathed in the radiance of the embroidered screen, my seat adjoins the Three Terraces. How could this pedantic Confucian scholar undeservedly receive such extraordinary favor!

Humbly I reflect that I, Your servant [Xue] Xuan, am a person of the lowest grade from the Yellow and Fen river region, who in setting my heart on learning wished to trace the source of the Zhu and Si rivers [of Confucius]; a mediocre man from Ze and Jiang prefectures, who in transmitting the Way of the Mind earnestly sought the schools of Guanzhong [Zhang Zai] and Min [Zhu Xi]. Disciplining my person and sharpening my integrity, I held that illuminating the Way does not lie in many words; teaching others to recover their original nature, I maintained that artful writing brings no benefit to practical use. Early on I received my teachers' instruction, and grown up I undeservedly passed the examinations for the worthy. Taking up the reins as an inspector in the Huxiang region [Huguang], I was unable to enforce official discipline and punish greedy and corrupt officials; examining essays as Education Intendant in the Qi and Lu region [Shandong], I was somewhat able to rectify the habits of scholars and curb superficiality and boastfulness. Subsequently, because of an empty reputation, I was undeservedly selected for promotion; soon after, for upholding the law, I was fortunate to be allowed to retire into leisure. Then a gracious summons unexpectedly reached my thatched gate, and my solitary footsteps once again ascended the Court of Judicial Review. How could I have expected that High Heaven would open an era of great peace, …

title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
天仰
聖激切屏營之至謹奉
表稱
謝以
聞
第叁塲
策五道
第一問
===
同考試官教諭□□批
君臣孚敞我
祖宗朝盛事
皇上推誠禮下千載一時子能揄揚休美而篇終以保泰為言尤見忠愛宜冠
多士
考試官教授蔡批援古質今發明上下交成之意詳
盡讀之令人感奮他日必能効忠者敬服敬服
考試官教授朱批條答詳明獻納勤懇非徒工文者
君臣之交孚也其萬世之一時乎君臣之
punctuated:
天仰聖，激切屏營之至，謹奉表稱謝以聞。
第叁塲
策五道
第一問
同考試官教諭□□批：君臣孚敞，我祖宗朝盛事。皇上推誠禮下，千載一時。子能揄揚休美，而篇終以保泰為言，尤見忠愛，宜冠多士。
考試官教授蔡批：援古質今，發明上下交成之意，詳盡。讀之令人感奮，他日必能効忠者。敬服，敬服！
考試官教授朱批：條答詳明，獻納勤懇，非徒工文者。
君臣之交孚也，其萬世之一時乎！君臣之
translation_en:
…looking up to Heaven and revering the Sage, in the utmost earnestness and trepidation, I respectfully present this memorial of gratitude for Your Majesty's hearing.

Third Session
Five Policy Essays
First Question

Comment by Associate Examiner, Instructor [□□]: The mutual trust and openness [孚敞, reading 儆?] between sovereign and minister was a grand affair of our ancestral courts. His Majesty extends sincerity and treats his subordinates with courtesy—an opportunity that comes once in a thousand years. You are able to extol this fine beauty, and at the end of the piece you speak of preserving great peace (tai), which especially shows your loyalty and devotion. You deserve to be placed first among the many scholars.

Comment by Examiner, Prefectural Director of Studies Cai: Citing antiquity to examine the present, it elucidates the meaning of superior and inferior mutually bringing about completion [交成, reading 誠/儆?] with thorough completeness. Reading it makes one feel moved and inspired; in the future he will surely be one capable of rendering loyal service. Deepest admiration, deepest admiration!

Comment by Examiner, Prefectural Director of Studies Zhu: The point-by-point responses are detailed and clear, and the counsel offered is earnest and sincere; he is not merely someone skilled in literary composition.

The mutual trust between sovereign and minister—is it not a singular moment in ten thousand generations! The… between sovereign and minister…

title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
交儆也其萬世之常道乎時者運之所乗
而醇漓因之不可一也有交孚之殷則志
通于無間道者治之所出而否泰係之不
可易也有交儆之實則治保于無虞此自
古明良所以精神翕聚元氣融浹不謀而
自合不介而自親而成開泰保泰之鴻猷
者用此道也知此則我
皇祖
列聖基隆于前我
===
皇上媲美于後
君臣相與所以通地天之泰而成一德之治者
不可以颺庥於萬一乎甞考之易之泰九
二以剛中應五而六五柔中虛已以受之
此上下交而為泰之時也泰之初君與臣
交會而泰益開泰之極君與臣交儆而泰
益保時之隆也道之至也雖天地之交不
越此矣唐虞之興也中天也泰運撫矣當
其時君臣家視寰寓而身視天下喜起賡
punctuated:
交儆也，其萬世之常道乎？時者，運之所乗，而醇漓因之，不可一也；有交孚之殷，則志通于無間。道者，治之所出，而否泰係之，不可易也；有交儆之實，則治保于無虞。此自古明良所以精神翕聚、元氣融浹，不謀而自合，不介而自親，而成開泰、保泰之鴻猷者，用此道也。知此，則我皇祖、列聖基隆于前，我皇上媲美于後，君臣相與，所以通地天之泰而成一德之治者，不可以颺庥於萬一乎？

甞考之《易》之《泰》：九二以剛中應五，而六五柔中虛已以受之，此上下交而為泰之時也。泰之初，君與臣交會而泰益開；泰之極，君與臣交儆而泰益保。時之隆也，道之至也，雖天地之交不越此矣。唐虞之興也，中天也，泰運撫矣。當其時，君臣家視寰寓而身視天下，喜起賡
translation_en:
… mutual admonition of sovereign and minister—is it not the constant Way of ten thousand generations? The opportunity of the age is borne upon the cycle of destiny, and purity or decline follows accordingly—it cannot be uniform; yet where there is the earnestness of mutual trust, intentions communicate without the slightest gap.
