The Way is that from which governance emerges, and stagnation or flourishing (pi and tai) hinges upon it—it cannot be altered; yet where there is the substance of mutual admonition, good order is preserved without anxiety. That enlightened rulers and worthy ministers since antiquity have gathered their vital spirit in harmony and blended the primordial breath, agreeing without prior consultation and growing close without intermediary, thereby accomplishing the grand enterprise of inaugurating and preserving supreme peace (tai)—all of this was achieved by employing this Way. Understanding this, when our Imperial Ancestor and the successive Sacred Emperors laid the grand foundation before, and our Majesty matches their splendor after, in the fellowship of sovereign and minister whereby the communion of earth and heaven in supreme peace is achieved and the governance of unified virtue is perfected—can one not extol its auspicious grace in some small measure?

I have examined the hexagram Tai (Peace) in the Book of Changes (Yi): the Nine in the Second place responds to the Fifth with firm centrality, while the Six in the Fifth place, with yielding centrality, empties itself to receive it. This is the time when above and below commune to form supreme peace. At the beginning of Tai, sovereign and minister meet in fellowship and peace is further opened; at the culmination of Tai, sovereign and minister admonish one another and peace is further preserved. It is the flourishing of the age and the perfection of the Way; even the communion of Heaven and Earth does not surpass this. The rise of Tang and Yu [Yao and Shun] was like the sun at midday, embracing the cycle of supreme peace. At that time, sovereign and minister regarded the realm as their family and the world as their own person, rejoicing and rising to continue one another's…

title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
歌都俞吁咈何其孚也而違弼之戒時幾
之敕惓惓焉興道以乘時故言泰者莫唐
虞若也三代相與詩書所稱蓋猶得而想
見其盛迺孔子逖覽帝制近矚王猷喟然
興曰唐虞之際於斯爲盛蓋有感於希覯
之時相成之道云三代以還風斯下矣願
治者豈不嘉樂虞周名號長美哉然手足
腹心情旣隔閡而鹽梅麴糵德未交承豈
時之淳庬不齊而道之脩否頓異哉姑就
===
明問所及者言之漢帝續虞人之箴以示
羣臣唐宗發理人之策以試縣令宋主頒
訓廉謹刑之銘以敕百官非不煥然美矣
顧制作徒工而同心之誼則尠魏相條上
故事李絳進君臣屏風司馬光進稽古錄
孫奭進無逸圖非不井然備矣然章奏雖
愨而格心之道猶微交孚交儆之實開泰
保泰之方其謝三代亦已久矣而況唐虞
哉洪惟我
punctuated: 歌，都俞吁咈，何其孚也！而違弼之戒、時幾之敕，惓惓焉興道以乘時，故言泰者莫唐、虞若也。三代相與，《詩》、《書》所稱，蓋猶得而想見其盛。迺孔子逖覽帝制，近矚王猷，喟然興曰：「唐、虞之際，於斯爲盛。」蓋有感於希覯之時、相成之道云。三代以還，風斯下矣。願治者豈不嘉樂虞、周，名號長美哉？然手足腹心情旣隔閡，而鹽梅麴糵德未交承。豈時之淳庬不齊，而道之脩否頓異哉？姑就明問所及者言之。漢帝續《虞人之箴》以示羣臣，唐宗發理人之策以試縣令，宋主頒訓廉謹刑之銘以敕百官，非不煥然美矣；顧制作徒工，而同心之誼則尠。魏相條上故事，李絳進君臣屏風，司馬光進《稽古錄》，孫奭進《無逸圖》，非不井然備矣；然章奏雖愨，而格心之道猶微。交孚交儆之實，開泰保泰之方，其謝三代亦已久矣，而況唐、虞哉？洪惟我
translation_en: …Responsive Songs (Gengge), and their expressions of agreement and dissent ("Alas!", "Indeed!", "Oh!", "Nay!")—how deep was their mutual trust! Moreover, with the admonitions against opposing or failing to assist, and the injunctions to attend to the timely and the subtle, they earnestly promoted the Way to avail themselves of the times. Therefore, in speaking of Great Peace (Tai), nothing compares to the eras of Tang and Yu. As for the mutual relations of sovereign and minister in the Three Dynasties, from what is praised in the Classic of Odes (Shi) and the Classic of Documents (Shu), one can still imagine their flourishing state. Yet when Confucius surveyed the institutions of the Five Emperors from afar and observed the plans of the Three Kings up close, he sighed with emotion and said, "At the juncture of Tang and Yu, governance was more flourishing than in this dynasty." This was doubtless because he was moved by so rarely seen an era and by the Way of mutual fulfillment. From the Three Dynasties onward, customs declined. Among those who wished for good governance, who did not admire and delight in Yu and Zhou, wishing for their titles and reputations to remain forever admirable? Yet the feelings between sovereign and minister—like those of hands, feet, heart, and belly—had already become estranged, and the virtues of mutual assistance—like salt and plum, or yeast and malt—were no longer reciprocally upheld. Was this because the purity or mixed nature of the times was uneven, or because the cultivation or neglect of the Way had suddenly diverged? Let us speak tentatively of what is touched upon in Your brilliant question. An emperor of the Han continued the "Admonition of the Huntsman" (Yuren zhi zhen) to show to his assembled ministers; an ancestor of the Tang issued policy questions on governing the people to test District Magistrates; and a ruler of the Song promulgated inscriptions instructing integrity and caution in punishments to admonish the hundred officials. These were not without brilliant beauty; yet their literary compositions were merely skillful, while the bond of being of one mind was scarce. Wei Xiang 魏相 submitted item-by-item precedents from the past; Li Jiang 李絳 presented a screen depicting sovereigns and ministers; Sima Guang 司馬光 presented the Record of Investigating Antiquity (Jigu lu); and Sun Shi 孫奭 presented the "Diagram of Against Luxurious Ease" (Wuyi tu). These were not without orderly completeness; yet although their memorials were sincere, the Way of rectifying the ruler's heart remained faint. The reality of mutual trust and mutual admonition, and the methods of initiating and preserving Great Peace, had already fallen short of the Three Dynasties for a long time—how much more so of Tang and Yu! Humbly reflecting upon our…

title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
太祖高皇帝延攬英豪廓清華夏于是謀臣碩
輔應運雲蒸若徐達李文忠劉基宋濂諸
人相與訪議疇咨燕樂
賜予而萬世之
鴻圖肇於是矣嘗伏讀
大誥三篇首言君臣同遊曰同心一氣立綱陳
紀曰感格天地時和年豐大哉
皇謨所以交上下而啓泰階者何至也迨我
宣宗章皇帝厲精政治禮敬儒紳于時侍從論
思應期林會若楊榮楊溥楊士奇胡濙諸
人相與披豁雍容給饌
召對而萬世之駿烈弘於是矣嘗伏讀
賢姦傳官箴臣鑒三書或列人品之善惡而
勸懲具昭或嚴諸司之職掌而規戒咸備
大哉
帝典所以勵臣鄰而綿泰祚者何至也
列聖相承重熙累洽百辟交奮精白承休進鑑
古錄如李賢進講學篇如楊守陳進勤政
punctuated: 太祖高皇帝延攬英豪，廓清華夏，于是謀臣碩輔應運雲蒸，若徐達、李文忠、劉基、宋濂諸人，相與訪議疇咨，燕樂賜予，而萬世之鴻圖肇於是矣。嘗伏讀《大誥》三篇，首言「君臣同遊」，曰：「同心一氣，立綱陳紀。」曰：「感格天地，時和年豐。」大哉皇謨！所以交上下而啓泰階者，何至也！迨我宣宗章皇帝厲精政治，禮敬儒紳，于時侍從論思應期林會，若楊榮、楊溥、楊士奇、胡濙諸人，相與披豁雍容，給饌召對，而萬世之駿烈弘於是矣。嘗伏讀《賢姦傳》、《官箴》、《臣鑒》三書，或列人品之善惡而勸懲具昭，或嚴諸司之職掌而規戒咸備。大哉帝典！所以勵臣鄰而綿泰祚者，何至也！列聖相承，重熙累洽，百辟交奮，精白承休。進《鑑古錄》如李賢，進《講學篇》如楊守陳，進《勤政
translation_en:
…Grand Progenitor, Emperor Gao (Taizu Gaohuangdi), recruited heroic talents and swept clear the Chinese realm. Thereupon, strategic counselors and great ministers rose up like clouds in response to the Mandate—men such as Xu Da 徐達, Li Wenzhong 李文忠, Liu Ji 劉基, and Song Lian 宋濂—consulting and deliberating together with him, enjoying banquets and imperial bestowals; and thus the grand enterprise for ten thousand generations was founded. I have humbly read the three parts of the Grand Pronouncements (Dagao), which begin by speaking of "Ruler and Ministers Journeying Together," saying: "With one heart and one vital spirit, establishing the cardinal principles and setting forth the regulations," and saying: "Moving and reaching Heaven and Earth, so that the seasons are harmonious and the harvests abundant." Great indeed are the Imperial Plans! How consummate they are in uniting superior and inferior and opening the era of supreme peace!

Coming down to our Imperial Ancestor Xuanzong, Emperor Zhang (Xuanzong Zhanghuangdi), he devoted himself tirelessly to governance and treated Confucian scholars and officials with courteous respect. At that time, close attendants and advisors gathered like a forest in response to the auspicious age—men such as Yang Rong 楊榮, Yang Pu 楊溥, Yang Shiqi 楊士奇, and Hu Ying 胡濙—opening their hearts to him in dignified harmony, being granted meals and summoned for personal audiences; and thus the glorious achievements for ten thousand generations were enlarged. I have humbly read the three books—Biographies of the Worthy and the Treacherous (Xianjian zhuan), Admonitions for Officials (Guanzhen), and Mirror for Ministers (Chenjian)—which either set forth the good and evil of men's character so that encouragement and warning are both made clear, or strictly define the duties of the various offices so that rules and admonitions are fully provided. Great indeed are the Imperial Canons! How consummate they are in encouraging ministerial colleagues and prolonging the blessed dynastic fortune!

Successive Sacred Emperors have inherited the throne one after another in cumulative splendor and pervasive harmony, while the hundred officials have striven together, receiving imperial favor with pure and untarnished devotion. Men such as Li Xian 李賢 presented the Record of the Mirror of Antiquity (Jiangu lu), Yang Shouchen 楊守陳 presented the Essay on Expounding Learning (Jiangxue pian), and [Wang Ao 王鏊] presented the [Essentials of] Diligent Governance (Qinzheng [yao])…

title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
要如王鏊荷
累朝之優渥攄一得以開陳啓沃實資于
聖心獻納有功於
衮闕所以交孚交儆而昌泰運於無疆者又
不在於
列聖之禮遇而羣賢之交脩哉我
皇上以
聰明仁孝之資紹
祖宗帝王之統
===
踐祚以來動遵
成憲首
御平臺召見輔臣即成周之訪落不足以喻其
盛屢
書宸翰特昭
天寵雖有商之一德不足以匹其隆一時意氣
感動薦紳凡楊英舒翹逖聽垂聲者莫不
洗濯淬勵樂觀黃虞之化而欣承都俞之
風美哉洋洋乎固
punctuated: 要》如王鏊。荷累朝之優渥，攄一得以開陳，啓沃實資于聖心，獻納有功於衮闕。所以交孚交儆，而昌泰運於無疆者，又不在於列聖之禮遇，而羣賢之交脩哉？我皇上以聰明仁孝之資，紹祖宗帝王之統。踐祚以來，動遵成憲。首御平臺，召見輔臣，即成周之《訪落》，不足以喻其盛；屢書宸翰，特昭天寵，雖有商之《一德》，不足以匹其隆。一時意氣感動薦紳，凡楊英舒翹、逖聽垂聲者，莫不洗濯淬勵，樂觀黃、虞之化，而欣承都俞之風。美哉，洋洋乎！固
translation_en:
… Essentials of Diligent Governance (Qinzheng yao) by Wang Ao 王鏊. Receiving the generous favor of successive reigns, they set forth their humble insights to expound their views; their enlightening counsel truly aided the sagely mind, and their loyal advice and remonstrance were meritorious in mending deficiencies in the imperial conduct. That whereby sovereign and ministers mutually trusted and mutually cautioned one another, causing the era of peace and prosperity to flourish without limit—did it not lie in the courteous treatment bestowed by the successive sagely emperors and the reciprocal cultivation of the assembled worthies?

Our August Emperor, endowed with intelligence, benevolence, and filial piety, has succeeded to the line of his imperial ancestors. Since ascending the throne, in every action he has complied with the established constitutions. First, he appeared at the Platform Hall (Pingtai) and summoned his Grand Secretaries for audience—even the "Counsel at the Beginning of the Reign" (Fangluo) of the Zhou dynasty is insufficient to illustrate such splendor; repeatedly, he has written in his own imperial hand to specially manifest heavenly favor—even "Possessing Pure Virtue" (Yide) of the Shang dynasty is insufficient to match such eminence. At once, this spirit has moved and inspired the gentry and officials; all those who display their talents and raise their heads in aspiration, listening from afar to the reputation handed down, without exception cleanse and temper themselves in encouragement, rejoicing to witness the transformative rule of the Yellow Emperor and Yu Shun, and gladly receiving the ethos of harmonious consultation between ruler and minister. How splendid, how vast and overflowing! Truly it is…

title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
皇王之盛事而
宗社之洪庥也廼
宸衷益圖治理風示臣工
念士習澆漓官箴刓缺
特頒敕諭誕
誥多方大要言窺隙竇者巧於獵取快恩讐者
偏於愛惡老成擯而不用便捷喜爲有才
宜湔宿垢以襄王道
絲綸渙汗
===
詞旨森嚴與
高皇大誥之篇
章皇二書之旨均足以揭日月而垂宇宙者矣
頃輔臣仰荷
倚眷矢竭忠誠皇皇焉考歷代之事備媺惡之
詳繪圖直解兼資法戒分卷類列取數陰
陽名曰
帝鑒圖說進之
黼座較諸先臣所進尤爲簡易明白眞足以比
punctuated: 皇王之盛事，而宗社之洪庥也。廼宸衷益圖治理，風示臣工，念士習澆漓，官箴刓缺，特頒敕諭，誕誥多方。大要言：窺隙竇者巧於獵取，快恩讐者偏於愛惡；老成擯而不用，便捷喜爲有才。宜湔宿垢，以襄王道。絲綸渙汗，詞旨森嚴，與高皇《大誥》之篇、章皇二書之旨，均足以揭日月而垂宇宙者矣。頃輔臣仰荷倚眷，矢竭忠誠，皇皇焉考歷代之事，備媺惡之詳，繪圖直解，兼資法戒，分卷類列，取數陰陽，名曰《帝鑒圖說》，進之黼座，較諸先臣所進，尤爲簡易明白，眞足以比
translation_en: … a glorious undertaking of sovereigns and kings, and a vast blessing for the ancestral temple and the altars of soil and grain. Thereupon, in His imperial heart He has sought ever more to achieve good governance and to guide and instruct His officials and ministers. Mindful that the habits of scholars have grown thin and decadent, and that official conduct has become worn down and deficient, He specially issued an imperial edict of instruction to broadly admonish the many regions. In essence it states that those who peer into cracks and loopholes are clever at seizing advancement, while those who indulge personal gratitude and vengeance are partial in their loves and hatreds; mature and experienced men are cast aside and left unused, whereas the nimble and opportunistic are favored as possessing talent; and that old stains ought to be washed away in order to assist the Kingly Way. The imperial words poured forth, their phrasing and import stern and majestic; along with the chapters of the Grand Pronouncements (Da Gao) of the Exalted Emperor [Hongwu] and the purport of the two books of the Illustrious Emperor [Xuande], they are alike sufficient to shine as brightly as the sun and moon and be handed down throughout the universe. Recently, the Grand Secretaries, looking up in receipt of His reliance and favor and swearing to exhaust their loyalty and sincerity, have anxiously examined the events of successive dynasties, setting forth in full the details of good and evil, painting illustrations and providing plain explanations to serve as both models and warnings, dividing them into scrolls arranged by category in accordance with the numbers of yin and yang, and naming the work Illustrated Mirror for the Emperor (Dijian tushuo). When they presented it to the imperial throne, compared to what was presented by former ministers, it was even more concise, accessible, and clear—truly sufficient to be compared to…

title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
藥石而永龜鑑者矣統而言之道者歷萬
世而不更時則曠千載而一値天以時授
之
高皇而以其道作之於前有
君有臣以之交孚以之交儆先天而時不違焉
者也天以時授之
皇上而以其道繼之於後有
君有臣以之開泰以之保泰後天而時克奉焉
者也然則交會之際其一見於唐虞而再
===
見於
今日者乎雖然愚生芹曝之忱猶欲爲
皇上泰道之助者復有說焉謹幾微一也愼終
始二也防壅蔽三也辨名實四也夫干霄
之木起於青葱重溟之流成於涓滴言積
漸也今
臨御大廷元碩夾輔
外朝旣肅矣而退居深宫燕安易溺得無以
徑竇誘之乎必謹之于不見不聞而達之
punctuated: 藥石而永龜鑑者矣。統而言之，道者，歷萬世而不更；時則曠千載而一値。天以時授之高皇，而以其道作之於前；有君有臣，以之交孚，以之交儆，先天而時不違焉者也。天以時授之皇上，而以其道繼之於後；有君有臣，以之開泰，以之保泰，後天而時克奉焉者也。然則交會之際，其一見於唐虞，而再見於今日者乎？雖然，愚生芹曝之忱，猶欲爲皇上泰道之助者，復有說焉：謹幾微，一也；愼終始，二也；防壅蔽，三也；辨名實，四也。夫干霄之木，起於青葱；重溟之流，成於涓滴，言積漸也。今臨御大廷，元碩夾輔，外朝旣肅矣；而退居深宫，燕安易溺，得無以徑竇誘之乎？必謹之于不見不聞，而達之
translation_en: …to curative medicine and acupuncture stones, and serve eternally as a tortoise-shell divination and mirror. Speaking of it as a whole: the Way endures through ten thousand generations without changing, whereas the opportune moment is encountered only once in a thousand years. Heaven bestowed this opportune moment upon the Exalted Emperor (Gaozong/Hongwu), and by means of His Way He initiated it in the past; having such a ruler and such ministers, through it they shared mutual trust and through it they offered mutual admonition, preceding Heaven yet not违 [contravening] the times. Heaven has now bestowed this opportune moment upon Your Majesty, and by means of Your Way You succeed to it in the present; having such a ruler and such ministers, through it You open an era of great peace (tai) and through it You preserve that great peace, following Heaven and proving able to uphold the times. If that is so, has not this juncture of harmonious convergence been seen once in the eras of Tang (Yao) and Yu (Shun), and been seen a second time today? Even so, out of the humble sincerity of a peasant offering wild celery or warming his back in the sun, what this foolish student still wishes to offer as an aid to Your Majesty's Way of great peace may be further stated: first, to be vigilant over subtle incipient tendencies; second, to be heedful of the end as of the beginning; third, to guard against obstruction and concealment; and fourth, to distinguish between name and reality. Now, a tree that brushes the skies begins as a tender green shoot, and the currents of the deep ocean are formed from trickling drops—this speaks of gradual accumulation. At present, when You preside over the great court, eminent and great statesmen assist at Your side, so the outer court is already reverent and orderly; yet when You retire to reside in the deep palace, where it is easy to sink into leisure and comfort, could there not be those who entice You through side doors and crooked paths? You must be vigilant over what is unseen and unheard, and extend this vigilance…

title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
于起居食息一念之萌神明對焉一行之
動師保臨焉則防微杜漸其道大光矣故
幾微不可不謹也夫行百里者半九十爲
九仞者虧一簣言鮮終也今勵精伊始庶
寮儆惕百度惟貞矣然閱歷歲時玩愒易
生得無以近習移之乎必不徇之于目前
而慮之于百千萬世
經筵常講無廢學焉章奏躬覽無怠政焉則遐
思逖慮其永無愆矣故終始不可不慎也
===
帝王以視聽周天下一蔽於私即几席弗
察矣況萬里之外乎必作敢言之氣杜寵
倖之門面詰多慾者在所容而罔上羨餘
者罪之可也條奏水旱者在所嘉而日獻
符瑞者斥之可也別聰明益廓不降皇序
而四海周知矣故壅蔽不可不防也帝王
以崇尚風天下一眩於名則爲謾者將寡
力矣而何以臻考成之効乎必誅意不誅
文採實不採名勞心撫字者最之而偽增
punctuated: 于起居食息。一念之萌，神明對焉；一行之動，師保臨焉，則防微杜漸，其道大光矣。故幾微不可不謹也。夫行百里者半九十，爲九仞者虧一簣，言鮮終也。今勵精伊始，庶寮儆惕，百度惟貞矣；然閱歷歲時，玩愒易生，得無以近習移之乎？必不徇之于目前，而慮之于百千萬世，經筵常講，無廢學焉；章奏躬覽，無怠政焉，則遐思逖慮，其永無愆矣。故終始不可不慎也。帝王以視聽周天下，一蔽於私，即几席弗察矣，況萬里之外乎？必作敢言之氣，杜寵倖之門，面詰多慾者在所容，而罔上羨餘者罪之可也；條奏水旱者在所嘉，而日獻符瑞者斥之可也。別聰明益廓，不降皇序，而四海周知矣。故壅蔽不可不防也。帝王以崇尚風天下，一眩於名，則爲謾者將寡力矣，而何以臻考成之効乎？必誅意不誅文，採實不採名，勞心撫字者最之，而偽增
translation_en: …to daily movements, meals, and rest. At the sprouting of a single thought, it is as if facing the gods and spirits; at the stirring of a single action, it is as if the Grand Preceptor and Grand Guardian are present. Thus, by checking the incipient and halting the gradual, the Way will shine forth brightly. Therefore, the subtle beginnings cannot but be guarded with care. Now, he who travels a hundred li is only halfway at ninety, and he who builds a mound of nine ren may fall short by a single basket of earth—this means that few carry things through to the end. Today, at the very outset of vigorous governance, the various officials are alert and vigilant, and all measures are upright. Yet as the months and years pass, laxity and idleness easily arise; could it be that intimate attendants might sway the sovereign's resolve? One must not yield to what is merely before the eyes, but take thought for a hundred, a thousand, ten thousand generations. If the Classics Colloquium (jingyan) is held regularly without neglecting learning, and memorials are reviewed in person without slackening in governance, then through far-reaching thought and distant foresight, there will forever be no fault. Therefore, the end and the beginning cannot but be treated with caution. An emperor or king encompasses all under Heaven through his sight and hearing; once obscured by partiality, he cannot perceive even what lies at his own desk and mat, let alone ten thousand li away! He must foster a spirit of outspokenness and close the gates of favoritism: those who rebuke excessive desires to his face should be tolerated, while those who deceive their superior with surplus revenues should be punished; those who submit itemized memorials on floods and droughts should be commended, while those who daily present auspicious omens should be dismissed. Then [reading 則 for 別] his keenness of sight and hearing will broaden ever further, and without descending from the imperial steps, he will know all within the Four Seas. Therefore, obstruction and concealment cannot but be guarded against. An emperor or king transforms all under Heaven through what he esteems; once dazzled by empty reputation, those who practice deceit will spare their efforts [?], and how then can the efficacy of evaluating achievements be attained? He must judge intentions rather than mere words, and gather substance rather than reputation: those who labor wholeheartedly in nurturing the people should be ranked highest, while those who falsely inflate…

title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
戶口者勿賞也無書抵政府者拔之而捷
徑終南者勿徵也則真僞不淆無事綜覈
而百工競勸矣故名實不可不辨也是四
者
今日之急務皆
勅諭之所已及而
帝鑒之所備載者也繹而思之推而廣之斷而
行之則泰道益隆澤被海隅名垂天壤而
億萬年雍熈之盛端在茲矣敢以是爲
===
當宁
獻
第二問
同考試官教諭批經學不明人持異議此作折衷
羣言而末歸于讀書窮理居敬持志是沉潜經術而有得
者宜錄以式
考試官教授蔡批闡明六經之旨犁然深中肯綮取之
考試官教授朱批以高古之文發精確之見佳士佳士
punctuated:
戶口者勿賞也；無書抵政府者拔之，而捷徑終南者勿徵也。則真僞不淆，無事綜覈，而百工競勸矣。故名實不可不辨也。是四者，今日之急務，皆勅諭之所已及，而《帝鑒》之所備載者也。繹而思之，推而廣之，斷而行之，則泰道益隆，澤被海隅，名垂天壤，而億萬年雍熈之盛，端在茲矣。敢以是爲當宁獻。

第二問

同考試官教諭批：經學不明，人持異議。此作折衷羣言，而末歸于讀書窮理、居敬持志，是沉潜經術而有得者。宜錄以式。
考試官教授蔡批：闡明六經之旨，犁然深中肯綮，取之。
考試官教授朱批：以高古之文，發精確之見，佳士！佳士！
translation_en:
… the household registers should not be rewarded; promote those who send no letters to the central administration, and do not summon those who take the Mount Zhongnan shortcut to office. Then truth and falsehood will not be confused, there will be no need for exhaustive verification, and all officials will vie with one another in diligence. Therefore, reputation and reality cannot but be distinguished. These four matters are the urgent tasks of the present day; all have already been touched upon in the imperial edicts of instruction and are fully recorded in the Mirror for the Emperor (Dijian). If one ponders and reflects upon them, extends and broadens them, and resolutely puts them into practice, then the Way of great peace will flourish ever more, benevolent grace will reach the corners of the seas, renown will endure as long as heaven and earth, and the盛 splendor of ten thousand myriad years of harmonious prosperity will truly rest in this. I venture to offer this to His Majesty upon the throne.

Second Question

Comment by Associate Examiner and Instructor: Classical learning is obscured, and people hold divergent views. This essay weighs and reconciles the various opinions, and in the end returns to reading books to exhaustively investigate principle and abiding in reverence to maintain one's resolution. This is someone who has immersed himself deeply in classical scholarship and gained true insight. It should be recorded as a model.
Comment by Examiner and Instructor Cai: It clarifies the meaning of the Six Classics, clearly and deeply hitting the crucial points. Selected.
Comment by Examiner and Instructor Zhu: With lofty and ancient prose, he expresses precise and sound views. A fine scholar! A fine scholar!

title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
知事心之學者可語窮經之本矣知致用
之方者可語窮經之實矣夫道也者原于
一心而見之萬事者也六經也者聖人舉
斯道以筆之書示人求諸心而致之用者
也故不知事心之學而摘句尋章者末焉
耳矣不知致用之方而計功謀利者虛焉
耳矣是故六經聖人心學究其本言也君
子反而求之心焉浩浩乎萬理一原而格
致誠正貫之矣六經聖人之用舉其實言
===
也君子推而致之用焉淵淵乎一本萬殊
而脩齊治平舉之矣故易以言此心之時
焉吉凶之所以考者取是以考之也書以
言此心之中焉政事之所以達者取是以
達之也詩以言此心之正焉淑慝之所以
辨者取是以辨之也春秋言心之變焉是
非之所以公者取是以公之也禮樂言心
之敬和焉而暴慢鄙詐之遠者取是以遠
之也天下之道豈有餘蘊哉知此可以復
punctuated: 知事心之學者，可語窮經之本矣；知致用之方者，可語窮經之實矣。夫道也者，原于一心，而見之萬事者也；六經也者，聖人舉斯道以筆之書，示人求諸心而致之用者也。故不知事心之學，而摘句尋章者，末焉耳矣；不知致用之方，而計功謀利者，虛焉耳矣。是故六經，聖人心學，究其本言也，君子反而求之心焉，浩浩乎萬理一原，而格、致、誠、正貫之矣；六經，聖人之用，舉其實言也，君子推而致之用焉，淵淵乎一本萬殊，而脩、齊、治、平舉之矣。故《易》以言此心之時焉，吉凶之所以考者，取是以考之也；《書》以言此心之中焉，政事之所以達者，取是以達之也；《詩》以言此心之正焉，淑慝之所以辨者，取是以辨之也；《春秋》言心之變焉，是非之所以公者，取是以公之也；《禮》、《樂》言心之敬和焉，而暴慢鄙詐之遠者，取是以遠之也。天下之道，豈有餘蘊哉？知此可以復
translation_en: With one who understands the learning of serving the mind, one may speak of the root of thoroughly mastering the Classics; with one who understands the method of putting knowledge into practical application, one may speak of the reality of thoroughly mastering the Classics. Now the Way originates in the one mind and manifests itself in the myriad affairs; the Six Classics are that whereby the sages took up this Way and committed it to writing, showing people how to seek it in the mind and bring it forth into practical application. Therefore, those who do not understand the learning of serving the mind and merely pluck out phrases and hunt for passages are dealing only with the branches; those who do not understand the method of practical application and merely calculate accomplishments and scheme for profit are dealing only with what is hollow. For this reason, to say that the Six Classics are the sages' learning of the mind is to speak of investigating their root; when the gentleman turns back and seeks it in his mind, how vast it is—the myriad principles sharing a single source, with the investigation of things, extension of knowledge, making the intentions sincere, and rectifying the mind threading through them all! To say that the Six Classics are the sages' practical application is to speak of setting forth their reality; when the gentleman extends it and brings it into practical application, how abyssal it is—a single root branching into a myriad differentiations, with the cultivation of the person, regulation of the family, ordering of the state, and pacification of the world encompassing them all! Thus the Book of Changes (Yi) speaks of the timeliness of this mind, and that whereby good and bad fortune are examined is examined by drawing upon this; the Book of Documents (Shu) speaks of the centrality of this mind, and that whereby affairs of government are carried through is carried through by drawing upon this; the Book of Odes (Shi) speaks of the correctness of this mind, and that whereby virtue and evil are distinguished is distinguished by drawing upon this; the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu) speaks of the adaptability of the mind, and that whereby right and wrong are made impartial is made impartial by drawing upon this; the Record of Rites (Li) and Book of Music (Yue) speak of the reverence and harmony of the mind, and that whereby violence, negligence, vulgarity, and deceit are kept at a distance is kept at a distance by drawing upon this. How could the Way of the world have any remaining profundities left unexpressed? Understanding this, one can reply…

title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
師鄕黨諸篇合詩禮樂之義焉是其度彼
參此粲然有條然不知聖人立言之際果
各有所主焉否也毋亦近于牽合與六經
之道同歸而教與詞亦不可泥也昔人又
于此比擬焉故論其教則易之知來藏往
非不疏通知遠也書之惟精惟一非不潔
靜精微也詩之發乎性情止乎禮義亦非
不恭儉莊敬也是其說猶近若辭則聖人
因經命意各自爲體原不相通雖韓子正
===
法奇葩之言已屬文人之習或者乃于易
取中孚九二鳴鶴在陰數語于詩取抑三
章其在于今數語以例經文之互似特偶
合者耳不知聖人作經之時果有意于兼
通模擬否也毋亦過于推求歟夫六經之
道一也自四者之說興而言始煩然而未
害也若夫生于心而見于言害于事者其
議經僭經叛經者乎是故劉知幾疑書伯
益之事何休以周禮爲六國陰謀之書王
punctuated: 師〉、〈鄕黨〉諸篇，合《詩》、《禮》、《樂》之義焉。是其度彼參此，粲然有條，然不知聖人立言之際，果各有所主焉否也？毋亦近于牽合與？《六經》之道同歸，而教與詞亦不可泥也，昔人又于此比擬焉。故論其教，則《易》之「知來藏往」，非不疏通知遠也；《書》之「惟精惟一」，非不潔靜精微也；《詩》之「發乎性情，止乎禮義」，亦非不恭儉莊敬也。是其說猶近。若辭，則聖人因經命意，各自爲體，原不相通，雖韓子「正法」、「奇葩」之言，已屬文人之習。或者乃于《易》取〈中孚〉九二「鳴鶴在陰」數語，于《詩》取〈抑〉三章「其在于今」數語，以例經文之互似，特偶合者耳。不知聖人作經之時，果有意于兼通模擬否也？毋亦過于推求歟？夫《六經》之道一也，自四者之說興，而言始煩，然而未害也。若夫生于心而見于言、害于事者，其議經、僭經、叛經者乎！是故劉知幾疑《書》伯益之事，何休以《周禮》爲六國陰謀之書，王
translation_en: … chapters such as "Tai Bo" [or "Zi Zhang" / "Shao Shi"?] and "Xiang Dang" (The Rustic District) [of the Analects] match the meanings of the Odes (Shi), Rites (Li), and Music (Yue). In measuring that against this and cross-referencing them, the arrangement is brilliantly systematic; yet one wonders whether, when the sages established their words, they truly had such specific correspondences in mind for each? Is this not rather close to forced association? The Way of the Six Classics leads to the same destination, and neither their teachings nor their diction should be clung to rigidly; yet men of the past also drew comparisons here. Thus, if we discuss their teachings: the "knowing the future and storing the past" of the Changes (Yi) is by no means lacking in broad comprehension and far-reaching vision; the "be pure and be unified" of the Documents (Shu) is by no means lacking in purity, tranquility, and subtle profundity; and the "issuing from nature and emotions, and stopping at ritual and righteousness" of the Odes is likewise by no means lacking in respectfulness, frugality, gravity, and reverence. These explanations are still reasonably close. As for their diction, the sages formulated their ideas in accordance with each classic, each forming its own style without originally being interchangeable. Even Master Han's [Han Yu's] remarks about "orthogonal models" and "marvelous blossoms" already belong to the habits of belletrists. Yet some go so far as to take from the Changes the several lines on "A crane calling in the shade" under the second nine of the "Zhongfu" (Inner Trust) hexagram, and from the Odes the several lines on "As for how it is today" in the third stanza of "Yi" (Restraint), using them as examples of mutual resemblance in classical prose—when in fact these are merely coincidental matches. One wonders whether, when the sages composed the classics, they truly intended to blend styles and imitate one another? Is this not also searching too far? Now, the Way of the Six Classics is one. Since the rise of these four theories, discourse has grown convoluted, yet it has done no real harm. As for that which arises in the mind, manifests in words, and brings harm to affairs—is it not those who disparage the classics, usurp the classics, and betray the classics? For this reason, Liu Zhiji doubted the accounts of Boyi in the Documents, He Xiu regarded the Rites of Zhou (Zhouli) as a book of sinister intrigues from the Six States, and Wang…

title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
安石以春秋爲斷爛朝報議者如此然以
歐陽脩之賢且疑十翼焉况其他乎揚雄
之擬易白居易之續書束晳之賡華黍僭
者如此然以司馬光之賢且作潛虛焉况
其他乎公孫弘之阿世劉歆之獻符命張
禹以不語怪神欺君叛者如此然杜鎬老
儒乃以圖書爲神道設敎不近于叛乎夫
由前觀之析言也偏重也牽合也過求也
似于聖人作經之旨未能渾融然推重專
===
經亦不易之論也豈盡出于尋章摘句者
乎由後觀之議也僭也叛也則于聖人作
經之旨大相乖戾然叛經之害尤大孰非
所謂計功謀利者乎是故窮經者亦惟求
諸心以致之用而已矣何以紛紛辭說爲
哉故能求諸心則雖孔明之獨觀大旨陶
潛之不求甚解君子以爲通經矣能致其
用則雖劉元城守不妄語之一言李沆誦
節用愛人之數語君子亦以爲通經矣然
punctuated: 安石以《春秋》爲斷爛朝報，議者如此，然以歐陽脩之賢，且疑《十翼》焉，况其他乎？揚雄之擬《易》、白居易之續《書》、束晳之賡《華黍》，僭者如此，然以司馬光之賢，且作《潛虛》焉，况其他乎？公孫弘之阿世、劉歆之獻符命、張禹以不語怪神欺君，叛者如此，然杜鎬老儒，乃以圖書爲神道設敎，不近于叛乎？夫由前觀之，析言也，偏重也，牽合也，過求也，似于聖人作經之旨未能渾融，然推重專經，亦不易之論也，豈盡出于尋章摘句者乎？由後觀之，議也，僭也，叛也，則于聖人作經之旨大相乖戾，然叛經之害尤大，孰非所謂計功謀利者乎？是故窮經者，亦惟求諸心以致之用而已矣，何以紛紛辭說爲哉？故能求諸心，則雖孔明之獨觀大旨、陶潛之不求甚解，君子以爲通經矣；能致其用，則雖劉元城守「不妄語」之一言、李沆誦「節用愛人」之數語，君子亦以爲通經矣。然
translation_en:
… [Wang] Anshi 王安石 dismissed the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu) as "fragmentary and rotten court gazettes." Such were those who impugned the Classics; yet if even a worthy like Ouyang Xiu 歐陽脩 doubted the Ten Wings (Shiyi), how much more so with others? Yang Xiong 揚雄 imitated the Book of Changes (Yi), Bai Juyi 白居易 wrote a continuation of the Book of Documents (Shu), and Shu Xi 束晳 composed replacement verses for the "Huashu" ode. Such were those who usurped the Classics; yet if even a worthy like Sima Guang 司馬光 composed the Latent Void (Qianxu), how much more so with others? Gongsun Hong 公孫弘 flattered his age, Liu Xin 劉歆 presented auspicious portents of Heaven's Mandate, and Zhang Yu 張禹 deceived his sovereign by citing the maxim of not speaking of prodigies or spirits. Such were those who betrayed the Classics; yet when an aged Confucian scholar like Du Hao 杜鎬 explained the River Chart and Luo Writing as mere devices for establishing instruction by the way of the spirits, was that not close to betrayal?

Viewed from the former cases—splitting hairs in discourse, giving lopsided emphasis, forcing connections, and reading too much into the text—they seem to have failed to achieve a seamless grasp of the sages' intent in creating the Classics. Yet holding a specialized Classic in high esteem is also an unalterable principle; how could all of that have come merely from pedants who pluck out chapters and sentences? Viewed from the latter cases—impugning, usurping, and betraying—they are utterly at odds with the sages' intent in creating the Classics. Yet the harm of betraying the Classics is especially great: which of those men was not what we call a calculator of merit and seeker of profit?

Therefore, he who would master the Classics should simply seek their meaning in his own mind so as to carry it into practical application; what need is there for such a clamor of competing doctrines? Thus, if one is able to seek it in the mind, then even though Kongming 孔明 [Zhuge Liang 諸葛亮] looked only at the broad meaning and Tao Qian 陶潛 did not seek overly literal explanations, the superior man still considers them to have understood the Classics. And if one is able to carry it into practical application, then even though Liu Yuancheng 劉元城 [Liu Anshi 劉安世] held fast to the single phrase "do not speak falsely," and Li Hang 李沆 recited the few words on "economizing in expenditures and loving the people," the superior man likewise considers them to have understood the Classics. Yet…

title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
則養心之要致用之實豈待于遠求哉雖
然未易言也亦嘗聞王禕之言而有得矣
蓋六經聖人心學以心畫心法心聲心制
與夫史外傳心之要典言也可謂窮經得
其本矣六經聖人之用以趨吉避凶圖治
立政別勸懲辨上下象功德明道義言也
可謂窮經知其實矣是故取諸心焉則知
六經之理無一非吾之所固有而拘于章
句祗見其蔽也已致諸用焉則知六經之
===
道無一非吾之所當爲而溺于功利祗見
其舛也已然則窮經者何居以心驗之以
身體之從容默會于幽閑靜一之中超然
自得于意言象數之表一念之發一息之
存必涵泳乎六經焉由是持之恒久而所
謂時也中也正也變也敬與和也一以貫
之矣是之謂有本之學將有言也將有行
也必準則于六經焉由是措諸事業所謂
考吉凶也達政事也辨淑慝也公是非也
punctuated: 則養心之要、致用之實，豈待于遠求哉？雖然，未易言也。亦嘗聞王禕之言而有得矣。蓋「六經，聖人心學」，以心畫、心法、心聲、心制，與夫史外傳心之要典言也，可謂窮經得其本矣；「六經，聖人之用」，以趨吉避凶、圖治立政、別勸懲、辨上下、象功德、明道義言也，可謂窮經知其實矣。是故取諸心焉，則知六經之理，無一非吾之所固有，而拘于章句，祗見其蔽也已；致諸用焉，則知六經之道，無一非吾之所當爲，而溺于功利，祗見其舛也已。然則窮經者何居？以心驗之，以身體之，從容默會于幽閑靜一之中，超然自得于意言象數之表。一念之發，一息之存，必涵泳乎六經焉。由是持之恒久，而所謂時也、中也、正也、變也、敬與和也，一以貫之矣。是之謂有本之學。將有言也，將有行也，必準則于六經焉。由是措諸事業，所謂考吉凶也、達政事也、辨淑慝也、公是非也、
translation_en: … then why should one need to seek far afield for the essentials of nourishing the mind and the substance of practical application? Even so, this is not easy to speak of. Yet I have also heard the words of Wang Yi 王禕 and gained insight from them. When he says, "The Six Classics are the learning of the mind of the sages," he speaks of them in terms of the drawings of the mind [the Changes], the method of the mind [the Documents], the voice of the mind [the Odes], the regulations of the mind [the Rites and Music], and the essential canon for transmitting the mind beyond mere history [the Spring and Autumn Annals]; this may be called exhausting the Classics and grasping their root. When he says, "The Six Classics are the practical application of the sages," he speaks of them in terms of pursuing good fortune and avoiding calamity, planning governance and establishing administration, distinguishing encouragement and warning, differentiating superior and inferior, symbolizing merit and virtue, and clarifying the Way and righteousness; this may be called exhausting the Classics and knowing their substance. Therefore, if one draws them from one's own mind, one knows that not a single principle of the Six Classics is not inherently one's own, and that being bound to chapter and verse only reveals one's blindness. If one extends them into practical application, one knows that not a single way of the Six Classics is not what one ought to practice, and that drowning in utilitarianism and profit only reveals one's perversity. What, then, should one who exhausts the Classics abide in? One must verify them with the mind and embody them in the person, calmly and silently comprehending them in secluded leisure and tranquil unity, and transcendently attaining them for oneself beyond ideas, words, images, and numbers. Every thought that arises, every breath that remains, must be immersed in the Six Classics. Holding to this constantly over time, what are called timeliness, centrality, correctness, change, reverence, and harmony will all bethreaded together by a single principle. This is called learning that has a root. Whenever one is about to speak or about to act, one must take the Six Classics as the standard. Putting this into practice in one's undertakings, what are called examining good fortune and calamity, mastering governmental affairs, distinguishing the good and the wicked, making impartial judgments of right and wrong, …

title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
莊敬和樂也一以貫之矣是之謂務實之
學由是德以立道以行倫以篤物以化文
以成業以著由是性盡命至而教彰六經
不于是而會通耶雖然經未易窮也苟不
得其要則求諸心而或淪于空虛致諸用
而未免于駁雜何以立本而務實乎朱子
曰爲學莫先於窮理窮理惟在於讀書讀
書之法貴循序而至精其本又在居敬而
持志噫此固承學之所勉焉而未逮者也
===
第三問
同考試官教諭　批　敷對詳而趨向正蓋留心於君
子儒者
考試官教授蔡　批　發明純儒之道而推本於躬行
關係世教不尠取之
考試官教授朱　批　發揮儒道一貫之旨詳盡
天下之道一而已矣二之非道也儒者之
學亦一而已矣二之非學也夫道非他也
punctuated:
莊敬和樂也，一以貫之矣，是之謂務實之學。由是德以立、道以行、倫以篤、物以化、文以成、業以著；由是性盡、命至而教彰，六經不于是而會通耶？雖然，經未易窮也。苟不得其要，則求諸心而或淪于空虛，致諸用而未免于駁雜，何以立本而務實乎？朱子曰：「爲學莫先於窮理，窮理惟在於讀書。讀書之法，貴循序而至精；其本，又在居敬而持志。」噫！此固承學之所勉焉而未逮者也。

第三問
同考試官教諭　批：敷對詳而趨向正，蓋留心於君子儒者。
考試官教授蔡　批：發明純儒之道，而推本於躬行，關係世教不尠，取之。
考試官教授朱　批：發揮儒道一貫之旨，詳盡。

天下之道，一而已矣，二之非道也；儒者之學，亦一而已矣，二之非學也。夫道非他也，
translation_en:
…and solemn reverence and harmonious joy are all bound together by a single thread. This is what is called learning devoted to practical reality. Through this, virtue is established, the Way is put into practice, human relationships are made sincere, all things are transformed, cultural refinement is achieved, and accomplishments are made manifest; through this, one's nature is fully realized, heaven's decree is attained, and moral teaching is illuminated. Do the Six Classics not thereby converge into a unified comprehension? Even so, the Classics are not easily exhausted. If one fails to grasp their essentials, then seeking them in the mind may sink into emptiness, while applying them in practice will not escape being mixed and impure; how then could one establish the root and attend to practical reality? Master Zhu [Zhu Xi 朱熹] said: "In pursuing learning, nothing comes before fathoming principle, and fathoming principle lies solely in reading books. As for the method of reading books, one values following an orderly sequence and achieving the utmost precision; and its root, in turn, lies in abiding in reverence and holding fast to one's determination." Alas! This is indeed what I, as a student, strive after yet have not been able to reach.

Third Question
Associate Examiner, Instructor [name blank], comments: The exposition and reply are detailed and the orientation is proper; this is someone who sets his mind on being a Confucian scholar of the gentlemanly sort.
Examiner, Instructor Cai, comments: It elucidates the Way of the pure Confucian scholar and traces its root back to personal practice. Its bearing on moral education in the world is not slight; I select it.
Examiner, Instructor Zhu, comments: It elaborates the purport of the single thread running through the Confucian Way in full detail.

The Way under heaven is one and nothing more; to divide it into two is not the Way. The learning of the Confucian scholar is likewise one and nothing more; to divide it into two is not learning. Now the Way is nothing other than…

title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
原於天地散於民物流行於古今待人而
行者也儒者之學非他也統天地之心握
民物之紀貫古今之緒以待後學者也是
故明此以立本則盡性而至命焉明此以
達用則政立而敎彰焉明此而得位則爲
君爲相焉明此而不得位則爲師爲弟子
焉以脩於家則宗族鄉黨孚化焉以行於
天下則中外遠邇歸心焉是豈有二道亦
豈有二學也哉故主之者心也辨之者志
===
也考之者經也運之者才也驗之者功化
也故擬之弗精者其失也雜與之弗愼者
其失也輕析之過詳者其失也支而儒者
之學晦矣執事發策以儒道爲問豈以諸
生列儒林將以究其志乎愚非其人也敢
誦所聞以對且儒之名何始也昔唐虞三
代之際以君則曰皇曰帝曰王以臣則曰
聖曰賢曰俊乂曰忠良而儒之名不少槩
見何哉蓋是時明良交會世運方隆非無
punctuated:
原於天地，散於民物，流行於古今，待人而行者也；儒者之學，非他也，統天地之心，握民物之紀，貫古今之緒，以待後學者也。是故明此以立本，則盡性而至命焉；明此以達用，則政立而敎彰焉；明此而得位，則爲君爲相焉；明此而不得位，則爲師爲弟子焉；以脩於家，則宗族鄉黨孚化焉；以行於天下，則中外遠邇歸心焉。是豈有二道，亦豈有二學也哉？故主之者心也，辨之者志也，考之者經也，運之者才也，驗之者功化也。故擬之弗精者，其失也雜；與之弗愼者，其失也輕；析之過詳者，其失也支，而儒者之學晦矣。

執事發策，以儒道爲問，豈以諸生列儒林，將以究其志乎？愚非其人也，敢誦所聞以對。且儒之名何始也？昔唐、虞、三代之際，以君則曰皇、曰帝、曰王；以臣則曰聖、曰賢、曰俊乂、曰忠良，而儒之名不少槩見，何哉？蓋是時明良交會，世運方隆，非無…
translation_en:
…originates in Heaven and Earth, is dispersed among the people and all things, flows through antiquity and the present, and awaits human beings in order to be put into practice. The learning of the Confucians (ru) is nothing other than uniting the mind of Heaven and Earth, grasping the governing principles of the people and all things, and threading together the lineage of antiquity and the present so as to await later scholars. Therefore, when one illuminates this to establish the fundamental root, one fully realizes one's nature and reaches the Mandate; when one illuminates this to achieve practical application, governance is established and moral teaching becomes manifest; when one illuminates this and attains office, one acts as ruler or chief minister; when one illuminates this and does not attain office, one acts as teacher or disciple; when one cultivates it in the family, clansmen and village neighbors are won over and transformed in trust; when one puts it into practice throughout the realm, those within and without, far and near, turn their hearts in allegiance. How could there be two Ways in this, and how could there be two kinds of learning? Thus, that which presides over it is the mind; that which discerns it is the will; that by which it is examined is the Classics; that by which it is put into operation is talent; and that by which it is verified is meritorious transformation. Therefore, when those who emulate it lack precision, their failing is eclecticism; when those who grant the name lack caution, their failing is frivolity; when those who analyze it are overly minute, their failing is fragmentation—and thus the learning of the Confucians becomes obscured.

Your Excellency has posed this policy question inquiring into the Way of the Confucian: could it be that, since we students are ranked in the forest of Confucians, you intend thereby to probe our aspirations? Unworthy though I am of being such a person, I venture to recite what I have heard by way of reply. Moreover, how did the name "Confucian" (ru) begin? In the past, during the eras of Tang, Yu, and the Three Dynasties, with respect to rulers they were called August Ones (huang), Emperors (di), or Kings (wang); with respect to subjects they were called sages, worthies, men of eminence and ability, or the loyal and good—yet the name "Confucian" is not seen at all. Why is that? It is because at that time enlightened rulers and worthy ministers met in harmony, and the fortune of the age was just then flourishing; it was not that there were no…

title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
儒也夫人而爲儒也迨周公以文德致太
平而太宰之九兩大司徒之本俗始有儒
之名焉孔子以君子小人定趨向始分儒
之品焉儒行一篇詞繁意複固非聖筆也
然讀其篇章彬彬馴雅不詭于道亦聖門
之流裔耳可盡廢乎是故通天地人舉其
全也魯國之儒一人昭其實也乃或岐而
爲四爲五爲七不亦言愈詳而道愈晦乎
彼大儒小儒雅儒俗儒並列者荀卿子之
===
言也然大與雅君子之謂也小與俗小人
之謂也奚四之云乎淳于髠荀卿慎到騶
奭與孟子同傳馬遷之史也自今觀之博
聞强記迂大閎衍果與述唐虞三代之德
者若是班乎田仲王孟游俠之儒遷固文
史之儒莊列曠達之儒良平智數之儒毛
萇鄭玄章句之儒管晏事功之儒孔孟道
德之儒此宋濂之七儒解也自今觀之游
俠曠達謬也智數事功譎也文史章句淺
punctuated: 儒也，夫人而爲儒也。迨周公以文德致太平，而太宰之九兩、大司徒之本俗，始有儒之名焉；孔子以君子、小人定趨向，始分儒之品焉。《儒行》一篇，詞繁意複，固非聖筆也；然讀其篇章，彬彬馴雅，不詭于道，亦聖門之流裔耳，可盡廢乎？是故通天地人，舉其全也；魯國之儒一人，昭其實也。乃或岐而爲四、爲五、爲七，不亦言愈詳而道愈晦乎？彼大儒、小儒、雅儒、俗儒並列者，荀卿子之言也。然大與雅，君子之謂也；小與俗，小人之謂也，奚四之云乎？淳于髠、荀卿、慎到、騶奭與孟子同傳，馬遷之史也。自今觀之，博聞强記、迂大閎衍，果與述唐、虞、三代之德者若是班乎？田仲、王孟游俠之儒，遷、固文史之儒，莊、列曠達之儒，良、平智數之儒，毛萇、鄭玄章句之儒，管、晏事功之儒，孔、孟道德之儒，此宋濂之《七儒解》也。自今觀之，游俠、曠達，謬也；智數、事功，譎也；文史、章句，淺
translation_en: … Confucians (ru); rather, every person was a Confucian. Only when the Duke of Zhou brought about Great Peace through civil virtue did the name "Confucian" first appear in the Nine Bonds (jiu liang) of the Grand Councilor (Taizai) and the Fundamental Customs (ben su) of the Grand Minister of Education (Da situ); and only when Confucius fixed moral orientation in terms of the "gentleman Confucian" (junzi) and the "petty Confucian" (xiaoren) were the grades of Confucians first distinguished. As for the chapter "Conduct of the Confucian" (Ruxing) [in the Record of Rites], its words are prolix and its ideas repetitive, so it is certainly not from the brush of the Sage; yet when one reads its sections, they are refined, gentle, and elegant, not contrary to the Way, and are after all a legacy from the disciples of the Sage's school—how could they be entirely discarded? Therefore, "penetrating Heaven, Earth, and Man" captures its entirety, and "in the state of Lu there was but one true Confucian" manifests its reality. When people diverge and split them into four, five, or seven types, does not the Way become all the more obscure the more detailed the discussion becomes? Placing the "great Confucian" (da ru), "petty Confucian" (xiao ru), "refined Confucian" (ya ru), and "vulgar Confucian" (su ru) side by side are the words of Master Xun Qing (Xunzi). Yet "great" and "refined" refer to the gentleman, while "petty" and "vulgar" refer to the petty man—why speak of four? Putting Chunyu Kun, Xun Qing, Shen Dao, and Zou Shi in the same biographical chapter with Mencius (Mengzi) is the work of Sima Qian's history [Records of the Grand Historian]. Viewed from the present, can those who merely had broad learning and strong memory, or who were circuitous, grandiose, and expansive, truly be ranked on a par like this with one who transmitted the virtue of Tang, Yu, and the Three Dynasties? Confucians of wandering knights-errant like Tian Zhong and Wang Meng, Confucians of literature and history like Sima Qian and Ban Gu, Confucians of untrammeled emancipation like Zhuangzi and Liezi, Confucians of cleverness and calculation like Zhang Liang and Chen Ping, Confucians of chapter-and-verse exegesis like Mao Chang and Zheng Xuan, Confucians of practical achievements like Guan Zhong and Yan Ying, and Confucians of the Way and virtue like Confucius and Mencius—this is Song Lian's Explication of the Seven Confucians (Qi ru jie). Viewed from the present, knights-errant and untrammeled emancipation are perverse; cleverness, calculation, and practical achievements are crafty; literature, history, and chapter-and-verse exegesis are shallow …

title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
也豈道全德備者可並論乎然司馬談敘
六家指要列儒于道法之後遷史蓋有所
授矣韓愈論二家相用援墨于儒道之中
宋氏亦囿于見矣若是者皆不知儒道之
大也豈不失之雜乎自是而後此義益微
當漢之時六學殘缺則尚訓詁故儒林傳
所載丁寬施讐劉昆洼丹輩耳而賢如董
仲舒下帷發憤潛心大業先儒謂有儒者
氣象乃別為傳述豈以繁露諸篇非專門
===
訓詁者比耶則漢之所謂儒可知已唐之
時正學晦蝕則尚疏義故儒學傳所載顏
師古孔穎達輩耳賢如韓愈文本六經心
存仁義論者謂起八代之衰乃亦別為傳
述豈以原道諸篇非專經討論者比耶則
唐之所謂儒可知已宋承五季之後聖學
日雜故尚理學作史者乃以胡瑗蔡元定
陸九淵眞德秀列諸儒林而周敦頤程顥
兄弟張載朱熹而下又別為道學豈以周
punctuated: 也，豈道全德備者可並論乎？然司馬談敘《六家指要》，列儒于道、法之後，遷史蓋有所授矣；韓愈論二家相用，援墨于儒道之中，宋氏亦囿于見矣。若是者，皆不知儒道之大也，豈不失之雜乎？自是而後，此義益微。當漢之時，六學殘缺，則尚訓詁，故《儒林傳》所載，丁寬、施讐、劉昆、洼丹輩耳。而賢如董仲舒，下帷發憤，潛心大業，先儒謂有儒者氣象，乃別為傳述。豈以《繁露》諸篇非專門訓詁者比耶？則漢之所謂儒可知已。唐之時，正學晦蝕，則尚疏義，故《儒學傳》所載，顏師古、孔穎達輩耳。賢如韓愈，文本六經，心存仁義，論者謂起八代之衰，乃亦別為傳述。豈以《原道》諸篇非專經討論者比耶？則唐之所謂儒可知已。宋承五季之後，聖學日雜，故尚理學。作史者乃以胡瑗、蔡元定、陸九淵、眞德秀列諸《儒林》，而周敦頤、程顥兄弟、張載、朱熹而下，又別為《道學》。豈以周、
translation_en:
… [shallow]; how can they be discussed on the same level as those whose Way is complete and whose virtue is perfected? Yet Sima Tan 司馬談, in setting forth the "Essentials of the Six Schools" (Liujia zhiyao 六家指要), ranked the Confucians after the Daoists and Legalists, so Sima Qian's 司馬遷 history doubtless inherited this view; and Han Yu 韓愈, in arguing that the two schools were mutually complementary, drew Mozi 墨子 into the fold of the Confucian Way, so Mr. Song [Song Lian 宋濂] was likewise hemmed in by such views. All such men failed to understand the greatness of the Confucian Way; did they not err on the side of eclecticism?

From that time onward, this true meaning grew ever more obscure. In the Han dynasty, the Six Arts were fragmented and incomplete, so scholars prized philological exegesis (xungu 訓詁). Thus those recorded in the "Biographies of Confucian Scholars" (Rulin zhuan 儒林傳) were merely the likes of Ding Kuan 丁寬, Shi Chou 施讐, Liu Kun 劉昆, and Wa Dan 洼丹. Meanwhile, a worthy like Dong Zhongshu 董仲舒—who lowered his curtain and applied himself with zeal, immersing his mind in the great enterprise, and whom earlier Confucians described as possessing the true bearing of a Confucian—was instead given a separate biography. Was this not because the chapters of his Luxuriant Dew of the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu fanlu 春秋繁露) were not comparable to the work of specialists in philological exegesis? From this, what the Han meant by "Confucian" can readily be seen.

In the Tang dynasty, orthodox learning was darkened and eclipsed, so scholars prized subcommentaries and expositions (shuyi 疏義). Thus those recorded in the "Biographies of Confucian Scholars" (Ruxue zhuan 儒學傳) were merely the likes of Yan Shigu 顏師古 and Kong Yingda 孔穎達. A worthy like Han Yu, whose writings were rooted in the Six Classics, whose mind abided in benevolence and righteousness, and whom critics praised for reviving literature from eight dynasties of decline, was likewise given a separate biography. Was this not because essays such as his "Inquiry on the Way" (Yuan Dao 原道) were not comparable to the work of those who specialized in debating a single classic? From this, what the Tang meant by "Confucian" can readily be seen.

The Song succeeded the Five Dynasties, when sagely learning had grown daily more eclectic, so scholars prized the learning of principle (lixue 理學). Yet the compilers of the history placed Hu Yuan 胡瑗, Cai Yuanding 蔡元定, Lu Jiuyuan 陸九淵, and Zhen Dexiu 眞德秀 in the "Biographies of Confucian Scholars" (Rulin 儒林), while for Zhou Dunyi 周敦頤, Cheng Hao 程顥 and his brother [Cheng Yi 程頤], Zhang Zai 張載, Zhu Xi 朱熹, and those after them, they created a separate section on "Learning of the Way" (Daoxue 道學). Was this because Zhou…

title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
程諸子者得孔孟之正傳而非儒林可槩
乎夫道不行百世無善治學不傳千載無
眞儒未有道而非儒亦未有儒而不本于
道者也今乃分傳焉何其視儒之輕而岐
道于二乎竊意宋史既創道學傳則儒林
不當復見周程張朱固爲正宗矣其餘諸
子或同時或生乎前後其聲應氣求獨非
羽翼斯道者乎而胡可别也然考漢人論
序惟錄通經名家之徒唐人紀載祗取誦
習傳授之學則宋史别儒林於道學亦因
陋承誤耳若是者亦不知儒道之大也其
不失之輕乎元儒劉因又爲之說曰周至
精邵至大程至正朱子極大盡精而貫之
以正蓋于圖書之旨見其精也于經世之
書見其大也于辨異端闢邪說見其正也
于居敬窮理反躬見其集諸儒之大成也
初讀之未甞不快其言之當徐而察之大
非淪于粗也正非局于器也毋亦言之詳
punctuated: 程諸子者得孔、孟之正傳，而非儒林可槩乎？夫道不行，百世無善治；學不傳，千載無眞儒。未有道而非儒，亦未有儒而不本于道者也。今乃分傳焉，何其視儒之輕而岐道于二乎？竊意《宋史》既創《道學傳》，則《儒林》不當復見。周、程、張、朱固爲正宗矣，其餘諸子，或同時，或生乎前後，其聲應氣求，獨非羽翼斯道者乎？而胡可别也？然考漢人論序，惟錄通經名家之徒；唐人紀載，祗取誦習傳授之學；則《宋史》别《儒林》於《道學》，亦因陋承誤耳。若是者，亦不知儒道之大也，其不失之輕乎？元儒劉因又爲之說曰：「周至精，邵至大，程至正，朱子極大盡精而貫之以正。」蓋于圖、書之旨，見其精也；于經世之書，見其大也；于辨異端、闢邪說，見其正也；于居敬、窮理、反躬，見其集諸儒之大成也。初讀之，未甞不快其言之當；徐而察之，大非淪于粗也，正非局于器也，毋亦言之詳
translation_en:
…and the Cheng brothers (Cheng Hao 程顥 and Cheng Yi 程頤), along with the other masters, attained the orthodox transmission of Confucius and Mencius, and thus could not be lumped together under the "Forest of Confucians" (Rulin 儒林)? Now, when the Way is not practiced, there is no good governance for a hundred generations; when learning is not transmitted, there are no true Confucians for a thousand years. There has never been the Way apart from Confucians, nor has there ever been a Confucian who was not rooted in the Way. Yet here they are given separate biographical sections—how lightly they regard the term "Confucian," and how they bifurcate the Way into two! In my humble opinion, once the History of the Song (Songshi 宋史) created the "Biographies of the Learning of the Way" (Daoxue zhuan 道學傳), the "Forest of Confucians" section should no longer have appeared. Zhou Dunyi 周敦頤, the Cheng brothers, Zhang Zai 張載, and Zhu Xi 朱熹 were assuredly the orthodox patriarchs; as for the remaining masters, whether contemporaries or born before or after them, responding in voice and seeking in spirit, were they not also wings supporting this Way? How then could they be separated? Yet if we examine the discussions and prefaces of the Han historians, they recorded only those who mastered a classic and founded a specialist school; and the records of the Tang historians selected only the learning of recitation, practice, and textual transmission. Thus, when the History of the Song separated the "Forest of Confucians" from the "Learning of the Way," it was merely following narrow precedents and perpetuating errors. To act like this is also to fail to understand the greatness of the Confucian Way—does it not err in treating it too lightly?

The Yuan Confucian Liu Yin 劉因 also formulated a theory about them, saying: "Zhou Dunyi is the most subtle, Shao Yong 邵雍 is the most vast, the Cheng brothers are the most correct, and Master Zhu Xi reaches the utmost vastness and exhausts the subtle, threading them together with correctness." This is because in the purport of the Diagram of the Supreme Ultimate (Taijitu 太極圖) and the Book of Penetrating the Book of Changes (Tongshu 通書) one sees Zhou's subtlety; in the Book of Supreme World-Ordering Principles (Huangji jingshi shu 皇極經世書) one sees Shao's vastness; in distinguishing heterodoxies and refuting perverse doctrines one sees the Chengs' correctness; and in abiding in reverence, exhausting principle, and self-reflection one sees Zhu Xi's grand synthesis of all the Confucians. When one first reads this, one cannot help but be delighted by the aptness of his words. Yet when one examines it unhurriedly, vastness does not mean sinking into coarseness, and correctness does not mean being confined to concrete vessels; is his statement not perhaps so detailed…

title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
而過于析與宋濂又復舉宋諸儒之學而
並論之曰永嘉曰永康曰金谿曰橫浦則
各有所評焉若金華若廣漢若武夷則獨
有所取焉是其微意要自有在以愚言之
摘其微而議之者方人之事取其長而師
之者為己之功況諸君子入道之途雖有
異同非判然黑白若前之五儒七儒之辨
也豈易差別于其間哉嗚呼道一也儒者
之學亦一也一則精精則不可雜陳矣一
===
則大大則不可輕與矣一則全全則不可
過析矣而諸說紛紛何以明道於天下也
哉洪惟
聖祖開天崇儒重道經書傳註頒布學宮
列聖紹統聿申
謨訓教一文同天下士皆知崇正學迪正道
不以異說參之故今人才輩出光輔
盛治儒者之効昭著一時矣董仲舒所謂百
家殊方指意不同者非今所患也韓愈所
punctuated:
而過于析與？宋濂又復舉宋諸儒之學而並論之：曰永嘉、曰永康、曰金谿、曰橫浦，則各有所評焉；若金華、若廣漢、若武夷，則獨有所取焉。是其微意要自有在。以愚言之，摘其微而議之者，方人之事；取其長而師之者，為己之功。況諸君子入道之途雖有異同，非判然黑白若前之五儒、七儒之辨也，豈易差別于其間哉！嗚呼！道一也，儒者之學亦一也。一則精，精則不可雜陳矣；一則大，大則不可輕與矣；一則全，全則不可過析矣。而諸說紛紛，何以明道於天下也哉！
洪惟聖祖開天，崇儒重道，經書傳註，頒布學宮；列聖紹統，聿申謨訓。教一文同，天下士皆知崇正學、迪正道，不以異說參之。故今人才輩出，光輔盛治，儒者之効，昭著一時矣。董仲舒所謂「百家殊方，指意不同」者，非今所患也；韓愈所
translation_en:
…and excessive in drawing distinctions? Song Lian 宋濂 also brought together the teachings of the various Confucian scholars of the Song dynasty and discussed them side by side: of those of Yongjia 永嘉, Yongkang 永康, Jinxi 金谿, and Hengpu 橫浦, he offered his respective critiques; whereas in those of Jinhua 金華, Guanghan 廣漢, and Wuyi 武夷, he found singular merits to adopt. In this, his subtle intent surely had its own point. In my humble opinion, picking out subtle flaws to criticize them is the business of comparing others, whereas taking their strengths and modeling oneself upon them is the effort of self-cultivation. Moreover, although the paths by which these gentlemen entered the Way had their similarities and differences, they were not as starkly black and white as the aforementioned distinctions among the five types or seven types of Confucians—how could one easily rank and differentiate among them! Alas! The Way is one, and the learning of the Confucians is likewise one. Being one, it is refined; being refined, it cannot be set forth in a motley manner. Being one, it is great; being great, it cannot be lightly granted. Being one, it is complete; being complete, it cannot be overly dissected. Yet with various theories in profusion, how can the Way be made clear to the world!

Reverently reflecting on how Our Sacred Progenitor founded the dynasty, he venerated Confucians and esteemed the Way, promulgating the Classics and their commentaries to the schools; the Successive Sages inherited the line and further reiterated his counsels and instructions. With teaching unified and writing standardized, scholars throughout the realm all know to revere orthodox learning and walk the orthodox Way, without adulterating it with heterodox theories. Therefore, men of talent now come forth in succession to gloriously assist the flourishing governance, and the efficacy of Confucians is brightly manifest in our time. What Dong Zhongshu 董仲舒 called "the hundred schools having divergent methods and different aims" is not what we need to worry about today; what Han Yu 韓愈…

title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
謂入主出奴入附出汚者非今所憂也程
氏所謂彌近理而大亂眞者非今所慮也
愚謂今之急者其責士以實行乎蓋論儒
於聖學未明之前擇之不可不精論儒於
聖學旣明之後行之不可不力今天下士
日盛矣文日昌矣乃或闊議論而缺反躬
貴詞華而畧名檢析玄奧而忽切近駕成
說而炫巳見儒云儒云豈是之謂哉夫道
非難行也孔子曰道不遠人孟子曰人人
===
親其親長其長而天下平歸而求之有餘
師是豈待辨說者哉誠使今之爲儒者於
家庭倫理之間食息起居之際辭受取與
之節謹而不踰是卽所謂君子儒而孔孟
程朱之徒也雖議論微有不同吾且將師
之而况粹然出于正者乎若越禮義之閑
忽孝弟之義蔑存省之功弛廉靖之防卽
使日誦虞庭危微精一之言孔門博約一
貫之旨祇爲口耳之學爾吾何取焉故曰
punctuated: 謂入主出奴、入附出汚者，非今所憂也；程氏所謂彌近理而大亂眞者，非今所慮也。愚謂今之急者，其責士以實行乎！蓋論儒於聖學未明之前，擇之不可不精；論儒於聖學旣明之後，行之不可不力。今天下士日盛矣，文日昌矣，乃或闊議論而缺反躬，貴詞華而畧名檢，析玄奧而忽切近，駕成說而炫巳見。「儒云儒云」，豈是之謂哉！夫道非難行也。孔子曰：「道不遠人。」孟子曰：「人人親其親、長其長，而天下平。」「歸而求之，有餘師。」是豈待辨說者哉！誠使今之爲儒者，於家庭倫理之間、食息起居之際、辭受取與之節，謹而不踰，是卽所謂君子儒，而孔、孟、程、朱之徒也。雖議論微有不同，吾且將師之，而况粹然出于正者乎？若越禮義之閑，忽孝弟之義，蔑存省之功，弛廉靖之防，卽使日誦虞庭「危微精一」之言、孔門「博約一貫」之旨，祇爲口耳之學爾，吾何取焉？故曰：
translation_en: … what [Han Yu] called “treating one’s own school as master and outsiders as slaves, praising those who join and slandering those who leave” is not what we worry about today; and what the Cheng brothers called “coming ever closer to principle and yet greatly confounding the truth” is not what concerns us today. In my humble view, what is urgent today is surely to hold scholars accountable for substantive conduct! For in discussing Confucianism before the learning of the sages was clarified, one could not fail to be discerning in one’s choice; in discussing Confucianism after the learning of the sages has been clarified, one cannot fail to be strenuous in one’s practice. Today the scholars of the realm grow more numerous by the day, and letters flourish more by the day. Yet some indulge in grandiose discourse while lacking self-reflection, prize florid diction while neglecting moral restraint, dissect abstruse mysteries while overlooking what is close at hand, and override established doctrines to show off their own views. “Confucians, Confucians!”—is this what is meant by the term? Now, the Way is not difficult to practice. Confucius said, “The Way is not far from man.” Mencius said, “If everyone would love his parents and treat his elders as elders, the world would be at peace,” and “Go home and seek it, and you will have more than enough teachers.” Does this require disputation and argument? Truly, if those who act as Confucians today are careful not to transgress in the moral relations of the family, in the moments of eating, resting, rising, and dwelling, and in the proprieties of declining, accepting, taking, and giving, then they are indeed what are called “gentleman Confucians” and followers of Confucius, Mencius, the Cheng brothers, and Zhu Xi. Even if their discussions differ slightly, I would still take them as my teachers—how much more so when their words issue purely from orthodoxy! But if one oversteps the bounds of ritual and righteousness, neglects the duties of filial piety and fraternal respect, scorns the effort of preserving the mind and self-examination, and relaxes the defenses of integrity and quietude, then even if he daily recites the words of the court of Yu on the “precarious and subtle, refined and single-minded,” or the teachings of the school of Confucius on “broad learning and restraint, and the single thread,” it is merely learning of the mouth and ear—what use do I have for it? Therefore it is said, …

title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
與其行不足而言有餘也不若言不足而
行有餘也又曰天下有道則行有枝葉爲
儒者豈必他求哉于已取之而已矣是故
知儒道之出于一則不可以輕擬知儒道
之貴于行則不在於繁言謹對
第四問
同考試官教諭　批〔將家者流材品靡一此作摭采悉〕
〔評騰當而以天下之將屬之郭中令是今古確論至陳選任〕
〔將帥之道尤鑿鑿可行非經生漫語也敬羨敬羨〕
考試官教授蔡　批〔天下未甞無將顧所以選任之〕
〔者何如耳子能亹亹談之謂予頗俊士非耶〕
考試官教授朱　批〔該而中腴而不浮〕
執事發策承學而以將材下詢因及所以
選將之道愚生鉛槧士也不習介胄之技
安足奉條對哉顧詮伏草莽甞聽鼓鼙而
思將帥久矣敢誦所聞以復執事試垂聽
焉夫將者國之輔也輔周則國强輔隙則
punctuated:
「與其行不足而言有餘也，不若言不足而行有餘也。」又曰：「天下有道，則行有枝葉。」爲儒者豈必他求哉？于已取之而已矣。是故知儒道之出于一，則不可以輕擬；知儒道之貴于行，則不在於繁言。謹對。

第四問
同考試官教諭　批〔將家者流，材品靡一。此作摭采悉，評騰當，而以天下之將屬之郭中令，是今古確論。至陳選任將帥之道，尤鑿鑿可行，非經生漫語也。敬羨，敬羨。〕
考試官教授蔡　批〔天下未甞無將，顧所以選任之者何如耳。子能亹亹談之，謂予頗俊士，非耶？〕
考試官教授朱　批〔該而中，腴而不浮。〕

執事發策承學，而以將材下詢，因及所以選將之道。愚生鉛槧士也，不習介胄之技，安足奉條對哉？顧詮伏草莽，甞聽鼓鼙而思將帥久矣，敢誦所聞以復，執事試垂聽焉。夫將者，國之輔也；輔周則國强，輔隙則
translation_en:
… "Rather than having conduct that is insufficient while words are in excess, it is better that words be insufficient while conduct is in excess." And it is also said: "When the Way prevails in the world, conduct produces branches and leaves." Why should those who act as Confucians need to seek elsewhere? They need only draw it from themselves. Therefore, if one understands that the Confucian Way issues from unity, one cannot lightly draw comparisons; if one understands that the Confucian Way values practice, then it does not lie in prolix words. I respectfully reply.

Fourth Question
Comment by the Associate Examiner, Instructor [surname blank]: [Those of the school of military commanders vary widely in talent and character. This essay is thorough in its selection of examples and apt in its critical evaluations, and in assigning the status of a commander for the entire realm to Secretariat Director Guo (Guo Ziyi 郭子儀), it states an indisputable judgment for past and present. As for its exposition of the way of selecting and appointing generals and commanders, it is especially concrete and practicable, not the idle talk of a mere student of the Classics. Respectful admiration, respectful admiration!]
Comment by the Examiner, Instructor Cai 蔡: [The world has never lacked generals; everything depends simply on how they are selected and appointed. You are able to discourse on this tirelessly—may we not call you a man of outstanding talent [?]?]
Comment by the Examiner, Instructor Zhu 朱: [Comprehensive yet hits the mark; rich yet not superficial.]

Your Excellency has issued a policy question to us students, inquiring into military talent and thereby extending to the way of selecting generals. I, your foolish student, am a scholar of writing tablets and ink; unpracticed in the skills of armor and helmet, how could I be worthy of offering a point-by-point reply? Yet while crouching in rustic obscurity, I have long heard the war drums and thought of generals and commanders. I venture to recite what I have heard in reply; may Your Excellency deign to listen. Now, the general is the bulwark of the state: if the bulwark is complete, the state is strong; if the bulwark is flawed, then …

title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
天子自裁之蓋不敢席肺腑之寵擅專誅
于境外耳史著其以和柔自媚于上天下
靡得而稱述之誠知言哉臥不設席行不
騎乘者吳起也為魏將擊秦親裹贏糧與
士卒最下者同衣食其待下亦仁矣然卒
以刻暴少恩亡其軀仁安在焉驃騎將軍
霍去病封狼居胥禪姑衍厥功不世乃還
軍重車餘粱肉而士有饑者蓋其少而侍
中貴不省士耳然為將尚方略匈奴未滅
===
無心治第又可盡訾耶程李東西衞尉也
廣軍無部伍行陣就善水草屯舍止不擊
刁斗未嘗遇害不識正部曲行伍營陣士
吏治軍簿至明軍不休息虜亦不得犯其
時士卒樂從廣之簡而苦不識之煩然廣
之勇氣無雙名震匈奴結髮從軍大小七
十餘戰竟以數奇不侯千載而下猶為扼
腕彼不識廑廑謹于文法惡足軼聲飛將
也李郭齊名一時也光弼嚴毅沈果治師
punctuated: 天子自裁之。蓋不敢席肺腑之寵，擅專誅于境外耳。史著其以和柔自媚于上，天下靡得而稱述之，誠知言哉！臥不設席、行不騎乘者，吳起也。為魏將擊秦，親裹贏糧，與士卒最下者同衣食，其待下亦仁矣。然卒以刻暴少恩亡其軀，仁安在焉？驃騎將軍霍去病，封狼居胥，禪姑衍，厥功不世。乃還軍，重車餘粱肉，而士有饑者。蓋其少而侍中貴，不省士耳。然為將尚方略，匈奴未滅，無心治第，又可盡訾耶？程、李，東西衞尉也。廣軍無部伍行陣，就善水草屯舍止，不擊刁斗，未嘗遇害；不識正部曲行伍營陣，士吏治軍簿至明，軍不休息，虜亦不得犯。其時士卒樂從廣之簡，而苦不識之煩。然廣之勇氣無雙，名震匈奴，結髮從軍，大小七十餘戰，竟以數奇不侯，千載而下，猶為扼腕。彼不識廑廑謹于文法，惡足軼聲飛將也？李、郭，齊名一時也。光弼嚴毅沈果，治師
translation_en:
… the Son of Heaven decide it himself. This was because he did not dare to rely on the favor he enjoyed as a close kinsman to arrogantly exercise the power of execution on his own authority beyond the borders. The histories record that he ingratiated himself with his sovereign through compliant gentleness, so that the world found nothing in him to praise or recount—truly discerning words indeed!

He who did not spread a mat when sleeping and did not ride a mount or carriage when traveling was Wu Qi 吳起. As a general of Wei 魏 attacking Qin 秦, he personally wrapped and carried his own surplus rations, sharing the same clothing and food as the lowest of his soldiers; his treatment of his subordinates was benevolent indeed. Yet in the end, because of his harshness, cruelty, and lack of grace, he lost his own life—where, then, was his benevolence?

General of Agile Cavalry (Piaoji jiangjun 驃騎將軍) Huo Qubing 霍去病 performed the feng sacrifice at Mount Langjuxu 狼居胥 and the shan sacrifice at Guyan 姑衍, achieving merits unmatched in his generation. Yet when he led his army back, his heavy supply wagons had millet and meat to spare while there were soldiers who went hungry. This was simply because from youth he had served in the palace as a favored noble and did not know how to look after his troops. Still, as a general he valued strategic planning, and declaring that while the Xiongnu 匈奴 were not yet destroyed he had no heart to tend to a residence—can he be wholly faulted?

Cheng Bushi 程不識 and Li Guang 李廣 served as the Western and Eastern Commandants of Palace Guards (Weiwei 衞尉). Li Guang's army kept no fixed divisions, ranks, or battle formations; they encamped and halted wherever they found good water and grass, did not strike the night-watch kettles, and yet never came to harm. Cheng Bushi, by contrast, strictly enforced divisions, ranks, and camp formations; his officers and clerks maintained the military registers right until dawn, so the army got no rest, yet the northern raiders could not violate his lines either. At that time, the soldiers were happy to follow Li Guang's simplicity and found Cheng Bushi's meticulousness burdensome. Moreover, Li Guang's valor was unmatched, his fame shook the Xiongnu, and from the time he first bound up his hair to join the army he fought in more than seventy battles large and small; that he ultimately failed to be enfeoffed as a marquis owing to ill fortune still makes people wring their hands in regret a thousand years later. As for Cheng Bushi, who was merely cautious in following rules and regulations, how could he suffice to surpass the renown of the "Flying General" (Feijiang 飛將)?

Li Guangbi 李光弼 and Guo Ziyi 郭子儀 enjoyed equal fame in their age. Li Guangbi was stern, resolute, deep, and decisive, governing his troops…

title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
訓整始至朔方斬張用濟而軍中爲之股
慄子儀恕以御下賞罰必信頤指宿將若
部曲然而寬厚得人過之其時將士樂子
儀之寬而憚光弼之嚴然子儀略平大難
再造王室屢遭讒忌聞命就道無纖芥顧
望以身繫天下安危者二十年完名高節
爛然獨著若光弼被構奄寺遂陷嫌郄而
拙于謀已君子有遺慨焉合而觀之由數
子致用之異以定數子爲將之品汾陽賢
===
將哉其天下乎臨淮蓋庶幾焉衛霍而下
竝稱才將矣未可均茵伏也雖然之數子
者莫不際時遘會而當時之君亦皆能慎
選而善任之以盡其用固宜休烈顯乎無
窮聲稱浹乎千兹也已方
今天下之患北構于胡南桂于越邇者雲中
上谷黠虜雖款關矣而薊鎭遼左尤滋訌
焉東西兩粤捷書雖交馳矣而山海殘孽
日蠢蠢也
punctuated:
訓整，始至朔方，斬張用濟，而軍中爲之股慄。子儀恕以御下，賞罰必信，頤指宿將若部曲，然而寬厚得人過之。其時將士樂子儀之寬而憚光弼之嚴。然子儀略平大難，再造王室，屢遭讒忌，聞命就道，無纖芥顧望，以身繫天下安危者二十年，完名高節，爛然獨著。若光弼被構奄寺，遂陷嫌郄，而拙于謀已，君子有遺慨焉。合而觀之，由數子致用之異，以定數子爲將之品：汾陽，賢將哉，其天下乎！臨淮蓋庶幾焉。衛、霍而下，竝稱才將矣，未可均茵伏也。雖然，之數子者，莫不際時遘會，而當時之君亦皆能慎選而善任之，以盡其用。固宜休烈顯乎無窮，聲稱浹乎千兹也已。
方今天下之患，北構于胡，南桂于越。邇者，雲中、上谷黠虜雖款關矣，而薊鎭、遼左尤滋訌焉；東西兩粤捷書雖交馳矣，而山海殘孽日蠢蠢也。
translation_en:
… well-drilled and orderly. When he first arrived at Shuofang, he executed Zhang Yongji 張用濟, causing the entire army to tremble with fear. Guo Ziyi 郭子儀 governed his subordinates with magnanimity, yet his rewards and punishments were unfailingly trustworthy; he directed veteran generals with a nod of his chin as though they were mere rank-and-file troops, yet in winning people's hearts through宽generosity and kindness, he surpassed Li Guangbi 李光弼. At the time, the officers and soldiers delighted in Ziyi's leniency and dreaded Guangbi's severity. Yet Ziyi quelled the great crisis, restored the royal house, and though repeatedly subjected to slander and jealousy, the moment he heard an imperial summons he set out on the road without the slightest hesitation or reservation. For twenty years, the safety and peril of the empire rested upon his person alone, and his flawless reputation and lofty integrity shone forth uniquely. As for Guangbi, when framed by the eunuchs, he fell into suspicion and estrangement, proving inept at safeguarding himself—for which gentlemen feel lingering regret. Viewing them together, if we determine their rank as generals on the basis of the different ways these several men were put to use: the Prince of Fenyang [Guo Ziyi] was a worthy general indeed—a general for the whole empire! The Prince of Linhuai [Li Guangbi] came close to that. From Wei Qing 衛青 and Huo Qubing 霍去病 downward, all may be called talented generals, yet they do not deserve to share the same carriage mat as equals. Even so, none of these several men failed to meet with the right times and opportunities, and the rulers of their day were likewise all able to select them with care and employ them well so as to exhaust their usefulness. Truly is it fitting that their glorious achievements shine endlessly and their renown pervades a thousand ages [? 千兹, likely a block-cutter's error for 千載]!
At present, the troubles of the empire are entangled with the northern barbarians in the north and ensnared [? 桂, likely for 挂/罣] with the Yue tribes in the south. Recently, although the cunning caitiffs of Yunzhong and Shanggu have come knocking at the passes in submission, in the Jizhen defense command and Liaodong they stir up ever more disorder; and although dispatches of victory have crisscrossed from both Eastern and Western Yue [Guangdong and Guangxi], the remnantbandits in the mountains and seas still stir restlessly day by day. …

title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
廟堂之上忖計樽俎決筴前筯所以爲尅敵
制勝之䇿靡不備至而烽燧未盡熄邊鄙
未盡寧議者謂患在無將且今之握鈐擁
纛仗鉞執綏者豈少也大都溺其職矣巽
愞首鼠者率庸𦋇而木強奸黠狙獪者多
奧援而竊重又其賈名飾實之流每每習
褒衣之揖讓而騎射罔閑弄墨士之筆端
而措施則悖若而將也
國家安所賴之洪惟
===
聖天子御極兼統覆載乂安區夏德威四訖然
邊境之慮尚廑
宵旰思得桓桓文武之士布列中外
詔下所司廣開薦辟而搜羅將材視文吏益梀
眞虎臣驍帥據鞍躍馬之秋也顧寥寥罕
睹豈以天下之大遂無其人耶毋亦選任
之道尚有可議者歟以言乎選將也非出
世胄之廕授則由武科之拔遷膏粱紈袴
每闇于韜鈐弓馬記誦未盡乎跅弛以言
punctuated: 廟堂之上，忖計樽俎，決筴前筯，所以爲尅敵制勝之䇿，靡不備至。而烽燧未盡熄，邊鄙未盡寧，議者謂患在無將。且今之握鈐擁纛、仗鉞執綏者，豈少也？大都溺其職矣。巽愞首鼠者，率庸𦋇而木強；奸黠狙獪者，多奧援而竊重。又其賈名飾實之流，每每習褒衣之揖讓，而騎射罔閑；弄墨士之筆端，而措施則悖。若而將也，國家安所賴之？洪惟聖天子御極，兼統覆載，乂安區夏，德威四訖。然邊境之慮，尚廑宵旰，思得桓桓文武之士，布列中外。詔下所司，廣開薦辟，而搜羅將材，視文吏益梀，眞虎臣驍帥據鞍躍馬之秋也。顧寥寥罕睹，豈以天下之大，遂無其人耶？毋亦選任之道，尚有可議者歟？以言乎選將也，非出世胄之廕授，則由武科之拔遷。膏粱紈袴，每闇于韜鈐；弓馬記誦，未盡乎跅弛。以言乎…
translation_en:
At the imperial court, strategies are deliberated over banquet tables and plans are decided with chopsticks in hand; nothing has been spared in devising policies for overcoming the enemy and securing victory. Yet the beacon fires are not completely extinguished, and the borderlands are not entirely at peace. Commentators say the trouble lies in a lack of generals. Moreover, are there few today who grasp the military tallies and hold the great standards, who wield the battle-axe and hold the chariot-mounting strap? For the most part, they neglect their duties. Those who are timid and vacillating like a rat at its hole are generally mediocre, weak, and stiffly obstinate; those who are crafty, cunning, and deceitful mostly rely on secret backers at court to usurp weighty authority. Furthermore, the sort who peddle their reputation and dress up their true nature constantly practice the bowing and yielding of wide-robed scholars, while remaining untrained in horsemanship and archery; they play with the brush-tips of literary men, yet their practical measures are perverse. With generals such as these, what can the state rely upon?

We humbly reflect that the Sage Son of Heaven has ascended the throne, uniting all between heaven and earth under his rule, bringing peace and order to the Chinese realm, his virtue and majesty reaching in all four directions. Yet anxieties over the frontiers still occupy his thoughts before dawn and after dusk, as he longs to obtain martial and civil men of valor to fill posts inside and outside the capital. An imperial decree has been issued to the competent authorities to broadly open the way for recommendations and special summonses, and the search for generalship talent is even more urgent than that for civil officials. Truly, this is the season for tiger-like ministers and valiant commanders to mount their saddles and leap upon their steeds! Yet such men are稀少 and rarely seen. Could it be that in the vastness of the empire there are truly no such men? Or is it not rather that the methods of selecting and appointing them still leave room for discussion? To speak of the selection of generals: if they do not come from hereditary noble houses by privilege of protection, then they rise through promotion from the military examinations. Yet pampered scions of wealthy families are often ignorant of military strategy, while testing archery, horsemanship, and memorization does not fully capture untrammeled, extraordinary talent. To speak of…

title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
策方畧毋取其支辭力足以挽強引重者
收之而豐軀碩幹者弗與焉智足以運籌
決勝者收之而記錄章句者弗與焉昔歐
陽脩欲于軍伍中求將選其技精而最勇
者百人之中得一人以為隊將合十隊得
一人為裨將合十裨得一人為大將蘇軾
欲試之于治兵觀其顔色和易以見其氣
約束堅明以見其威坐作進退以見其能
斯兩言者最得擇將之意誠能採而行之
===
則進取之途闢拘攣之見越而山林竒傑
之士將杖策而效命矣然選將非難任將
為難既選之矣而任之不專雖選何益是
故其機在於明功罪而其要在於重事權
夫張鵠以行賞罔不射矣立標而使赴罔
不趨矣今將領有功稽覈遷延積歲未敘
而望風折北與夫玩寇養亂之徒或得以
脫於吏議而法不少加則誰為之激勸而
奔走者故必倣古人賞不踰時之制小之
punctuated: …策方畧，毋取其支辭。力足以挽強引重者收之，而豐軀碩幹者弗與焉；智足以運籌決勝者收之，而記錄章句者弗與焉。昔歐陽脩欲于軍伍中求將，選其技精而最勇者，百人之中得一人以為隊將，合十隊得一人為裨將，合十裨得一人為大將。蘇軾欲試之于治兵，觀其顔色和易以見其氣，約束堅明以見其威，坐作進退以見其能。斯兩言者，最得擇將之意。誠能採而行之，則進取之途闢，拘攣之見越，而山林竒傑之士將杖策而效命矣。然選將非難，任將為難。既選之矣，而任之不專，雖選何益？是故其機在於明功罪，而其要在於重事權。夫張鵠以行賞，罔不射矣；立標而使赴，罔不趨矣。今將領有功，稽覈遷延，積歲未敘；而望風折北，與夫玩寇養亂之徒，或得以脫於吏議，而法不少加，則誰為之激勸而奔走者？故必倣古人賞不踰時之制，小之…
translation_en: …[test them on] strategic plans and tactics, and do not select them for verbose rhetoric. Accept those whose strength suffices to draw strong bows and haul heavy loads, while excluding those who merely have bulky bodies and large frames; accept those whose wisdom suffices to devise strategies and secure victory, while excluding those who merely memorize texts and parse sentences. In the past, Ouyang Xiu 歐陽脩 wished to seek generals from within the military ranks by selecting those most skilled in martial arts and most courageous: out of a hundred men, obtaining one to serve as a Company Commander (duijiang 隊將); combining ten companies, obtaining one man to serve as a Deputy General (pijiang 裨將); and combining ten deputies, obtaining one man to serve as a Grand General (dajiang 大將). Su Shi 蘇軾 wished to test them in training troops: observing whether their countenance is calm and composed to see their spirit, whether their discipline is firm and clear to see their authority, and how they direct halting, rising, advancing, and retreating to see their capability. These two proposals best capture the true meaning of selecting generals. If we can truly adopt and put them into practice, then avenues for advancement will be opened, narrow and restrictive views will be transcended, and extraordinary heroes from the mountains and forests will grasp their whips and come forward to offer their lives in service. Yet selecting generals is not what is difficult; entrusting generals with responsibility is what is difficult. Once they have been selected, if they are not entrusted with undivided authority, what benefit is there in having selected them? Therefore, the pivotal mechanism lies in clarifying merits and offenses, and the essential point lies in giving weight to their operational authority. When a target is set up and rewards are offered, no one fails to shoot at it; when a marker is erected and men are sent toward it, no one fails to hasten there. Nowadays, when commanders achieve merit, the verification process drags on, and for years they go unrewarded; meanwhile, those who flee in defeat at the mere wind of the enemy, as well as those who trifle with bandits and foster rebellion, sometimes manage to escape the impeachment of judicial officials without the law being applied to them in the slightest—who then would be roused to encouragement and hasten into service? Therefore, we must emulate the ancients' system of bestowing rewards without delay: in minor cases…

title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
不威迺欲人君敦以付授之義固以親信
之恩假以便宜之權待以殊常之賞使大
小咸極其分賢愚各適其懷斯言也最得
任將之意誠能採而行之則浮議不奪精
神自奮定計於胷臆之中而制勝於千里
之外決策於毫芒之際而收功於指顧之
間吾之幕下將馳孫吳而走頗牧也事權
又安得而不重哉選任有道則才賢之將
輩出効用由是北掃匈奴可以奏凱於龍
===
城由是南翦兇酋可以勒勳于銅柱而奠
南北赤子于衽席之安者端在是矣書生
之論如此不識執事以為何如
第五問
同考試官教諭　批　兵食二事正今日粵西急務子能洞
晰弊源計處詳盡非有先憂之慮者不能吾將天下事屬子矣勉之
考試官教授蔡　批　地方重務若屑屑照數計然有志經濟者
考試官教授朱　批　明達時務而文足以發之宜錄以式
punctuated:
不威。迺欲人君敦以付授之義，固以親信之恩，假以便宜之權，待以殊常之賞，使大小咸極其分，賢愚各適其懷。斯言也，最得任將之意。誠能採而行之，則浮議不奪，精神自奮，定計於胷臆之中，而制勝於千里之外；決策於毫芒之際，而收功於指顧之間。吾之幕下，將馳孫、吳而走頗、牧也，事權又安得而不重哉！選任有道，則才賢之將輩出効用。由是北掃匈奴，可以奏凱於龍城；由是南翦兇酋，可以勒勳于銅柱。而奠南北赤子于衽席之安者，端在是矣。書生之論如此，不識執事以為何如？

第五問
同考試官教諭　批：兵食二事，正今日粵西急務。子能洞晰弊源，計處詳盡，非有先憂之慮者不能。吾將天下事屬子矣，勉之。
考試官教授蔡　批：地方重務，若屑屑照數計，然有志經濟者。
考試官教授朱　批：明達時務，而文足以發之，宜錄以式。
translation_en:
… lacks authority. Thus, he wished the ruler to strengthen the principle of commissioning generals, consolidate the grace of intimate trust, grant them the authority to act at their own discretion, and treat them with extraordinary rewards, so that great and small alike fulfill their proper roles and both the worthy and the dull find satisfaction in their hearts. These words best capture the true meaning of employing generals. If one can truly adopt and put them into practice, then baseless criticisms will not sway their resolve, and their vigor will naturally be roused; they will formulate plans within their own breasts and secure victory a thousand li away; they will make decisive choices on the finest points and reap success in the blink of an eye. Within our command tents, we shall have men who outrun Sun Wu 孫武 and Wu Qi 吳起 and put Lian Po 廉頗 and Li Mu 李牧 to flight—how then could their authority and responsibility fail to carry weight! When selection and appointment follow the proper way, talented and worthy generals will emerge in succession to render service. Thereby, sweeping away the Xiongnu in the north, we can play the music of triumph at Longcheng; thereby, cutting down the fierce chieftains in the south, we can engrave our merits upon the Bronze Pillars. And placing the infant subjects of both north and south upon the peace of their sleeping mats truly rests entirely upon this. Such is the discourse of a mere scholar; I do not know what Your Excellency thinks of it?

Question Five
Associate Examiner and Instructor [name omitted], comment: Military affairs and provisions are precisely the urgent priorities in Guangxi today. You are able to penetrate to the root of the abuses and devise detailed, thorough measures; none without the foresight to worry before the world worries could achieve this. I would entrust the affairs of the empire to you—strive on!
Examiner and Prefectural Director of Studies Cai, comment: Crucial regional affairs are calculated item by item as if tallying up a ledger, yet this is someone who aspires to statecraft.
Examiner and Prefectural Director of Studies Zhu, comment: Clear and well-versed in current affairs, with literary skill sufficient to express them; it should be recorded as a model answer.

title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
而可覆蹈焉哉戶口稅額半爲夷侵乘兵
威而丈勘非多事也顧借口賊占逋負爲
常駕言抛荒影射得計細民稅浮于田則
喜輕豪右田浮于稅則懼重轉相構煽妄
騰加賦之名而阻撓有司牢不可破夫禹
貢則壤周禮辨方食土之毛而忘其報獨
非王民耶子粒屯田半爲官占奉部檄而
清查非生擾也顧倔强武弁日肆侵漁占
據豪强久紊經界軍樂于脫伍而棄之若
===
遺官利于營私而視爲已有轉相蒙蔽倡
爲年遠之說而粉飾文具弊不可詰夫屯
田湟中積穀塞下因地之利而且耕守寧
非往事耶嘗觀漢韓安國之說曰利不什
不易業功不百不變常故懲噎而廢食者
愚也逆緒而理棼者亂也今所以處廣右
者寧有他哉要不過通權變酌要機無改
絃易轍之名而得補偏捄弊之術耳夫平
時人自爲耕不費尺帛斗粟之養而有事
punctuated: 而可覆蹈焉哉？戶口稅額，半爲夷侵，乘兵威而丈勘，非多事也。顧借口賊占，逋負爲常；駕言抛荒，影射得計。細民稅浮于田，則喜輕；豪右田浮于稅，則懼重。轉相構煽，妄騰加賦之名，而阻撓有司，牢不可破。夫《禹貢》則壤，《周禮》辨方，食土之毛而忘其報，獨非王民耶？子粒屯田，半爲官占，奉部檄而清查，非生擾也。顧倔强武弁，日肆侵漁；占據豪强，久紊經界。軍樂于脫伍，而棄之若遺；官利于營私，而視爲已有。轉相蒙蔽，倡爲年遠之說，而粉飾文具，弊不可詰。夫屯田湟中，積穀塞下，因地之利而且耕守，寧非往事耶？嘗觀漢韓安國之說曰：「利不什，不易業；功不百，不變常。」故懲噎而廢食者，愚也；逆緒而理棼者，亂也。今所以處廣右者，寧有他哉？要不過通權變，酌要機，無改絃易轍之名，而得補偏捄弊之術耳。夫平時人自爲耕，不費尺帛斗粟之養，而有事
translation_en: …and how could one tread the same disastrous path again? Half of the registered households and tax quotas have been encroached upon by the native tribes; taking advantage of military prestige to survey and investigate the land is not making unnecessary trouble. Yet people use bandit occupation as an excuse, making tax evasion their regular practice; they fabricated claims of abandoned and uncultivated land, succeeding in their schemes of fraudulent registration. Commoners of modest means whose taxes exceed their actual landholdings rejoice at the prospect of a lighter burden, whereas powerful magnates whose landholdings exceed their taxes fear a heavier assessment. They collude to stir up agitation, falsely spreading rumors of tax increases to obstruct the local authorities, forming an unbreakable resistance. Yet the Tribute of Yu (Yugong) graded taxes according to soil quality, and the Rites of Zhou (Zhouli) differentiated the regions; those who eat the produce of the land and yet forget their obligation to repay the state—are they alone not the subjects of the King? Half of the military state farms and their grain revenues have been seized by officers; conducting a thorough audit in compliance with a directive from the Ministry is not creating disturbance. Yet recalcitrant military officers daily indulge in predatory encroachment, and powerful local bullies who occupy the land have long thrown the boundaries into confusion. Soldiers delight in deserting the ranks and cast the land aside as if it were nothing; officers profit from pursuing private gain and regard the land as their own property. They cover up for one another, advancing the excuse that too many years have passed, and dress up official paperwork to the point that the abuses cannot be investigated. Yet establishing military farms in Huangzhong and stockpiling grain along the frontiers, taking advantage of local resources while simultaneously farming and defending—are these not precedents from the past? I have observed the words of Han Anguo 韓安國 of the Han dynasty, who said: "If the profit is not tenfold, one does not change one's occupation; if the achievement is not a hundredfold, one does not alter established norms." Therefore, to give up eating for fear of choking is foolishness; to untangle knotted silk by pulling against the threads only brings chaos. Today, in dealing with Guangxi, is there any other way? In essence, it is nothing more than adapting to changing circumstances and weighing the critical mechanisms, so that without the reputation of restringing the instrument or changing the tracks, we achieve the art of rectifying imbalances and remedying abuses. Now, those who in peacetime farm for themselves, costing not a foot of silk nor a peck of grain to maintain, and yet in times of crisis…

title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
坐得其力可當衝鋒冒鏑之能者粤之狼
兵是矣往者朝下三尺之紙夕報數千之
集匪我抗也邇來稍稍驕蹇一二奉法不
前者何哉連歲疲于征調精壯困于傷殘
有功則賞多踰時出征則漢將朘削欲以
服其心而得其力難矣故戍守會省者先
務軍聲而已誠得一良將領之時其教習
申之軍令戒戢將校毋事漁獵班軍兵欵
汰冗覈實恩可以結則分甘損滋法可以
===
伸則徇師釁鼓果得勝兵三千大舉則大
創小戰則小勝縱横闔闢惟吾所指較之
召集無賴人鮮固志杼軸坐耗帑藏日虚
而一有不給則脫巾呼道如往歲者功相
千萬也故土兵不可不練也兵臨則有禽
奔獸駭之恐兵退則有蜂屯蟻聚之虞者
粤之夷獠是矣往者兩江勾劫無虚日古
田蚕食無寧歲患非細也邇來大事掃蕩
一二時復跳梁者何哉蛇虺志在吞噬窟
punctuated:
坐得其力，可當衝鋒冒鏑之能者，粤之狼兵是矣。往者朝下三尺之紙，夕報數千之集，匪我抗也；邇來稍稍驕蹇，一二奉法不前者，何哉？連歲疲于征調，精壯困于傷殘，有功則賞多踰時，出征則漢將朘削，欲以服其心而得其力，難矣。故戍守會省者，先務軍聲而已。誠得一良將領之，時其教習，申之軍令，戒戢將校毋事漁獵，班軍兵欵，汰冗覈實，恩可以結則分甘損滋，法可以伸則徇師釁鼓。果得勝兵三千，大舉則大創，小戰則小勝，縱横闔闢，惟吾所指，較之召集無賴，人鮮固志，杼軸坐耗，帑藏日虚，而一有不給，則脫巾呼道如往歲者，功相千萬也。故土兵不可不練也。
兵臨則有禽奔獸駭之恐，兵退則有蜂屯蟻聚之虞者，粤之夷獠是矣。往者兩江勾劫無虚日，古田蚕食無寧歲，患非細也；邇來大事掃蕩，一二時復跳梁者，何哉？蛇虺志在吞噬，窟…
translation_en:
…we can effortlessly obtain their strength, and who are capable of charging the front lines and braving arrows—these are the native "wolf troops" (langbing) of Guangxi. In the past, when a three-foot slip of paper was issued in the morning, the gathering of several thousand men was reported by evening; they did not defy us.
