Recently, however, they have grown somewhat arrogant and refractory, and one or two fail to obey the law and advance—why is this? Year after year they have been exhausted by requisitions and deployments, and their able-bodied men are worn down by wounds and casualties. When they achieve merit, rewards are often delayed past the proper time; when they go out on campaign, Han commanders exploit and fleece them. To wish under such circumstances to win their hearts and obtain their strength is difficult indeed. Therefore, in garrisoning the provincial capital, the first priority is simply to establish military prestige. If we truly obtain a capable general to command them, conduct their training at the proper seasons, reiterate military orders to them, restrain the officers from engaging in predatory extortion, regulate the rotating garrison troops and military funds [?], weed out the superfluous and verify the actual numbers, share delicacies and reduce excess where grace can bind them, and parade the troops and anoint the war drums with blood where the law must be enforced—if we truly obtain three thousand victorious soldiers thus, then a major campaign will inflict a major blow, and a minor battle will yield a minor victory. Charging in any direction and maneuvering at will, they will go wherever we point. Compared to recruiting riffraff who lack firm resolve, idly exhausting the looms and daily emptying the treasuries, and who—the moment supplies fall short—tear off their headscarves and shout in the streets as happened in past years, the achievement is ten thousand times greater. Therefore, the local troops must be trained.

Those who scatter in terror like startled birds and beasts when the army arrives, yet cause worry by swarming like bees and gathering like ants when the army withdraws—these are the non-Han Liao tribes (yiliao) of Guangxi. In the past, along the Two Rivers (Liangjiang) there was not a day without collusion and plundering, and in Gutian there was not a peaceful year free from their gradual encroachment; the trouble was far from trivial. Recently, after major sweeping-out campaigns, one or two still occasionally leap into rebellion—why is this? Vipers and adders are bent on devouring, and their lairs…

title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
穴易以依憑而奸猾從中鼓之恐官則曰
糾黨復聚恐賊則曰大兵將臨欲以安漢
法而制其命難矣故分戍營堡者先禁交
通而已誠得各將領嚴守信地杜絕私交
里排籍名官府毋容反復誘煽聽撫則量
輸煙竈出劫則先事報聞一切包食庇賊
如柳慶諸郡廉得其狀盡爲釐正大舉則
集各堡以爲防小入則時鵰勦以示武或
撫或勦勝算在我較之豺狼當道日煩公
===
===
家膏腴厚利盡歸私室而簸弄得計戕官
據邑如懷遠者利相什百也故交通不可
不嚴也丈地均糧立法本善銖稱寸度弊
孔實多近日
明詔停止深爲擾民耳顧二三郡邑
詔書以前已經丈量者欲援而盡罷之過矣蓋
粤之田非江南比也江南有水患田之高
下患在不均粤西有夷患糧之失額患在
不明即興全灌臨諸州邑或舊額什九而
punctuated:
穴易以依憑，而奸猾從中鼓之，恐官則曰「糾黨復聚」，恐賊則曰「大兵將臨」。欲以安漢法而制其命，難矣。故分戍營堡者，先禁交通而已。誠得各將領嚴守信地，杜絕私交；里排籍名官府，毋容反復誘煽。聽撫則量輸煙竈，出劫則先事報聞。一切包食庇賊如柳、慶諸郡，廉得其狀，盡爲釐正。大舉則集各堡以爲防，小入則時鵰勦以示武。或撫或勦，勝算在我，較之豺狼當道，日煩公家，膏腴厚利盡歸私室，而簸弄得計，戕官據邑如懷遠者，利相什百也。故交通不可不嚴也。

丈地均糧，立法本善，銖稱寸度，弊孔實多。近日明詔停止，深爲擾民耳。顧二三郡邑，詔書以前已經丈量者，欲援而盡罷之，過矣。蓋粤之田，非江南比也。江南有水患，田之高下患在不均；粤西有夷患，糧之失額患在不明。即興、全、灌、臨諸州邑，或舊額什九而
translation_en:
…dens are easy for them to rely upon, and treacherous scoundrels stir them up from within. To intimidate the officials, they say, "They are rallying their bands to gather again"; to intimidate the bandits, they say, "A great army is about to arrive." Under such circumstances, wishing to settle them under Chinese law and hold control over their lives is difficult indeed. Therefore, in stationing garrisons among the camps and forts, the first priority is simply to prohibit illicit collusion. If we can truly get the various commanders to strictly guard their assigned sectors and cut off private dealings, and have the tithing-heads (lipai) register their names with the authorities without allowing them to repeatedly entice and incite trouble—when the tribes submit to pacification, they should pay a measured levy by household hearth; when they go out to raid, it should be reported beforehand. All practices of monopolizing extortion and harboring bandits, such as those in prefectures like Liuzhou and Qingyuan, should be investigated to ascertain the facts and thoroughly rectified. When they launch a major incursion, we assemble the various forts to mount a defense; when they make minor raids, we conduct timely targeted strikes to display our martial might. Whether pacifying or suppressing, the winning strategy rests with us. Compared to having ravenous wolves blocking the roads, daily troubling the state while the rich profits of fertile lands go entirely into private hands, or having manipulators succeed in their schemes to murder officials and seize district seats as happened in Huaiyuan, the benefits are ten or a hundred times greater. Therefore, illicit collusion cannot but be strictly prohibited.

Surveying land to equalize the grain tax was originally a well-intentioned law, yet weighing to the grain and measuring to the inch truly creates many loopholes for abuse. Recently, an explicit imperial edict ordered a halt to it, simply because it deeply harassed the people. However, for the two or three prefectures and districts that had already completed their land surveys before the imperial edict arrived, wishing to invoke the edict to abolish their results entirely goes too far. For the fields of Guangxi cannot be compared to those of Jiangnan. Jiangnan suffers from floods, so the problem with high and low fields lies in inequality; western Guangxi suffers from non-Chinese tribes, so the problem with lost tax quotas lies in lack of clarity. Even in subprefectures and districts such as Xing'an, Quanzhou, Guanyang, and Lingui, perhaps nine-tenths of the old quota…

title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
其人以之練兵馭夷隱然韓白之望以之
查屯清賦藹然龔卓之風故曰牧帥不可
以不慎也夫多指亂視多言亂聽今事之
難任凡以議論之多耳一人稱便則朝而
攘臂一人以為不便則夕而投杼十羊九
牧誰其聽之故議事之始必根究弊源熟
思其便定議之後必詢謀僉同委任責成
不惑于羣議不阻于邪謀不怵于勢要雖
毀言日至而不以為疑雖人心稍拂而不
===
以為懼如此則練兵也制夷也丈勘也興
屯也皆次第舉矣故曰議論不可不一也
粤西僻遠禁網疎闊習俗獷悍易動難安
吏茲土者一切姑息因仍務為寬大人心
玩愒非一日矣故大將之令必伸于偏裨
偏裨之令必伸于士卒監司之令必行于
守令守令之法必行于豪强大將令肅則
土官之虚冒里排之交通可按法而治也
文臣令行則奸豪之阻撓武弁之頑梗可
punctuated:
其人，以之練兵馭夷，隱然韓、白之望；以之查屯清賦，藹然龔、卓之風。故曰：牧帥不可以不慎也。
夫多指亂視，多言亂聽。今事之難任，凡以議論之多耳。一人稱便，則朝而攘臂；一人以為不便，則夕而投杼。十羊九牧，誰其聽之？故議事之始，必根究弊源，熟思其便；定議之後，必詢謀僉同，委任責成。不惑于羣議，不阻于邪謀，不怵于勢要；雖毀言日至而不以為疑，雖人心稍拂而不以為懼。如此，則練兵也、制夷也、丈勘也、興屯也，皆次第舉矣。故曰：議論不可不一也。
粤西僻遠，禁網疎闊，習俗獷悍，易動難安。吏茲土者，一切姑息因仍，務為寬大，人心玩愒，非一日矣。故大將之令必伸于偏裨，偏裨之令必伸于士卒；監司之令必行于守令，守令之法必行于豪强。大將令肅，則土官之虚冒、里排之交通，可按法而治也；文臣令行，則奸豪之阻撓、武弁之頑梗，可
translation_en:
…the right men; if employed to drill troops and control the non-Chinese tribes, they will quietly command the prestige of Han Xin 韓信 and Bai Qi 白起; if employed to inspect military farms and clear up tax assessments, they will graciously manifest the style of Gong Sui 龔遂 and Zhuo Mao 卓茂. Therefore it is said: the choice of civil governors and military commanders must be made with care.
Now, too many pointing fingers confuse the sight, and too many words confuse the hearing. Today, the difficulty in shouldering responsibilities lies entirely in the proliferation of competing discussions. If one person pronounces a measure convenient, people roll up their sleeves in zeal in the morning; if another considers it inconvenient, they drop the shuttle in doubt by evening. With nine herdsmen for ten sheep, whom is one to heed? Therefore, at the outset of deliberating upon a matter, one must thoroughly trace the roots of existing abuses and carefully ponder what is advantageous; once a policy is settled, one must ensure that consultations have reached unanimous agreement, and then delegate authority and demand results. Do not be bewildered by the chatter of the crowd, do not be obstructed by perverse schemes, and do not be intimidated by the powerful and influential; even if slanderous words arrive daily, do not harbor doubts, and even if popular sentiment is slightly rubbed the wrong way, do not be afraid. If this is done, then training troops, subduing the tribes, surveying land, and promoting military agricultural colonies will all be carried out in turn. Therefore it is said: policy discussions must be unified.
Guangxi is remote and distant; the net of prohibitions is loose and wide, and customs are fierce and unruly, making the people easy to stir up and hard to pacify. Those who serve as officials in this land uniformly indulge in laxity and routine, striving only to appear magnanimous, so that people's minds have grown negligent and idle for more than a single day. Therefore, the orders of the Grand Generals must be enforced among the assistant and偏將 (subordinate) commanders, and the orders of the subordinate commanders must be enforced among the rank-and-file soldiers; the orders of the Surveillance and Circuit Intendants must be carried out by the Prefects and Magistrates, and the laws of the Prefects and Magistrates must be enforced upon the local bullies and powerful families. When the Grand General's orders are strictly observed, then fraudulent claims by Native Officials and illicit collusion by village tithing-heads (lipai 里排) can be punished according to the law; when the civil officials' orders are carried out, then obstruction by treacherous magnates and stubborn defiance by military officers can…

title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
廣西鄉試錄後序
今天子纘承丕丕基握符紀元聿
新
鴻猷濬哲徇齊神資絕出
聖學日蒸彰聞中外寤寐賢雋賓
興海宇爰自畿甸達于侯綏
江介嶺海之間甌脫斗辟之
內士有章縫而咕嗶者咸忻
聖作而快先覩于時巡按御史唐
鍊監臨廣西試事錄成存省
以職事宜敘諸末簡存省聞
之重華南巡警蹕賁于衡湘
聲教達于梧野西粵固古帝
之流化區也秦漢以戈船載
banxin: 廣西鄉試錄後序 一
punctuated:
廣西鄉試錄後序
今天子纘承丕丕基，握符紀元，聿新鴻猷，濬哲徇齊，神資絕出，聖學日蒸，彰聞中外。寤寐賢雋，賓興海宇，爰自畿甸，達于侯綏，江介嶺海之間，甌脫斗辟之內，士有章縫而咕嗶者，咸忻聖作而快先覩。于時巡按御史唐鍊監臨廣西試事，錄成，存省以職事，宜敘諸末簡。存省聞之：重華南巡，警蹕賁于衡、湘，聲教達于梧野，西粵固古帝之流化區也。秦、漢以戈船載
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Guangxi Provincial Examination

Today the Son of Heaven has succeeded to the vast foundation, grasping the tally to inaugurate a new reign era and renewing the grand enterprise. Profoundly wise and swiftly discerning, of surpassing divine endowments, his sage learning advances daily and is manifestly heard of at court and abroad. Waking and sleeping he seeks out worthy and outstanding men, raising them up as guests of the state throughout the realm. Thus from the imperial domain out to the pacified and feudal zones, between the Yangtze marches and the Southern Ridges and seas, and within the frontier outposts and secluded corners, all scholars who wear the robe and cap of literati and chant their texts rejoice in the rise of the Sage and delight to be the first to behold it. At this time Regional Investigating Censor Tang Lian 唐鍊 served as Supervising Official for the examination affairs of Guangxi. When the record was completed, I, Cunxing 存省, by virtue of my official duties, ought to write a postface on the final slips. I, Cunxing, have heard that when Chonghua 重華 [Emperor Shun] made his southern tour of inspection, his imperial cortege graced Heng 衡 and Xiang 湘, and his prestige and teachings reached the wilds of Cangwu 蒼梧; Western Yue [Guangxi] was indeed a region where the ancient sovereign's transforming influence flowed. The Qin and Han used warship-boats to…

title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
闢桂林象郡歷唐彌顯奇人
墨士往往與桂蠹翠羽文犀
馴象竝貢稱珍
明興樹藩設學材賢彙征名卿碩
輔勛猷代著下至酋長莫不
慕義趨風觧結投弩競列纓
緌之林猗其盛哉然存省甞
===
涉湘浮灕攬結西粵之勝海
陽中峙支嶂萬分攢戟列珪
翥鳳翔駕獻錡柴虎岺巆閜
砢雲譎波詭不可狀陳而其
間二三巍巒赤立乎漢表若
偉丈人儒長者高踞俯視羣
子弟蒲伏趨走聽指授之不
punctuated: 闢桂林、象郡，歷唐彌顯，奇人墨士，往往與桂蠹、翠羽、文犀、馴象，竝貢稱珍。明興，樹藩設學，材賢彙征，名卿碩輔，勛猷代著。下至酋長，莫不慕義趨風，觧結投弩，競列纓緌之林，猗其盛哉！然存省甞涉湘浮灕，攬結西粵之勝。海陽中峙，支嶂萬分，攢戟列珪，翥鳳翔駕，獻錡柴虎，岺巆閜砢，雲譎波詭，不可狀陳。而其間二三巍巒，赤立乎漢表，若偉丈人、儒長者高踞俯視，羣子弟蒲伏趨走，聽指授之不
translation_en: …opened up Guilin and Xiang commanderies, and through the Tang dynasty it became ever more prominent; extraordinary men and literary scholars were often presented to the court alongside cassia grubs, kingfisher feathers, patterned rhinoceros horns, and trained elephants, all acclaimed as treasures. With the rise of the Ming, provincial administrations were established and schools founded; talented and worthy men advanced together in multitude, and renowned ministers and great counselors made their meritorious achievements and statecraft plans manifest from generation to generation. Down to the native chieftains, there were none who did not admire righteousness and gravitate toward our civilizing influence, untying their hair-knots and casting aside their crossbows to vie for a place in the forest of cap-strings—ah, how flourishing indeed! Yet I, Cunxing, once crossed the Xiang River and floated down the Li River, taking in the scenic wonders of Western Yue. Mount Haiyang stands towering in the center, its branching peaks dividing into ten thousand forms: like clustered halberds and arrayed jade tablets, soaring phoenixes and flying steeds, presenting tripods and crouching tigers [?], precipitous and craggy, shifting like clouds and surging like waves, beyond all power to describe. And among them, two or three lofty peaks stand stark above the Milky Way, like a grand patriarch or a Confucian elder seated high and looking down, while a crowd of younger disciples prostrate themselves and hasten about, having no [leisure] to listen to his instructions…

title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
皇也又若元戎搴旗連百萬
熊羆追垓下戰昆陽虎臣驍
騎角力之恐後也斯其山川
奇勝雖秦蜀莫之甲也蓋蹶
然嘆曰西粵材賢之眾多其
間名公卿之勛猷以揆之今
日其方權輿而未可津涯者
===
與何則昆侖之氣鼓行域內
自北徂南而西粵固南國之
極壤精華之尤萃也以彼其
山川而值精華之萃故曰今
日未可以津涯也曩又聞莅
茲土者唯固守簡闊舊畫多
未嘗事事曰吾無櫻也已而
punctuated: 皇也。又若元戎搴旗，連百萬熊羆，追垓下、戰昆陽，虎臣驍騎角力之恐後也。斯其山川奇勝，雖秦、蜀莫之甲也。蓋蹶然嘆曰：西粵材賢之眾多，其間名公卿之勛猷，以揆之今日，其方權輿而未可津涯者與！何則？昆侖之氣鼓行域內，自北徂南，而西粵固南國之極壤，精華之尤萃也。以彼其山川，而值精華之萃，故曰今日未可以津涯也。曩又聞莅茲土者，唯固守簡闊舊畫，多未嘗事事，曰：「吾無櫻也已。」而
translation_en: … the time to spare. And again, they are like a supreme commander capturing enemy banners, leading a million bear-like warriors in the pursuit at Gaixia 垓下 or the battle at Kunyang 昆陽, with tiger-like officers and valiant horsemen vying in strength for fear of falling behind. In the wondrous beauty of its mountains and rivers, even Qin 秦 and Shu 蜀 cannot surpass it. Thus I started up and sighed, saying: "The multitude of talented and worthy men in Western Yue 西粵 [Guangxi], and the meritorious plans of the famed grandees and ministers among them—when we measure them from the perspective of today, are they not just at their very beginning and boundless in their future scope?" Why is this so? The vital pneuma of the Kunlun 昆侖 mountains surges across the realm, moving from north to south; and Western Yue is indeed the farthest reach of the southern lands, where the finest essence especially gathers. Possessing such mountains and rivers as those, and coinciding with the gathering of this finest essence—that is why I say its scope today cannot yet be bounded. In the past, I also heard that those who came to govern this land merely clung fast to simple and loose old routines, mostly refraining from actively managing affairs, saying: "We simply avoid provoking trouble, that is all." And…

title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
虺穴木樵𧖟跣之餘孽卵育
日繁豪噬我民其極至侵疆
奪邑戕官剚吏歳罔虛日襟
喉爲之鬲塞諸司猶然視曰
吾無櫻也頃得節鉞大吏繡
斧使臣毅然議征於是古田
先復府江繼通刋除蓊鬱旁
===
===
鬯日南之遐談者則曰西粵
之人事又何其與天運地靈
相協應也然則西粵材賢駿
發而鴻宣引長而勿替斯又
非其時與玆者大比賓興羅
蒐卓犖諸士乘
昌運遘
punctuated: 虺穴木樵，𧖟跣之餘孽，卵育日繁，豪噬我民。其極至侵疆奪邑，戕官剚吏，歳罔虛日，襟喉爲之鬲塞，諸司猶然視曰：「吾無櫻也。」頃得節鉞大吏、繡斧使臣毅然議征，於是古田先復，府江繼通，刋除蓊鬱，旁鬯日南之遐。談者則曰：「西粵之人事，又何其與天運地靈相協應也！」然則西粵材賢駿發而鴻宣，引長而勿替，斯又非其時與？玆者大比賓興，羅蒐卓犖。諸士乘昌運，遘
translation_en: …lairing like vipers and nesting in trees, the remnant spawn of barefooted barbarians bred and multiplied day by day, violently devouring our people. At the extreme, they encroached upon borders and seized towns, slaying officials and stabbing clerks—hardly a day passed in the year without such incidents, and the strategic thoroughfares were choked off because of them. Yet the various officials still looked on just the same and said, "We should not provoke them." Recently, however, high commanders bearing the battle-axe of authority and imperial commissioners in embroidered robes resolutely deliberated on a punitive campaign. Thereupon Gutian was recovered first, the Fu River was cleared next, the dense overgrowth was cut away, and imperial influence spread far and wide to the distant reaches south of the sun. Those who discuss the matter say, "How remarkably the human affairs of Western Yue [Guangxi] harmonize and correspond with the cycle of Heaven and the numinous power of the earth!" If that is so, then for the men of talent and worth in Western Yue to burst forth swiftly and manifest themselves grandly, continuing indefinitely without decline—is this not indeed the very time for it? Now, at the triennial examination when worthy guests are raised up, we gather in the preeminent and extraordinary. Riding upon this prosperous cycle of destiny and encountering…

title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
盛時而適際
聖作之期則三試之所揮霍有司
之所鑑遴閎詞奧義鏗耳溢
眥纚纚藝林固足以進叩南
宮矣不知其翊
運應時仰對
聖人求賢之實詎止斯藝已乎夫
===
士之爲藝談儒行則宗聖脩
而詆老佛論治法則尊王道
而卑五伯籌國計則上商周
而下管桑非不彰彰著也然
一朝布之中外較其行事與
曩所言者若兩人焉何哉則
以未達
punctuated: 盛時，而適際聖作之期，則三試之所揮霍，有司之所鑑遴，閎詞奧義，鏗耳溢眥，纚纚藝林，固足以進叩南宮矣。不知其翊運應時，仰對聖人求賢之實，詎止斯藝已乎？夫士之爲藝，談儒行則宗聖脩而詆老、佛，論治法則尊王道而卑五伯，籌國計則上商、周而下管、桑，非不彰彰著也；然一朝布之中外，較其行事，與曩所言者若兩人焉，何哉？則以未達
translation_en: …a flourishing era, and happening to coincide with a time when the Sage Ruler initiates anew, what they have poured forth across the three examination sessions and what the authorities have discerned and selected—grand words and profound meanings, ringing in the ears and filling the eyes, a rich array in the forest of literary arts—are indeed sufficient for them to advance and knock at the gates of the Southern Palace [for the Metropolitan Examination]. Yet I do not know whether their assisting the dynastic destiny, responding to the times, and looking up to answer the substantive reality of the Sage Ruler's search for worthies can really be limited to these literary arts alone! Now, when scholars compose their examination essays: in discussing Confucian conduct, they revere sagely self-cultivation and disparage Laozi and the Buddha; in debating methods of governance, they honor the Kingly Way and belittle the Five Hegemons; in planning state finances, they exalt the Shang and Zhou dynasties and look down upon Guan Zhong and Sang Hongyang. All of this is by no means unclear or unmanifest. And yet, once they are placed in offices at court and in the provinces, if one compares their actual deeds with what they previously wrote, it is as though they were two different people. Why is this? It is because they have not yet comprehended…

title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
國家求賢之實者也詩曰濟濟
多士維周之楨士胡以克楨
哉書曰不惟逸豫惟以亂民
詩又曰百爾君子百辟卿士
不解于位民之攸墍是則
國家自養士布列有位冀爲國
楨非斯世斯民無爲也士自
===
始學至列有位爰楨乃國非
斯世斯民無事也此
國家求賢之實亦士之自靖也
士既不知其實而脩之方其
學操翰輒私心卜曰吾得繇
是飽刀泉華閭里足矣他吾
奚有有晉是者曰吾得繇是
punctuated: 國家求賢之實者也。《詩》曰：「濟濟多士，維周之楨。」士胡以克楨哉？《書》曰：「不惟逸豫，惟以亂民。」《詩》又曰：「百爾君子，百辟卿士，不解于位，民之攸墍。」是則國家自養士、布列有位，冀爲國楨，非斯世斯民無爲也；士自始學至列有位，爰楨乃國，非斯世斯民無事也。此國家求賢之實，亦士之自靖也。士既不知其實而脩之，方其學操翰，輒私心卜曰：「吾得繇是飽刀泉、華閭里足矣，他吾奚有？」有晉是者曰：「吾得繇是
translation_en:
… the true substance of the state's search for worthies. The Classic of Poetry (Shijing) says: "Stately are the many scholars; they are the pillars of Zhou." How is it that scholars are able to serve as pillars? The Classic of Documents (Shujing) says: "Not for indulgence in ease and pleasure, but so as to govern the people." The Classic of Poetry again says: "All you noble men, all you lords and high ministers, do not be remiss in your offices, for in you the people find their rest." Thus, from the time the state nurtures scholars to when it places them in official positions, hoping they will serve as pillars of the state, it acts solely for this world and this people. And from the time a scholar begins his studies to when he takes his place in office and thereby serves as a pillar of the state, he occupies himself solely with this world and this people. This is the true substance of the state's search for worthies, and it is also how a scholar fulfills his own duty in conscience.

When scholars do not understand this substance and cultivate it, from the moment they learn to wield the writing brush they privately calculate in their hearts, saying: "If by means of this I can get my fill of coin and cash and bring glory to my home village, that will be enough; what else is any concern of mine?" There are those who go a step beyond this, saying: "If by means of this I can…

title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
translation_en: […] day […], […] Provincial Surveillance Commission […].

title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
廣西鄉試錄序
聖天子御寓紀元是爲萬曆癸酉
天下士當大比于鄉
上採言官議
詔下郡國諸所登進皆崇本實毋
爲浮夸骯骸習海內人士亦
旣仰承
===
德意斌斌嚮風矣維時廣西巡按
監察御史唐鍊職司監臨賡
飭百度先期走幣延諸文學
至則以洛及教授蔡存省爲
考試教諭劉起鵬李子象爲
同考試而提調則屬之左布
政使楊成左參議高則益監
punctuated:
廣西鄉試錄序
聖天子御寓紀元，是爲萬曆癸酉，天下士當大比于鄉。上採言官議，詔下郡國：諸所登進，皆崇本實，毋爲浮夸骯骸習。海內人士，亦旣仰承德意，斌斌嚮風矣。維時廣西巡按監察御史唐鍊職司監臨，賡飭百度，先期走幣延諸文學；至，則以洛及教授蔡存省爲考試，教諭劉起鵬、李子象爲同考試；而提調則屬之左布政使楊成、左參議高則益，監
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Guangxi Provincial Examination

When the Sacred Son of Heaven assumed rule over the realm and inaugurated his reign era, it was the guiyou year of Wanli (1573), the time when the scholars of the Empire were due for the triennial examination in the provinces. His Majesty adopted the deliberations of the speaking officials and sent down an edict to the commanderies and principalities: that in all promotions and selections of talent, everyone should esteem fundamental substance and avoid the habits of bombast and grotesque eccentricity [骯骸?]. Scholars within the seas have already reverently received His virtuous intent and in refined abundance turned toward his transforming influence.

At this time, the Regional Inspector of Guangxi and Investigating Censor Tang Lian 唐鍊 held the office of Supervising Official. Continuing to put all administrative measures in order, ahead of schedule he sent out gifts to invite various men of letters. When they arrived, he appointed me, [Luo] 洛, together with Prefectural Director of Studies Cai Cunxing 蔡存省 as Examiners, and District Directors of Studies Liu Qipeng 劉起鵬 and Li Zixiang 李子象 as Associate Examiners; the duties of Proctor were entrusted to Left Administration Commissioner Yang Cheng 楊成 and Left Assistant Administration Commissioner Gao Zeyi 高則益, while the surveillance of…

title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
試則屬之按察使高察僉事
夏道南諸執事皆慎簡以充
先是府江諸夷弗靖提督兩
廣軍務都察院右都御史兼
兵部右侍郎殷正茂巡撫廣
西都察院右副都御史郭應
聘與御史會疏
===
請討一舉蕩平故士得益脩絃誦
之業即洛等祗役而來也亦
夷猶即次無復曩時震駭之
警矣既鎖闈合提學僉事江
圻所簡士一千四百有奇試
之遵
制拔其雋五十五人復梓其文為
punctuated: 試則屬之按察使高察、僉事夏道南，諸執事皆慎簡以充。先是，府江諸夷弗靖，提督兩廣軍務、都察院右都御史兼兵部右侍郎殷正茂，巡撫廣西、都察院右副都御史郭應聘，與御史會疏請討，一舉蕩平。故士得益脩絃誦之業，即洛等祗役而來也，亦夷猶即次，無復曩時震駭之警矣。既鎖闈，合提學僉事江圻所簡士一千四百有奇試之。遵制拔其雋五十五人，復梓其文為
translation_en: … while the duties of Surveillance Official were assigned to Surveillance Commissioner Gao Cha 高察 and Assistant Surveillance Commissioner Xia Daonan 夏道南; all the other functionaries were carefully selected to fill their posts. Earlier, when the various non-Han tribes along the Fu River (Fujiang 府江) were unruly, Yin Zhengmao 殷正茂, Supreme Commander of Military Affairs in Guangdong and Guangxi, Right Censor-in-Chief of the Censorate, and concurrently Right Vice Minister of War, along with Guo Yingping 郭應聘, Grand Coordinator of Guangxi and Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief of the Censorate, submitted a joint memorial with the Regional Inspector requesting permission to launch a punitive expedition, and swept them away at a single stroke. Consequently, the scholars were able to devote themselves all the more to their studies and recitation; and even as I, Luo, and my colleagues came with due reverence to perform our duties, we traveled at ease and lodged peacefully along the way, free from the alarming alerts of former times. Once the examination compound was locked, we gathered the more than one thousand four hundred scholars selected by Education Intendant and Assistant Surveillance Commissioner Jiang Qi 江圻 and examined them. In compliance with the imperial system, we selected fifty-five of the most outstanding candidates, and further had their essays carved onto woodblocks to form…

title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
錄以
獻洛宜敘諸簡端洛惟賢喆之
生雖乾坤鍾秀川嶽孕靈其
所涵濡造就于
聖人之化者良不淺尠載昔姬周
文武迭興道化隆洽至成王
以緝熙宥密荷厥仔肩于時
===
周公居左召公居右同德協
心廑吐握之謀廣延攬之策
故其所布列於常伯常任準
人及執贄而見者濟濟多俊
乂士然大都皆岐酆西土之
產此固成周氣運之盛昌謂
非聖世作人之明徵不可也
punctuated:
錄，以獻。洛宜敘諸簡端。

洛惟賢喆之生，雖乾坤鍾秀，川嶽孕靈，其所涵濡造就于聖人之化者，良不淺尠。載昔姬周，文、武迭興，道化隆洽；至成王以緝熙宥密，荷厥仔肩。于時周公居左，召公居右，同德協心，廑吐握之謀，廣延攬之策。故其所布列於常伯、常任、準人，及執贄而見者，濟濟多俊乂士。然大都皆岐、酆西土之產，此固成周氣運之盛昌，謂非聖世作人之明徵，不可也。
translation_en:
…a record to be presented to the throne. It is fitting that I, Luo, should write a preface at the beginning of these pages.

I, Luo, reflect that in the birth of worthy and wise men, although Heaven and Earth concentrate their finest essences and rivers and mountains gestate their spiritual luminescence, the degree to which they are steeped in and molded by the transforming influence of the Sage is truly not shallow or slight. Looking back to the Zhou dynasty of the Ji clan, Kings Wen and Wu arose in succession, and their moral transformation was grand and pervasive; down to King Cheng, with radiant brightness and serene profundity, he shouldered that heavy responsibility. At that time, the Duke of Zhou stood at his left and the Duke of Shao stood at his right; sharing the same virtue and uniting their hearts, they were diligent in plans that made them spit out their food and grasp their hair to welcome the worthy, and broadened their policies for recruiting talent. Therefore, those who were arrayed as Regular Senior Advisors (changbo), Regular Functionaries (changren), and Law Officials (zhunren), as well as those who presented ceremonial gifts to be received in audience, were a multitude of outstanding and capable men. Yet for the most part they were all natives of the western lands of Qi and Feng. While this was assuredly due to the flourishing cycle of destiny of the reigning Zhou, one cannot say that it was not also a clear proof of a sage age's cultivation of men.

title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
廣右固山川殊異之區也洛
觀諸士子之文覃思經籍綜
貫理道言人人殊而其裹精
吐奇含貞抒素類能熠目快
心是故有博大閎肆者則桂
嶺堯山之亘峙也有澎湃浤
泂一瀉千里者則湘灕三江
===
之瀠洄也有峭拔蘢嵷不事
雕繪而瓌巧天成者則勾漏
仙都七星龍隱之掩映也瓊
裾玉佩和鳴鏗鏘泠然宣成
柳州之遺響而萬夫不奪之
氣視銅柱崑崙之槩相頡頏
焉玆特山川之能哉
punctuated: 廣右固山川殊異之區也。洛觀諸士子之文，覃思經籍，綜貫理道，言人人殊，而其裹精吐奇，含貞抒素，類能熠目快心。是故有博大閎肆者，則桂嶺、堯山之亘峙也；有澎湃浤泂、一瀉千里者，則湘、灕、三江之瀠洄也；有峭拔蘢嵷、不事雕繪而瓌巧天成者，則勾漏、仙都、七星、龍隱之掩映也。瓊裾玉佩，和鳴鏗鏘，泠然宣成、柳州之遺響；而萬夫不奪之氣，視銅柱、崑崙之槩，相頡頏焉。玆特山川之能哉？
translation_en: Guangxi is indeed a region of extraordinarily distinctive mountains and rivers. As I, Luo, observe the writings of the various scholars, they ponder deeply over the classics and texts, comprehensively mastering principles and the Way. Though their words differ from person to person, in their wrapping of essence and uttering of the extraordinary, in their harboring of purity and expressing of unadorned truth, they are generally all able to dazzle the eyes and delight the heart. Thus, where there are writings that are vast, grand, and unconstrained, they are like the continuous towering of Guiling and Mount Yao; where there are those that surge with vast, echoing currents, pouring forth a thousand li in a single rush, they are like the swirling confluence of the Xiang, the Li, and the Three Rivers; where there are those that are precipitous and lofty, not engaging in carved embellishments yet marvelously ingenious by nature's own making, they are like the mutual shading and reflection of Goulou, Xiandu, Seven Stars (Qixing), and Dragon Hid (Longyin). Like jade-adorned hems and jade pendants chiming in clear, resonant harmony, they coolly carry the lingering echoes of Lu Zhi (Duke Xuancheng) and Liu Zongyuan (Liuzhou); while their indomitable spirit, which ten thousand men could not strip away, rivals the heroic bearing of the Bronze Pillars (Tongzhu) and Kunlun Pass. Yet could this merely be the capability of the mountains and rivers alone?

title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
國朝二百餘年崇儒重道鼓鑄
陶冶非一朝夕而
今上神聖
出震繼離與周成媲美一時碩
輔精白賛襄蘄垂周召之勳
以紹豐鎬之盛誠為千載一
遘然則諸士子漸磨之深與
===
感奮之勇不覺其得心應手
之若是也其在玆乎其在玆
乎夫覩圓折者識其珍闚丹
穴者神其羽因言考德洛固
知諸士之必能楨世而殿邦
矣然洛猶有說焉夫士隱約
蓬茨孰不兾乗時顯庸也廼
punctuated: 國朝二百餘年，崇儒重道，鼓鑄陶冶，非一朝夕；而今上神聖，出震繼離，與周成媲美。一時碩輔，精白賛襄，蘄垂周、召之勳，以紹豐、鎬之盛，誠為千載一遘。然則諸士子漸磨之深，與感奮之勇，不覺其得心應手之若是也。其在玆乎？其在玆乎？夫覩圓折者識其珍，闚丹穴者神其羽。因言考德，洛固知諸士之必能楨世而殿邦矣。然洛猶有說焉。夫士隱約蓬茨，孰不兾乗時顯庸也？廼
translation_en:
For more than two hundred years, our Dynasty has revered Confucian scholars and valued the Way, smelting and molding them not merely for a single morning or evening. Moreover, the reigning Emperor is divinely sage; emerging in the East [the trigram Zhen] to succeed to the Radiance [the trigram Li], he rivals the excellence of King Cheng of Zhou. At this moment, great chief ministers assist him with pure and untainted devotion, aspiring to pass down the meritorious achievements of the Dukes of Zhou and Shao so as to continue the flourishing of Feng and Hao. Truly, this is an encounter that occurs once in a thousand years! This being so, the depth of the scholars' gradual refinement and the courage of their inspired exertion have unconsciously made their writing as effortlessly responsive as this. Does it not lie in this? Does it not lie in this?

Now, one who observes the circular eddies of a stream recognizes the pearls within, and one who peers into the Cinnabar Cave marvels at the plumage of the phoenix. By examining their virtue through their words, I, Luo, certainly know that these scholars will surely be able to serve as pillars for the age and bulwarks of the state. Yet I, Luo, still have something more to say. When scholars live in obscurity and poverty beneath thatched roofs, who among them does not hope to seize the moment and achieve illustrious employment? Yet…

title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
今顯庸矣顧庳庳然不自振
燿至偭規矩而改錯斯何以
故素絲之染易緇百鍊之鋼
難淬自昔嘅之矣爾諸士在
膠庠中亦聞
主上之董正百官乎蓋嘗莊誦
勅詞首欲正人心湔宿垢共襄王
===
道與海內更始其有依阿淟
涊噂沓潝訛者國有常憲大
哉
王言與周官三事大夫之訓先後
同符焉夫周官者成王致太
平之書而周召所與共篤棐
者也其言曰功崇惟志業廣
punctuated: 今顯庸矣，顧庳庳然不自振燿，至偭規矩而改錯，斯何以故？素絲之染易緇，百鍊之鋼難淬，自昔嘅之矣。爾諸士在膠庠中，亦聞主上之董正百官乎？蓋嘗莊誦勅詞，首欲正人心、湔宿垢，共襄王道，與海內更始；其有依阿淟涊、噂沓潝訛者，國有常憲。大哉王言！與《周官》三事大夫之訓先後同符焉。夫《周官》者，成王致太平之書，而周、召所與共篤棐者也。其言曰：「功崇惟志，業廣
translation_en: …now they are brought to prominence and employed, yet they remain lowly and uninspired, failing to rouse and distinguish themselves, even going so far as to turn their backs on standards and rules and alter their measures—why is this so? That white silk is easily dyed black, and steel forged a hundred times is hard to temper, has been lamented since antiquity. While you scholars were in the state schools, did you not also hear of the Sovereign's supervision and rectification of the hundred officials? Indeed, I have reverently recited the words of the imperial edict: first and foremost, He wishes to rectify men's minds and wash away old filth, so as jointly to assist in the Kingly Way and make a fresh start with all within the seas; as for those who are sycophantic and befouled, or who babble together in collusion and slander, the state has its constant penal laws. Great are the King's words! Though separated in time, they tally perfectly with the instructions to the Three High Ministers and Grand Masters in the Officers of Zhou (Zhou guan). Now, the Officers of Zhou is the text by which King Cheng brought about Great Peace, and that in which the Dukes of Zhou and Shao joined to give devoted assistance. Its words say: "Achievement is exalted through resolution; enterprise is broadened…

title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
惟勤爾諸士旣隨計吏以上
異日布列有位展采錯事則
將何以辨志而貞業哉亦惟
皇極之敷言是訓是迪其庶幾永
底于休以無負爾山川之靈
乃或澤鞭以倖售抱腊以爲
璞使人得而詬訾其後豈洛
===
所望於爾多士也歟是舉也
詰兵鎮遠則總兵署都督同
知李錫綜理防範于內外則
右參政鄭茂副使金柱沈子
木莊國禎徐作右參議李文
續僉事高克謙參將錢鳳翔
王世科王承恩都司署都指
punctuated: 惟勤。爾諸士旣隨計吏以上，異日布列有位，展采錯事，則將何以辨志而貞業哉？亦惟皇極之敷言，是訓是迪，其庶幾永底于休，以無負爾山川之靈。乃或澤鞭以倖售，抱腊以爲璞，使人得而詬訾其後，豈洛所望於爾多士也歟！是舉也，詰兵鎮遠，則總兵署都督同知李錫；綜理防範于內外，則右參政鄭茂，副使金柱、沈子木、莊國禎、徐作，右參議李文續，僉事高克謙，參將錢鳳翔、王世科、王承恩，都司署都指
translation_en:
… only through diligence.” Now that you scholars are about to go up to the capital along with the officials bearing the administrative accounts, and in the future will be arrayed in official positions to display your talents and manage affairs, how then will you discern your aspirations and keep your undertakings upright? Only by taking the amplified words of the August Ultimate as your instruction and your guide may you perhaps forever attain excellence, so as not to fail the numinous spirit of your mountains and rivers. If, however, anyone should gloss a whip hoping to pass it off for sale, or clutch dried rat meat while taking it to be uncut jade, thereby allowing people afterward to revile and criticize him—could that be what I, Luo, hope for from you many scholars?

In this undertaking, the one who drilled the troops and pacified the distant regions was the Regional Commander and Acting Vice Commissioner-in-Chief Li Xi 李錫; those who comprehensively managed and maintained security inside and outside were Administration Vice Commissioner of the Right Zheng Mao 鄭茂, Surveillance Vice Commissioners Jin Zhu 金柱, Shen Zimu 沈子木, Zhuang Guozhen 莊國禎, and Xu Zuo 徐作, Assistant Administration Commissioner of the Right Li Wenxu 李文續, Assistant Surveillance Commissioner Gao Keqian 高克謙, Assistant Regional Commanders Qian Fengxiang 錢鳳翔, Wang Shike 王世科, and Wang Cheng'en 王承恩, and the Regional Military Commission Acting Assistant Military Commissioners…

title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
揮僉事汪可大許文楊照以
入
賀行者右參政李鳳副使劉廷
舉以遷秩行者左參政胡直
咸先後與勞以使節莅止者
成安伯郭應乾大理寺評事
杜詩中書舍人王蓕蔣務稼
===
行人司行人彭應時咸有事
玆土法得竝書
湖廣承天府儒學敎授朱洛
謹序
punctuated:
揮僉事汪可大、許文、楊照；以入賀行者，右參政李鳳、副使劉廷舉；以遷秩行者，左參政胡直，咸先後與勞。以使節莅止者，成安伯郭應乾、大理寺評事杜詩、中書舍人王蓕、蔣務稼、行人司行人彭應時，咸有事玆土，法得竝書。

湖廣承天府儒學敎授朱洛謹序。
translation_en:
…Acting Assistant Regional Military Commissioners Wang Keda 汪可大, Xu Wen 許文, and Yang Zhao 楊照. Those who departed to present congratulations at court—Right Administration Vice Commissioner Li Feng 李鳳 and Surveillance Vice Commissioner Liu Tingju 劉廷舉—and he who departed upon promotion to a new post—Left Administration Vice Commissioner Hu Zhi 胡直—all contributed their labors either earlier or later. As for those who arrived bearing imperial credentials as envoys—Earl of Cheng'an (Cheng'an bo 成安伯) Guo Yingqian 郭應乾, Case Reviewer in the Court of Judicial Review Du Shi 杜詩, Drafters in the Central Drafting Office Wang Hui 王蓕 and Jiang Wujia 蔣務稼, and Messenger in the Messenger Office Peng Yingshi 彭應時—all had official business in this territory, and by regulation deserve to be recorded together.

Respectfully prefaced by Zhu Luo 朱洛, Instructor in the Confucian School of Chengtian Prefecture in Huguang.

title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
子曰志於道據於德依於仁游於藝
脩身則道立尊賢則不惑
孟子曰禹惡旨酒而好善言湯執中立賢
無方文王視民如傷望道而未之見武
王不泄邇不忘遠周公思兼三王以施
四事其有不合者仰而思之夜以繼日
幸而得之坐以待旦
===
易
厥孚交如信以發志也
晉康侯用錫馬蕃庶晝日三接
萬有一千五百二十
天地之道貞觀者也日月之道貞明者也
天下之動貞夫一者也夫乾確然示人
易矣夫坤隤然示人簡矣爻也者效此
者也象也者像此者也
書
punctuated:
第壹場

四書

子曰：「志於道，據於德，依於仁，游於藝。」

脩身則道立，尊賢則不惑。

孟子曰：「禹惡旨酒而好善言。湯執中，立賢無方。文王視民如傷，望道而未之見。武王不泄邇，不忘遠。周公思兼三王，以施四事；其有不合者，仰而思之，夜以繼日；幸而得之，坐以待旦。」

易

厥孚交如，信以發志也。

晉，康侯用錫馬蕃庶，晝日三接。

萬有一千五百二十。

天地之道，貞觀者也；日月之道，貞明者也；天下之動，貞夫一者也。夫乾，確然示人易矣；夫坤，隤然示人簡矣。爻也者，效此者也；象也者，像此者也。

書
translation_en:
First Session

The Four Books

The Master said: "Set your heart upon the Way, base yourself upon virtue, rely upon benevolence, and find recreation in the arts."

By cultivating one's person, the Way is established; by honoring the worthy, one is free from perplexity.

Mencius said: "Yu hated fine wine and loved good words. Tang held fast to the Mean and employed the worthy without regard to their origins. King Wen looked upon the people as if they were wounded, and gazed toward the Way as though he had not yet seen it. King Wu did not treat familiarly those near at hand, nor did he forget those far away. The Duke of Zhou sought to combine the achievements of the Three Kings so as to carry out their four courses of action. Whenever there was anything that did not accord with them, he looked up and thought about it, continuing from night into day; and when he was fortunate enough to grasp it, he sat waiting for the dawn."

Book of Changes (Yi)

"His sincerity is reciprocated": his trustworthiness inspires the wills of others.

"Advancement (Jin): The peaceful Marquis uses his bestowed horses in great numbers, and in a single day is received three times."

"Ten thousand one hundred and fifty-two."

The Way of Heaven and Earth is to be constant in what they manifest; the Way of the sun and moon is to be constant in their brightness; all movements under Heaven are constant in the One. Now Qian with firm certainty shows men what is easy; Kun with yielding compliance shows men what is simple. The lines (yao) are what imitate this; the images (xiang) are what figure this.

Book of Documents (Shu)

title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
明四目達四聰
惟學遜志務時敏厥修乃來允懷于茲道
積于厥躬惟斅學半念終始典于學厥
德修罔覺監于先王成憲其永無愆
時人斯其惟皇之極
迪知忱恂于九德之行乃敢告教厥后曰
拜手稽首后矣曰宅乃事宅乃牧宅乃
準茲惟后矣
詩
===
七月在野八月在宇九月在戶
鶴鳴于九皐聲聞于天魚在于渚或潜在
淵樂彼之園爰有樹檀其下維穀他山
之石可以攻玉
威儀抑抑德音秩秩無怨無惡率由羣匹
受福無疆四方之綱
儀式刑文王之典日靖四方
春秋
夏齊侯衞侯胥命于蒲〔桓公三年〕公會晉
punctuated:
明四目，達四聰。
惟學遜志，務時敏，厥修乃來。允懷于茲，道積于厥躬。惟斅學半，念終始典于學，厥德修罔覺。監于先王成憲，其永無愆。
時人斯其惟皇之極。
迪知忱恂于九德之行，乃敢告教厥后，曰：「拜手稽首后矣！曰：『宅乃事，宅乃牧，宅乃準，茲惟后矣！』」

詩
七月在野，八月在宇，九月在戶。
鶴鳴于九皐，聲聞于天。魚在于渚，或潜在淵。樂彼之園，爰有樹檀，其下維穀。他山之石，可以攻玉。
威儀抑抑，德音秩秩。無怨無惡，率由羣匹。受福無疆，四方之綱。
儀式刑文王之典，日靖四方。

春秋
夏，齊侯、衞侯胥命于蒲。〔桓公三年〕公會晉
translation_en:
“To see with the eyes of all the four quarters, and to hear with the ears of all the four quarters.”
“In learning, keep a humble will and strive to be constantly diligent; then your cultivation will come. Truly cherish this, and the Way will accumulate in your person. Teaching is half of learning. Let your thoughts from beginning to end be constantly fixed on learning, and your virtue will be cultivated without your being aware of it. Take as your mirror the established statutes of the former kings, and you will forever be free from error.”
“Then will the men of the time take the August Perfection as their standard.”
“Who truly knew and sincerely trusted in the practice of the nine virtues, and thus dared to inform and instruct their sovereign, saying: ‘With hands joined and head bowed to the ground, O Sovereign! We say: Establish your managers of affairs, establish your pastors, establish your officers of the law; by doing this, you will truly be the Sovereign!’”

Book of Odes (Shijing)
“In the seventh month, it is in the wilds; in the eighth month, under the eaves; in the ninth month, at the door.”
“The crane cries in the九皋 [nine marshes], and its voice is heard in the heavens. The fish is by the islet, or plunges into the deep. Pleasant is that garden, where there are sandalwood trees, and beneath them the paper-mulberry. The stones of those other hills may be used to polish jade.”
“His dignified demeanor is circumspect; his virtuous reputation is orderly. Without resentment, without hatred, he follows the example of his peers. He receives boundless blessings, the guiding cord of the four quarters.”
“Take as model and pattern the statutes of King Wen, and daily pacify the four quarters.”

Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu)
“In summer, the Marquis of Qi and the Marquis of Wei mutually bound themselves by a charge at Pu.” [3rd year of Duke Huan] “The Duke met the [Marquis of] Jin…”

天子布德行惠
===
五行四時十二月還相為本也五聲六律
十二管還相為宮也五味六和十二食
還相為質也五色六章十二衣還相為
質也故人者天地之心也五行之端也
食味別聲被色而生者也
禮者殊事合敬者也樂者異文合愛者也
邇臣守和宰正百官大臣慮四方
第貳場
論
punctuated:
侯、宋公、衛侯、曹伯、齊世子光、莒子、邾子、滕子、薛伯、杞伯、小邾子伐鄭。會于蕭魚。襄公十有一年。
秋，公會宋人、齊人伐徐。莊公二十有六年。晉欒書帥師救鄭。成公六年。夏，五月，甲午，遂滅偪陽。襄公十年。
齊人來歸鄆、讙、龜陰田。定公十年。

《禮記》：
「天子布德行惠。」
「五行、四時、十二月，還相為本也；五聲、六律、十二管，還相為宮也；五味、六和、十二食，還相為質也；五色、六章、十二衣，還相為質也。故人者，天地之心也，五行之端也，食味、別聲、被色而生者也。」
「禮者，殊事合敬者也；樂者，異文合愛者也。」
「邇臣守和，宰正百官，大臣慮四方。」

第貳場

論：
translation_en:
… Marquis of Jin, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Cao, Heir Apparent Guang of Qi, the Viscount of Ju, the Viscount of Zhu, the Viscount of Teng, the Earl of Xue, the Earl of Qi, and the Viscount of Little Zhu attacked Zheng. They met at Xiaoyu. (Eleventh year of Duke Xiang.)
In autumn, the Duke joined an officer of Song and an officer of Qi in attacking Xu. (Twenty-sixth year of Duke Zhuang.) Luan Shu of Jin led an army to rescue Zheng. (Sixth year of Duke Cheng.) In summer, in the fifth month, on the jiawu day, they thereupon extinguished Biyang. (Tenth year of Duke Xiang.)
An officer of Qi came to restore the lands of Yun, Huan, and Guiyin. (Tenth year of Duke Ding.)

Record of Rites (Liji):
"The Son of Heaven disseminates virtue and exercises kindness."
"The five phases, the four seasons, and the twelve months take turns serving as the fundamental basis; the five notes, the six pitch-standards, and the twelve pitch-pipes take turns serving as the tonic; the five flavors, the six seasonings, and the twelve dishes take turns serving as the principal substance; the five colors, the six emblems, and the twelve garments take turns serving as the principal substance. Therefore, man is the heart of Heaven and Earth, and the sprouts of the five phases, born to eat flavors, distinguish sounds, and wear colors."
"Rites are that which unites respect across distinct affairs; music is that which unites affection across different patterns."
"Attendant ministers maintain harmony, the Prime Minister rectifies the hundred officials, and the great ministers deliberate upon the four quarters."

Second Session

Discourse:

title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
為聖本由學而成
詔誥表內科一道
擬漢却千里馬詔文帝元年
擬唐以張九齡為中書令誥開元二十二
年
擬以薛瑄為禮部侍郎兼翰林院學士直
文淵閣謝表天順元年
判語五條
官吏給由
===
功臣田土
服舍違式
飛報軍情
脩理倉庫
第叁塲
策五道
問自古明良相遇不偶然也喜起賡歌都
俞吁咈三代以還不可尚矣漢唐而下
雖治不埒古然英主賢臣亦時相與規
punctuated:
「為聖本由學而成」。

詔、誥、表內科一道：
擬漢却千里馬詔（文帝元年）。
擬唐以張九齡為中書令誥（開元二十二年）。
擬以薛瑄為禮部侍郎兼翰林院學士直文淵閣謝表（天順元年）。

判語五條：
官吏給由。
功臣田土。
服舍違式。
飛報軍情。
脩理倉庫。

第叁塲
策五道

問：自古明良相遇，不偶然也。喜起賡歌，都俞吁咈，三代以還，不可尚矣。漢、唐而下，雖治不埒古，然英主賢臣，亦時相與規
translation_en:
"Becoming a sage originally is accomplished through learning."

One composition chosen from among Imperial Edicts, Imperial Mandates, and Memorials:
An imitation of the Han dynasty Imperial Edict declining a thousand-li horse (1st year of Emperor Wen, 179 BCE).
An imitation of the Tang dynasty Imperial Mandate appointing Zhang Jiuling 張九齡 as Secretariat Director (22nd year of the Kaiyuan era, 734).
An imitation of a Memorial of Thanks by Xue Xuan 薛瑄 upon being appointed Vice Minister of Rites concurrently Serving as Hanlin Academician on duty in the Hall of Literary Profundity (1st year of the Tianshun era, 1457).

Five Legal Judgments:
Evaluation reports for officials and subofficial functionaries.
Landholdings of meritorious officials.
Clothing and housing in violation of regulations.
Express reporting of military intelligence.
Repairing and maintaining granaries and treasuries.

Third Session
Five Policy Questions

Question: Since antiquity, the auspicious encounter of an enlightened ruler and worthy ministers has not been a matter of chance. The joyous arousal and responsive songs, the expressions of agreement and dissent—from the Three Dynasties onward, nothing could surpass this. From the Han and Tang dynasties downward, although governance did not equal that of antiquity, heroic rulers and worthy ministers nevertheless at times mutually admonished…

title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
切若續虞人之箴試理人之策頒訓廉
謹刑之銘者載在史冊當時果可以飭
臣工歟條上故事進君臣屏風進稽古
錄無逸諸圖者亦有裨於君道否歟洪
惟我
太祖高皇帝開天立極名臣碩彥應運雲蒸
大誥三篇首敘
君臣同遊
宣宗章皇帝勵精勤政禮敬大臣
===
君臣一體千載一時也然伏讀
賢姦傳官箴臣鑒三書詞嚴義正袞鉞竝陳
秩秩乎儆位之謨也其詳可得聞歟
列聖相承重熙累洽大臣保泰持盈悉心獻納
有進鑑古錄者有進講學親政篇者孜
孜乎輔德之誠也其槩亦可指歟我
皇上聰明天縱作求
世德
嗣位之初
punctuated: 切，若續《虞人之箴》、試《理人之策》、頒《訓廉》《謹刑》之銘者，載在史冊，當時果可以飭臣工歟？條上故事、進《君臣屏風》、進《稽古錄》《無逸》諸圖者，亦有裨於君道否歟？洪惟我太祖高皇帝開天立極，名臣碩彥，應運雲蒸。《大誥》三篇，首敘《君臣同遊》；宣宗章皇帝勵精勤政，禮敬大臣，君臣一體，千載一時也。然伏讀《賢姦傳》《官箴》《臣鑒》三書，詞嚴義正，袞鉞竝陳，秩秩乎儆位之謨也，其詳可得聞歟？列聖相承，重熙累洽，大臣保泰持盈，悉心獻納，有進《鑑古錄》者，有進《講學親政篇》者，孜孜乎輔德之誠也，其槩亦可指歟？我皇上聰明天縱，作求世德，嗣位之初，
translation_en:
… earnestly with one another. Such instances as composing a sequel to the "Admonition of the Huntsman" (Yuren zhi zhen), testing with "Policies on Governing the People" (Liren zhi ce), or promulgating the inscriptions "Instruction on Integrity" (Xunlian) and "Caution in Punishments" (Jinxing) are recorded in the historical annals; at the time, were they truly effective in disciplining officials? And as for presenting itemized precedents from the past, submitting the Screen of Sovereign and Minister (Junchen pingfeng), or presenting the Record of Investigating Antiquity (Jigu lu) and various illustrations of "Against Luxurious Ease" (Wuyi)—were these also of benefit to the way of the ruler, or not?

We humbly reflect upon how our Grand Progenitor, Emperor Gao (Taizu, the Hongwu Emperor), opened up Heaven and established the supreme standard, while renowned ministers and eminent worthies rose like clouds in response to the Mandate. In the three parts of the Grand Pronouncements (Dagao), he opened with an account of "Sovereign and Ministers Sharing in Fellowship" (Junchen tongyou). Emperor Zhang, the Ancestor of Proclamation (Xuanzong, the Xuande Emperor), exerted his spirit in diligent governance and treated his grand ministers with courteous respect; sovereign and minister formed a single body—truly a moment seen once in a thousand years. Yet when we humbly read the three works—the Biographies of the Worthy and the Treacherous (Xianjian zhuan), the Admonitions for Officials (Guanzhen), and the Mirror for Ministers (Chenjian)—their words are stern and their principles righteous, setting forth both praise and condemnation side by side. How orderly are these counsels for admonishing those in office! May their details be heard?

As the successive Sacred Emperors inherited the throne one after another in cumulative splendor and enduring harmony, grand ministers preserved peace and maintained fullness, devoting their whole hearts to offering counsel. There were those who presented the Record of the Mirror of Antiquity (Jiangu lu), and those who presented the Essay on Expounding Learning and Personally Attending to Governance (Jiangxue qinzheng pian). How tireless was their sincerity in assisting imperial virtue! May the general outlines of these also be pointed out?

Our Emperor Above, endowed by Heaven with intelligence and wisdom, strives to emulate the virtue of his forebears. At the very beginning of his succession to the throne, …

title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
平臺召見輔臣虛懷訪落
御書示渥一德和衷後先一致也乃因士習澆
漓官方刓缺特頒
勅諭述敝習以示戒明職守以定準不知視
二聖所製諸書之旨同歟異歟輔臣仰承
德意思宏啓沃爰製
帝鑑圖說分帙兼資乎法戒採事稽數于陰陽
不知於先臣所進三書其孰為詳略歟
爾諸生夙抱忠愛之忱願揚厲而敷陳
===
之以彰
上下交脩之實
問六經之稱雖見于經解至莊子述孔子
之言治六經遷史則名為六藝此其得
名之始與夫六經聖人所以統天地之
心使人不悖其本性其理一也而楊雄
班固王通之徒皆分屬而言之至有配
五行分四時者其果得六經之旨歟又
有謂易為五經之原者有謂六經莫備
punctuated:
平臺召見輔臣，虛懷訪落，御書示渥；一德和衷，後先一致也。乃因士習澆漓，官方刓缺，特頒勅諭，述敝習以示戒，明職守以定準，不知視二聖所製諸書之旨同歟？異歟？輔臣仰承德意，思宏啓沃，爰製《帝鑑圖說》，分帙兼資乎法戒，採事稽數于陰陽，不知於先臣所進三書，其孰為詳略歟？爾諸生夙抱忠愛之忱，願揚厲而敷陳之，以彰上下交脩之實。
問：「六經」之稱，雖見于《經解》，至《莊子》述孔子之言「治六經」，遷《史》則名為「六藝」，此其得名之始與？夫六經，聖人所以統天地之心，使人不悖其本性，其理一也；而楊雄、班固、王通之徒，皆分屬而言之，至有配五行、分四時者，其果得六經之旨歟？又有謂《易》為五經之原者，有謂六經莫備
translation_en:
… summoned the Grand Secretaries to the Platform Hall, humbling himself to take counsel at the beginning of his reign, and bestowed imperial calligraphy to show his rich favor; sharing one virtue in harmonious accord, the present and the past are completely at one. Yet because the customs of the literati had grown thin and decadent, and official standards were worn down and deficient, he specially promulgated an imperial edict recounting corrupt practices to serve as a warning and clarifying official duties to establish a standard. How does its purport compare with the books composed by the two sage emperors—is it the same, or different? The Grand Secretaries, reverently receiving his virtuous intentions and seeking to broaden his enlightenment and counsel, thereupon compiled the Illustrated Mirror for the Emperor (Dijian tushuo), dividing it into volumes that provide both models for emulation and warnings for admonition, and selecting historical events whose numbers correspond to yin and yang. Compared with the three works presented by former ministers, which are more detailed and which more concise? You students have long cherished sentiments of loyalty and devotion; I hope you will amplify and set them forth in full, so as to manifest the reality of mutual cultivation between ruler and ministers.

Question: Although the term "Six Classics" appears in the "Explanations of the Classics" (Jingjie) chapter, it is in the Zhuangzi that Confucius is quoted as speaking of "ordering the Six Classics," while Sima Qian's Historical Records (Shiji) calls them the "Six Arts." Was this the beginning of how they acquired their name? Now, the Six Classics are the means by which the sages unified the mind of Heaven and Earth and enabled people not to go against their inherent nature; their principle is one. Yet writers such as Yang Xiong, Ban Gu, and Wang Tong all discussed them by assigning them to separate categories, even going so far as to match them with the Five Phases and divide them among the Four Seasons—did they truly grasp the purport of the Six Classics? Furthermore, some say that the Changes (Yi) is the source of the Five Classics, while others say that among the Six Classics none is more complete…

title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
于書者有謂春秋兼五經之用者有謂
禮爲道德之極者然則聖人作經亦有
所偏重歟有謂治六經者必先通乎四
書不知四書六經所以相通之類可得
聞歟有謂六經之道同歸其教相通而
文詞亦有近似者可指而言之歟後世
有議經者有僭經者有叛經者其生於
心而害於事可究其實歟先儒有云六
經聖人之心學也又曰六經聖人之用
===
其論說甚備可謂得聖人之旨矣不知
所以爲養心之要致用之實者何居試
詳言以觀明經之學
問周官曰儒以道得民而儒之名始著孔
子有君子小人之辨而其義益明禮記
儒行一篇其條十有五然詞繁意複論
者謂非孔子之言然歟否歟揚子稱通
天地人曰儒似矣而荀子析而爲四司
馬遷列而爲五宋濂又分爲七而作解
punctuated:
于《書》者，有謂《春秋》兼五經之用者，有謂《禮》爲道德之極者，然則聖人作經，亦有所偏重歟？有謂治六經者必先通乎四書，不知四書、六經所以相通之類，可得聞歟？有謂六經之道同歸，其教相通，而文詞亦有近似者，可指而言之歟？後世有議經者，有僭經者，有叛經者，其生於心而害於事，可究其實歟？先儒有云：「六經，聖人之心學也。」又曰：「六經，聖人之用。」其論說甚備，可謂得聖人之旨矣。不知所以爲養心之要、致用之實者何居？試詳言以觀明經之學。

問：《周官》曰：「儒以道得民。」而儒之名始著。孔子有君子、小人之辨，而其義益明。《禮記·儒行》一篇，其條十有五，然詞繁意複，論者謂非孔子之言，然歟？否歟？揚子稱「通天地人曰儒」，似矣；而荀子析而爲四，司馬遷列而爲五，宋濂又分爲七而作解，
translation_en:
… than in the Book of Documents (Shu), some who say that the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu) combines the functions of the other Five Classics, and some who say that the Record of Rites (Li) is the ultimate expression of moral virtue—if so, did the sages also place unequal emphasis when composing the Classics? Some say that those who study the Six Classics must first thoroughly understand the Four Books; may we hear about the categories through which the Four Books and the Six Classics interrelate? Some say that the Way of the Six Classics leads to the same end, that their teachings are mutually connected, and that their wording also bears similarities; can you point these out and discuss them? In later ages there were those who criticized the Classics, those who usurped the authority of the Classics, and those who rebelled against the Classics; arising in their minds and doing harm to affairs, can the realities of these cases be investigated? Former Confucian scholars have said, "The Six Classics are the sages' learning of the mind," and have also said, "The Six Classics are the practical application of the sages." Their discussions are very thorough and may be said to have grasped the intent of the sages. Yet what are the essentials for nourishing the mind and the realities of putting them to practical use? Try to speak of this in detail so that we may observe your learning in illuminating the Classics.

Question: The Offices of Zhou (Zhouguan) says, "Confucian scholars (ru) win the people through the Way," and from this the name "Confucian scholar" first became prominent. Confucius made the distinction between the gentleman (junzi) and the petty man (xiaoren), and its meaning became even clearer. The "Conduct of the Scholar" (Ruxing) chapter in the Record of Rites (Liji) has fifteen clauses, yet its wording is prolix and its ideas repetitive; commentators say that these are not the words of Confucius—is this so or not? Master Yang (Yang Xiong) stated that "one who comprehends Heaven, Earth, and Man is called a Confucian scholar," which seems plausible; yet Master Xun (Xunzi) divided them into four types, Sima Qian arranged them into five, and Song Lian further divided them into seven and wrote an explanation…

title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
是歟非歟漢唐而下載在儒林傳者固
多矣其果以道得民而爲君子乎有宋
眞儒輩出作史者別立道學傳不知道
與儒果可分乎濂洛關閩諸子道學之
宗也豈儒果不足稱乎先儒又謂周至
精程至正邵至大朱極大盡精而貫之
以正果奚別乎又有謂金華廣漢武夷
之學與濂洛鼎立爲三而諸家不與焉
亦有見否歟諸士列在儒林久矣盍亦
===
究其同異以明志乎毋徒支詞漫對也
問將才難得而論將尤難古今稱名將者
多矣然勛名雖同致用各異試捃摭一
二與諸生評之有監軍後期戮以正法
者有不斬裨將示不敢專者有與卒同
衣食致士死戰者有重車餘粱肉士有
饑色者有行無部伍而軍極簡易者有
嚴正部曲而軍不得休者有治師訓整
而諸將不敢仰視者有齊名一時而寬
punctuated:
是歟？非歟？漢、唐而下，載在《儒林傳》者固多矣，其果以道得民而爲君子乎？有宋眞儒輩出，作史者別立《道學傳》，不知道與儒果可分乎？濂、洛、關、閩諸子，道學之宗也，豈儒果不足稱乎？先儒又謂：「周至精，程至正，邵至大，朱極大盡精而貫之以正。」果奚別乎？又有謂金華、廣漢、武夷之學與濂、洛鼎立爲三，而諸家不與焉，亦有見否歟？諸士列在儒林久矣，盍亦究其同異以明志乎？毋徒支詞漫對也。
問：將才難得，而論將尤難。古今稱名將者多矣，然勛名雖同，致用各異。試捃摭一二，與諸生評之。有監軍後期，戮以正法者；有不斬裨將，示不敢專者；有與卒同衣食，致士死戰者；有重車餘粱肉，士有饑色者；有行無部伍，而軍極簡易者；有嚴正部曲，而軍不得休者；有治師訓整，而諸將不敢仰視者；有齊名一時，而寬
translation_en:
… Is this right or wrong? From the Han and Tang dynasties onward, those recorded in the "Biographies of Confucian Scholars" (Rulin zhuan) were indeed numerous; did they truly win the people through the Way and act as gentlemen (junzi)? In the Song dynasty, true Confucians emerged in succession, and the compilers of the dynastic history established a separate "Biographies of Masters of the Learning of the Way" (Daoxue zhuan). One wonders: can the Way and the Confucian truly be separated? The masters of Lian (Zhou Dunyi), Luo (Cheng Hao and Cheng Yi), Guan (Zhang Zai), and Min (Zhu Xi) were the patriarchs of the Learning of the Way; was the title of "Confucian" truly insufficient to designate them? Earlier scholars also said: "Zhou [Dunyi] was supremely subtle, Cheng [Hao and Cheng Yi] supremely orthodox, Shao [Yong] supremely great, while Zhu [Xi] reached the utmost greatness and exhausted subtlety, threading them together with orthodoxy." How are these truly distinguished? Others have maintained that the learning of Jinhua (Lü Zuqian), Guanghan (Zhang Shi), and Wuyi (Zhu Xi) stood like a tripod of three alongside Lian and Luo, while other schools were not included among them—is there any insight in this view or not? You scholars have been ranked in the forest of Confucians for a long time; why not investigate their similarities and differences to make clear your aspirations? Do not merely reply with rambling, digressive words.

Question: Military talent is hard to find, and evaluating generals is harder still. Those acclaimed as famous generals from antiquity to the present are numerous; yet although their meritorious fame was the same, their methods of practical application differed. Let us gather a few examples and evaluate them with you students. There was one who executed an Army Supervisor (jianjun) to uphold the law when he arrived past the appointed time; there was one who refrained from beheading a deputy general to show that he dared not act on his own authority; there was one who shared the same clothing and food as his privates, inspiring his men to fight to the death; there was one whose heavy wagons had a surplus of fine grain and meat while his soldiers wore a look of hunger; there was one who marched without formal ranks and files, keeping his army extremely simple and unencumbered; there was one who strictly regulated his divisions and companies so that the army got no rest; there was one who governed his troops with such disciplined order that the various generals dared not look up at him; and there was one who shared equal fame with him at the time, yet through tolerance…

title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
厚得人過之者是數子皆良將家也而
行事不同若此將人品亦因之歟甞睹
載籍有謂將之術五有謂將之品二又
或謂必六術五權三至五無壙而後可
語天下之將不識前數子者果皆能無
媿否乎夫將者國之輔也君不擇將以
國予敵其要在上選用而信任之爾陸
贄歐陽脩蘇軾蓋甞言之抑可采而行
歟方今南北之兵未甞罷也乃善將兵
===
者寥寥罕聞焉則慎選將帥其道宜何
如而後可
問士抱藝待用出則攄自靖之業處則懷
當世之憂廣右民貧土瘠供億稱艱夷
獠錯居兵釁易動試舉時務所急者與
諸士商之會省屯兵設將所以居重馭
輕也乃土兵三千十冒六七班軍兵欵
徒寄空名卒然有警即煩征調議者欲
盡撤狼兵召練客兵俾緩急可恃似矣
punctuated:
厚得人過之者。是數子皆良將家也，而行事不同若此，將人品亦因之歟？甞睹載籍，有謂將之術五，有謂將之品二，又或謂必六術、五權、三至、五無壙，而後可語天下之將。不識前數子者，果皆能無媿否乎？夫將者，國之輔也；君不擇將，以國予敵。其要在上選用而信任之爾。陸贄、歐陽脩、蘇軾蓋甞言之，抑可采而行歟？方今南北之兵未甞罷也，乃善將兵者寥寥罕聞焉，則慎選將帥，其道宜何如而後可？
問：士抱藝待用，出則攄自靖之業，處則懷當世之憂。廣右民貧土瘠，供億稱艱；夷獠錯居，兵釁易動。試舉時務所急者，與諸士商之。會省屯兵設將，所以居重馭輕也。乃土兵三千，十冒六七；班軍兵欵，徒寄空名。卒然有警，即煩征調。議者欲盡撤狼兵，召練客兵，俾緩急可恃，似矣。
translation_en:
… surpassed him in generosity and winning people's hearts. These several men were all fine generals, yet their actions differed like this—could it be that their personal character also corresponded to these differences? Looking through historical records, some say there are five arts of generalship, some say there are two grades of generals, and others say that only when one possesses the six arts, five authorities, three attainments, and five absences of deficiency [壙 for 曠] can one speak of being a general for the world. I do not know whether the several men mentioned above could indeed all be worthy of this without shame? Now, a general is the bulwark of the state; if a ruler does not select his generals carefully, he hands his state over to the enemy. The key lies simply in the ruler above selecting, employing, and trusting them. Lu Zhi 陸贄, Ouyang Xiu 歐陽脩, and Su Shi 蘇軾 have all discussed this—can their words be adopted and put into practice? At present, military operations in the north and south have not ceased, yet those who are skilled at leading troops are few and rarely heard of. In carefully selecting generals and commanders, what is the proper way to proceed so that it may succeed?

Question: Scholars embrace their skills and await employment; when taking office they set forth achievements that bring peace and order, and when remaining in retirement they harbor concern for the present age. In Guangxi [Guangyou 廣右], the people are poor and the soil is barren, so providing supplies and requisitions is considered difficult; non-Han tribes [Yi 夷 and Lao 獠] live interspersed among the population, so military hostilities are easily stirred up. Let me raise the most urgent affairs of the day and discuss them with you gentlemen. Stationing troops and establishing generals at the provincial capital is the means to hold weight at the center and control the periphery. Yet among the three thousand native troops, six or seven out of ten are fraudulent substitutes, while the rotating guards and military quotas [?] merely exist as empty names on a register. Whenever there is a sudden alarm, it immediately requires the trouble of conscripting and mobilizing forces. Some advisers wish to completely withdraw the native "wolf troops" [langbing 狼兵] and recruit and train outside mercenary troops so that they can be relied upon in emergencies; this seems reasonable. …

title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
顧漢兵一日食而當狼兵五坐食之久
公私交困何策以善其終歟營堡分兵
列戍所以保境安民也乃戍守之卒既
寡且疲田主里排與賊勾結甚者豪勢
包食其田議者欲專意招安量輸煙竈
俾歲時羈縻似矣然夷性喜攻殺者十
九而奉漢法者十一巨奸大猾鼓煽出
沒何計以消其黨歟量地制賦則壤之
遺也曩戶口稅畝半爲夷侵疆理紊矣
===
邇者兵威稍振有司方議平均乃影射
成風清之未幾而告訐踵至豈丈量之
法卒不可行歟分屯給軍養兵之遺也
今屯田子粒半爲官占行伍耗矣邇者
地方多故部檄日行清理乃詭冒成習
督之愈急而玩愒如故豈屯種之制獨
不可講歟夫計兵食以固根本嚴交通
以杜釁端清田賦以厚民生復屯種以
資軍實皆粵西所宜急講而有司掣肘
punctuated: 顧漢兵一日食而當狼兵五，坐食之久，公私交困，何策以善其終歟？營堡分兵列戍，所以保境安民也。乃戍守之卒，既寡且疲；田主里排，與賊勾結，甚者豪勢包食其田。議者欲專意招安，量輸煙竈，俾歲時羈縻，似矣。然夷性喜攻殺者十九，而奉漢法者十一；巨奸大猾，鼓煽出沒，何計以消其黨歟？量地制賦，則壤之遺也。曩戶口稅畝，半爲夷侵，疆理紊矣。邇者兵威稍振，有司方議平均，乃影射成風，清之未幾而告訐踵至，豈丈量之法卒不可行歟？分屯給軍，養兵之遺也。今屯田子粒，半爲官占，行伍耗矣。邇者地方多故，部檄日行清理，乃詭冒成習，督之愈急而玩愒如故，豈屯種之制獨不可講歟？夫計兵食以固根本，嚴交通以杜釁端，清田賦以厚民生，復屯種以資軍實，皆粵西所宜急講，而有司掣肘…
translation_en: Yet a single day's rations for regular Chinese troops equals five days' rations for native "Wolf troops" (langbing). When they sit idle eating rations for long, both public finances and private livelihoods become exhausted—by what policy can this be brought to a good conclusion? Dividing troops among camps and forts to form a line of garrisons is the means to protect the borders and pacify the people. Yet the garrison soldiers are both few and exhausted, while landowners and community heads (lipai) collude with bandits; worse still, powerful magnates engross and live off the garrison lands. Some advisers wish to focus exclusively on pacification and amnesty, assessing only a modest hearth tax so as to keep them under loose rein ("haltered and bridled") from year to year; this seems plausible. However, nine out of ten natives by nature delight in raiding and killing, while scarcely one in ten obeys Chinese law; moreover, great villains and arch-knaves incite them to appear and disappear unpredictably—by what plan can their factions be dissolved? Surveying the land to determine taxes is the legacy of grading the soil. In the past, half of the registered households and taxable acreage were encroached upon by native tribes, throwing land boundaries and records into disorder. Recently, as military prestige has been somewhat restored, the authorities have just begun deliberating on equalization; yet fraudulent tax evasion and concealment have become a prevailing custom, so that scarcely has a clearance begun before accusations and lawsuits follow on one another's heels—can it be that the method of land measurement is ultimately impossible to carry out? Allotting state farms to supply the military is the legacy of sustaining troops. Today, half of the grain yield from military farms (tuntian) is occupied by officers, and the ranks have been depleted. Recently, because the region has faced many troubles, dispatches from the Ministry daily order a clearance and audit; yet fraudulent registration and falsification have become habitual, so that the more urgently supervision is pressed, the more negligence and procrastination continue as before—can it be that the system of military farming alone cannot be pursued? Now, calculating troops and rations to strengthen the foundation, strictly forbidding illicit collusion to cut off the sources of conflict, clearing up land taxes to enrich the people's livelihood, and restoring military farming to supply army provisions—all these are matters that must be urgently addressed in Guangxi, yet in which the authorities find their hands tied…

title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
難任者諸生桑梓之慮必有槪于中矣
惟悉心著于篇俟執事者採焉
punctuated: 難任者。諸生桑梓之慮，必有槪于中矣。惟悉心著于篇，俟執事者採焉。
translation_en: … find difficult to undertake. In your concern for your native region, you students must surely have been deeply moved in your hearts by these matters. Devote your full minds to setting them forth in your essays, so that the authorities may select and adopt them.
