title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
子曰志於道據於德依於仁游於藝
徐尚實
同考試官教諭劉批認理精切而詞復力洗塵套字
字皆有根據且以心字貫之必邃于理學者
考試官教授蔡批講道德仁藝深得大旨錄之
考試官教授朱批簡明切當
聖人論心學在會其全而已蓋道德仁藝皆統
===
于心也君子脩此四者爲學其全乎夫子示人
之意謂夫天下之理不外於心而君子之學善
事其心然有兼體之功焉不可偏廢者也何則
自其率性而見於日用之謂道學以致道非其
志弗至也必研幾於進脩之始求端於物則之
常其所擇之精辨之早者一惟天下之達道焉
此則先明諸心而不迷所往矣自道之得於心
而爲德德之不恒以其守弗固也必秉其自得
之機懋夫服膺之力其所始乎由是終乎由是
punctuated:
第壹場

四書

「子曰：『志於道，據於德，依於仁，游於藝。』」

徐尚實

同考試官教諭劉批：認理精切，而詞復力洗塵套，字字皆有根據。且以「心」字貫之，必邃于理學者。
考試官教授蔡批：講道、德、仁、藝，深得大旨，錄之。
考試官教授朱批：簡明切當。

聖人論心學，在會其全而已。蓋道、德、仁、藝，皆統于心也。君子脩此四者，爲學其全乎！夫子示人之意，謂夫天下之理不外於心，而君子之學善事其心，然有兼體之功焉，不可偏廢者也。何則？自其率性而見於日用之謂道，學以致道，非其志弗至也。必研幾於進脩之始，求端於物則之常，其所擇之精、辨之早者，一惟天下之達道焉。此則先明諸心，而不迷所往矣。自道之得於心而爲德，德之不恒，以其守弗固也。必秉其自得之機，懋夫服膺之力，其所始乎由是、終乎由是
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

"The Master said: 'Set your will on the Way, hold firm to virtue, lean upon humaneness, and take recreation in the arts.'"

Xu Shangshi 徐尚實

Comment by Associate Examiner County Director of Studies Liu 劉: His grasp of moral principle is precise and to the point, and his wording vigorously washes away hackneyed clichés, with every single word well-grounded. Moreover, by threading the whole essay together through the concept of the "mind," he must be someone of deep attainment in the Learning of Principle.
Comment by Examiner Prefectural Director of Studies Cai 蔡: His exposition of the Way, virtue, humaneness, and the arts deeply grasps the main purport. Selected for inclusion.
Comment by Examiner Prefectural Director of Studies Zhu 朱: Concise, clear, and apt.

When the Sage discussed the learning of the mind, it consisted simply in comprehending it in its entirety. For the Way, virtue, humaneness, and the arts are all unified within the mind. When the gentleman cultivates these four, is his learning not complete! The Master's intention in instructing others was to say that all principles under heaven do not lie outside the mind, and the learning of the gentleman consists in tending well to his mind; yet there is an effort of comprehensive embodiment therein, none of which can be one-sidedly neglected. Why is this so? Viewed as following nature and manifesting in daily affairs, it is called the Way; learning in order to reach the Way will not arrive there without setting the will upon it. One must investigate the subtle springs at the very start of one's advancement and cultivation, and seek the beginnings in the constant norms of things and their rules; what one selects with precision and discerns early on is solely the universal Way under heaven. In this way, one first illuminates it in the mind and does not lose direction in where one is going. Viewed as the Way having been attained in the mind, it becomes virtue; when virtue is not constant, it is because one's hold on it is not firm. One must grasp the vital mechanism of self-attainment and exert the strength of clasping it to one's breast, so that what one follows from beginning to end…

title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
者湛然德性之常用焉此則恒以一德而無所
事志矣自德之全於心而為仁仁之難成以違
仁者衆也必操存罔間于須臾虛明不雜以私
欲其所造次於是顛沛於是者渾乎天理之周
流焉此則中心安仁而無所事守矣學而至此
庶可與語純心已乎至若藝者道德仁之散見
亦養心者所不廢也是必會而通之以繹其趣
優而游之以適其情斯則應務因以不匱而此
心庶其有養矣豈曰藝成而下非君子之所貴
===
也而可無游歟要之由道德仁以及于藝而吾
心之理盡之矣自志道據德依仁以及游藝而
事心之功盡之矣兼內外該本末其斯以為善
學乎抑論古者小學教以六藝而夫子論學乃
以游藝終焉何也記有之不興其藝不能樂學
故操縵安弦施于正業之後此大學之教也然
非其要也夫子天縱之聖自謂不在多能而三
月不違一貫授受惟回之愚參之魯得之藝如
求達如賜不與焉噫聖學傳心之要端可識矣
punctuated: 者，湛然德性之常用焉。此則恒以一德，而無所事志矣。自德之全於心而為仁，仁之難成，以違仁者衆也。必操存罔間于須臾，虛明不雜以私欲，其所造次於是、顛沛於是者，渾乎天理之周流焉。此則中心安仁，而無所事守矣。學而至此，庶可與語純心已乎！至若藝者，道德仁之散見，亦養心者所不廢也。是必會而通之以繹其趣，優而游之以適其情，斯則應務因以不匱，而此心庶其有養矣。豈曰「藝成而下」，非君子之所貴也，而可無游歟？要之，由道德仁以及于藝，而吾心之理盡之矣；自志道、據德、依仁以及游藝，而事心之功盡之矣。兼內外，該本末，其斯以為善學乎！抑論古者小學教以六藝，而夫子論學乃以游藝終焉，何也？《記》有之：「不興其藝，不能樂學。」故操縵安弦，施于正業之後，此大學之教也，然非其要也。夫子天縱之聖，自謂不在多能；而三月不違、一貫授受，惟回之愚、參之魯得之，藝如求、達如賜不與焉。噫！聖學傳心之要，端可識矣。
translation_en: … is simply the limpid, constant operation of one's moral nature. At this stage, one is constant in a single virtue and no longer needs to work at setting the will. From virtue being complete in the mind, it becomes humanity (ren); humanity is difficult to bring to completion because the things that work against it are many. One must grasp and preserve it without a moment's interruption, keeping the mind empty and luminous, unmixed with selfish desires, so that whether in moments of haste or in times of peril one abides in it—a seamless, all-pervading flow of Heavenly Principle. At this stage, one rests peacefully in humanity at the center of one's mind and no longer needs to work at holding fast. When learning reaches this point, perhaps one may be spoken with about a pure mind! As for the arts, they are the scattered manifestations of the Way, of virtue, and of humanity, and are likewise not neglected by one who nourishes the mind. One must bring them together and comprehend them thoroughly so as to draw out their meaning, and stroll at ease and take recreation in them so as to suit one's feelings; thus in responding to practical affairs one will never be at a loss, and this mind will be well nourished. How could one say that "the arts, once formed, belong to what is below," are not what the gentleman prizes, and that one may therefore dispense with taking recreation in them? In sum, proceeding from the Way, virtue, and humanity down to the arts, the principles of our mind are exhausted; proceeding from setting the will on the Way, holding fast to virtue, and relying on humanity down to taking recreation in the arts, the effort of serving the mind is exhausted. Combining inner and outer, encompassing root and branch—is this not what it means to be good at learning? Yet if we consider that in antiquity the Lesser Learning taught the Six Arts, why is it that when the Master discussed learning he placed taking recreation in the arts at the very end? The Record of Rites has it: "If one does not take delight in the arts, one cannot find joy in learning." Therefore, practicing the varied strings and settling the tuning were carried out after one's regular studies; this was the teaching of the Greater Learning, yet it was not its essential point. The Master, whom Heaven endowed with sagely wisdom, said of himself that his sagehood did not lie in having many abilities; and as for not departing from humanity for three months and the transmission of the single thread, only the "foolish" Yan Hui and the "dull" Zeng Shen attained them, whereas one as accomplished in the arts as Ran Qiu and one as discerning as端木賜 [Zigong] had no part in it. Alas! The essential point of the sagely learning's transmission of the mind can truly be recognized here …

title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
希聖者念之
脩身則道立尊賢則不惑
莫與高
同考試官教諭李批講道立不惑處脫去浮詞直明
本旨而語復渾融時義之佳者
考試官教授蔡批鎔意鑄詞潔雅不凡宜式多士
考試官教授朱批明淨典雅
聖人指言常道之效有本之身者有取之人者
蓋脩身尊賢九經之先務也行之而各有其效
===
人君可不知所力哉夫子告哀公若曰九經之
目始於脩身而繼以尊賢者以身者出政之本
而賢者輔政之具也是惟不脩脩則必有其效
是惟不尊尊則必有其效玆試言之君道貴立
不立非所以示衆庶也今惟脩身則大本大原
之地無所偏倚而標準於是乎植焉彞倫敘而
物軌斯端以御家邦而道立於邇也人紀脩而
儀刑斯著以臨天下而道立於遠也所謂樹之
風聲陳之藝極此身庶乎其無愧矣非脩身之
punctuated:
希聖者念之。

脩身則道立，尊賢則不惑。
莫與高
同考試官教諭李批：講道立、不惑處，脫去浮詞，直明本旨，而語復渾融，時義之佳者。
考試官教授蔡批：鎔意鑄詞，潔雅不凡，宜式多士。
考試官教授朱批：明淨典雅。

聖人指言常道之效，有本之身者，有取之人者。蓋脩身、尊賢，九經之先務也，行之而各有其效，人君可不知所力哉？夫子告哀公若曰：九經之目，始於脩身而繼以尊賢者，以身者出政之本，而賢者輔政之具也。是惟不脩，脩則必有其效；是惟不尊，尊則必有其效。玆試言之。君道貴立，不立非所以示衆庶也。今惟脩身，則大本大原之地無所偏倚，而標準於是乎植焉。彞倫敘而物軌斯端，以御家邦而道立於邇也；人紀脩而儀刑斯著，以臨天下而道立於遠也。所謂「樹之風聲，陳之藝極」，此身庶乎其無愧矣，非脩身之
translation_en:
…May those who aspire to sagehood keep this in mind!

"By cultivating his personal life, the Way is established; by honoring the worthy, he is free from delusion."
Mo Yugao 莫與高
Associate Examiner Instructor Li 李 comments: In explaining where the Way is established and how one is free from delusion, it sheds empty rhetoric and directly illuminates the essential purport, while the language is moreover well-rounded and harmonious—a fine piece of contemporary-style exposition.
Examiner Professor Cai 蔡 comments: Melting ideas and casting words, pure, elegant, and extraordinary; it is fit to serve as a model for the many scholars.
Examiner Professor Zhu 朱 comments: Clear, clean, and classically elegant.

The Sage points out and speaks of the effects of the constant Way: there is that which is rooted in one's own person, and that which is drawn from others. For cultivating one's personal life and honoring the worthy are the foremost tasks among the Nine Standard Rules; when put into practice, each has its own effect—how could a ruler of men not know where to exert his strength? The Master, instructing Duke Ai, spoke as if to say: The items of the Nine Standard Rules begin with cultivating one's personal life and are followed by honoring the worthy, because one's person is the root from which governance issues, while the worthy are the instruments that assist in governance. Only if one does not cultivate himself will it be otherwise; if he cultivates himself, there will surely be its effect. Only if one does not honor them will it be otherwise; if he honors them, there will surely be its effect. Let us now try to speak of this. The Way of the ruler values being established; if it is not established, there is no means by which to display it to the multitude. Now, only when he cultivates his personal life is there no partiality or leaning in the place of the great root and great source, and the standard is thereby planted therein. The constant human relationships are set in order and the rules of things are thus made upright, so that in governing family and state, the Way is established nearby; the bonds of human society are cultivated and the model of conduct is thus made manifest, so that in overseeing All under Heaven, the Way is established afar. Of what is called "setting up a moral voice and displaying a standard of ultimate criteria," this person may perhaps have nothing of which to be ashamed! Is this not the…

title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
效乎君德貴明有惑其何以辨幾微也今惟尊
賢則啓心沃心之餘必多聞見而藻鑑於是乎
彰焉涵育深而聰明亶大賢明其大者不惑于
其大也論思久而智慮融次賢明其小者不惑
于其小也所謂察乎人倫明乎庶物斯理庶乎
其無疑矣非尊賢之效乎有是道立之身則賢
益知所尊有是不惑之心則身益知所脩以是
身以是賢而立政政其有不舉乎經常之道其
益如此抑論九經之目雖繁而脩身尊賢巳思
===
過半然其始則在立志故文之敬止武之敬勝
皆志以率氣也志立則誠誠則道德九經一以
貫之矣哀公曰寡人不能進於是也惡在其爲
志也夫子未言脩身尊賢之事而先及其效亦
懼哀公之畏難也夫後之有志於文武之政者
自立志始
孟子曰禹惡旨酒而好善言湯執中立賢
無方文王視民如傷望道而未之見武
王不泄邇不忘遠周公思兼三王以施
punctuated:
效乎？君德貴明，有惑其何以辨幾微也？今惟尊賢，則啓心沃心之餘，必多聞見，而藻鑑於是乎彰焉。涵育深而聰明亶，大賢明其大者，不惑于其大也；論思久而智慮融，次賢明其小者，不惑于其小也。所謂察乎人倫，明乎庶物，斯理庶乎其無疑矣，非尊賢之效乎？有是道立之身，則賢益知所尊；有是不惑之心，則身益知所脩。以是身、以是賢而立政，政其有不舉乎？經常之道，其益如此。抑論九經之目雖繁，而脩身、尊賢巳思過半，然其始則在立志。故文之敬止，武之敬勝，皆志以率氣也。志立則誠，誠則道德、九經一以貫之矣。哀公曰：「寡人不能進於是也。」惡在其爲志也？夫子未言脩身、尊賢之事，而先及其效，亦懼哀公之畏難也夫！後之有志於文、武之政者，自立志始。

孟子曰：「禹惡旨酒而好善言。湯執中，立賢無方。文王視民如傷，望道而未之見。武王不泄邇，不忘遠。周公思兼三王，以施
translation_en:
… the effect of [cultivating one's person]? The virtue of a ruler prizes clarity; if there is perplexity, how can he discern subtle incipiencies? Now, if only he honors the worthy, then beyond opening and enriching his mind, he will surely broaden his hearing and seeing, and his discerning judgment will thereby be made manifest. When nurturing is deep and intelligence is genuine, the great worthies clarify what is great, so he is not perplexed regarding great matters; when deliberation is long and wisdom and reflection are thoroughly integrated, the lesser worthies clarify what is small, so he is not perplexed regarding small matters. As for what is called examining closely into human relationships and clearly understanding the multitude of things, this principle will nearly be free of doubt—is this not the effect of honoring the worthy? Possessing a person in whom the Way is thus established, he will all the more know how to honor the worthy; possessing a mind that is thus free of perplexity, he will all the more know how to cultivate his person. Establishing governance with such a person and with such worthies, how could governance fail to be upheld? Such are the benefits of the constant Way. Moreover, if we discuss the items of the Nine Standard Rules, although they are numerous, with cultivating one's person and honoring the worthy one has already grasped more than half; yet their beginning lies in establishing the will. Therefore, King Wen's resting in reverence and King Wu's overcoming through reverence were both cases of the will leading the vital氣 (qi). When the will is established, there is sincerity; when there is sincerity, then moral virtue and the Nine Standard Rules are threaded together as one. Duke Ai said, "I, the lonely one, am unable to advance to this." Wherein, then, lay his will? Before the Master spoke of the affairs of cultivating one's person and honoring the worthy, he first touched upon their effects, fearing indeed that Duke Ai would shrink from the difficulty! Those in later times who set their will upon the governance of King Wen and King Wu must begin by establishing their will.

Mencius said: "Yu hated fine wine and loved good words. Tang held fast to the Mean, and in establishing the worthy he knew no bounds. King Wen looked upon the people as if they were wounded, and gazed toward the Way as though he had not yet seen it. King Wu did not treat with familiarity those who were near, nor did he forget those who were distant. The Duke of Zhou sought to combine the achievements of the Three Kings, so as to carry out…

title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
四事其有不合者仰而思之夜以繼日
幸而得之坐以待旦
劉業成
同考試官教諭劉批此題重羣聖憂勤惕勵之心上
而道統意于言外見之是作發揮明爽不事纏擾宜錄以式
考試官教授蔡批理明詞雅
考試官教授朱批峻潔
大賢於羣聖而各舉其任道之心焉蓋聖人以
斯道為己任也任之切則其心之憂勤惕勵也
===
寧容已乎且聖人之經世以道而其任道以心
心之不息道之所以常存也吾甞仰稽羣聖而
觀其憂勤惕勵之心豈惟堯舜為然哉于夏而
得禹焉禹之心何心也旨酒是惡善言是好危
微之戒禹之祇承於舜者也于商而得湯焉湯
之心何心也惟中是執惟賢是用日躋之敬湯
之纘服于禹者也于周而得文武焉文作于前
而加意于斯道斯民視之如傷也望之未見也
文其純臨保之心者乎武承于後而致謹于易
punctuated:
四事。其有不合者，仰而思之，夜以繼日；幸而得之，坐以待旦。

劉業成
同考試官教諭劉批：此題重羣聖憂勤惕勵之心上，而道統意于言外見之。是作發揮明爽，不事纏擾，宜錄以式。
考試官教授蔡批：理明詞雅。
考試官教授朱批：峻潔。

大賢於羣聖而各舉其任道之心焉。蓋聖人以斯道為己任也，任之切，則其心之憂勤惕勵也，寧容已乎？且聖人之經世以道，而其任道以心。心之不息，道之所以常存也。吾甞仰稽羣聖，而觀其憂勤惕勵之心，豈惟堯、舜為然哉？于夏而得禹焉。禹之心何心也？旨酒是惡，善言是好，危微之戒，禹之祇承於舜者也。于商而得湯焉。湯之心何心也？惟中是執，惟賢是用，日躋之敬，湯之纘服于禹者也。于周而得文、武焉。文作于前，而加意于斯道斯民，視之如傷也，望之未見也，文其純臨保之心者乎！武承于後，而致謹于易
translation_en:
…these four things. Whenever there was anything that did not fit the circumstances, he looked up and thought about it, from daytime into the night; and when he was fortunate enough to grasp it, he sat waiting for the dawn."

Liu Yecheng 劉業成
Comment by Associate Examiner, County Director of Schools Liu: "This topic places its emphasis on the anxious diligence and vigilant exertion in the minds of the various sages, while the meaning of the transmission of the Way is seen beyond the literal words. This composition develops the theme with clarity and briskness, without indulging in tangled elaborations; it should be recorded as a model."
Comment by Examiner, Prefectural Director of Schools Cai: "The reasoning is clear and the diction is elegant."
Comment by Examiner, Prefectural Director of Schools Zhu: "Lofty and pure."

The great worthy speaks of the various sages and in each case cites the mind with which they took up the burden of the Way. For the sages took this Way as their personal responsibility; since they took on this responsibility so earnestly, how could the anxious diligence and vigilant exertion of their minds ever be allowed to cease?

Moreover, the sages ordered the world through the Way, and they took up the burden of the Way through their minds. The unceasingness of the mind is the reason why the Way constantly endures. I have respectfully examined the various sages and observed their minds of anxious diligence and vigilant exertion—how could it be only Yao and Shun who were thus?

In the Xia dynasty, we find Yu. What sort of mind was Yu's mind? Fine wine he detested, and good words he loved; the admonition concerning the precariousness of the human mind and the subtlety of the mind of the Way was what Yu reverently received from Shun.

In the Shang dynasty, we find Tang. What sort of mind was Tang's mind? Only the Mean did he hold fast, and only the worthy did he employ; the reverence that daily ascended was how Tang continued the work of Yu.

In the Zhou dynasty, we find King Wen and King Wu. Wen arose before, and devoted his attention to this Way and this people: he looked upon the people as if they were wounded, and he gazed toward the Way as if he had not yet seen it—how pure was Wen in his mind of overseeing and protecting! Wu succeeded him afterward, and exercised the utmost caution toward what is easily…

title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
忽易忘邇之不泄也遠之不忘也武其秉執競
之心者乎夫得禹湯之心者文武也成文武之
德者周公也公則以三王之道雖各行于當時
而三王之事當變通于今日故因其時與勢之
所值思欲兼而施之方其未合則反覆以思不
知繼日之爲勤也及其既得則黽勉于行不知
待旦之爲勞也周公之善繼善述而敷求哲王
者又何如其爲心也哉吁此道統之所由傳也
繼周公者又豈無以周公之心爲心而繩斯道
===
于不墜者乎此孔孟之心所以不容已也大抵
聖賢以心相傳而究其所以爲心亦惟致謹于
幾希之間爾蓋理欲之幾甚微而心之存亡甚
易衆人惟肆而失之故愈危而愈微聖人惟敬
而存之故既聖而益聖此一中之所由傳而萬
世心學之原也孔子之作春秋孟子之闢楊墨
無非欲人存此心而已有斯道之責者念之
易
厥孚交如信以發志也
punctuated:
忽易忘，邇之不泄也，遠之不忘也，武其秉執競之心者乎！夫得禹、湯之心者，文、武也；成文、武之德者，周公也。公則以三王之道雖各行于當時，而三王之事當變通于今日，故因其時與勢之所值，思欲兼而施之。方其未合，則反覆以思，不知繼日之爲勤也；及其既得，則黽勉于行，不知待旦之爲勞也。周公之善繼善述，而敷求哲王者，又何如其爲心也哉！吁，此道統之所由傳也。繼周公者，又豈無以周公之心爲心，而繩斯道于不墜者乎？此孔、孟之心所以不容已也。大抵聖賢以心相傳，而究其所以爲心，亦惟致謹于幾希之間爾。蓋理欲之幾甚微，而心之存亡甚易。衆人惟肆而失之，故愈危而愈微；聖人惟敬而存之，故既聖而益聖。此一中之所由傳，而萬世心學之原也。孔子之作《春秋》，孟子之闢楊、墨，無非欲人存此心而已。有斯道之責者，念之。

《易》
「厥孚交如，信以發志也。」
translation_en:
… neglected and easily forgotten: he did not treat the near with familiarity, nor did he forget the distant. Did King Wu 武 not uphold a mind of steadfast vigor? Now, those who grasped the minds of Yu 禹 and Tang 湯 were Kings Wen 文 and Wu; and he who brought to completion the virtue of Kings Wen and Wu was the Duke of Zhou 周公. The Duke considered that although the Ways of the Three Kings were each practiced in their own times, the affairs of the Three Kings ought to be adapted to the present day. Therefore, according to the circumstances and conditions he encountered, he pondered with the desire to combine and apply them. While they did not yet fit together, he turned them over and over in his thoughts, not counting it toil to continue day into night; and once he had apprehended something, he strove diligently to put it into practice, not counting it wearisome to sit waiting for the dawn. How great indeed was the mind of the Duke of Zhou, who so ably carried on their intentions and transmitted their achievements, extensively seeking after the wise kings of antiquity!

Alas, this is how the orthodox transmission of the Way (daotong 道統) was handed down! Among those who succeeded the Duke of Zhou, how could there be none who took the mind of the Duke of Zhou as their own mind and carried on this Way so that it would not fall to the ground? This is why the minds of Confucius 孔子 and Mencius 孟子 could not rest. On the whole, sages and worthies transmitted the Way from mind to mind, and if we examine what constituted their mind, it was simply exercising the utmost caution over that slight distinction. For the incipient stirrings of principle and desire are exceedingly subtle, and the preservation or loss of the mind happens all too easily. Ordinary people, through indulgence, lose it, and so the human mind becomes ever more precarious and the moral mind ever more subtle; the sages, through reverence, preserve it, and so being already sagely they become even more sagely. This is how the single norm of centrality was transmitted, and it is the source of the learning of the mind (xinxue 心學) for ten thousand generations. Confucius's composition of the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu 春秋) and Mencius's refutation of Yang Zhu 楊朱 and Mo Di 墨翟 were nothing other than a desire for people to preserve this mind. Let those who bear responsibility for this Way take heed of it!

Book of Changes (Yi 易)
"His sincerity is reciprocated: his trustworthiness draws forth the wills of others."

title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
張孫繼
同考試官教諭李批發志處發揮殆盡一結尤見忠
愛取之
考試官教授蔡批講上下交孚宛然盛世氣象
考試官教授朱批清雅脫塵
爻有同心之化由其誠能動物也蓋至誠而不
動者未之有也信以發志其交孚也固宜夫子
象傳之意以為人君之治有也保大定功莫尚
乎賢養賢致民莫先乎信一信立而君道其庶
===
幾矣大有六五柔順虛中信之質也虛己以應
九二之賢而上下歸之周公之辭曰厥孚交如
蓋言其始也純心以任賢其繼也因賢以得衆
誼之相維分不得而間之觀心于朝君臣其一
體也情之相繫跡不得而疎之觀心于野天下
猶一家也若是者非強之也亦非私也乃信以
發志爾蓋人臣之媚玆其君孰無是志也惟上
無以發之則雖其義不可逃求其感奮而興未
必然也天下之歸向其君孰無是志也惟上無
punctuated:
張孫繼
同考試官教諭李批：發志處發揮殆盡，一結尤見忠愛，取之。
考試官教授蔡批：講上下交孚，宛然盛世氣象。
考試官教授朱批：清雅脫塵。

爻有同心之化，由其誠能動物也。蓋至誠而不動者，未之有也；信以發志，其交孚也固宜。夫子《象傳》之意，以為人君之治有也，保大定功莫尚乎賢，養賢致民莫先乎信。一信立而君道其庶幾矣。大有六五，柔順虛中，信之質也，虛己以應九二之賢，而上下歸之。周公之辭曰：「厥孚交如。」蓋言其始也，純心以任賢；其繼也，因賢以得衆。誼之相維，分不得而間之，觀心于朝，君臣其一體也；情之相繫，跡不得而疎之，觀心于野，天下猶一家也。若是者，非強之也，亦非私也，乃信以發志爾。蓋人臣之媚玆其君，孰無是志也？惟上無以發之，則雖其義不可逃，求其感奮而興，未必然也。天下之歸向其君，孰無是志也？惟上無
translation_en:
Zhang Sunji 張孫繼
Associate Examiner, Instructor Li 李 comments: The exposition on "inspiring the will" is thoroughly developed, and the conclusion especially shows loyalty and affection. Selected.
Examiner, Professor Cai 蔡 comments: Its discussion of mutual trust between superior and inferior vividly evokes the atmosphere of a flourishing age.
Examiner, Professor Zhu 朱 comments: Pure, elegant, and free from vulgarity.

When a hexagram line embodies the transformative power of shared minds, it is because its sincerity can move all things. Indeed, there has never been one of utmost sincerity who could not move others; when trustworthiness inspires the wills of others, it is only natural that mutual trust is achieved. The meaning of Confucius's Commentary on the Images (Xiangzhuan) is that in a ruler's governance of Great Possession (Dayou), nothing is more vital for preserving greatness and establishing merit than employing the worthy, and nothing comes before trustworthiness in nourishing the worthy and winning over the people. Once trustworthiness is established, the Way of the ruler is nearly complete. The Six in the Fifth place of the Great Possession hexagram is gentle, compliant, and receptive in the center, which is the substance of trustworthiness; humbling himself to respond to the worthy Nine in the Second place, both superiors and inferiors turn to him in allegiance. The Duke of Zhou's line statement reads: "His sincerity is reciprocated." This means that in the beginning, he employs the worthy with a pure heart, and subsequently, through the worthy he wins the multitude. Bound together by righteous duty, differences in rank cannot divide them; observing their hearts at court, ruler and minister are of one body. Connected by affection, outward distance cannot estrangethem; observing their hearts in the countryside, the realm is like a single family. That it is so is neither forced nor born of partiality; it is simply trustworthiness inspiring their wills. After all, among ministers who are devoted to their ruler, who does not possess this will? Yet if the superior has nothing with which to inspire it, then although they cannot escape their duty, one cannot be certain that they will be moved to rise up with enthusiasm. Among all in the realm who turn toward their ruler, who does not possess this will? Yet if the superior has nothing…

title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
以發之則雖其情不容已求其激昻而起未必
然也茲惟信也則因其心之所固有動其機之
所自然百官承式莫不曰君之用上敬下如是
其眞純也有是中孚之主而忍以不忠事之乎
惇德之信所以發其靖獻之心也萬民從欲莫
不曰君之以貴下賤如是其懇至也有是至誠
之主而忍以不誠事之乎任人之信所以發其
效順之懷也夫是以其孚交如不可解也以此
治有何有之足虞雖然此君道爾若乃臣子之
===
分則豈必其君之信而後發哉周公之爲臣也
几赤舄而遜碩膚信固此誠也不信亦此誠也
孔子不信於魯而父母之邦依依不舍然則此
爻之義爲治有之君告也若夫臣道則必如周
孔而後可
天地之道貞觀者也日月之道貞明者也
天下之動貞夫一者也夫乾確然示人
易矣夫坤隤然示人簡矣爻也者效此
者也象也者像此者也
punctuated:
以發之，則雖其情不容已，求其激昻而起，未必然也。茲惟信也，則因其心之所固有，動其機之所自然。百官承式，莫不曰：「君之用上敬下，如是其眞純也，有是中孚之主，而忍以不忠事之乎？」惇德之信，所以發其靖獻之心也。萬民從欲，莫不曰：「君之以貴下賤，如是其懇至也，有是至誠之主，而忍以不誠事之乎？」任人之信，所以發其效順之懷也。夫是以其孚交如，不可解也。以此治有，何有之足虞？雖然，此君道爾；若乃臣子之分，則豈必其君之信而後發哉？周公之爲臣也，几赤舄而遜碩膚，信固此誠也，不信亦此誠也；孔子不信於魯，而父母之邦依依不舍。然則此爻之義，爲治有之君告也；若夫臣道，則必如周、孔而後可。

天地之道，貞觀者也；日月之道，貞明者也；天下之動，貞夫一者也。夫乾，確然示人易矣；夫坤，隤然示人簡矣。爻也者，效此者也；象也者，像此者也。
translation_en:
…to inspire them, then even though their feelings cannot be suppressed, if one seeks for them to be stirred and roused to action, it will not necessarily happen. Here, only through trust does one build upon what is inherent in their minds and set in motion what comes naturally to their inclinations. The hundred officials follow the model, and none fails to say: "The ruler's respecting of inferiors from above is so genuine and pure! Having such a sovereign of inner trust (zhongfu), how could we bear to serve him with disloyalty?" The trust that esteems virtue is what inspires their hearts to calmly offer their devotion. The myriad people follow their desires, and none fails to say: "The ruler's humbling of himself as a noble before the lowly is so earnest and utmost! Having such a sovereign of supreme sincerity, how could we bear to serve him with insincerity?" The trust shown in employing men is what inspires their sentiments of rendering obedience. Therefore, their mutual trust (jue fu jiao ru) is inextricable. Governing Great Possession (Dayou) by this means, what anxiety could there be about maintaining possession? Even so, this is the Way of the ruler. As for the duty of subjects and sons, must they wait for their ruler's trust before their devotion is inspired? When the Duke of Zhou served as a minister, leaning on his armrest in red slippers and yielding with great composure, when trusted he maintained this sincerity, and when not trusted he also maintained this sincerity. Confucius was not trusted in Lu, yet he remained fondly attached to the state of his parents and could not bear to leave it. That being so, the meaning of this line is an admonition for rulers who govern Great Possession; as for the Way of the minister, one must be like the Duke of Zhou and Confucius before it is acceptable.

"The Way of Heaven and Earth is constant in its manifestation; the Way of the sun and moon is constant in its illumination; all movements under Heaven are constant in the One. Now Qian resolutely shows men what is easy; Kun compliantly shows men what is simple. The lines (yao) are what imitate this; the images (xiang) are what resemble this."

title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
黃尚學
同考試官教諭李批既不失卦爻吉凶通章大旨而
因題立意前後聯屬無斧鑿痕錄之
考試官教授蔡批易旨渾融文義雅潔
考試官教授朱批簡明貫徹
大傳卽造化以明人事因言造化之理備於易
書也蓋貞一之理通之天人者也乾坤之所示
爻象之所陳何莫非此理哉大傳論卦爻吉凶
至此若曰易書之所有卦爻而已卦爻之吉凶
===
貞勝不獨人事之必然已也有理焉盍觀之造
化乎道莫大於天地渾淪旁薄人不得而名之
也其所正而常者觀而已矣觀之外無貞也有
天地則有日月往來推遷人不得而窮之也其
所正而常者明而已矣明之外無貞也天下之
動吉凶相勝曷有紀哉順此理則吉逆此理則
凶其所正而常者一而已矣猶之貞觀貞明之
不易者也然是貞觀也非徒以其形體焉也夫
乾確然健也其示人也以易顯仁藏用無容心
punctuated:
黃尚學
同考試官、教諭李批：「既不失卦爻吉凶通章大旨，而因題立意，前後聯屬，無斧鑿痕，錄之。」
考試官、教授蔡批：「《易》旨渾融，文義雅潔。」
考試官、教授朱批：「簡明貫徹。」

《大傳》卽造化以明人事，因言造化之理備於《易》書也。蓋貞一之理，通之天人者也。乾坤之所示，爻象之所陳，何莫非此理哉？《大傳》論卦爻吉凶至此，若曰：《易》書之所有，卦爻而已。卦爻之吉凶貞勝，不獨人事之必然已也，有理焉，盍觀之造化乎？道莫大於天地，渾淪旁薄，人不得而名之也；其所正而常者，觀而已矣，觀之外無貞也。有天地則有日月，往來推遷，人不得而窮之也；其所正而常者，明而已矣，明之外無貞也。天下之動，吉凶相勝，曷有紀哉？順此理則吉，逆此理則凶，其所正而常者，一而已矣，猶之貞觀、貞明之不易者也。然是貞觀也，非徒以其形體焉也。夫乾確然健也，其示人也以易，顯仁藏用，無容心…
translation_en:
Huang Shangxue 黃尚學
Associate Examiner and Instructor Li commented: "Not only does this capture the overall purport of the chapter regarding the good and bad fortune of the hexagrams and lines, it also establishes its theme directly from the prompt, with beginning and end smoothly connected and no trace of forced artifice. Selected for inclusion."
Examiner and Confucian School Director Cai commented: "The meaning of the Book of Changes (Yi) is harmoniously integrated, and the style and sense are refined and clean."
Examiner and Confucian School Director Zhu commented: "Concise, clear, and thoroughly coherent."

The Great Treatise (Dazhuan) draws upon the creative transformations of nature to illuminate human affairs, and goes on to state that the principles of creative transformation are fully contained in the Book of Changes. Indeed, the principle of constant unity bridges Heaven and humanity. What Qian and Kun reveal to us, and what the lines and images set forth—how could any of it be other than this principle? Discussing the good and bad fortune of the hexagrams and lines up to this point, the Great Treatise seems to say: All that the Book of Changes possesses is hexagrams and lines. That good and bad fortune in the hexagrams and lines prevail through constancy is not merely an inevitability of human affairs; there is a principle therein—why not observe it in the creative transformations of nature? There is no Way greater than that of Heaven and Earth: vast, undifferentiated, and all-pervading, people cannot put a name to it; yet that wherein it is correct and constant is simply what it displays to view—outside of what is displayed to view, there is no constancy. Given Heaven and Earth, there are sun and moon: coming and going in shifting succession, people cannot exhaust them; yet that wherein they are correct and constant is simply their brightness—outside of brightness, there is no constancy. As for all movements under Heaven, good and bad fortune prevail over one another—how could they be numbered? Following this principle brings good fortune, while defying this principle brings misfortune; that wherein it is correct and constant is simply the One, just like the unchangeability of constant display and constant brightness. Yet this constant display does not reside merely in physical form. Now Qian is firm and vigorous; it reveals itself to people through easiness, manifesting benevolence and concealing its function without deliberate calculation…

title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
也夫坤隤然順也其示人也以簡效法作成無
多事也所謂貞觀者不在此耶是易簡也非徒
以其法象言也易之有爻效此者也奇偶之變
一節之乾坤也易之有象像此者也消息之異
全體之乾坤也所謂易簡者不在此耶乾坤立
而爻象生易書之本也爻象成而吉凶著衆動
之原也彼其貞一之理信乎猶之天地日月不
可易也吁君子觀于貞勝之機察乎貞一之理
則知所以愼其動矣抑論之觀象玩辭觀變玩
===
占學易之功也苟徒以之趨避也豈不淺之乎
用易哉君子心天地之心體易簡之德當不囿
於吉凶之内者故嘗爲之說曰吉凶同患聖人
之心趨吉避凶凡民之事盡性至命君子之易
書
明四目達四聰
劉業成
同考試官教諭劉批講明達二字親切經義之可
錄者
punctuated:
也；夫坤，隤然順也，其示人也以簡，效法作成，無多事也。所謂貞觀者，不在此耶？是易簡也，非徒以其法象言也。《易》之有爻，效此者也，奇偶之變，一節之乾坤也；《易》之有象，像此者也，消息之異，全體之乾坤也。所謂易簡者，不在此耶？乾坤立而爻象生，《易》書之本也；爻象成而吉凶著，衆動之原也。彼其貞一之理，信乎猶之天地日月不可易也。吁！君子觀于貞勝之機，察乎貞一之理，則知所以愼其動矣。抑論之：觀象玩辭，觀變玩占，學《易》之功也；苟徒以之趨避也，豈不淺之乎用《易》哉！君子心天地之心，體易簡之德，當不囿於吉凶之内者。故嘗爲之說曰：吉凶同患，聖人之心；趨吉避凶，凡民之事；盡性至命，君子之《易》。

《書》：「明四目，達四聰。」
劉業成
同考試官教諭劉批：講「明」、「達」二字親切，經義之可錄者。
translation_en:
… [deliberate] intent; and Kun is docilely compliant, showing itself to people through simplicity—emulating models and bringing things to completion without superfluous effort. Does not what is called "correct and constant manifestation" lie right here? Yet this ease and simplicity are not spoken of merely in terms of their visible models and images. That the Changes (Yi) has lines is to emulate this: the alternations of odd and even are Qian and Kun in a single aspect. That the Changes has images is to figure this: the variations of waxing and waning are Qian and Kun in their entirety. Does not what is called "ease and simplicity" lie right here? When Qian and Kun are established, the lines and images are generated—this is the foundation of the Book of Changes. When the lines and images are completed, good fortune and misfortune become manifest—this is the source of all movements. Truly, that principle of being correct and constant in unity is, just like heaven and earth, the sun and the moon, immutable! Ah! When the gentleman observes the subtle mechanism of prevailing through correctness and constancy, and examines the principle of being correct and constant in unity, he knows how to be cautious in his movements. Furthermore, let us consider this: observing the images and savoring the words, observing the changes and savoring the prognostications—this is the work of studying the Changes. If one merely uses it to pursue good fortune and avoid misfortune, how shallow a use of the Changes that would be! The gentleman takes the mind of heaven and earth as his own mind and embodies the virtue of ease and simplicity; he surely ought not to be confined within the bounds of good fortune and misfortune. Thus I have ventured to formulate the saying: "Sharing the anxieties of the people over good fortune and misfortune is the mind of the sage; pursuing good fortune and avoiding misfortune is the business of ordinary folk; fully realizing one's nature and reaching the decree of Heaven is the Changes of the gentleman."

Book of Documents (Shu): "Illumine the four eyes; open the four ears."
By Liu Yecheng 劉業成.
Associate Examiner and County Director of Studies Liu comments: The explanation of the two words "illumine" (ming) and "open" (da) is trenchant and to the point; an essay on the meaning of the Classic worthy of selection.

title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
考試官教授蔡批發出大舜命岳之意宛然
考試官教授朱批詞理俱到
聖君謀治於大臣欲其廣視聽于天下焉夫視
聽以天下則民情無不達矣此道盡而民焉有
不得其所者哉宜帝舜首詢于四岳也意曰人
君通天下以為一身則必公天下以為視聽四
岳者作朕耳目而民情之通塞繫焉者也將何
以輔我哉誠以今日紹堯致治固甞見時雍之
化矣然四海至大而民情之伏也無窮則遺于
===
吾明之外者尚多也爾其為我明四目焉倡率
作之權以廓吾大觀之晢太和景象吾固得而
快覩也而四海困窮吾亦得而兼照焉合四方
之明為一人之明固有不下堂階而視周於萬
里矣昔之時雍者庶其再見矣乎亦甞聞擊壤
之歌矣然四方至廣而民情之隱也無盡則遺
于吾聰之外者何限也爾其為我達四聰焉任
率先之責以大吾兼聽之公九敘惟歌固得而
聞其休也而下民其咨亦得而聞其戚焉合四
punctuated:
考試官教授蔡批：發出大舜命岳之意，宛然。
考試官教授朱批：詞理俱到。
聖君謀治於大臣，欲其廣視聽于天下焉。夫視聽以天下，則民情無不達矣。此道盡，而民焉有不得其所者哉？宜帝舜首詢于四岳也。意曰：人君通天下以為一身，則必公天下以為視聽。四岳者，作朕耳目，而民情之通塞繫焉者也，將何以輔我哉？誠以今日紹堯致治，固甞見時雍之化矣。然四海至大，而民情之伏也無窮，則遺于吾明之外者尚多也。爾其為我明四目焉！倡率作之權，以廓吾大觀之晢。太和景象，吾固得而快覩也；而四海困窮，吾亦得而兼照焉。合四方之明為一人之明，固有不下堂階而視周於萬里矣。昔之時雍者，庶其再見矣乎！亦甞聞擊壤之歌矣。然四方至廣，而民情之隱也無盡，則遺于吾聰之外者何限也。爾其為我達四聰焉！任率先之責，以大吾兼聽之公。九敘惟歌，固得而聞其休也；而下民其咨，亦得而聞其戚焉。合四
translation_en:
Examiner and Prefectural Director of Studies Cai comments: It brings out the intent of the great Shun's charge to the Chiefs of the Four Mountains vividly.
Examiner and Prefectural Director of Studies Zhu comments: Both diction and reasoning reach the mark.
When the sage ruler takes counsel on governance with his great ministers, he wishes them to broaden his sight and hearing throughout the realm. Now, when one sees and hears by means of the whole realm, there are no circumstances of the people that fail to reach above. When this way is fulfilled to the utmost, how could there be any among the people who do not find their proper place? Rightly indeed did Emperor Shun make this his very first inquiry of the Chiefs of the Four Mountains!
The meaning of the passage is as follows: Because a ruler unites the whole realm as a single body, he must make the whole realm his shared sight and hearing. You Chiefs of the Four Mountains act as my ears and eyes, and upon you depends whether the conditions of the people are communicated or obstructed—how then will you assist me?
Truly, today as I succeed Yao in bringing about order, I have indeed already witnessed the transformation of universal harmony. Yet the Four Seas are vast in the extreme, and the unexpressed conditions of the people are endless; thus what remains left out beyond the reach of my vision is still great. Do you therefore clarify the four eyes for me! Take the initiative in exercising the authority to rouse and lead, so as to widen the brightness of my comprehensive view. Scenes of supreme harmony I shall of course be able to behold with delight; yet the distress and poverty within the Four Seas I shall also be able to illuminate together with them. Combining the vision of the four quarters into the vision of the One Man, I shall truly, without descending the hall steps, see all around for ten thousand li. May that universal harmony of the past perhaps be seen once again!
I have also already heard the song of tapping on the earth. Yet the four quarters are broad in the extreme, and the hidden conditions of the people are inexhaustible; thus what remains left out beyond the reach of my hearing—what limit is there to it? Do you therefore open the four ears for me! Bear the responsibility of leading the way, so as to enlarge the impartiality of my comprehensive hearing. When the nine divisions of governance are in order and celebrated in song, I shall of course be able to hear of their blessings; yet when the common people sigh and murmur, I shall also be able to hear of their griefs. title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
方之聰爲一人之聰固有不降皇序而聽徹于
閭閻矣昔之擊壤者庶其常聞矣乎是蓋人君
不自用其聰明而憲天以爲聰明大臣不自有
其視聽而因民以爲視聽此嘉言所以罔伏而
萬邦所由咸寧也帝舜以此首詢四岳其急先
務也哉抑古之帝王黈纊塞耳冕旒蔽目誠不
欲以聰明徇天下也迺帝舜有明目達聰之說
豈徒以好察爲明偏聽爲務哉蓋天下大勢如
一人身精神流貫則元氣充實此好問好察而
===
用其中舜之所以爲大智也君天下者尚鑒茲
哉
迪知忱恂于九德之行乃敢告敎厥后曰
拜手稽首后矣曰宅乃事宅乃牧宅乃
準茲惟后矣
秦中權
同考試官敎諭劉批迪知忱恂即皐謨采采意是作
不用繁詞而題意明徹可式多士
考試官敎授蔡批典雅順鬯
punctuated:
方之聰爲一人之聰，固有不降皇序而聽徹于閭閻矣，昔之擊壤者庶其常聞矣乎！是蓋人君不自用其聰明，而憲天以爲聰明；大臣不自有其視聽，而因民以爲視聽。此嘉言所以罔伏，而萬邦所由咸寧也。帝舜以此首詢四岳，其急先務也哉！抑古之帝王，黈纊塞耳，冕旒蔽目，誠不欲以聰明徇天下也。迺帝舜有「明目達聰」之說，豈徒以好察爲明、偏聽爲務哉？蓋天下大勢，如一人身，精神流貫，則元氣充實。此好問好察而用其中，舜之所以爲大智也。君天下者，尚鑒茲哉！

迪知忱恂于九德之行，乃敢告敎厥后，曰：「拜手稽首，后矣！曰：『宅乃事，宅乃牧，宅乃準，茲惟后矣！』」
秦中權
同考試官敎諭劉批：迪知忱恂，即《皐謨》「采采」意。是作不用繁詞，而題意明徹，可式多士。
考試官敎授蔡批：典雅順鬯。
translation_en:
… combine the hearing of the four quarters into the hearing of the One Man, then indeed, without descending the steps of the imperial hall, my hearing will penetrate into the village lanes. May that ancient song of beating the clods perhaps be heard constantly again! This is because a ruler does not rely solely on his own hearing and sight, but patterns himself on Heaven for his hearing and sight; great ministers do not claim their own seeing and hearing as private, but take the people as the basis of their seeing and hearing. This is why good words are never hidden away, and whereby all the myriad states enjoy peace. When Emperor Shun made this his very first inquiry of the Four Peaks, how urgent a priority he considered it! Yet the emperors and kings of antiquity stopped their ears with yellow silk floss and veiled their eyes with the pendants of their ceremonial caps, truly not wishing to pursue the world with their own personal acuity. When Emperor Shun spoke of "brightening the eyes of the four quarters and opening the ears of the four quarters," how could he merely be taking a fondness for prying as clear sight, or partial listening as his task? For the great configuration of the realm is like the body of a single person: when vital spirit circulates unimpeded throughout, the primordial qi is full and substantial. Loving to question, loving to examine, and using the Mean—this is why Shun possessed great wisdom. May those who rule the realm take this as their mirror!

"Only when they truly knew and sincerely trusted a man's practice of the nine virtues did they dare to inform and instruct their sovereign, saying: 'Doing obeisance with hands to the head and head to the ground, O Sovereign! We say: fill your offices of state, fill your posts of regional pastorship, fill your positions of law; in this way be a true Sovereign!'"
Qin Zhongquan 秦中權
Associate Examiner, Instructor (jiaoyu) Liu comments: "Truly knowing and sincerely trusting" (dizhi chenxun) has the same meaning as "judging by one's varied actions" (caicai) in the "Counsels of Gao Yao" (Gao Yu mo). This composition dispenses with superfluous words, yet the meaning of the theme is clear and penetrating; it may serve as a model for the many scholars.
Examiner, Instructor (jiaoshou) Cai comments: Classically elegant, smooth, and fluent.

title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
考試官敎授朱批雅潔
大臣明于知人而敬以薦之君也甚矣君道在
知人也大臣知之明而後薦之君其斯以為知
恤也歟周公述以告成王蓋曰用賢以尊帝者
君也求賢以事君者大臣也禹之籲俊尊帝觀
諸臣之薦賢見矣彼九德者蘊之心而彰諸行
人君所賴以充三宅之用者胥此也使大臣知
之未明固不敢以薦之上矣今惟同心同德旣
以契其心得之原而曰宣曰嚴又能稽其載采
===
之實蓋迪知而忱恂之斯則薦賢之誠在我而
所以致之君者有本矣乃敢告敎其君焉先之
拜稽以明有敬而繼之曰后以尊其名將望之
以其實也于是告之曰所貴乎后者匪徒以位
高天下而貴以賢理天下后于九德之行也以
之宅乃事宅乃牧宅乃準焉體上天生賢之心
而翕受以弘其用則九德咸事而后之所以對
上帝者于是乎克盡矣承上天付托之重而委
任以責其成則天工人代而天之所以作元后
punctuated:
考試官敎授朱批：雅潔。

大臣明于知人，而敬以薦之君也。甚矣，君道在知人也；大臣知之明而後薦之君，其斯以為知恤也歟！周公述以告成王，蓋曰：用賢以尊帝者，君也；求賢以事君者，大臣也。禹之籲俊尊帝，觀諸臣之薦賢見矣。彼九德者，蘊之心而彰諸行，人君所賴以充三宅之用者胥此也。使大臣知之未明，固不敢以薦之上矣。今惟同心同德，旣以契其心得之原；而曰宣曰嚴，又能稽其載采之實。蓋迪知而忱恂之，斯則薦賢之誠在我，而所以致之君者有本矣。乃敢告敎其君焉。先之拜稽以明有敬，而繼之曰「后」以尊其名，將望之以其實也。于是告之曰：所貴乎后者，匪徒以位高天下，而貴以賢理天下。后于九德之行也，以之宅乃事、宅乃牧、宅乃準焉。體上天生賢之心，而翕受以弘其用，則九德咸事，而后之所以對上帝者于是乎克盡矣；承上天付托之重，而委任以責其成，則天工人代，而天之所以作元后…
translation_en:
Examiner and Confucian School Instructor Zhu comments: Elegant and concise.

Great ministers are discerning in knowing men, and reverently recommend them to their ruler. Indeed, the Way of the ruler lies in knowing men; when great ministers know them clearly and only then recommend them to their ruler, is this not what is meant by knowing how to show anxious concern? The Duke of Zhou recounted this to instruct King Cheng, as if to say: It is the ruler who employs the worthy to honor the Supreme Ancestor; it is the great ministers who seek out the worthy to serve the ruler. That Yu called upon men of eminence to honor the Supreme Ancestor can be seen from how his ministers recommended the worthy. Those nine virtues are cherished in the mind and manifested in conduct; what the ruler relies upon to fill the appointments of the Three Positions all comes from this. If great ministers do not yet know them clearly, they certainly would not dare to recommend them to their superior. Now, because they are of one mind and one virtue, they already grasp the source of what those men have attained in their minds; and whether manifesting three virtues daily or six virtues strictly, they are also able to verify the reality of their actions and undertakings. Having truly known them and sincerely trusted them, the sincerity of recommending the worthy rests within oneself, and the means of presenting them to the ruler has a solid foundation. Only then do they dare to inform and instruct their ruler. First they bow their heads to the hands and to the ground to show their reverence, and next they address him as "Sovereign" to honor his title, intending to expect from him its reality. Thereupon they inform him, saying: What makes a Sovereign valuable is not merely that his position is exalted above the world, but that he governs the world through the worthy. With respect to men who practice the nine virtues, the Sovereign employs them to fill his offices of state affairs, his offices of regional governance, and his offices of the law. When he embodies High Heaven's mind in bringing forth the worthy and receives them all together to broaden their use, then those of the nine virtues will all be in service, and the means by which the Sovereign answers to the Supreme Ancestor is thereby fully realized; when he upholds the weighty trust of High Heaven and delegates responsibilities to demand their accomplishment, then Heaven's work is carried out by human deputies, and the reason why Heaven made him the Great Sovereign…

title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
者于是為無負矣是蓋履其位思盡其實有其
實斯稱其名夏臣之忠愛至矣禹之籲俊尊帝
以此吾王其知法哉抑此大禹得之臯陶而見
知于虞廷者也堯舜禹以一中照臨於上而孔
壬之畏猶兢兢焉則當時君臣致謹于迪知忱
恂有道矣蓋惟中則好惡不偏而官人斯當此
當時所以庶明勵翼而野無遺賢也不然用舍
偏而匪人進所謂九德者皆非矣然則君相用
人其有本哉故曰取人以身
===
詩
鶴鳴于九臯聲聞于天魚在于渚或潜在
淵樂彼之園爰有樹檀其下維穀他山
之石可以攻玉
莫與高
同考試官教諭李批體認含蓄是得詩人言外之意
者錄之
考試官教授蔡批詠物處清奇可玩
考試官教授朱批擺脫宿塵宜式多士
punctuated:
者，于是為無負矣。是蓋履其位，思盡其實，有其實，斯稱其名。夏臣之忠愛至矣！禹之籲俊尊帝以此，吾王其知法哉！抑此大禹得之臯陶，而見知于虞廷者也。堯、舜、禹以一中照臨於上，而孔壬之畏猶兢兢焉，則當時君臣致謹于迪知忱恂有道矣。蓋惟中則好惡不偏，而官人斯當，此當時所以庶明勵翼，而野無遺賢也。不然，用舍偏而匪人進，所謂九德者皆非矣。然則君相用人，其有本哉！故曰：「取人以身。」

詩
「鶴鳴于九臯，聲聞于天。魚在于渚，或潜在淵。樂彼之園，爰有樹檀，其下維穀。他山之石，可以攻玉。」
莫與高
同考試官教諭李批：體認含蓄，是得詩人言外之意者，錄之。
考試官教授蔡批：詠物處清奇可玩。
考試官教授朱批：擺脫宿塵，宜式多士。
translation_en:
… [whereby Heaven made the great sovereign] is thus not betrayed. This is because, occupying his position, he thought to fulfill its substance; possessing the substance, he thereby matched its name. The loyalty and devotion of the ministers of Xia were supreme indeed! It was by this that Yu called upon men of excellence to honor the Lord on High—may our King know to take it as his model!

Moreover, this is what the Great Yu received from Gao Yao and knew firsthand in the court of Yu [Shun]. Yao, Shun, and Yu shone down from above with a single Mean, yet they were still cautiously fearful of great artfulness; thus, the sovereigns and ministers of that time had a Way in exercising utmost care to truly know those who were sincere and trustworthy. For only when there is the Mean are likes and dislikes unbiased, and the appointment of men to office becomes fitting. This is why at that time the众 [numerous] enlightened ones exerted themselves to assist like wings, and no worthy was left neglected in the wilds. Otherwise, if employment and dismissal are biased and unworthy men advance, what are called the Nine Virtues would all be falsified. This being so, does not the employment of men by sovereign and chief minister have its root? Therefore it is said: "One selects men by means of one's own person."

Classic of Poetry (Shi)
"The crane cries in the nine marshes, and its voice is heard in the sky. The fish is by the islet, or else plunges into the deep. Pleasant is that garden, where there are sandalwood trees, and beneath them the paper-mulberry. The stones of those other hills may be used to polish jade."

Mo Yugao
Associate Examiner and County Director of Studies Li comments: His personal comprehension is subtle and reserved; he has grasped the poet's meaning beyond the words. Record it for publication.
Examiner and Prefectural Director of Studies Cai comments: Where he sings of things, the writing is clear, striking, and worthy of appreciation.
Examiner and Prefectural Director of Studies Zhu comments: Casting off stale dust, it is fitting to serve as a model for the many scholars.

title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
詩人屢托物以致詠其旨遠矣蓋理微而物顯
也卽物而觀理詩人其得諷諫之遺者哉且夫
由誠明以合德公好惡而不偏君人之理道盡
矣詩人欲遠有所明而近有所托也故其詞曰
鶴鳴于九皐聲聞于天夫鶴物之善鳴者也矢
音于坎澤而清響之上聞地不得而限之九皐
雖邃也而有聲斯應者四達而不悖矣魚在于
渚或潜在淵夫魚物之善藏者也悠然于清淺
而淵泉之潜躍跡不得而拘之淵渚雖異也而
===
有動斯遊者兩在而無方矣園有樹檀景與地
皆可樂也而維穀生焉佳植而雜之以凡枒造
化其無全美乎他山之石形與質皆可憎也而
治玉資焉良璞而藉之以磨礪天地其無棄物
乎夫觀九皐之鳴鶴而誠不容掩者可推矣觀
淵渚之潜魚而理無定在者可察矣檀園而其
下維穀則之其所愛而辟者非也山石而用以
攻玉則之其所惡而辟者非也誠則明明則誠
聖脩可以立極好知惡惡知美絜矩足以平情
punctuated: 詩人屢托物以致詠，其旨遠矣。蓋理微而物顯也，卽物而觀理，詩人其得諷諫之遺者哉！且夫由誠明以合德，公好惡而不偏，君人之理道盡矣。詩人欲遠有所明，而近有所托也，故其詞曰：「鶴鳴于九皐，聲聞于天。」夫鶴，物之善鳴者也。矢音于坎澤，而清響之上聞，地不得而限之；九皐雖邃也，而有聲斯應者，四達而不悖矣。「魚在于渚，或潜在淵。」夫魚，物之善藏者也。悠然于清淺，而淵泉之潜躍，跡不得而拘之；淵渚雖異也，而有動斯遊者，兩在而無方矣。園有樹檀，景與地皆可樂也，而維穀生焉。佳植而雜之以凡枒，造化其無全美乎？他山之石，形與質皆可憎也，而治玉資焉。良璞而藉之以磨礪，天地其無棄物乎？夫觀九皐之鳴鶴，而誠不容掩者可推矣；觀淵渚之潜魚，而理無定在者可察矣。檀園而其下維穀，則之其所愛而辟者非也；山石而用以攻玉，則之其所惡而辟者非也。誠則明，明則誠，聖脩可以立極；好知惡，惡知美，絜矩足以平情。
translation_en: The poet repeatedly uses physical things as metaphors to convey his songs, and his meaning is far-reaching. For principle is subtle while things are manifest; by observing principle through things, has the poet not grasped the legacy of indirect remonstrance! Moreover, proceeding from sincerity and intelligence to unite with virtue, and being impartial in one's likes and dislikes without bias—herein the principles and Way of ruling men are exhausted. Desiring to illuminate what is distant by relying on what is near at hand, the poet thus says in his verses: "The crane cries in the nine marshes, and its voice is heard in heaven." Now the crane is a creature skilled at crying out. It sends forth its note from the low-lying marshes, and as its clear resonance is heard above, the terrain cannot confine it; though the nine marshes are deep and remote, wherever there is a sound there is a response, reaching in all four directions without impediment. "The fish is by the islet, or plunges into the deep." Now the fish is a creature skilled at concealing itself. Unhurried in the clear shallows, yet plunging and leaping in the deep springs, its tracks cannot be constrained; though the deep pool and the shallow islet are different, that which swims whenever it moves is present in both places without fixed bounds. In the garden are planted sandalwood trees, where both scenery and site are delightful, yet paper-mulberries grow beneath them. Fine trees are mingled with ordinary branching shrubs—does the Creator then allow nothing to be wholly perfect? The stones of other hills are repulsive in both form and substance, yet the working of jade relies upon them. A fine uncarved jade depends on them for grinding and polishing—do heaven and earth then have no useless things? Thus, by observing the crane crying in the nine marshes, one may infer that sincerity cannot be concealed; by observing the fish plunging in the deep or by the islet, one may discern that principle has no fixed abode. When a sandalwood garden has paper-mulberries beneath it, then to be partial toward what one loves is wrong; when mountain stones are used to polish jade, then to be partial against what one dislikes is wrong. Given sincerity, there will be intelligence, and given intelligence, there will be sincerity—thus sagely self-cultivation can establish the supreme standard; loving while recognizing faults, and hating while recognizing beauties—thus the measuring square suffices to level the passions. …

title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
由是引而伸之觸類而長之則天下皆物皆道
也君人之理其殆庶幾乎吁詩人其善于陳善
納誨者矣嗟夫進諫之道未易言也使人君畏
吾之言不若使樂吾之言言之者無罪聽之者
易入其有裨于人國也大矣此作詩者之微旨
也孔子曰吾其從諷諫乎其有取于鶴鳴者歟
儀式刑文王之典日靖四方
經仁木
同考試官教諭李批全用本色語而言簡意足若親
===
見當時登歌之盛者允宜髙薦
考試官教授蔡批有結構有鋪叙佳士佳士
考試官教授朱批明暢中有典實取之
周王法典安民而享親者有道矣蓋文王之典
所以安民者也周王法而行之感格其有本哉
我將之詩及此意謂文王與昊天一道也後王
于文祖一氣也明堂啓而將享行庶幾天之我
右矣而感格于文王者寧不可必哉誠以監觀
四方求民之莫者天之心也怙冒西土視民如
punctuated:
由是引而伸之，觸類而長之，則天下皆物皆道也，君人之理其殆庶幾乎！吁！詩人其善于陳善納誨者矣。嗟夫！進諫之道，未易言也。使人君畏吾之言，不若使樂吾之言。言之者無罪，聽之者易入，其有裨于人國也大矣，此作詩者之微旨也。孔子曰：「吾其從諷諫乎！」其有取于《鶴鳴》者歟？

儀式刑文王之典，日靖四方。
經仁木
同考試官教諭李批：全用本色語，而言簡意足，若親見當時登歌之盛者，允宜髙薦。
考試官教授蔡批：有結構，有鋪叙，佳士，佳士！
考試官教授朱批：明暢中有典實，取之。

周王法典安民，而享親者有道矣。蓋文王之典，所以安民者也；周王法而行之，感格其有本哉！《我將》之詩及此，意謂：文王與昊天一道也，後王于文祖一氣也。明堂啓而將享行，庶幾天之我右矣，而感格于文王者，寧不可必哉？誠以監觀四方、求民之莫者，天之心也；怙冒西土、視民如…
translation_en:
… If from this one extends and expands the principle, reasoning by analogy to broaden one's understanding, then throughout the world every thing is an embodiment of the Way, and the principles of ruling men will nearly be attained! Ah, the poet was truly skilled at setting forth the good and offering admonition! Alas, the way of remonstrance is not easy to speak of. Making a ruler fear one's words is not as good as making him delight in one's words. When the speaker incurs no blame and the listener easily takes the message to heart, the benefit to the state is great indeed. This was the subtle intent of the author of the ode. Confucius said, "I would follow remonstrance by indirection!" Did he not find something to draw upon in the ode "Crane's Cry" (He ming)?

"We take as our pattern and model the statutes of King Wen, and daily bring peace to the four quarters."
Jing Renmu
Associate Examiner and County Director of Studies Li's comment: It entirely uses natural, unadorned language, yet the words are concise and the meaning is complete, as though he had personally witnessed the grand occasion of the sacrificial hymns being sung at that time. He truly deserves a high recommendation.
Examiner and Prefectural Director of Studies Cai's comment: Well-structured and well-elaborated. A fine scholar, a fine scholar!
Examiner and Prefectural Director of Studies Zhu's comment: Clear and fluent, yet grounded in classical substance. Selected.

When the Zhou king modeled himself on the statutes to bring peace to the people, he possessed the true way of presenting offerings to his royal ancestor. For the statutes of King Wen were the very means to bring peace to the people; when the Zhou king took them as his model and put them into practice, his ability to move and reach the ancestral spirit truly had a foundation! When the ode "We Present" (Wo jiang) touches upon this, the meaning is that King Wen and Vast Heaven share a single Way, and the later king and his Accomplished Ancestor share a single vital breath. When the Hall of Light is opened and the presentation of offerings is performed, one may hope that Heaven will assist us—and how could moving and reaching King Wen not be assured? Truly, to look down over the four quarters and seek the settlement of the people is the heart of Heaven; to shelter and cover the western lands and regard the people as if…

title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
傷者文王之心也文王往矣而孫謀之燕貽者
至備也是彝是訓奉以爲綏輯之猷文王遠矣
而典則之佑啓者至詳也不愆不忘率以爲惠
和之具以脩五禮以宣六樂載在周官固四方
所繹思者我其儀而刑之而駿惠之無斁日與
天下共守焉而自西徂東其用以咸寧矣以明
五刑以齊八政布在方策固四方所媚茲者我
其則而效之而緝煕之有常日與天下共循焉
而自南自北其賴以丕懷矣時有損益無改于
===
垂訓之初惟茲衆庶藉以保乂者特此典刑爾
敢作聰明以失求寧之意哉勢有會通一仍其
開創之始凡厥下民賴以康阜者惟此典章爾
敢任智術以失觀成之意哉夫法文之典所以
存文之心也存文之心所以體天之意也文王
旣右享矣而天不可知乎抑明堂大享周人尊
尊親親之禮也乃其登歌首以靖四方爲言者
何居蓋敬天勤民法祖君道之大端也燔柴越
紼黃琮蒼璧禮之文爾不以文而以實周人其
punctuated: 傷者，文王之心也。文王往矣，而孫謀之燕貽者至備也，是彝是訓，奉以爲綏輯之猷；文王遠矣，而典則之佑啓者至詳也，不愆不忘，率以爲惠和之具。以脩五禮，以宣六樂，載在《周官》，固四方所繹思者，我其儀而刑之，而駿惠之無斁，日與天下共守焉，而自西徂東，其用以咸寧矣。以明五刑，以齊八政，布在方策，固四方所媚茲者，我其則而效之，而緝煕之有常，日與天下共循焉，而自南自北，其賴以丕懷矣。時有損益，無改于垂訓之初，惟茲衆庶藉以保乂者，特此典刑爾，敢作聰明以失求寧之意哉？勢有會通，一仍其開創之始，凡厥下民賴以康阜者，惟此典章爾，敢任智術以失觀成之意哉？夫法文之典，所以存文之心也；存文之心，所以體天之意也。文王旣右享矣，而天不可知乎？抑明堂大享，周人尊尊親親之禮也，乃其登歌首以靖四方爲言者，何居？蓋敬天、勤民、法祖，君道之大端也；燔柴、越紼、黃琮、蒼璧，禮之文爾。不以文而以實，周人其
translation_en: …as if they were wounded—this was the heart of King Wen. King Wen has passed on, yet the plans he comfortably bequeathed to his descendants are utterly complete; taking them as constant norms and instructions, we uphold them as our plan for pacification and harmony. King Wen is distant now, yet the canons and rules with which he aided and enlightened us are utterly detailed; neither erring nor forgetting, we follow them as our means of bestowing kindness and concord. To cultivate the Five Rites and to proclaim the Six Musics, as recorded in the Offices of Zhou (Zhouguan), are indeed what the four quarters ever reflect upon; we take them as our model and pattern, grandly complying with them without weariness, daily observing them together with the realm, and from west to east all are thereby brought to complete peace. To clarify the Five Punishments and to regulate the Eight Administrations, as set forth on wooden tablets and bamboo slips, are indeed what the four quarters devotedly cherish; we take them as our rule and emulate them, continuing and brightening them with constancy, daily following them together with the realm, and from south to north all rely on them to be greatly comforted. Though times bring additions and subtractions, there is no altering the original instructions he handed down; that whereby the multitude are protected and governed is solely these exemplary statutes—how dare we contrive cleverness and so lose the intention of seeking peace? Though circumstances require adaptation, we wholly cleave to the beginning of his founding work; that upon which the common people rely for peace and abundance is solely these institutions—how dare we rely on artful calculations and so lose the intention of witnessing his completed achievement? Now, to model oneself on the canons of King Wen is the means to preserve the heart of King Wen; to preserve the heart of King Wen is the means to embody the will of Heaven. Since King Wen favors and accepts the sacrifice, can Heaven's mind not be known? Yet the great sacrifice in the Hall of Light (Mingtang) was the Zhou people's rite for honoring the venerable and showing affection to kin; why, then, does its hymn upon ascending the hall speak first of pacifying the four quarters? Because revering Heaven, laboring for the people, and modeling oneself on the ancestors are the great essentials of the ruler's way; burning firewood on the altar, ropes of boiled palm-bark, the yellow octagonal jade, and the azure jade disk are merely the outward forms of ritual. By relying not on outward form but on substance, the people of Zhou…

title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
合祭義矣彼棄德神吐祝史媿辭何足語此主
祀者辨之
春秋
夏齊侯衞侯胥命于蒲桓公三年公會晉
侯宋公衞侯曹伯齊世子光莒子邾子
滕子薛伯杞伯小邾子伐鄭會于蕭魚
襄公十有一年
徐尚實
同考試官教諭劉批此題傳意甚明作者多失之牽
===
合此篇詞理俱到深得聖人公世之志
考試官教授蔡批明暢典雅
考試官教授朱批理明詞順
春秋志公天下兩有取于以信相與者焉夫盟
非公世之志也蒲之命蕭魚之會皆相信而不
盟焉故春秋取之昔齊侯與衞以牧伯相推也
于是有蒲之命焉春秋善之者何蓋自司盟之
官設而詛祝之習成焉亦先王所不禁也彼二
國分党而伯圖肇興各愛其情者孰不曰必盟
punctuated:
合祭義矣。彼棄德神吐、祝史媿辭，何足語此？主祀者辨之。

《春秋》
「夏，齊侯、衞侯胥命于蒲。」桓公三年。「公會晉侯、宋公、衞侯、曹伯、齊世子光、莒子、邾子、滕子、薛伯、杞伯、小邾子伐鄭。會于蕭魚。」襄公十有一年。
徐尚實
同考試官教諭劉批：此題傳意甚明，作者多失之牽合。此篇詞理俱到，深得聖人公世之志。
考試官教授蔡批：明暢典雅。
考試官教授朱批：理明詞順。

《春秋》志公天下，兩有取于以信相與者焉。夫盟，非公世之志也。蒲之命、蕭魚之會，皆相信而不盟焉，故《春秋》取之。昔齊侯與衞以牧伯相推也，于是有蒲之命焉，《春秋》善之者何？蓋自司盟之官設，而詛祝之習成焉，亦先王所不禁也。彼二國分党而伯圖肇興，各愛其情者，孰不曰必盟
translation_en:
…accords with the principles of sacrifice! As for those who abandon virtue so that the spirits spurn their offerings, and whose invocators and scribes feel ashamed of their own words—how could they be worthy of discussing this? Let those who preside over sacrifices discern this.

Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu)
"In summer, the Marquis of Qi and the Marquis of Wei mutually commissioned each other at Pu" (3rd year of Duke Huan). "The Duke met the Marquis of Jin, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Cao, Heir Apparent Guang of Qi, the Viscount of Ju, the Viscount of Zhu, the Viscount of Teng, the Earl of Xue, the Earl of Qi, and the Viscount of Little Zhu to attack Zheng. They met at Xiaoyu" (11th year of Duke Xiang).
Xu Shangshi
Associate Examiner, Instructor Liu comments: The meaning of the commentary on this topic is very clear, yet writers often err by forcing the connection between the two passages. This essay achieves both eloquence and sound reasoning, deeply grasping the Sage's aspiration for a world shared in common.
Examiner, Professor Cai comments: Clear, fluent, and refined.
Examiner, Professor Zhu comments: The reasoning is clear and the phrasing smooth.

The Spring and Autumn Annals aspires to a world shared in common for all under Heaven, and thus in two instances approves of those who associated with one another in good faith. Now, swearing covenants was not the aspiration of an age of common spirit. In the mutual commission at Pu and the meeting at Xiaoyu, in both cases they trusted one another without swearing a covenant; therefore the Spring and Autumn Annals approved of them. In the past, when the Marquis of Qi and the Marquis of Wei deferred to each other as regional pastors and overlords, there took place the mutual commission at Pu. Why did the Spring and Autumn Annals commend it? Ever since the office of the Director of Covenants was established and the custom of oaths and imprecations took form, even the former kings did not prohibit it. When those two states divided into factions and hegemonic ambitions first arose, among those who each guarded their own interests, who would not say that one must first swear a covenant…

title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
而後約也今齊衞不事明神之質而善詞命以
相諭東州之伯自衞戴之北州之牧自齊推之
而不貳不參之心交如矣噫大道之公隱矣而
乃有以信相守如二君者不亦善乎故春秋特
起胥命之文見其事為近正也若晉悼服鄭因
行成相結也于是有蕭魚之會焉春秋美之者
何蓋自盟載之法立而約劑之俗興焉亦叔世
所不免也彼二境交款而誓言屢違以疑待鄭
者孰不曰必盟而後定也今晉悼無事載書之
===
尋而申禮文以相接斥堠納焉什其疑也侵掠
禁焉布其惠也而無詐無虞之心坦如矣噫傾
危之俗熾矣而乃有以信待人如晉侯者不亦
美乎故春秋特紀蕭魚之會見其績為可序也
夫善于蒲之命則戴伯者不必于盟也美蕭魚
之會則招攜者亦不必于盟也此聖人志公天
下彼參盟者又奚為哉雖然于蒲命而桃丘之
會中違衞雖得于齊而竟失于魯蕭魚會而伐
陳之師罔功晉雖得于鄭而竟失于陳是以君
punctuated: 而後約也？今齊、衞不事明神之質，而善詞命以相諭；東州之伯自衞戴之，北州之牧自齊推之，而不貳不參之心交如矣。噫！大道之公隱矣，而乃有以信相守如二君者，不亦善乎？故《春秋》特起「胥命」之文，見其事為近正也。若晉悼服鄭，因行成相結也，于是有蕭魚之會焉。《春秋》美之者何？蓋自盟載之法立，而約劑之俗興焉，亦叔世所不免也。彼二境交款而誓言屢違，以疑待鄭者，孰不曰必盟而後定也？今晉悼無事載書之尋，而申禮文以相接；斥堠納焉，什其疑也；侵掠禁焉，布其惠也；而無詐無虞之心坦如矣。噫！傾危之俗熾矣，而乃有以信待人如晉侯者，不亦美乎？故《春秋》特紀「蕭魚之會」，見其績為可序也。夫善于蒲之命，則戴伯者不必于盟也；美蕭魚之會，則招攜者亦不必于盟也。此聖人志公天下，彼參盟者又奚為哉？雖然，于蒲命而桃丘之會中違，衞雖得于齊而竟失于魯；蕭魚會而伐陳之師罔功，晉雖得于鄭而竟失于陳。是以君
translation_en:
… before entering into a pact? Now Qi and Wei did not resort to calling upon the bright spirits as witnesses, but instead instructed one another through cordial diplomatic exchanges. The hegemony over the eastern region was acknowledged by Wei, and the governorship of the northern region was deferred to by Qi; their minds, free of duplicity and suspicion, met in mutual harmony. Alas! Once the public spirit of the Great Way had faded from view, was it not admirable that there were still those like these two rulers who held fast to one another through good faith? Therefore, the Spring and Autumn Annals specially originated the phrasing "issued mutual declarations" (xuming) to show that this affair came close to what is right.

As for Duke Dao of Jin bringing Zheng to submission and binding their relations upon the conclusion of peace, this gave rise to the meeting at Xiaoyu. Why did the Spring and Autumn Annals praise it? Ever since the institution of written covenant texts was established and the custom of binding contracts arose, such practices had become unavoidable in an age of decline. When those two states exchanged terms of peace yet repeatedly violated their oaths, who among those treating Zheng with suspicion would not say that they must swear a covenant before matters could be settled? Now Duke Dao of Jin did not bother with renewing covenant documents, but instead received them by extending ritual courtesy. He withdrew his frontier scouts to dispel [?; 什, perhaps for 釋] their doubts, and prohibited plundering raids to spread his kindness; thus a mind free of deceit and mutual guardedness was openly displayed. Alas! Once treacherous customs had grown rampant, was it not praiseworthy that there was still someone like the Marquis of Jin who treated others with good faith? Therefore, the Spring and Autumn Annals specially recorded the "meeting at Xiaoyu" to show that his achievement was worthy of being recounted.

To approve of the declarations at Pu means that acknowledging a hegemon does not require a covenant; to praise the meeting at Xiaoyu means that winning over the estranged likewise does not require a covenant. In this way the Sage set his mind on a world shared in common—what need, then, was there for those who engaged in repeated covenant-making? Even so, after the declarations at Pu, the meeting at Taoqiu broke faith midway, so that although Wei gained the goodwill of Qi, it ultimately lost that of Lu; and after the meeting at Xiaoyu, the expedition against Chen achieved nothing, so that although Jin won over Zheng, it ultimately failed with Chen. For this reason, the gentleman…

title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
子猶惜齊衞爲五伯濫觴之始而晋悼爲善之
弗克終也良可慨夫
齊人來歸鄆讙龜陰田定公十年
曹學蘇
同考試官教諭劉批此題多以聖人不嫌序績立意
似非作經者之本義此作頗出常套取之
考試官教授蔡批詞嚴義正
考試官教授朱批深得經旨
春秋紀大國歸地之誠見聖人用禮之績焉夫
禮者服人之本也三田歸而齊人之服誠矣非
聖人以禮化强之績乎蓋自夾谷會而齊人謀
黎彌言而萊兵劫魯之危也岌岌矣孰意三田
之來歸乎維時孔子具官而從以禮相見神人
德義禮之大也則舉而詔之以啓其良干盟偪
好禮之悖也則因而折之以讋其志是以景公
以夷狄之俗責巳而改過是圖晏子以君子之
道畜君而謝過以質邪謀寢焉强敵爲之傾心
也侵疆歸焉土宇爲之光復也噫表東海者齊
punctuated:
子猶惜齊、衞爲五伯濫觴之始，而晋悼爲善之弗克終也，良可慨夫！

齊人來歸鄆、讙、龜陰田（定公十年）
曹學蘇
同考試官教諭劉批：此題多以聖人不嫌序績立意，似非作經者之本義。此作頗出常套，取之。
考試官教授蔡批：詞嚴義正。
考試官教授朱批：深得經旨。

《春秋》紀大國歸地之誠，見聖人用禮之績焉。夫禮者，服人之本也。三田歸而齊人之服誠矣，非聖人以禮化强之績乎？蓋自夾谷會而齊人謀，黎彌言而萊兵劫，魯之危也岌岌矣，孰意三田之來歸乎？維時孔子具官而從，以禮相見。神人德義，禮之大也，則舉而詔之，以啓其良；干盟偪好，禮之悖也，則因而折之，以讋其志。是以景公以夷狄之俗責巳，而改過是圖；晏子以君子之道畜君，而謝過以質。邪謀寢焉，强敵爲之傾心也；侵疆歸焉，土宇爲之光復也。噫！表東海者齊
translation_en:
… the gentleman still regrets that Qi and Wei marked the very beginning of the Five Hegemons, and that Duke Dao of Jin was unable to carry his goodness through to the end. How truly lamentable!

"The Men of Qi Came to Restore the Fields of Yun, Huan, and Guiyin" (Tenth Year of Duke Ding)
By Cao Xuesu 曹學蘇
Comment by Associate Examiner, Instructor Liu: On this topic, most candidates frame their essays around the idea that the Sage did not shy away from recording his own achievements, which seems contrary to the original intent of the author of the Classic. This composition rises well above conventional clichés; I select it.
Comment by Examiner, Professor Cai: The diction is rigorous and the reasoning upright.
Comment by Examiner, Professor Zhu: It deeply grasps the purport of the Classic.

The Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu) records the sincerity of a great state in restoring territory, thereby revealing the achievement of the Sage in employing ritual propriety. Now, ritual propriety is the fundamental means of winning people's submission. When the three tracts of fields were restored, the submission of the men of Qi was sincere indeed—was this not the achievement of the Sage in transforming the strong through ritual propriety? Ever since the meeting at Jiagu, where the men of Qi plotted, and Li Mi 黎彌 spoke out while the troops of Lai attempted coercion, the peril to Lu was acute indeed! Who would have expected the three tracts of fields to be restored? At that time, Confucius 孔子 attended with a full complement of officials, meeting them in accordance with ritual propriety. Virtue and righteousness toward spirits and men are the great principles of ritual propriety; thus he cited these to instruct them, thereby awakening their innate goodness. Violating a covenant and coercing a friendly state are contraventions of ritual propriety; thus he rebuked them on these grounds, thereby striking awe into their resolve. Consequently, Duke Jing reproached himself for following the customs of the Yi and Di barbarians and sought to reform his faults; Yanzi 晏子 nourished his ruler with the Way of the gentleman and apologized for their faults with concrete pledges. Nefarious plots were put to rest, as the powerful adversary was won over in heart; encroached territories were restored, as the state's domain was gloriously recovered. Ah! The state that stands preeminent by the Eastern Sea is Qi…

title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
也縱有睦魯之心則不執兵于邊鄙亦已幸矣
今隨感而化是聖人一言重於三軍也綏之斯
來動之斯和吾于是知禮之可以爲國矣爭伯
業者景也縱有歸地之心則待請而後與固其
常也今誠服而歸是聖人功化神於俄頃也期
月而可三年有成吾于是知聖人用世之績矣
然則斯歸也其諸異乎濟西讙闡之歸歟斯來
也其亦猶夫屈完之來歟春秋特書齊人來歸
鄆讙龜陰田所以見齊人心服而歸田孔子以
===
禮化强之績也聖人以天自處何自序之爲嫌
哉抑聞之晏嬰知矣而不知仲尼乃導其君以
謝過獨何歟蓋孔子之聖夫人能知之豈晏子
果不知乎其託爲詞說以沮之或亦歸女樂之
意歟雖然三田歸而齊景服義之美著矣其獻
替之功不可誣也故曰晏子以其君顯
禮記
天子布德行惠
李敷華
punctuated:
也，縱有睦魯之心，則不執兵于邊鄙，亦已幸矣；今隨感而化，是聖人一言重於三軍也。「綏之斯來，動之斯和」，吾于是知禮之可以爲國矣。爭伯業者，景也，縱有歸地之心，則待請而後與，固其常也；今誠服而歸，是聖人功化神於俄頃也。「期月而可，三年有成」，吾于是知聖人用世之績矣。然則斯歸也，其諸異乎濟西、讙、闡之歸歟？斯來也，其亦猶夫屈完之來歟？《春秋》特書「齊人來歸鄆、讙、龜陰田」，所以見齊人心服而歸田，孔子以禮化强之績也。聖人以天自處，何自序之爲嫌哉！抑聞之，晏嬰知矣，而不知仲尼，乃導其君以謝過，獨何歟？蓋孔子之聖，夫人能知之，豈晏子果不知乎？其託爲詞說以沮之，或亦歸女樂之意歟？雖然，三田歸而齊景服義之美著矣，其獻替之功不可誣也。故曰：晏子以其君顯。

《禮記》
天子布德行惠
李敷華
translation_en:
… Even if it had the intention of maintaining friendly relations with Lu, it would already have been fortunate had it simply refrained from taking up arms on the borders; yet now it was immediately moved and transformed, showing that a single word from the Sage carried more weight than three armies. "He comforted them and they came; he moved them and they were harmonious"—from this I know that ritual propriety can be used to govern a state. He who contended for hegemony was Duke Jing. Even if he had the intention of returning the lands, waiting for a request before granting them would certainly have been the norm; yet now he sincerely submitted and returned them, showing that the transformative achievement of the Sage worked miraculously in an instant. "In the course of a year it would be adequate, and in three years there would be results"—from this I know the achievements of the Sage when employed in the world.

This being so, is not this return of land different from the return of Jixi, Huan, and Chan? And is not this coming comparable to the coming of Qu Wan? The Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu) specially recorded that "The people of Qi came to return the fields of Yun, Huan, and Guiyin" in order to show that the people of Qi submitted in their hearts and returned the fields—the achievement of Confucius in transforming the strong through ritual propriety. The Sage conducted himself as Heaven does; why should he have any qualms about recording his own deeds!

Yet I have heard it said that Yan Ying was wise, though he did not truly know仲尼 (Confucius); why, then, did he alone guide his ruler to apologize for his fault? Indeed, the sagehood of Confucius was something anyone could recognize—how could Master Yan truly not have known it? When he fabricated pretexts and arguments to thwart him, was that perhaps out of the same motive as sending the female musicians? Even so, with the return of the three fields, the admirable virtue of Duke Jing of Qi in submitting to righteousness became manifest, and Yanzi's merit in offering counsel on what to adopt and what to reject cannot be denied. Therefore it is said: Master Yan became illustrious through his ruler.

Book of Rites (Liji)
"The Son of Heaven disseminates virtue and practices kindness."
Li Fuhua

title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭劉批以一仁字櫽括德惠而上下文意
聯綴含蓄是精於禮者宜冠本房
考試官教授蔡批發得人君順時行政意出
考試官教授朱批醞藉簡潔
王者因時之政在以仁育民焉蓋布德行惠仁
政也王者順時以施之其能奉若天道者乎記
者之意謂夫天之立君以爲民也君之行政以
憲天也彼季春之月生氣盛矣陽氣泄矣人君
及是時也當何如故天之大德曰生者也君則
===
體天之生氣而好生之心于斯洽焉天以陽生
萬物者也君則順天之陽氣而答陽之治于斯
出焉對時茂育而慈祥愷悌之念誕布于無方
與物皆春而博施濟眾之澤流行于莫禦天下
雖至廣也德敎之洋溢則胥一世以惠綏之蓋
恩不必自已出凡所以行令而致之民者是卽
大君之深恩矣其猶乾始不言而庶類均沐其
美利之休乎生民雖至眾也帝德之廣運則合
萬民而惠孚之蓋愛不必自已施凡所以宣上
punctuated:
同考試官教諭劉批：以一「仁」字櫽括「德」、「惠」，而上下文意聯綴含蓄，是精於《禮》者，宜冠本房。
考試官教授蔡批：發得人君順時行政意出。
考試官教授朱批：醞藉簡潔。
王者因時之政，在以仁育民焉。蓋布德行惠，仁政也。王者順時以施之，其能奉若天道者乎！記者之意，謂夫天之立君，以爲民也；君之行政，以憲天也。彼季春之月，生氣盛矣，陽氣泄矣，人君及是時也，當何如？故天之大德曰生者也，君則體天之生氣，而好生之心于斯洽焉；天以陽生萬物者也，君則順天之陽氣，而答陽之治于斯出焉。對時茂育，而慈祥愷悌之念，誕布于無方；與物皆春，而博施濟眾之澤，流行于莫禦。天下雖至廣也，德敎之洋溢，則胥一世以惠綏之。蓋恩不必自已出，凡所以行令而致之民者，是卽大君之深恩矣，其猶乾始不言，而庶類均沐其美利之休乎！生民雖至眾也，帝德之廣運，則合萬民而惠孚之。蓋愛不必自已施，凡所以宣上…
translation_en:
Associate Examiner and County Director of Studies Liu comments: Using the single word "humaneness" (ren) to encompass both "virtue" (de) and "kindness" (hui), while linking the meaning of the preceding and following context with subtle depth, shows someone well-versed in the Record of Rites (Liji) who deserves to be placed first in this examination ward.
Examiner and Prefectural Director of Studies Cai comments: It brings out the meaning of how a ruler carries out governance in accordance with the seasons.
Examiner and Prefectural Director of Studies Zhu comments: Cultivated, restrained, and concise.

The season-attuned governance of a true king lies in nurturing the people through humaneness. For spreading virtue and practicing kindness is humane governance. When a true king puts it into practice in accordance with the season, is he not reverently conforming to the Way of Heaven? The compiler of the Record meant to say that Heaven establishes a ruler for the sake of the people, and the ruler carries out governance by taking Heaven as his model. In that last month of spring, the vital energy of life is flourishing and the yang energy is surging forth; when the ruler reaches this season, how ought he to act? The great virtue of Heaven is called life; the ruler therefore embodies Heaven's vital energy, and his love for life is thereby diffused throughout. Heaven gives life to the myriad things through yang; the ruler therefore conforms to Heaven's yang energy, and governance that responds to the yang issues forth from this. Matching the season to nurture flourishing growth, his compassionate and fraternal thoughts are broadly spread without bound; sharing springtime with all things, the beneficence of廣泛 bestowal and relief to the multitudes flows forth irresistibly. Although the realm under Heaven is vast indeed, the overflowing of his virtuous instruction brings comfort and peace to the entire age through kindness. For grace need not issue from his own person alone; every measure by which orders are carried out and extended to the people is in fact the profound grace of the great sovereign. Is this not like the originating power of Heaven (Qian), which does not speak, yet the multitude of beings all bathe in the blessing of its fine benefit? Although the common people are numerous indeed, the far-reaching operation of the sovereign's virtue unites the myriad people and wins their trust through kindness. For love need not be bestowed by his own hand alone; every measure by which what is above is proclaimed…

title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
而達之下者莫非人君之至愛矣其猶天載無
聲而品彙均荷其竝育之化乎要之德與惠非
二也自仁之存諸心爲德自仁之及于物爲惠
德者惠之本惠行而德斯布矣王者憲天之政
固如此則其參天地而賛化育也有由然哉抑
論賑乏周困是爲德惠固矣而繼之以聘賢禮
士者何也蓋天生物不能自遂而付之君君繼
天不能獨理而寄之臣則任賢圖治尤帝王要
務而爲天下得人所以爲仁之大也堯之舉舜
===
舜之舉禹臯陶率是道爾不然春和議賑一代
賢主也而胡以未遑少之故曰堯舜之仁不徧
愛人急親賢也
禮者殊事合敬者也樂者異文合愛者也
蔣在廷
同考試官教諭劉批敬愛卽在事文之中特不因事文
而有殊異爾是作足以發之
考試官教授蔡批講合敬合愛處精透
考試官教授朱批詞氣雅暢
punctuated:
而達之下者，莫非人君之至愛矣，其猶天載無聲而品彙均荷其竝育之化乎！要之，德與惠非二也。自仁之存諸心爲德，自仁之及于物爲惠。德者，惠之本；惠行而德斯布矣。王者憲天之政固如此，則其參天地而賛化育也有由然哉！抑論賑乏周困，是爲德惠固矣，而繼之以聘賢禮士者，何也？蓋天生物不能自遂而付之君，君繼天不能獨理而寄之臣，則任賢圖治尤帝王要務，而爲天下得人，所以爲仁之大也。堯之舉舜、舜之舉禹、臯陶，率是道爾。不然，春和議賑，一代賢主也，而胡以未遑少之？故曰：「堯舜之仁，不徧愛人，急親賢也。」
禮者殊事，合敬者也；樂者異文，合愛者也。
蔣在廷
同考試官教諭劉批：敬愛卽在事文之中，特不因事文而有殊異爾。是作足以發之。
考試官教授蔡批：講合敬合愛處精透。
考試官教授朱批：詞氣雅暢。
translation_en:
…and convey it to those below is nothing less than the ruler's utmost love. Is this not like the workings of Heaven, which are soundless, yet all categories of beings equally receive its transformative power of nurturing them together? In sum, virtue and kindness are not two different things. From the standpoint of benevolence preserved in the mind, it is called virtue; from the standpoint of benevolence extended to creatures, it is called kindness. Virtue is the root of kindness; when kindness is practiced, virtue is thereby spread abroad. Since the governance of a true king in modeling himself on Heaven is assuredly like this, is there not a clear reason why he can form a triad with Heaven and Earth and assist in the transforming and nourishing processes of nature?

Yet if we consider relieving the needy and aiding the distressed, that is certainly virtue and kindness; why then does the text follow this with inviting the worthy and treating scholars with ritual courtesy? Because while Heaven gives birth to things, it cannot bring them to completion by itself and so entrusts them to the ruler; and while the ruler succeeds Heaven, he cannot govern alone and so delegates the task to his ministers. Thus, employing the worthy to plan for governance is especially the most vital duty of an emperor or king, and finding the right men for the empire is what constitutes the greatness of benevolence. Yao's elevation of Shun, and Shun's elevation of Yu and Gao Yao, all followed this principle. Otherwise, discussing famine relief in the mildness of spring is the mark of a worthy ruler of an era—why then would anyone belittle it as failing to attend to what is urgent? Therefore it is said: "The benevolence of Yao and Shun did not extend its love to all men alike; it held cleaving to the worthy as its urgent priority."

"Ritual has differing affairs, yet unites in reverence; music has differing patterns, yet unites in love." [Record of Rites (Liji), "Record of Music" (Yueji)]

Jiang Zaiting

Comment by Associate Examiner and County Director of Studies Liu: Reverence and love reside right within the affairs and patterns; they simply do not vary because the affairs and patterns differ. This essay is sufficient to bring out this meaning.

Comment by Examiner and Prefectural Director of Studies Cai: The explanation of uniting in reverence and uniting in love is precise and penetrating.

Comment by Examiner and Prefectural Director of Studies Zhu: The diction and tone are elegant and fluent.

title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
記者于禮樂而著其情之出於一焉甚矣禮樂
有自然之情也事文異而敬愛一是可見其情
之同矣此禮樂感化之由而記者著之意謂禮
樂之道合乎造化而感夫人心然人心之所由
感亦以禮樂本無異情爾自聖人防民偽以教
之中而禮制焉禮自外作有其事必有其敬者
也人皆以事殊則敬與之俱殊矣而不知至賾
不齊者其燦然之迹至敬無文者其秩然之原
經禮固惟三百矣而所以綱紀乎人道一中正
===
以為之質也曲禮固惟三千矣而所以品節乎
人情一恭順以為之制也善觀大禮者不求諸
事求諸敬斯其悉禮之精乎自聖人防民情以
教之和而樂作焉樂由中出有其文必有其愛
者也人皆以文異則愛與之俱異矣而不知治
其飾無非英華之發動其本悉出和順之休五
聲雖異其音而聲之所以成文為音者皆欣喜
之發越也六律雖異其數而律之所以得數有
常者皆歡愛之流行也善觀大樂者不求諸文
punctuated: 記者于禮樂，而著其情之出於一焉。甚矣，禮樂有自然之情也！事文異而敬愛一，是可見其情之同矣。此禮樂感化之由，而記者著之。意謂禮樂之道，合乎造化而感夫人心；然人心之所由感，亦以禮樂本無異情爾。自聖人防民偽以教之中，而禮制焉。禮自外作，有其事必有其敬者也。人皆以事殊則敬與之俱殊矣，而不知至賾不齊者，其燦然之迹；至敬無文者，其秩然之原。經禮固惟三百矣，而所以綱紀乎人道，一中正以為之質也；曲禮固惟三千矣，而所以品節乎人情，一恭順以為之制也。善觀大禮者，不求諸事，求諸敬，斯其悉禮之精乎！自聖人防民情以教之和，而樂作焉。樂由中出，有其文必有其愛者也。人皆以文異則愛與之俱異矣，而不知治其飾，無非英華之發；動其本，悉出和順之休。五聲雖異其音，而聲之所以成文為音者，皆欣喜之發越也；六律雖異其數，而律之所以得數有常者，皆歡愛之流行也。善觀大樂者，不求諸文，
translation_en: With regard to rites and music, the author of the Record of Music brings to light that their sentiments arise from unity. How profound it is that rites and music possess natural sentiments! Though their practices and patterns differ, their reverence and affection are each one, which reveals the sameness of their inner sentiments. This is the basis upon which rites and music move and transform people, and the author of the Record sets it forth. The meaning is that the way of rites and music accords with the creative transformations of nature and moves the human heart; yet the reason the human heart is moved is simply that rites and music originally harbor no divergent sentiments. Ever since the sages guarded against hypocrisy among the people to teach them centrality, rites were instituted. Rites operate from the outside, and wherever there is a ritual practice, there must be its corresponding reverence. People all assume that because the practices are distinct, the reverence must likewise be distinct, not realizing that what is most complex and uniform in appearance is merely its resplendent outward trace, whereas supreme reverence devoid of ornament is its orderly source. The canonical rites are indeed three hundred in number, yet that by which they regulate the way of humanity takes a single impartiality and uprightness as its substance; the detailed ceremonial usages are indeed three thousand in number, yet that by which they grade and moderate human feelings takes a single respectfulness and compliance as its rule. Those who are skilled at observing great rites do not seek them in the practices, but seek them in reverence—is this not to comprehend the essence of rites in full? Ever since the sages guarded against the unruly passions of the people to teach them harmony, music was created. Music issues from within, and wherever there is a musical pattern, there must be its corresponding affection. People all assume that because the patterns differ, the affection must likewise differ, not realizing that in cultivating its outward adornments, all is the blossoming of its brilliance, while in stirring its root, all springs from the excellence of harmony and accord. Although the five notes differ in their tones, that by which the notes form patterns to become music is in every case the efflorescence of joy; although the six pitch-pipes differ in their numerical proportions, that by which the pitch-pipes attain constant numbers is in every case the flowing forth of joyful affection. Those who are skilled at observing great music do not seek it in the patterns, …

title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
求諸愛斯其知樂之深乎吁禮樂有敬愛之情
如此情同而四海之內合敬同愛也固其所哉
雖然聖人之禮樂通天地而感四海固也君子
于此有致禮樂之功焉誠能以禮治躬以樂治
心則莊敬嚴威易直子諒愛敬備于一身而中
和之極建矣舉而措之天下民莫不承聽承順
參贊位育之化亦繇是致焉然則禮樂可斯須
去身哉圖治者盍審諸
第貳塲
===
論
爲聖本由學而成
徐尚實
同考試官教諭劉批以盡人合天立意得聖學要領
至發揮大禹作聖工夫無餘蘊高薦允宜
考試官教授蔡批議論根據造語高古佳士
考試官教授朱批典實莊重
論曰聖人不以其得之天者自恃而以其脩之
人者事天故其成聖也不以天而以人夫聖人
punctuated:
求諸愛，斯其知樂之深乎？吁！禮樂有敬愛之情如此，情同而四海之內合敬同愛也，固其所哉！雖然，聖人之禮樂通天地而感四海，固也，君子于此有致禮樂之功焉。誠能以禮治躬，以樂治心，則莊敬嚴威、易直子諒，愛敬備于一身，而中和之極建矣。舉而措之天下，民莫不承聽承順，參贊位育之化亦繇是致焉。然則禮樂可斯須去身哉？圖治者盍審諸！
第貳塲
論
爲聖本由學而成
徐尚實
同考試官教諭劉批：以盡人合天立意，得聖學要領；至發揮大禹作聖工夫，無餘蘊，高薦允宜。
考試官教授蔡批：議論根據，造語高古，佳士。
考試官教授朱批：典實莊重。
論曰：聖人不以其得之天者自恃，而以其脩之人者事天，故其成聖也，不以天而以人。夫聖人
translation_en:
… but seeks it in affection—does such a person not understand the depth of music? Ah! Since rites and music embody the feelings of reverence and affection in this way, and since these feelings are shared, it is only natural that within the four seas all unite in reverence and join in affection! Even so, while it is true that the rites and music of the sages communicate with heaven and earth and move all within the four seas, the noble man has the work of bringing rites and music to realization in this regard. If he can truly govern his person with rites and govern his mind with music, then solemn reverence and stern majesty, along with easy directness and filial sincerity—affection and reverence—will be complete within his own person, and the ultimate standard of equilibrium and harmony will be established. When he takes this and applies it to the world, none among the people will fail to heed and obey, and the transforming work of participating in the cosmic triad and bringing all things to their proper place and nourishment will also be achieved through this. This being so, can rites and music leave one's person even for a moment? Why do those who plan for governance not examine this closely?

"Becoming a Sage Basically Comes About Through Learning"

Xu Shangshi 徐尚實
