title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
者天之所生以寄斯道之統者也生之也不偶
故其畀之也獨厚畀之也獨厚故其望之也獨
隆使聖人自恃其厚於天也而不思學以成之
則天下萬事萬物之理寧能會之於至精至一
以無失其中而當天之意乎是故其憂勤惕勵
之心不能自釋而盡人合天之學不容已也張
敬夫曰禹之為聖本由學而成噫其知禹者乎
其善言天人之際者乎且夫學之名何始乎伏
羲神農黃帝各以其道而為君仰觀俯察制器
===
尚象天下稱聖焉不聞其所謂學也孔子刪書
斷自唐虞而下其言堯舜之聖一則曰放勳格
天一則曰重華協帝不聞其所謂學也是數聖
人者皆繼天立極之君也豈其得之天者至厚
而無俟於學與抑禹之聖不及三皇二帝而必
待於學與曰是不然洪荒之世吾無得而論矣
堯之克明非學以明之乎舜之大智非學以知
之乎是故都俞吁咈皆學之事百揆岳牧皆學
之人總章衢室皆學之地耄老倦勤皆學之時
punctuated: 者，天之所生以寄斯道之統者也。生之也不偶，故其畀之也獨厚；畀之也獨厚，故其望之也獨隆。使聖人自恃其厚於天也，而不思學以成之，則天下萬事萬物之理，寧能會之於至精至一，以無失其中而當天之意乎？是故其憂勤惕勵之心不能自釋，而盡人合天之學不容已也。張敬夫曰：「禹之為聖，本由學而成。」噫！其知禹者乎？其善言天人之際者乎？且夫學之名何始乎？伏羲、神農、黃帝，各以其道而為君，仰觀俯察，制器尚象，天下稱聖焉，不聞其所謂學也。孔子刪《書》，斷自唐虞而下，其言堯、舜之聖，一則曰「放勳格天」，一則曰「重華協帝」，不聞其所謂學也。是數聖人者，皆繼天立極之君也，豈其得之天者至厚而無俟於學與？抑禹之聖不及三皇、二帝而必待於學與？曰：是不然。洪荒之世，吾無得而論矣。堯之克明，非學以明之乎？舜之大智，非學以知之乎？是故都俞吁咈，皆學之事；百揆岳牧，皆學之人；總章衢室，皆學之地；耄老倦勤，皆學之時。
translation_en:
… is one whom Heaven brings forth in order to entrust with the transmission of this Way. Since bringing him forth is no mere accident, what Heaven endows in him is uniquely generous; and since what Heaven endows in him is uniquely generous, what it expects of him is uniquely high. Suppose the sage were to rely presumptuously upon the generosity he received from Heaven and give no thought to bringing it to completion through learning—how then could he gather the principles of the myriad affairs and myriad things of the world into the utmost refinement and utmost unity, so as not to lose hold of the Mean and thereby fulfill the will of Heaven? For this reason, his anxious diligence and vigilant self-exertion cannot be set aside, and the learning by which he fully realizes the human to unite with Heaven cannot cease. Zhang Jingfu 張敬夫 (Zhang Shi 張栻) said: “Yu’s becoming a sage was fundamentally achieved through learning.” Ah! Did he not truly understand Yu? Was he not skilled at speaking of the relation between Heaven and humanity?

Moreover, when did the word “learning” first arise? Fuxi 伏羲, Shennong 神農, and the Yellow Emperor (Huangdi 黃帝) each ruled as sovereign by means of his own Way. Looking up to contemplate and looking down to examine, they fashioned implements and revered symbolic images; the world acclaimed them as sages, yet nothing was heard of what is called “learning.” When Confucius (Kongzi 孔子) edited the Book of Documents (Shu 書), he began from Tang 唐 and Yu 虞 onward. In speaking of the sageliness of Yao 堯 and Shun 舜, of the one it says, “Of vast merit, reaching to Heaven,” and of the other, “Of twofold brilliance, harmonizing with the前の sovereign,” yet nothing is heard of what is called “learning.” These several sages were all sovereigns who succeeded Heaven and established the supreme standard. Was it that what they received from Heaven was so supremely generous that they had no need of learning? Or was it that Yu’s sageliness fell short of the Three Sovereigns and Two Emperors, so that he had to depend upon learning? I say: It is not so. Of the era of primordial antiquity, we have no way to speak. As for Yao’s ability to make bright his virtue, was it not through learning that he made it bright? As for Shun’s great wisdom, was it not through learning that he came to know? Therefore, the exclamations of approval and dissent in court counsels (“du, yu, xu, fu” 都俞吁咈) were all matters of learning; the General Regulator (baikui 百揆), the Four Peaks (yue 岳), and the Twelve Pastors (mu 牧) were all companions in learning; the Hall of Bright Administration (zongzhang 總章) and the Chamber of the Crossroads (qushi 衢室) were all places of learning; even advanced age and weariness with toil were all times of learning. …

title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
堯與舜焉不學特無學之名爾無學之名而有
學之實此聖人之心學均之爲善事其天也何
獨於禹而疑之禹得統於舜者也堯之命舜曰
允執厥中中之一言帝王心學之傳盡之矣舜
之命禹則益之以三言蓋至於禹之時沕穆之
氣恐其漸漓也故人心不得不戒其危道心不
得不戒其微非精非一何以守中禹之聞斯言
也曰曆數在我矣民心屬我矣天之厚而望我
何以副之於是有所默然長思焉有所惕然深
===
省焉有所汲汲不能自已焉不以有天下爲樂
而以任天下是懼民生未遂何以上追夫標枝
野鹿之世民心不古何以遠紹夫協和於變之
風九載弗績幹蠱蓋愆何以近傚乎克諧蒸乂
之孝危者如何而安微者如何而著精者何以
不雜一者何以不二任之重故憂之深憂之深
故學之篤是故一饋十起一沐三握無時非學
也克勤于邦克儉于家無地非學也昌言拜益
底績俞臯無人非學也飲食菲之宮室卑之衣
punctuated: 堯與舜焉不學？特無學之名爾。無學之名而有學之實，此聖人之心學，均之爲善事其天也，何獨於禹而疑之？禹，得統於舜者也。堯之命舜曰：「允執厥中。」中之一言，帝王心學之傳盡之矣。舜之命禹，則益之以三言，蓋至於禹之時，沕穆之氣恐其漸漓也，故人心不得不戒其危，道心不得不戒其微，非精非一，何以守中？禹之聞斯言也，曰：「曆數在我矣，民心屬我矣，天之厚而望我，何以副之？」於是有所默然長思焉，有所惕然深省焉，有所汲汲不能自已焉。不以有天下爲樂，而以任天下是懼：民生未遂，何以上追夫標枝野鹿之世？民心不古，何以遠紹夫協和於變之風？九載弗績，幹蠱蓋愆，何以近傚乎克諧蒸乂之孝？危者如何而安？微者如何而著？精者何以不雜？一者何以不二？任之重故憂之深，憂之深故學之篤。是故一饋十起、一沐三握，無時非學也；克勤于邦、克儉于家，無地非學也；昌言拜益、底績俞臯，無人非學也；飲食菲之、宮室卑之、衣
translation_en: How could Yao and Shun not have engaged in learning? It is simply that they did not have the name of "learning." Lacking the name of learning yet possessing its reality—this was the learning of the mind-and-heart of the sages, through which all alike served their Heaven well. Why, then, have doubts solely in the case of Yu? Yu was the one who received the succession from Shun. When Yao charged Shun, he said, "Sincerely hold fast the Mean." With that single word, "Mean," the transmission of the emperors' and kings' learning of the mind-and-heart was completely expressed. When Shun charged Yu, however, he added three phrases to it. This was because by the time of Yu, it was feared that the profound and pure ethos might gradually thin out; therefore, with the human mind one could not but guard against its precariousness, and with the moral mind one could not but guard against its subtlety. Without refinement and without singleness, how could one preserve the Mean? When Yu heard these words, he said to himself: "The heavenly succession now rests with me, and the hearts of the people are attached to me. Heaven has been generous to me and places its hopes in me—how shall I live up to them?" Thereupon he fell into silent, prolonged reflection; he examined himself deeply with anxious vigilance; and he strove tirelessly without being able to stop himself. He did not regard possessing the world as a joy, but rather took bearing the burden of the world as cause for fear: If the people's livelihood is not yet fulfilled, how can I match the ancient age when rulers were like high branches and the people like wild deer? If the people's hearts lack ancient simplicity, how can I carry on the distant customs of harmony and universal transformation? After nine years without success in the flood control, in rectifying my father's failure and covering his fault, how can I emulate the recent filial piety that brought harmony and progressive order? How can what is precarious be made secure? How can what is subtle be made manifest? How can what is refined be kept free of admixture? How can what is single be kept undivided? Because his responsibility was heavy, his anxiety was deep; because his anxiety was deep, his learning was earnest. Therefore, rising ten times during a single meal and grasping his hair three times during a single wash—there was no time that was not learning. Being diligent for the state and frugal in his household—there was no place that was not learning. Bowing to Yi for his splendid words and expressing approval to Gao Yao for his accomplishments—there was no person from whom he did not learn. Making his food and drink frugal, keeping his palaces and chambers low, and making his clothing…

title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
服惡之無事非學也猶未也克艱之謨幾康之
迪其祗承于帝者皆學也鼓鐘之設磬鐸之陳
其下詢于人者皆學也九功之敘九敘之歌其
錫之天下者皆學也典則之貽疇範之列其垂
之後世者皆學也夫以尊居九重富有四海之
身而勞心焦思胼手胝足不自暇逸以學如此
豈聖人誠有所不足哉不以天之厚我者是恃
而以天之望我者是憂耳聰目明天之厚我也
而必以視聽明威之學廣之聲律身度天之厚
===
我也而必以準繩規矩之學約之天無外聖人
之心亦無外天不息聖人之心亦不息心不息
故學不已學不已故聖必成九州攸同四隩旣
宅人皆曰禹其輔相天地之聖人乎而不知其
成允成功之學成之也六府孔脩三事允治人
皆曰禹其左右生民之聖人乎而不知其祗台
德先之學成之也危者安而微者著精者不雜
而一者不二以紹執中之傳人皆曰禹其繼往
開來之聖人乎而不知其寸陰必惜思曰孜孜
punctuated: 服惡之，無事非學也。猶未也，克艱之謨、幾康之迪，其祗承于帝者，皆學也；鼓鐘之設、磬鐸之陳，其下詢于人者，皆學也；九功之敘、九敘之歌，其錫之天下者，皆學也；典則之貽、疇範之列，其垂之後世者，皆學也。夫以尊居九重、富有四海之身，而勞心焦思、胼手胝足，不自暇逸以學如此，豈聖人誠有所不足哉？不以天之厚我者是恃，而以天之望我者是憂。耳聰目明，天之厚我也，而必以視聽明威之學廣之；聲律身度，天之厚我也，而必以準繩規矩之學約之。天無外，聖人之心亦無外；天不息，聖人之心亦不息。心不息，故學不已；學不已，故聖必成。九州攸同，四隩旣宅，人皆曰：「禹其輔相天地之聖人乎！」而不知其成允成功之學成之也。六府孔脩，三事允治，人皆曰：「禹其左右生民之聖人乎！」而不知其祗台德先之學成之也。危者安而微者著，精者不雜而一者不二，以紹執中之傳，人皆曰：「禹其繼往開來之聖人乎！」而不知其寸陰必惜、思曰孜孜…
translation_en: …and making his clothing coarse—there was no affair that was not learning. Nor was that all: the counsels on overcoming difficulties and the guidance on attending to the subtle and securing peace, by which he reverently succeeded to the Sovereign, were all learning; the setting up of drums and bells and the displaying of stone chimes and wooden-clappered bells, by which he inquired of men below, were all learning; the ordering of the nine achievements and the singing of the nine ordenings, which he bestowed upon the world, were all learning; the bequeathing of canons and rules and the arrangement of the categories of the Great Plan, which he handed down to later generations, were all learning. Now, with a person of such exalted station as to dwell in the ninefold palace and of such wealth as to possess all within the四海 (Four Seas), yet to toil in heart and racked in thought, with calloused hands and feet, allowing himself no leisure or ease in order to learn like this—was it that the sage truly had some deficiency? Rather, he did not rely upon that with which Heaven had generously endowed him, but felt anxiety over that which Heaven expected of him. Acute hearing and clear sight were Heaven's generous endowment to him, yet he必ず broadened them through the learning of seeing, hearing, brightness, and awe; a voice that was a standard pitch and a person that was a measure were Heaven's generous endowment to him, yet he necessarily restrained them through the learning of the plumb-line, cord, compass, and square. Heaven has no bounds, and the heart of the sage likewise has no bounds; Heaven never ceases, and the heart of the sage likewise never ceases. Because his heart never ceased, his learning never ended; because his learning never ended, his sagehood was necessarily brought to completion. When the Nine Provinces were harmonized and the four quarters made habitable, everyone said, "Was not Yu a sage who assisted and complemented Heaven and Earth!"—yet they did not know that it was accomplished by his learning of fulfilling hisices in good faith and bringing work to completion. When the six treasuries of nature were greatly ordered and the three affairs of governance were truly regulated, everyone said, "Was not Yu a sage who aided and sustained the living people!"—yet they did not know that it was accomplished by his learning of reverently putting his own virtue first. When what was precarious was made secure and what was subtle was made manifest, when what was refined was kept unmixed and what was single was kept undivided, so as to carry on the transmission of holding fast to the Mean, everyone said, "Was not Yu a sage who continued the past and opened up the future!"—yet they did not know that it was [accomplished by his learning of] cherishing every inch of shadow on the sundial and thinking tirelessly…

title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
之學成之也雖其得之天者不同而其脩之人
者實刀譬之百尺之臺雖由丘陵而增築之功
不可誣也九仞之淵雖由川澤而疏浚之勞不
可誣也孰謂禹之為聖而不由學以成之乎噫
殷湯聖也而制事制心文武聖也而緝熈敬勝
周公聖也而繼日待旦孔子聖也而忘食忘憂
千聖授受共此學也而又何疑於禹也雖然學
一也而後之學者何其多岐矣乎卑之以功利
左之以刑名陷溺之以詞章訓詁而精一執中
===
之旨晦矣彼功利刑名無論也而詞章訓詁亦
豈希聖者所事哉朱子曰帝王之學與韋布不
同誠以帝王之所重者此心此中之外無餘事
也故經傳雖博取其足以裨益身心而已矣史
籍雖繁取其足以監戒興亡而已矣不此之務
而誇多涉獵樂此不疲於心學乎何有也此又
有志於聖者所當知
表
擬以薛瑄為禮部侍郎兼翰林院學士直
punctuated:
之學成之也。雖其得之天者不同，而其脩之人者實刀。譬之百尺之臺，雖由丘陵，而增築之功不可誣也；九仞之淵，雖由川澤，而疏浚之勞不可誣也。孰謂禹之為聖，而不由學以成之乎？噫！殷湯聖也，而制事制心；文武聖也，而緝熈敬勝；周公聖也，而繼日待旦；孔子聖也，而忘食忘憂。千聖授受，共此學也，而又何疑於禹也？雖然，學一也，而後之學者何其多岐矣乎！卑之以功利，左之以刑名，陷溺之以詞章訓詁，而精一執中之旨晦矣。彼功利、刑名無論也，而詞章、訓詁亦豈希聖者所事哉？朱子曰：「帝王之學，與韋布不同。」誠以帝王之所重者，此心、此中之外無餘事也。故經傳雖博，取其足以裨益身心而已矣；史籍雖繁，取其足以監戒興亡而已矣。不此之務，而誇多涉獵，樂此不疲，於心學乎何有也？此又有志於聖者所當知。
表
擬以薛瑄為禮部侍郎兼翰林院學士直
translation_en:
…it was brought to completion by his learning of [cherishing every inch of shadow and thinking tirelessly day by day]. Although what he received from Heaven was extraordinary, what he cultivated through human effort was truly strenuous [reading 力 for 刀]. Compare it to a hundred-foot terrace: though built upon a natural hill, the merit of adding to and constructing it cannot be denied; or an abyss of nine ren: though formed from rivers and marshes, the labor of dredging and deepening it cannot be denied. Who then could say that Yu's becoming a sage was not brought to completion through learning?

Ah! Tang of Yin was a sage, yet he regulated affairs through ritual and regulated his mind through righteousness; King Wen and King Wu were sages, yet they practiced continuous bright敬 (reverence) and let reverence triumph over indolence; the Duke of Zhou was a sage, yet he joined night to day and sat waiting for the dawn; Confucius was a sage, yet in his eagerness he forgot to eat and in his joy forgot his sorrows. A thousand sages handed down and received this same learning—how then can there be any doubt regarding Yu?

Even so, learning is one, yet how numerous are the diverging paths of later learners! They debase it with utilitarianism and profit, lead it astray with legalism and penalties [xingming], and drown it in belles-lettres and philological exegesis, so that the essential meaning of "refinement and singleness" and "holding fast to the Mean" is obscured. Utilitarianism and legalism need not even be discussed, yet how could belles-lettres and philological exegesis be the proper pursuit of one who aspires to sagehood? Master Zhu [Zhu Xi 朱熹] said: "The learning of emperors and kings is different from that of commoners in coarse cloth." Truly, this is because what emperors and kings value lies solely in this mind and this Mean, beyond which there is no other business. Therefore, although the Classics and commentaries are vast, one takes from them only what suffices to benefit one's person and mind; although historical records are voluminous, one takes from them only what suffices to serve as a mirror and warning of rise and fall. If one does not attend to this, but instead boasts of wide and superficial reading, delighting in it tirelessly, what does that have to do with the learning of the mind [xinxue]? This, too, is what those who set their will on sagehood ought to know.

同考試官教諭李批：詞藻典麗，才思悠長。陳謝中不忘獻替，非徒四六之工巳也。宜錄以式。
考試官教授蔡批：文非雕繪，語極渾成。讀之想見忠愛。佳士，佳士！
考試官教授朱批：駢麗典則。
天順元年某月某日，大理寺卿臣薛瑄伏蒙聖恩，以臣為禮部侍郎兼翰林院學士，文淵閣辦事，謹奉表稱謝者。秩佐寅清，備論思而聯紫禁；任隆調燮，叅帷幄而覲丹霄。殊恩下逮于儒臣，特簡首勤于
translation_en:
… the Hall of Literary Profundity (Wenyuan ge), a Memorial of Thanks [First year of the Tianshun era (1457)].

Mo Yugao 莫與高

Comment by Associate Examiner and Instructor Li: "The diction is classical and elegant, the talent and thought far-reaching. Amidst expressing gratitude, he does not forget to offer counsel on what to promote and what to discard; this is not merely skill in four-six parallel prose. It should be recorded as a model."

Comment by Examiner and Prefectural Director of Studies Cai: "The writing is not artificially ornate, and the language is utterly natural and complete. Reading it makes one envision his loyalty and devotion. A fine scholar, a fine scholar!"

Comment by Examiner and Prefectural Director of Studies Zhu: "Symmetric, elegant, and classical in form."

On a certain day of a certain month in the first year of the Tianshun era (1457), Your Servant Xue Xuan 薛瑄, Chief Minister of the Court of Judicial Review, having humbly received Imperial Grace appointing Your Servant as Vice Minister of Rites concurrent with Hanlin Academician, to handle affairs in the Hall of Literary Profundity, respectfully presents this memorial to express gratitude:

My rank assists in the reverent and pure administration of rites, providing deliberation and counsel while joined to the Purple Forbidden City; my charge is elevated to harmonizing and blending governance, participating in the inner tent of strategy and having audience beneath the Cinnabar Sky. Special grace reaches down to a Confucian minister; exceptional selection first occupies the diligent attention of…

title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
明聖翰史當清華之選春卿兼
密勿之司彌切冰兢深慙蚊負臣瑄誠惶誠
恐稽首頓首竊惟昊帝載分龍紀名五官
而順四時軒皇肇啟鴻圖奠三辰而任六
相虞廷典禮咨伯夷惟秩宗周室建官姬
公時兼太宰春曹居貳卿之亞隋代以侍
郎名銜學士擅兩制之榮唐宗以翰林待
草坐而論道股肱心膂以相資入則宣猷
舟楫鹽梅之是賴十載掌絲綸于紫殿寵
===
深雉尾之陪廿年握樞軸于黃扉恩厚龍
津之讌自兩漢而下咸崇敷瓊摛藻之英
由三代以還皆重論道經邦之彥故事雖
沿于往昔得人莫盛於
明時
高祖開基朱宋陶吳惟平文章而詳
奏啟
文皇膺曆黃胡金解始參軍國而預機謨如灒
如綸如時勉之賢名高一代惟溥惟榮惟
punctuated: 明聖。翰史當清華之選，春卿兼密勿之司，彌切冰兢，深慙蚊負。臣瑄誠惶誠恐，稽首頓首。竊惟昊帝載分龍紀，名五官而順四時；軒皇肇啟鴻圖，奠三辰而任六相。虞廷典禮，咨伯夷惟秩宗；周室建官，姬公時兼太宰。春曹居貳卿之亞，隋代以侍郎名銜；學士擅兩制之榮，唐宗以翰林待草。坐而論道，股肱心膂以相資；入則宣猷，舟楫鹽梅之是賴。十載掌絲綸于紫殿，寵深雉尾之陪；廿年握樞軸于黃扉，恩厚龍津之讌。自兩漢而下，咸崇敷瓊摛藻之英；由三代以還，皆重論道經邦之彥。故事雖沿于往昔，得人莫盛於明時。高祖開基，朱、宋、陶、吳，惟平文章而詳奏啟；文皇膺曆，黃、胡、金、解，始參軍國而預機謨。如灒、如綸、如時勉之賢，名高一代；惟溥、惟榮、惟
translation_en:
…your enlightened sageliness. As a Hanlin Academician I hold a post of pure distinction, and as an official of the Ministry of Rites I concurrently share in the duties of confidential deliberation; all the more deeply do I tremble as if treading on thin ice, profoundly ashamed that I am like a mosquito trying to bear a mountain on its back. Your servant [Xue] Xuan 薛瑄 is truly fearful and truly apprehensive, bowing his head to the ground again and again.

I humbly reflect that when the Emperor Taihao established the Dragon-ordered offices, he named the Five Officials to accord with the four seasons; when the Yellow Emperor first opened the great enterprise, he fixed the three luminaries and employed the six chief councillors. When the court of Yu-Shun instituted the rites, it consulted Boyi 伯夷 to serve as Arranger of Ancestral Temple Dignities (秩宗); when the house of Zhou established its offices, the Duke of Zhou (Jigong 姬公) at times concurrently served as Grand Counselor (太宰). In the Ministry of Rites, ranking next below the Minister, the Sui dynasty instituted the title of Vice Minister (侍郎); while the Academician (學士) enjoyed the glory of drafting both inner and outer edicts, as the Tang sovereigns relied on the Hanlin Academy to await the drafting of decrees. Sitting to discuss the Way, sovereign and minister support one another like limbs and heart and backbone; entering the court to set forth counsels, the ruler relies on them as oars and boats for crossing a river or salt and plum for seasoning. For ten years taking charge of imperial decrees in the Purple Hall, one enjoys deep favor attending beside the pheasant-tail fans; for twenty years holding the pivot of state in the Yellow Gate, one receives generous grace at the banquets by the Dragon Ford. From the Two Han dynasties downward, all have esteemed heroes who spread forth jade-like splendor and literary brilliance; from the Three Dynasties onward, all have valued worthies who discourse on the Way and order the state. Although the precedents have been handed down from antiquity, the winning of talented men has never been more flourishing than in our reigning era. When the Exalted Ancestor (Gaozu 高祖, the Hongwu Emperor) founded the dynasty, Zhu [Sheng] 朱升, Song [Lian] 宋濂, Tao [An] 陶安, and Wu [Chen] 吳沉 only weighed literary compositions and reviewed memorials and communications; when the Cultured Emperor (Wenhuang 文皇, the Yongle Emperor) received the mandate, Huang [Huai] 黃淮, Hu [Guang] 胡廣, Jin [Youzi] 金幼孜, and Xie [Jin] 解縉 first participated in military and state affairs and took part in confidential counsels. Worthies such as [Miao] Can 苗衷 [?], [Gao] Gu 高穀 [?], and [Li] Shimian 李時勉 held renown lofty throughout their generation; while [Yang] Pu 楊溥, [Yang] Rong 楊榮, and [Yang]…

title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
士奇之業望著
三朝蓋惇典代言必才行擅長者方稱其選而
調元補袞非謀斷兼資者莫充其員如臣
戇愚驟蒙顯錄一朝殊遘千載榮施恭惟
皇帝陛下
玄德神凝
英資天授
道符出震繫四夷萬國之懽心
位應明離纘
===
二祖
一宗之丕緒
留神問學
孝養久達于
重闈
注念老成敬恭克謹于羣祀飭風憲以開薦
舉敦節儉而謹灾祥省役蠲租惓惓民間
之疾苦進賢去慝孜孜吏治之勸懲屬當
帝命之維新特軫
punctuated: 士奇之業，望著三朝。蓋惇典代言，必才行擅長者方稱其選；而調元補袞，非謀斷兼資者莫充其員。如臣戇愚，驟蒙顯錄，一朝殊遘，千載榮施。恭惟皇帝陛下，玄德神凝，英資天授。道符出震，繫四夷萬國之懽心；位應明離，纘二祖一宗之丕緒。留神問學，孝養久達于重闈；注念老成，敬恭克謹于羣祀。飭風憲以開薦舉，敦節儉而謹灾祥。省役蠲租，惓惓民間之疾苦；進賢去慝，孜孜吏治之勸懲。屬當帝命之維新，特軫
translation_en:
… and Yang Shiqi 楊士奇, their achievements and prestige were renowned across three reigns. Indeed, to uphold the canons and draft imperial pronouncements, only those who excel in both talent and conduct are worthy of selection; and to harmonize the primal forces and mend the imperial robes of state, none who lack both strategic counsel and decisive judgment can fill the post. Someone as simple and foolish as your servant has suddenly received such illustrious appointment—an extraordinary encounter in a single morning, a glorious bestowal for a thousand years.

Reverently I reflect that Your Imperial Majesty possesses profound virtue spiritually concentrated and heroic endowments bestowed by Heaven. Your Way matches the emergence of the Zhen 震 trigram, binding the joyful hearts of the four borderlands and myriad states; Your position corresponds to the brilliance of the Li 離 trigram, continuing the grand patrimony of the Two Progenitors (Erzu 二祖) and One Ancestor (Yizong 一宗). You devote your mind to inquiry and learning, while your filial nurture has long reached the double宫 quarters of the empresses dowager; you fix your thoughts on seasoned elders, while your reverence and respect are faithfully maintained across all state sacrifices. You rectify the disciplinary and censorial institutions to open the path of recommendation, and cultivate frugality while heeding portents and prodigies. Reducing corvée labor and remitting taxes, you are earnestly concerned with the sufferings of the common people; advancing the worthy and removing the wicked, you are tireless in encouraging and reprimanding the administration of officials. Just as the imperial mandate is newly inaugurated, you show special solicitude for …

title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
宸扆之求舊惟爰立賢于夢卜乃
眷倚下及芻蕘晉貳南宮併兼藝苑瞻依
北斗侍直
文淵蘭省綴次于文昌已高曳履薇垣映躔
于
華蓋尚忝覆甌篚羽
彤墀班隨八座凝輝
黼扆位接三台俯媿迂儒濫承
異數伏念臣瑄河汾末品志學欲宗洙泗之
===
源澤絳庸流傳心切求關閩之派飭躬礪
節以明道不在多言復性教人謂工文無
裨實用夙承師訓長竊賢科攬轡湖湘未
能肅官常而懲貪墨校文齊魯亦頗正士
習而抑浮夸繼以虛名謬蒙拔擢旋因法
守幸遂投閒
優召偶及蓬門孤踪再登棘寺詎意
上天開泰
明主憐才既拜兼官復司直賛臣敢不講明心
punctuated: 宸扆之求舊。惟爰立賢于夢卜，乃眷倚下及芻蕘。晉貳南宮，併兼藝苑；瞻依北斗，侍直文淵。蘭省綴次于文昌，已高曳履；薇垣映躔于華蓋，尚忝覆甌。篚羽彤墀，班隨八座；凝輝黼扆，位接三台。俯媿迂儒，濫承異數。伏念臣瑄，河汾末品，志學欲宗洙泗之源；澤絳庸流，傳心切求關閩之派。飭躬礪節，以明道不在多言；復性教人，謂工文無裨實用。夙承師訓，長竊賢科。攬轡湖湘，未能肅官常而懲貪墨；校文齊魯，亦頗正士習而抑浮夸。繼以虛名，謬蒙拔擢；旋因法守，幸遂投閒。優召偶及蓬門，孤踪再登棘寺。詎意上天開泰，明主憐才，既拜兼官，復司直賛。臣敢不講明心
translation_en:
… the Imperial Screen's longing for veteran ministers. Wishing to establish the worthy through dream and divination, Your Majesty's favor and reliance have reached even down to a humble grass-gatherer like me. I have been promoted to serve as Vice Minister in the Southern Palace [Ministry of Rites] and concurrently appointed to the Hanlin Academy; gazing up in reliance at the Northern Dipper, I attend on duty at the Hall of Literary Profundity (Wenyuan ge). In the Orchid Department, my rank is arrayed beneath the Wenchang constellation, where I already walk on high in court shoes; in the Crape-Myrtle Enclosure [Grand Secretariat], my orbit reflects the Imperial Canopy constellation, where my name is undeservedly held beneath the golden bowl. Bearing feathered plumes on the vermilion steps, my rank follows the Eight Executives; bathed in the radiance of the axe-screened throne, my position adjoins the Three Terraces. Looking down at myself, I am ashamed that a pedantic scholar should so undeservedly receive such extraordinary favor.

Humbly I reflect that I, Your servant [Xue] Xuan 薛瑄, am a man of the lowest caliber from the He and Fen rivers, who in setting my heart on learning wished to follow the fountainhead of the Zhu and Si rivers [Confucius]; an ordinary person from Ze and Jiang prefectures, who in transmitting the mind earnestly sought the lineages of Guan [Zhang Zai] and Min [Zhu Xi]. Disciplining my person and honing my integrity, I held that illuminating the Way does not lie in many words; restoring human nature and instructing others, I maintained that artful writing is of no benefit to practical use. Early on I received my teachers' instructions, and when grown I undeservedly passed the civil service examinations. Holding the reins as an inspector in Huxiang [Huguang], I was unable to enforce official discipline and punish the corrupt and greedy; examining essays as education intendant in Qi and Lu [Shandong], I was nevertheless somewhat able to rectify the habits of scholars and curb superficiality and boastfulness. Subsequently, on account of an empty reputation, I was undeservedly selected for promotion; soon after, for upholding the law, I was fortunate enough to retire into leisure. A gracious summons unexpectedly reached my thatched gate, and my solitary footsteps once again ascended the Court of Judicial Review. How could I have expected that High Heaven would usher in an era of peace, and that an enlightened ruler, cherishing talent, would not only confer on me concurrent offices, but also assign me to direct assistance in the Grand Secretariat? How dare Your servant not elucidate the mind's…

title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
體究極化源夙夜
闕廷敷求
當世之彝典趨蹌
禁闥討論
累朝之憲章雖才略不逮宋祁願陳禦戎之策
顧純誠仰希吉甫竊附薦賢之忠庶
上下同心威靈丕振于夷夏而
君臣合德治理有光于
祖宗伏願
===
主善為師
親賢是寶太阿不移于嬖近慎選前後左右
之人三尺日總于
朝廷潜孚
天地鬼神之佑
外威嚴而内順治
景命煥六服之車書家禮樂而戸絃歌
皇圖新萬年之曆數臣瑄無任瞻
天仰
punctuated: 體，究極化源；夙夜闕廷，敷求當世之彝典；趨蹌禁闥，討論累朝之憲章。雖才略不逮宋祁，願陳禦戎之策；顧純誠仰希吉甫，竊附薦賢之忠。庶上下同心，威靈丕振于夷夏；而君臣合德，治理有光于祖宗。伏願主善為師，親賢是寶。太阿不移于嬖近，慎選前後左右之人；三尺日總于朝廷，潜孚天地鬼神之佑。外威嚴而内順治，景命煥六服之車書；家禮樂而戸絃歌，皇圖新萬年之曆數。臣瑄無任瞻天仰
translation_en: … the substance of the mind, and thoroughly investigate the source of moral transformation; day and night at the palace court, broadly seek out the enduring canons of the present age; hastening back and forth within the forbidden precincts, discuss and examine the institutional charters of successive reigns. Although my talent and strategy do not reach those of Song Qi 宋祁, I wish to set forth policies for defending against the western barbarians; yet in pure sincerity I look up in emulation of Jifu 吉甫, and humbly attach myself to the loyalty of recommending the worthy. May those above and below be of one mind, so that august prestige is grandly振兴 among both non-Chinese and Chinese; and may sovereign and minister unite in virtue, so that the order of governance brings glory to the Imperial Ancestors. I humbly pray that Your Majesty will take goodness as Your teacher, and treasure drawing close to the worthy. Let the great sword of state authority (Tai'e 太阿) not shift to favorites and close attendants, carefully selecting the men before, behind, to the left, and to the right; let the three-foot statutory code be daily held in the grasp of the royal court, silently winning the aid of Heaven, Earth, ghosts, and spirits. With awe-inspiring majesty abroad and harmonious governance within, may the glorious Mandate illumine the unified車書 (cart-axle gauges and written script) of the Six Domains; with rites and music in every family and stringed instruments and singing in every household, may the Imperial enterprise renew its calendrical destiny for ten thousand years. Your servant Xuan 瑄 is overcome with the utmost… gazing up at Heaven and looking up to…

title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
聖激切屏營之至謹奉
表稱
謝以
聞
第叁場
策五道
第一問
徐尚實
同考試官教諭劉批
===
君臣孚敏我
祖宗朝盛事
皇上推誠禮下千載一時子能揄揚休美而篇終以保泰爲言尤見忠愛宜冠多士
考試官教授蔡批援古質今發明上下交成之意
詳盡讀之令人感奮他日必能効忠者敬服敬服
考試官教授朱批條答詳明獻納勤懇非徒工文者
君臣之交孚也其千載之昌時乎君臣之
交儆也其萬世之常道乎時者運之所乘
而醇漓因之不可一也有交孚之殷則志
punctuated:
聖，激切屏營之至，謹奉表稱謝以聞。
第叁場：策五道。
第一問：徐尚實。
同考試官教諭劉批：君臣孚敏，我祖宗朝盛事；皇上推誠禮下，千載一時。子能揄揚休美，而篇終以保泰爲言，尤見忠愛，宜冠多士。
考試官教授蔡批：援古質今，發明上下交成之意詳盡。讀之令人感奮，他日必能効忠者，敬服，敬服！
考試官教授朱批：條答詳明，獻納勤懇，非徒工文者。
君臣之交孚也，其千載之昌時乎！君臣之交儆也，其萬世之常道乎！時者，運之所乘，而醇漓因之，不可一也；有交孚之殷，則志
translation_en:
… the Sacred Majesty, and is overcome with earnest trepidation and awe. I respectfully present this memorial of gratitude for the Imperial hearing.

Third Session: Five Policy Questions.

First Question: Xu Shangshi 徐尚實.
Associate Examiner, Instructor Liu, comments: Mutual trust and diligence [or mutual admonition 儆?] between ruler and minister were the glorious affairs of our Ancestors' reigns; His Majesty extends sincerity and treats his subordinates with courtesy, an opportunity that comes once in a thousand years. You are able to extol this fine beauty, and at the end of the essay you speak of preserving great peace, which especially shows your loyalty and affection. You deserve to be placed at the head of the many scholars.
Examiner, Professor Cai, comments: Citing antiquity to verify the present, he exhaustively elucidates the meaning of superior and inferior mutually bringing each other to completion. Reading it makes one feel moved and inspired; in the future he will surely be one capable of rendering loyal service. Truly admirable, truly admirable!
Examiner, Professor Zhu, comments: His point-by-point responses are detailed and clear, and his counsel is earnest and sincere; he is not merely someone skilled at literary composition.

When ruler and minister share mutual trust, is that not a prosperous era that comes once in a thousand years? When ruler and minister mutually admonish one another, is that not the constant way for ten thousand generations? The times are what fate rides upon, and whether customs are pure or thin depends on them—they cannot be uniform. When there is deep mutual trust, then intentions …

title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
通于無間道者治之所出而否泰係之不
可易也有交儆之實則治保于無虞此自
古明良所以精神翕聚元氣融浹不謀而
自合不介而自親而成開泰保泰之鴻猷
者用此道也知此則我
皇祖
列聖基隆于前我
皇上媲美于後
君臣相與所以通地天之泰而成一德之治者
===
不可以颺庥於萬一乎甞考之易之泰九
二以剛中應五而六五柔中虛已以受之
此上下交而為泰之時也泰之初君與臣
交會而泰益開泰之極君與臣交儆而泰
益保時之隆也道之至也雖天地之交不
越此矣唐虞之興也中天也泰運撫矣當
其時君臣家視寰寓而身視天下喜起賡
歌都俞吁咈何其孚也而違弼之戒時幾
之敕惓惓焉興道以乘時故言泰者莫唐
punctuated:
通于無間。道者，治之所出，而否泰係之，不可易也；有交儆之實，則治保于無虞。此自古明良所以精神翕聚，元氣融浹，不謀而自合，不介而自親，而成開泰、保泰之鴻猷者，用此道也。知此，則我皇祖、列聖基隆于前，我皇上媲美于後，君臣相與，所以通地天之泰而成一德之治者，不可以颺庥於萬一乎？

甞考之《易》之〈泰〉：九二以剛中應五，而六五柔中虛已以受之，此上下交而為泰之時也。泰之初，君與臣交會而泰益開；泰之極，君與臣交儆而泰益保。時之隆也，道之至也，雖天地之交不越此矣。唐、虞之興也，中天也，泰運撫矣。當其時，君臣家視寰寓而身視天下，喜起賡歌，都俞吁咈，何其孚也！而違弼之戒、時幾之敕，惓惓焉興道以乘時，故言泰者莫唐、
translation_en:
…communicate without any barrier. The Way is that from which good governance emerges, and upon which obstruction (pi) and peace (tai) depend—it cannot be altered; when there is the substance of mutual admonition, good governance is preserved without cause for alarm. Thus from antiquity, the reason enlightened rulers and worthy ministers have gathered their vital spirits together and harmonized the primal vitality—uniting naturally without prior consultation, growing close naturally without intermediaries, and accomplishing the grand designs of inaugurating peace and preserving peace—is that they employed this Way. Understanding this, may we not extol in some small measure how our Imperial Progenitor and the successive Sacred Emperors laid the flourishing foundation beforehand, and how Your Majesty matches their excellence afterward, with ruler and ministers working together to open the peace of Earth and Heaven in communion and achieve the governance of unified virtue?

I have examined the hexagram Peace (Tai) in the Book of Changes (Yi): the Nine in the Second place responds to the Fifth with firm centrality, while the Six in the Fifth place, with yielding centrality, humbles itself to receive it; this is the time when above and below are in communion and constitute Peace. At the beginning of Peace, ruler and minister meet in fellowship, and Peace is further inaugurated; at the culmination of Peace, ruler and minister admonish one another, and Peace is further preserved. It is the flourishing of the times and the perfection of the Way—even the communion of Heaven and Earth does not surpass this! The rise of Tang [Yao] and Yu [Shun] was like the sun at midday; they held the destiny of Peace in their hands. At that time, ruler and ministers regarded the realm as one family and the empire as one body; rejoicing and rising up to exchange songs, uttering approvals and admonitions ("du," "yu," "xu," "fu")—how profound was their mutual trust! Yet with the warnings against going astray and failing to assist, and the injunctions to attend to the moment and the subtle incipient tendencies, they earnestly promoted the Way to avail themselves of the times. Therefore, when speaking of Peace, none compares to Tang and…

title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
虞若也三代相與詩書所稱蓋猶得而想
見其盛廼孔子逖覽帝制近矚王猷喟然
興曰唐虞之際於斯爲盛蓋有感於希覯
之時相成之道云三代以還風斯下矣願
治者豈不嘉樂虞周名號長美哉然手足
腹心情旣相隔而鹽梅麴糵德未交承豈
時之淳龐不齊而道之脩否頓異哉姑就
明問所及者言之漢帝續虞人之箴以示
羣臣唐宗發理人之策以試縣令宋主頒
訓廉謹刑之銘以敕百官非不煥然美矣
顧制作徒工而同心之誼則尟魏相條上
故事李絳進君臣屏風司馬光進稽古錄
孫奭進無逸圖非不井然備矣然章奏雖
愾而格心之道猶微交孚交儆之實開泰
保泰之方其謝三代亦巳久矣而况唐虞
哉洪惟我
太祖高皇帝延攬英豪廓清華夏于時謀臣碩
輔應運雲蒸若徐達李文忠劉基宋濂諸
punctuated: 虞若也。三代相與，《詩》、《書》所稱，蓋猶得而想見其盛。廼孔子逖覽帝制，近矚王猷，喟然興曰：「唐、虞之際，於斯爲盛。」蓋有感於希覯之時、相成之道云。三代以還，風斯下矣。願治者豈不嘉樂虞、周，名號長美哉？然手足腹心，情旣相隔；而鹽梅麴糵，德未交承。豈時之淳龐不齊，而道之脩否頓異哉？姑就明問所及者言之：漢帝續《虞人之箴》以示羣臣，唐宗發理人之策以試縣令，宋主頒《訓廉》、《謹刑》之銘以敕百官，非不煥然美矣；顧制作徒工，而同心之誼則尟。魏相條上故事，李絳進君臣屏風，司馬光進《稽古錄》，孫奭進《無逸圖》，非不井然備矣；然章奏雖愾，而格心之道猶微。交孚交儆之實，開泰保泰之方，其謝三代亦巳久矣，而况唐、虞哉！洪惟我太祖高皇帝延攬英豪，廓清華夏。于時謀臣碩輔，應運雲蒸，若徐達、李文忠、劉基、宋濂諸
translation_en: … matches Tang and Yu. As for the mutual fellowship of ruler and minister in the Three Dynasties, from what is celebrated in the Classic of Poetry (Shi) and the Classic of Documents (Shu), one can still envision its flourishing state. Yet when Confucius surveyed the institutions of the ancient emperors from afar and observed the plans of the kings closer at hand, he sighed deeply and said, "At the juncture of Tang and Yu, it was more flourishing than in this dynasty"—for he was moved by the rarity of such an era and by the Way of mutual fulfillment. From the Three Dynasties onward, customs declined. Did those who wished for good governance not delight in Yu and Zhou, desiring that their titles and reputations remain forever admirable? Yet when ruler and minister are like limbs and heart-and-belly whose feelings have already grown estranged, or like salt and plum, yeast and malt whose virtues no longer complement and sustain one another, is this merely because the simplicity and generosity of the times are uneven, or because the cultivation or neglect of the Way has suddenly diverged? Let us speak tentatively of the examples touched upon in Your clear question: the Han Emperor continued the "Forester's Admonition" (Yuren zhi zhen) to display to his assembled ministers; the Tang ancestor issued policy questions on governing the people to test District Magistrates; the Song ruler promulgated the inscriptions on "Instructing in Integrity" (Xun lian) and "Carefulness in Punishments" (Jin xing) to admonish the hundred officials. These were not without resplendent beauty, yet their compositions were merely skillful in form, while the bond of shared mind was scarce. Wei Xiang 魏相 submitted itemized precedents from the past; Li Jiang 李絳 presented a screen depicting rulers and ministers; Sima Guang 司馬光 presented the Record of Investigating Antiquity (Jigu lu); and Sun Shi 孫奭 presented the Diagram of "Against Luxurious Ease" (Wuyi tu). These were not without orderly completeness, yet although their memorials were impassioned, the Way of rectifying the ruler's heart remained faint. The substance of mutual trust and mutual admonition, and the methods of initiating and preserving Great Peace (Tai), had already fallen short of the Three Dynasties for a long time—how much more so of Tang and Yu! Humbly reflecting upon our Grand Progenitor, Emperor Gao (Taizu Gao Huangdi), he drew in heroic talents and swept clear the Chinese realm. At that time, counseling ministers and great coadjutors rose like clouds in response to theheavenly Mandate—men such as Xu Da 徐達, Li Wenzhong 李文忠, Liu Ji 劉基, Song Lian 宋濂, and others…

title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
人相與訪議疇咨燕樂
賜予而萬世之
鴻圖肇於是矣甞伏讀
大誥三篇首言
君臣同遊曰同心一氣立綱陳紀曰感格天地
時和年豐大哉
皇謨所以交上下而啓泰階者何至也迨我
宣宗章皇帝厲精政治禮敬儒紳于時侍從論
思應期林會若楊榮楊溥楊士奇胡濙諸
===
人相與披豁雍容給饌
召對而萬世之駿烈弘於是矣甞伏讀
賢姦傳官箴臣鑒三書或列人品之善惡而
勸懲具昭或嚴諸司之職掌而規戒咸備
大哉
帝典所以厲臣鄰而綿泰祚者何至也
列聖相承重熙累洽百辟交奮精白承休進鑑
古錄如李賢進講學篇如楊守陳進勤政
要如王鏊荷
punctuated: 人，相與訪議疇咨，燕樂賜予，而萬世之鴻圖肇於是矣。甞伏讀《大誥》三篇，首言「君臣同遊」，曰「同心一氣，立綱陳紀」；曰「感格天地，時和年豐」。大哉皇謨！所以交上下而啓泰階者，何至也！迨我宣宗章皇帝厲精政治，禮敬儒紳，于時侍從論思，應期林會，若楊榮、楊溥、楊士奇、胡濙諸人，相與披豁雍容，給饌召對，而萬世之駿烈弘於是矣。甞伏讀《賢姦傳》、《官箴》、《臣鑒》三書，或列人品之善惡而勸懲具昭，或嚴諸司之職掌而規戒咸備。大哉帝典！所以厲臣鄰而綿泰祚者，何至也！列聖相承，重熙累洽，百辟交奮，精白承休。進《鑑古錄》如李賢，進《講學篇》如楊守陳，進《勤政要》如王鏊，荷
translation_en:
… men, consulting and deliberating with them, entertaining them at banquets and bestowing gifts upon them; and thus the grand plan for ten thousand generations was inaugurated here. I have humbly read the three sections of the Grand Pronouncements (Dagao 大誥), which begin by speaking of "Ruler and Ministers Sharing in Fellowship" (Junchen tongyou 君臣同遊), saying, "With one mind and one vital energy, they establish the cardinal principles and set forth the laws"; and saying, "They move and reach Heaven and Earth, so that the seasons are harmonious and the harvests abundant." Great indeed are the Imperial counsels! How supreme is the means by which they unite superior and inferior and open the way to an era of peace and prosperity!

Coming down to our Emperor Xuanzong Zhang [the Xuande Emperor], he applied himself vigorously to governance and treated Confucian officials with礼 (courtesy and respect). At that time, close attendants and counselors gathered like a forest in response to the auspicious age—men such as Yang Rong 楊榮, Yang Pu 楊溥, Yang Shiqi 楊士奇, and Hu Ying 胡濙—with whom he conversed in open-hearted and composed candor, providing them with meals and summoning them for personal audiences; and thus the glorious achievements for ten thousand generations were broadened here. I have humbly read the three books, Biographies of the Worthy and the Treacherous (Xianjian zhuan 賢姦傳), Admonitions for Officials (Guanzhen 官箴), and Mirror for Ministers (Chenjian 臣鑒): some set forth the good and evil of men's character so that encouragement and warning are both made manifest, while others strictly define the duties of the various offices so that rules and admonitions are fully provided. Great indeed are the Imperial canons! How supreme is the means by which they spur on ministerial associates and prolong the blessed dynastic fortune!

Successive Sacred Emperors have followed one another, bringing cumulative splendor and pervasive harmony, while the hundred officials have striven together, upholding the imperial grace with pure and untarnished devotion. Men such as Li Xian 李賢, who presented the Record of Mirrors from Antiquity (Jiangu lu 鑑古錄); Yang Shouchen 楊守陳, who presented the Essays on Imperial Lectures (Jiangxue pian 講學篇); and Wang Ao 王鏊, who presented the Essentials of Diligent Governance (Qinzheng yao 勤政要), received …

title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
累朝之優渥攄一得以開陳啓沃實資于
聖心獻納有功於
袞闕所以交孚交儆而昌泰運於無疆者又
不在於
列聖之禮遇而羣賢之交脩哉我
皇上以
聰明仁孝之資紹
祖宗帝王之統
踐祚以來動遵
===
成憲首
御平臺召見輔臣即成周之訪落不足以喻其
盛屢
灑宸翰特昭
天寵雖有商之一德不足以匹其隆一時意氣
感動薦紳凡揚英舒翹逖聽垂聲者莫不
洗濯淬勵樂觀黃虞之化而欣承都俞之
風美哉洋洋乎固
皇王之盛事而
punctuated: 累朝之優渥，攄一得以開陳，啓沃實資于聖心，獻納有功於袞闕。所以交孚交儆，而昌泰運於無疆者，又不在於列聖之禮遇，而羣賢之交脩哉？我皇上以聰明仁孝之資，紹祖宗帝王之統。踐祚以來，動遵成憲。首御平臺，召見輔臣，即成周之《訪落》，不足以喻其盛；屢灑宸翰，特昭天寵，雖有商之《一德》，不足以匹其隆。一時意氣感動薦紳，凡揚英舒翹、逖聽垂聲者，莫不洗濯淬勵，樂觀黃、虞之化，而欣承都俞之風。美哉，洋洋乎！固皇王之盛事，而
translation_en:
… the generous favor of successive reigns, expressed their modest insights to set forth their views; their enlightenment truly aided the Sacred Mind, and their counsel contributed to remedying the deficiencies of the imperial robes. Thus, that by which ruler and ministers mutually trusted and mutually admonished one another, thereby making the prosperous destiny flourish without bound—did it not lie in the courteous treatment shown by the Successive Sages and the mutual cultivation of the assembly of worthies?

Our Emperor, endowed with intelligence, benevolence, and filial piety, has succeeded to the line of his ancestral emperors and kings. Since ascending the throne, in every action he has abided by the established constitutions. First, he appeared at the Ping Platform (Pingtai) and summoned the Grand Secretaries for audience—even the "Counsel at the Beginning of the Reign" (Fangluo) of成周 (Cheng Zhou) is insufficient to illustrate such splendour; repeatedly he has洒 (bestowed) his imperial calligraphy to specially manifest Heavenly favor—even "Possessing Pure Virtue" (Yide) of the Shang dynasty is insufficient to match such eminence. All at once, the spirit of the moment moved the gentry and officials; all who display outstanding talent and crane their necks to listen from afar for his enduring fame have without exception cleansed their hearts and tempered their resolve, delighting to witness the transformative rule of the Yellow Emperor and Yu Shun, and joyfully receiving the spirit of harmonious deliberation between ruler and minister. How splendid, how vast and overflowing! Truly this is a grand enterprise of sovereigns and kings, and …

title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
宗社之洪庥也廼
宸衷益圖治理風示臣工
念士習澆漓官方刓缺
特頒勅諭誕
誥多方大要言窺隙竇者巧於獵取快恩讐者
偏於愛惡老成擯而不用便捷喜為有才
宜湔宿垢以襄王道
絲綸渙汗
詞旨森嚴與
===
高皇大誥之篇
章皇三書之旨均足以揭日月而垂宇宙者矣
頃輔臣仰荷
倚眷矢竭忠誠皇皇焉考歷代之事備媺惡之
詳繪圖直解兼資法戒分卷類列取數陰
陽名曰
帝鑒圖說進之
黼座較諸先臣所進尤為簡易明白真足以
比藥石而永龜鑑者矣統而言之道者歷
punctuated: 宗社之洪庥也。廼宸衷益圖治理，風示臣工，念士習澆漓，官方刓缺，特頒勅諭，誕誥多方。大要言窺隙竇者巧於獵取，快恩讐者偏於愛惡，老成擯而不用，便捷喜為有才，宜湔宿垢，以襄王道。絲綸渙汗，詞旨森嚴，與高皇《大誥》之篇、章皇三書之旨，均足以揭日月而垂宇宙者矣。頃輔臣仰荷倚眷，矢竭忠誠，皇皇焉考歷代之事，備媺惡之詳，繪圖直解，兼資法戒，分卷類列，取數陰陽，名曰《帝鑒圖說》，進之黼座，較諸先臣所進，尤為簡易明白，真足以比藥石而永龜鑑者矣。統而言之，道者歷
translation_en: …the great blessing of the Imperial Ancestors and Altars of the State. Moreover, the Imperial Mind seeks ever more earnestly to achieve good governance and to instruct and guide his officials. Mindful that the customs of the literati have become decadent and official standards have grown worn and deficient, His Majesty has specially issued an imperial edict, proclaiming his admonitions across all quarters. In essence, it states that those who peer into crevices and loopholes are clever at hunting for personal gain, while those who indulge personal gratitude and vengeance are biased in their likes and dislikes; experienced and mature men are cast aside and left unused, whereas theglib and opportunistic are favored as men of talent; therefore, officials ought to wash away old stains so as to assist in the Kingly Way. The imperial words pour forth like sweat, their language and purport solemn and stern; together with the chapters of the Grand Pronouncements (Dagao) of the Exalted Emperor [Hongwu] and the purport of the three books of the Illustrious Emperor [Xuanzong], they are all sufficient to shine as brightly as the sun and moon and endure throughout the universe. Recently, the Grand Secretaries, looking up in gratitude for His Majesty's reliance and favor, have sworn to exhaust their loyalty and sincerity. Anxiously examining the events of successive dynasties and setting forth in detail examples of both good and evil, they have painted illustrations with straightforward explanations to serve at once as models for emulation and warnings for avoidance. Divided into scrolls and arranged by category, taking their numbers from the principles of yin and yang, the work was entitled Illustrated Mirror for the Emperor (Dijian tushuo) and presented to the Imperial Throne. Compared with what was presented by former ministers, it is even simpler, easier, and clearer—truly worthy of being likened to medicinal stone and serving eternally as a tortoise-shell mirror. Speaking of the matter as a whole, the Way passes through…

title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
萬世而不更時則曠千載而一值天以時
授之
高皇而以其道作之於前有
君有臣以之交孚以之交儆先天而時不違焉
者也天以時授之
皇上而以其道繼之於後有
君有臣以之開泰以之保泰後天而時克奉焉
者也然則交會之際其一見於唐虞而再
見於
===
今日者乎雖然愚生芹曝之忱猶欲爲
皇上泰道之助者復有說焉謹幾微一也愼終
始二也防壅蔽三也辨名實四也夫干霄
之木起於青蔥重溟之流成於涓滴言積
漸也今
臨御大廷元碩夾輔
外朝旣肅矣而退居
深宮燕安易溺得無以徑竇誘之乎必謹之
于不見不聞而達之于起居食息一念之
punctuated: 萬世而不更，時則曠千載而一值。天以時授之高皇，而以其道作之於前，有君有臣，以之交孚，以之交儆，先天而時不違焉者也；天以時授之皇上，而以其道繼之於後，有君有臣，以之開泰，以之保泰，後天而時克奉焉者也。然則交會之際，其一見於唐虞，而再見於今日者乎？雖然，愚生芹曝之忱，猶欲爲皇上泰道之助者，復有說焉：謹幾微，一也；愼終始，二也；防壅蔽，三也；辨名實，四也。夫干霄之木，起於青蔥；重溟之流，成於涓滴，言積漸也。今臨御大廷，元碩夾輔，外朝旣肅矣；而退居深宮，燕安易溺，得無以徑竇誘之乎？必謹之于不見不聞，而達之于起居食息。一念之
translation_en:
… ten thousand generations without changing, whereas the opportune time is encountered only once in a thousand years. Heaven bestowed the opportune time upon the Exalted Emperor [Hongwu], who initiated it beforehand with this Way; having such a sovereign and such ministers, through it they shared mutual trust and mutual admonition, preceding Heaven and yet the time did not deviate from them. Heaven has bestowed the opportune time upon Your Majesty, who succeeds to it afterward with this Way; having such a sovereign and such ministers, through it they open an era of great peace (tai) and preserve that great peace, following Heaven and yet able to uphold its timing. If this is so, then has not such a juncture of harmonious convergence been seen once in the era of Tang [Yao] and Yu [Shun], and been seen a second time today?

Even so, out of my humble sincerity in offering wild celery and warm sunlight, I, a foolish student, still wish to offer further words to assist Your Majesty in the Way of great peace: first, be vigilant over subtleincipiencies; second, be prudent from beginning to end; third, guard against obstruction and concealment; fourth, distinguish between name and reality. Now, a tree that reaches the skies begins as a tender green shoot, and the currents of the deep ocean are formed from tiny drops—this speaks of gradual accumulation. Today, when You preside over the grand court, assisted by great and eminent ministers on either side, the outer court is already reverent and orderly; yet when You retire to the deep palace, where it is easy to indulge in comfort and ease, might there not be those who entice You through side doors and crooked paths? You must exercise vigilance in what is unseen and unheard, and extend it to Your daily movements, meals, and rest. At the sprouting of a single thought …

title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
萌神明對焉一行之動師保臨焉則防微
杜漸其道大光矣故幾微不可不謹也夫
行百里者半九十為九仞者虧一簣言鮮
終也今
勵精伊始庶寮儆惕百度惟貞矣然閱歷歲
時玩愒易生得無以近習移之乎必不徇
之于目前而慮之于百千萬世
經筵常講無廢學焉章奏
躬覽無怠政焉則遐思逖慮其永無愆矣故
===
終始不可不慎也帝王以視聽周天下一
蔽於私即几席弗察矣況萬里之外乎必
作敢言之氣杜寵倖之門面詰多愆者在
所容而罔上羨餘者罪之可也條奏水旱
者在所嘉而日獻符瑞者斥之可也則聰
明益廓不降皇序而四海周知矣故壅蔽
不可不防也帝王以崇尚風天下一眩於
名則為諼者將寘力矣而何以臻考成之
效乎必誅意不誅文採實不採名勞心撫
punctuated: 萌，神明對焉；一行之動，師保臨焉。則防微杜漸，其道大光矣。故幾微不可不謹也。夫行百里者半九十，為九仞者虧一簣，言鮮終也。今勵精伊始，庶寮儆惕，百度惟貞矣；然閱歷歲時，玩愒易生，得無以近習移之乎？必不徇之于目前，而慮之于百千萬世；經筵常講，無廢學焉；章奏躬覽，無怠政焉。則遐思逖慮，其永無愆矣。故終始不可不慎也。帝王以視聽周天下，一蔽於私，即几席弗察矣，況萬里之外乎？必作敢言之氣，杜寵倖之門；面詰多愆者在所容，而罔上羨餘者罪之可也；條奏水旱者在所嘉，而日獻符瑞者斥之可也。則聰明益廓，不降皇序而四海周知矣。故壅蔽不可不防也。帝王以崇尚風天下，一眩於名，則為諼者將寘力矣，而何以臻考成之效乎？必誅意不誅文，採實不採名；勞心撫…
translation_en:
…arises, it is as though standing face-to-face with the gods and spirits; when a single action is taken, it is as though the Grand Preceptor and Grand Protector are present. In this way, by checking the minute and stopping the gradual, the Way will shine forth in great brilliance. Therefore, one cannot fail to be cautious regarding the subtle and incipient.

Now, "for one traveling a hundred li, ninety li is only halfway," and "in building a mound of nine ren, the work may fall short by a single basket of earth"—this speaks of how rare it is to see things through to the end. Today, at the very beginning of Your Majesty's diligent governance, the various officials are alert and vigilant, and all regulations and institutions are upright. Yet as the years and seasons pass, negligence and idleness easily arise; could it be that intimate attendants might sway the sovereign's resolve? One must not yield to the immediate present, but rather take thought for hundreds, thousands, and tens of thousands of generations to come. Let the Classics Mat lectures be held regularly without neglecting learning; let memorials and reports be reviewed in person without slackening in governance. Then, with far-reaching thought and distant foresight, there will forever be no fault. Therefore, one cannot fail to be prudent regarding the end as well as the beginning.

An emperor encompasses the entire realm through his seeing and hearing; once obscured by partiality or selfishness, he cannot even perceive what lies beside his own desk and mat, let alone what is ten thousand li away! He must foster a spirit of bold remonstrance and close the gates to favored sycophants. Those who reprove him to his face for numerous faults should be tolerated, while those who deceive their superiors with surplus revenues should be punished; those who submit itemized memorials on floods and droughts should be commended, while those who daily present auspicious omens should be dismissed. Then his keenness of hearing and clarity of sight will expand ever further, and without descending from the imperial hall he will thoroughly know all within the four seas. Therefore, one cannot fail to guard against obstruction and concealment.

An emperor transforms the realm through what he exalts and values; once dazzled by mere reputation, those who practice deceit will exert their efforts therein, and how then can the efficacy of evaluating official performance be achieved? He must judge intentions rather than mere wording, and gather realities rather than empty names. Those who labor wholeheartedly in caring for…

title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
字者最之而偽增戶口者勿賞也無書抵
政府者拔之而捷徑終南者勿徵也則真
偽不淆無事綜覈而百工競勸矣故名實
不可不辨也是四者
今日之急務皆
勅諭之所已及而
帝鑒之所備載者也繹而思之推而廣之斷而
行之則泰道益隆澤被海隅名垂天壤而
億萬年雍熙之盛端在玆矣敢以是為
===
當宁
獻
第二問
莫與高
同考試官教諭李批經學不明人持異議此作折衷
羣言而末歸于讀書窮理居敬持志是沉潜經術而有得
者宜錄以式
考試官教授蔡批闡明六經之旨犁然深中肯綮取之
考試官教授朱批以高古之文發精確之見佳士佳士
punctuated:
字者最之，而偽增戶口者勿賞也；無書抵政府者拔之，而捷徑終南者勿徵也。則真偽不淆，無事綜覈而百工競勸矣。故名實不可不辨也。是四者，今日之急務，皆勅諭之所已及，而《帝鑒》之所備載者也。繹而思之，推而廣之，斷而行之，則泰道益隆，澤被海隅，名垂天壤，而億萬年雍熙之盛，端在玆矣。敢以是為當宁獻。

第二問
莫與高
同考試官教諭李批：經學不明，人持異議。此作折衷羣言，而末歸于讀書窮理、居敬持志，是沉潜經術而有得者，宜錄以式。
考試官教授蔡批：闡明六經之旨，犁然深中肯綮，取之。
考試官教授朱批：以高古之文，發精確之見。佳士，佳士！
translation_en:
… [labor in nurturing and] caring for the people should be ranked highest, while those who falsely inflate household and population figures should not be rewarded; those who send no letters to the grand secretaries in the central government should be promoted, while those who seek a shortcut to office via Mount Zhongnan should not be summoned. Then truth and falsehood will not be confused, and without the need for exhaustive verification, all officials will vie with one another in diligence. Therefore, reputation and reality must be distinguished. These four matters are the urgent tasks of the present day; all have already been touched upon in the imperial edicts of instruction and are fully recorded in the Mirror for the Emperor (Dijian). If one ponders and reflects upon them, extends and broadens them, and resolutely puts them into practice, then the Way of great peace will flourish ever more, benevolent grace will reach the farthest corners of the seas, renown will endure as long as heaven and earth, and thesplendor of harmonious prosperity for ahundred million years will truly lie right here. I venture to offer this to the throne.

Question Two
Mo Yugao
Associate Examiner and Instructor Li comments: Classical learning is obscured, and people hold divergent views. This essay weighs and reconciles the various opinions, and in the end returns to reading books to exhaustively investigate principle, and abiding in reverence to maintain one's resolve. This is someone who has immersed himself deeply in classical scholarship and gained true insight; it should be recorded as a model.
Examiner and Confucian Instructor Cai comments: It elucidates the essential meaning of the Six Classics, clearly and deeply hitting the crucial points. Selected.
Examiner and Confucian Instructor Zhu comments: In lofty and ancient prose, he sets forth precise and sound views. A fine scholar, a fine scholar!

title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
知事心之學者可語窮經之本矣知致用
之方者可語窮經之實矣夫道也者原于
一心而見之萬事者也六經也者聖人舉
斯道以筆之書示人求諸心而致之用者
也故不知事心之學而摘句尋章者末焉
爾矣不知致用之方而計功謀利者虚焉
爾矣是故六經聖人心學究其本言也君
子反而求之心焉浩浩乎萬理一原而格
致誠正貫之矣六經聖人之用舉其實言
===
也君子推而致之用焉淵淵乎一本萬殊
而脩齊治平舉之矣故易以言此心之時
焉吉凶之所以考者取是以考之也書以
言此心之中焉政事之所以達者取是以
達之也詩以言此心之正焉淑慝之所以
辨者取是以辨之也春秋言心之變焉是
非之所以公者取是以公之也禮樂言心
之敬和焉而暴慢鄙詐之遠者取是以遠
之也天下之道豈有餘蘊哉知此可以復
punctuated: 知事心之學者，可語窮經之本矣；知致用之方者，可語窮經之實矣。夫道也者，原于一心，而見之萬事者也；六經也者，聖人舉斯道以筆之書，示人求諸心而致之用者也。故不知事心之學，而摘句尋章者，末焉爾矣；不知致用之方，而計功謀利者，虚焉爾矣。是故六經，聖人心學，究其本言也，君子反而求之心焉，浩浩乎萬理一原，而格致誠正貫之矣；六經，聖人之用，舉其實言也，君子推而致之用焉，淵淵乎一本萬殊，而脩齊治平舉之矣。故《易》以言此心之時焉，吉凶之所以考者，取是以考之也；《書》以言此心之中焉，政事之所以達者，取是以達之也；《詩》以言此心之正焉，淑慝之所以辨者，取是以辨之也；《春秋》言心之變焉，是非之所以公者，取是以公之也；《禮》《樂》言心之敬和焉，而暴慢鄙詐之遠者，取是以遠之也。天下之道，豈有餘蘊哉？知此，可以復…
translation_en: One who understands the learning of serving the mind-and-heart may be spoken with about the root of thoroughly mastering the Classics; one who understands the method of putting knowledge into practical application may be spoken with about the substance of thoroughly mastering the Classics. Now, the Way originates in the single mind-and-heart and manifests itself in the myriad affairs; the Six Classics are that whereby the sages took up this Way and committed it to writing, showing people how to seek it in their own mind-and-heart and extend it to practical application. Therefore, to not understand the learning of serving the mind-and-heart while merely plucking out phrases and hunting through passages is nothing more than attending to the branches; to not understand the method of practical application while merely calculating achievements and scheming for profit is nothing more than emptiness. For this reason, to say that the Six Classics are the sages' learning of the mind-and-heart is to speak by tracing them to their root: when the noble man turns within to seek it in his own mind-and-heart, how vast it is—the myriad principles share a single origin, and investigating things, extending knowledge, making the intentions sincere, and rectifying the mind-and-heart thread through them all! To say that the Six Classics are the practical application of the sages is to speak by citing their substance: when the noble man extends them and brings them into practical application, how profound it is—a single root branches into myriad differentiations, and cultivating the person, regulating the family, ordering the state, and bringing peace to the world are all encompassed therein! Thus, the Classic of Changes (Yi) speaks of the timeliness of this mind-and-heart, and that whereby good and bad fortune are examined is examined by drawing upon this; the Classic of Documents (Shu) speaks of the centrality of this mind-and-heart, and that whereby governance and affairs are carried through is carried through by drawing upon this; the Classic of Odes (Shi) speaks of the correctness of this mind-and-heart, and that whereby the good and the wicked are distinguished is distinguished by drawing upon this; the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu) speaks of the adaptability of the mind-and-heart, and that whereby right and wrong are judged impartially is judged impartially by drawing upon this; the Classic of Rites (Li) and the Classic of Music (Yue) speak of the reverence and harmony of the mind-and-heart, and that whereby violence, negligence, vulgarity, and deceit are kept at a distance is kept at a distance by drawing upon this. Could the Way of all under Heaven hold any further unrevealed profundities? Understanding this, one can reply to…

title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
明問矣何則觀龍演卦文字未興學烏焉
文書契始立迨皇帝王伯迭興而孔子述
之于是而六經作焉考之經解其教可知
已執事謂始于莊子史遷之言固也然觀
論語孟子所載六經之名亦已散見而門
弟子之所誦習講求者也蓋六經之理不
外乎吾心聖人卽是筆之於書使人求諸
心以致其用焉爾故原於天之謂命具于
人之謂性脩于人之謂教蘊之爲德行之
===
爲道惇之爲倫散之爲物積于中而暢于
外爲文舉而措之爲事業夫固一而不二
也同而不異也至近至易而不可以求諸
遠且難者也故求諸心則六經之理會焉
謂之萬理一原可也致之用則六經之道
備焉謂之萬殊一本可也匡衡曰六經聖
人所以統天地之心使不悖其本性得之
矣而議者紛紛不同何哉自分析者言之
于楊子見說天說事說體說志說理之辨
punctuated: 明問矣。何則？觀龍演卦，文字未興；學鳥為文，書契始立。迨皇帝王伯迭興，而孔子述之，于是而六經作焉。考之《經解》，其教可知已。執事謂始于莊子、史遷之言，固也；然觀《論語》、《孟子》所載，六經之名亦已散見，而門弟子之所誦習講求者也。蓋六經之理不外乎吾心，聖人卽是筆之於書，使人求諸心以致其用焉爾。故原於天之謂命，具于人之謂性，脩于人之謂教；蘊之爲德，行之爲道，惇之爲倫，散之爲物，積于中而暢于外爲文，舉而措之爲事業。夫固一而不二也，同而不異也，至近至易而不可以求諸遠且難者也。故求諸心則六經之理會焉，謂之萬理一原可也；致之用則六經之道備焉，謂之萬殊一本可也。匡衡曰：「六經，聖人所以統天地之心，使不悖其本性。」得之矣！而議者紛紛不同，何哉？自分析者言之：于楊子見「說天」、「說事」、「說體」、「說志」、「說理」之辨…
translation_en:
… [answer] the enlightened question. Why is this so? When [Fuxi] observed the dragon [horse] and elaborated the trigrams, written characters had not yet arisen; when [Cangjie] studied the tracks of birds to make patterns [? 學烏焉文 for 學鳥為文], written records and tallies were first established. Down to the time when the August Ones, Emperors, Kings, and Hegemons successively arose, Confucius transmitted their legacy, and thereupon the Six Classics were created. If one examines the "Explanation of the Classics" (Jingjie) [in the Record of Rites], their teachings can already be known. Your Excellency's statement that [the term "Six Classics"] began with the words of Zhuangzi and the Grand Scribe Sima Qian (Shiqian 史遷) is certainly true. Yet if one looks at what is recorded in the Analects (Lunyu) and the Mencius (Mengzi), the names of the Six Classics already appear scattered throughout, and they were what the disciples recited, practiced, and investigated.

Indeed, the principles of the Six Classics are not external to our own mind; the sages simply wrote this down in books so as to cause people to seek it within their minds in order to carry it into practice. Therefore, as originating from Heaven it is called the Mandate; as endowed in man it is called human nature; as cultivated by man it is called instruction. Stored within, it becomes virtue; put into practice, it becomes the Way; earnestly fulfilled, it becomes human relationships; dispersed among affairs, it becomes things; accumulated within and expressed outwardly, it becomes literature and culture; taken up and applied in the world, it becomes great enterprises. Truly it is one and not dual, identical and not different—most near and most easy, and not something to be sought in what is distant and difficult. Thus, when one seeks it in the mind, the principles of the Six Classics converge there, and one may call it "the myriad principles sharing a single source"; when one carries it into practice, the Way of the Six Classics is complete therein, and one may call it "the myriad manifestations sharing a single root." Kuang Heng 匡衡 said: "The Six Classics are that whereby the sages unite the mind of Heaven and Earth, causing people not to go against their fundamental nature." He grasped it!

Yet why is it that commentators hold such a profusion of differing views? Speaking of those who divide and analyze them: in Master Yang (Yang Xiong 揚雄) we see the distinctions of "discoursing on Heaven," "discoursing on affairs," "discoursing on form," "discoursing on intent," and "discoursing on principle"…

title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
焉于班固見仁表義用知術信符之殊焉
于文中子見辨事正情制行和德舉往知
來之論焉于邵子見四府之述焉究其說
未為不是然六經同原謂聖人各有所因
而作則可謂六經各有所屬而殊則不可
觀者以意逆志斯已矣自偏重者言之周
子易為五經之原以時言也董鼎六經莫
備于書以事言也胡安國春秋五經之用
以斷言也荀子禮為道德之極以用言也
===
推其義未嘗不明然六籍並重謂其旨互
相通貫則可謂其書獨有所重則不可觀
者因言會意斯已矣先儒謂治六經者必
先通乎四書儒臣王禕嘗申其說矣今自
其言觀之治易始于中庸治書始于大學
治春秋始孟子治詩禮樂始論語及究其
詳則以中庸性命至誠合太極之旨焉大
學明德為本合峻德之訓焉孟子尊王抑
伯先義後利合春秋之法焉論語關雎太
punctuated: 焉；于班固，見仁表、義用、知術、信符之殊焉；于文中子，見辨事、正情、制行、和德、舉往知來之論焉；于邵子，見四府之述焉。究其說，未為不是；然六經同原，謂聖人各有所因而作則可，謂六經各有所屬而殊則不可。觀者以意逆志，斯已矣。自偏重者言之，周子《易》為五經之原，以時言也；董鼎六經莫備于《書》，以事言也；胡安國《春秋》五經之用，以斷言也；荀子《禮》為道德之極，以用言也。推其義，未嘗不明；然六籍並重，謂其旨互相通貫則可，謂其書獨有所重則不可。觀者因言會意，斯已矣。先儒謂治六經者，必先通乎四書，儒臣王禕嘗申其說矣。今自其言觀之，治《易》始于《中庸》，治《書》始于《大學》，治《春秋》始《孟子》，治《詩》、《禮》、《樂》始《論語》。及究其詳，則以《中庸》性命至誠，合太極之旨焉；《大學》明德為本，合峻德之訓焉；《孟子》尊王抑伯、先義後利，合《春秋》之法焉；《論語》關雎、太
translation_en:
… in Ban Gu 班固, one sees the distinctions of the manifestation of humaneness, the application of righteousness, the art of wisdom, and the tally of trustworthiness; in Master Wenzhong 文中子 (Wang Tong 王通), one sees the discussions of distinguishing affairs, rectifying emotions, regulating conduct, harmonizing virtue, and citing the past to know the future; in Master Shao 邵子 (Shao Yong 邵雍), one sees the account of the "Four Repositories" (Sifu 四府). If one examines their theories closely, they are not without merit. However, the Six Classics share the same origin: to say that the sages composed each of them in response to particular circumstances is permissible, but to say that the Six Classics each belong to separate domains and are fundamentally different is not permissible. The reader need only meet the authors' intentions with sympathetic understanding, and that is all.

Speaking from the perspective of those who lay particular emphasis on one classic: Master Zhou 周子 (Zhou Dunyi 周敦頤) held that the Book of Changes (Yi 易) is the source of the Five Classics, which was spoken in terms of time; Dong Ding 董鼎 held that none of the Six Classics is more complete than the Book of Documents (Shu 書), which was spoken in terms of affairs; Hu Anguo 胡安國 held that the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu 春秋) is the practical application of the Five Classics, which was spoken in terms of judgment; Master Xun 荀子 (Xunzi) held that the Record of Rites (Li 禮) is the culmination of the Way and its virtue, which was spoken in terms of function. If one traces out their meanings, they are by no means unclear. Yet the Six Classics are of equal importance: to say that their purports thoroughly interpenetrate one another is permissible, but to say that any single book holds exclusive weight is not permissible. The reader need only grasp the underlying meaning through the words, and that is all.

Earlier Confucians said that those who study the Six Classics must first thoroughly master the Four Books, and the Confucian official Wang Yi 王禕 once elaborated upon this view. Now, looking at his words: the study of the Book of Changes begins with the Doctrine of the Mean (Zhongyong 中庸); the study of the Book of Documents begins with the Great Learning (Daxue 大學); the study of the Spring and Autumn Annals begins with the Mencius (Mengzi 孟子); and the study of the Book of Odes (Shi 詩), the Record of Rites, and the Classic of Music (Yue 樂) begins with the Analects (Lunyu 論語). When we examine the details: because the Doctrine of the Mean treats of human nature, Heaven's mandate, and utmost sincerity, it accords with the purport of the Supreme Ultimate (Taiji 太極); because the Great Learning takes illuminating illustrious virtue as the root, it accords with the precept of "lofty virtue" (junde 峻德); because the Mencius reveres the True King and suppresses the Hegemon, putting righteousness first and profit last, it accords with the principles of the Spring and Autumn Annals; and because the Analects contains the chapters mentioning "Guanju" 關雎, the Grand…

title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
師鄉黨諸篇合詩禮樂之義焉是其度彼
參此燦然有條然不知聖人立言之際果
各有所主焉否也毋亦近于牽合與六經
之道同歸而教與詞亦不可泥也昔人又
于此比擬焉故論其教則易之知來藏往
非不疏通知遠也書之惟精惟一非不潔
淨精微也詩之發乎性情止乎禮義亦非
不恭儉莊敬也是其說猶近若辭則聖人
因經命意各自爲體原不相通雖韓子正
===
法奇葩之言已屬文人之習或者乃于易
取中孚九二鳴鶴在陰數語于詩取抑三
章其在于今數語以例經文之互似特偶
合者爾不知聖人作經之時果有意于兼
通模擬否也毋亦過于推求歟夫六經之
道一也自四者之說興而言始煩然而未
害也若夫生于心而見于言害于事者其
議經僭經叛經者乎是故劉知幾疑書伯
益之事何休以周禮爲六國陰謀之書王
punctuated: 師》、《鄉黨》諸篇，合《詩》、《禮》、《樂》之義焉。是其度彼參此，燦然有條。然不知聖人立言之際，果各有所主焉否也？毋亦近于牽合與？六經之道同歸，而教與詞亦不可泥也。昔人又于此比擬焉。故論其教，則《易》之「知來藏往」，非不疏通知遠也；《書》之「惟精惟一」，非不潔淨精微也；《詩》之「發乎性情，止乎禮義」，亦非不恭儉莊敬也。是其說猶近。若辭，則聖人因經命意，各自爲體，原不相通。雖韓子「正法奇葩」之言，已屬文人之習；或者乃于《易》取《中孚》九二「鳴鶴在陰」數語，于《詩》取《抑》三章「其在于今」數語，以例經文之互似，特偶合者爾。不知聖人作經之時，果有意于兼通模擬否也？毋亦過于推求歟？夫六經之道一也。自四者之說興，而言始煩，然而未害也。若夫生于心而見于言，害于事者，其議經、僭經、叛經者乎！是故劉知幾疑《書》伯益之事，何休以《周禮》爲六國陰謀之書，王
translation_en:
… the Grand Music Master (Taishi), and the "Xiangdang" chapter in the Analects correspond to the principles of the Odes (Shi), the Rites (Li), and the Music (Yue). Thus, in measuring that against this and cross-referencing them, the arrangement is brilliantly systematic. Yet one wonders whether, when the sages established their words, they truly had such specific correspondences in mind for each? Is this not rather close to forced matching?

The Way of the Six Classics leads to the same destination, yet their teachings and diction must not be rigidly conflated either. Scholars of the past also drew analogies among them in these respects. Thus, if we discuss their teachings: the "knowing the future and storing the past" of the Changes (Yi) is by no means lacking in breadth of comprehension and far-reaching vision; the "be discerning, be undivided" of the Documents (Shu) is by no means lacking in purity and subtle profundity; and the "arising from human nature and emotions, and stopping at ritual and righteousness" of the Odes is likewise by no means lacking in reverence, thrift, gravity, and respect. Such explanations are still reasonably close to the mark. As for their diction, however, the sages formulated their ideas in accordance with each Classic, each having its own distinct style and originally not being interchangeable. Even Master Han's [Han Yu 韓愈] remark about "orthodox models and marvelous blossoms" already belongs to the habits of belletrists. Yet someone went so far as to take from the Changes a few lines under the Second Nine of the Zhongfu hexagram—"A calling crane in the shade"—and from the Odes a few lines from the third stanza of "Yi"—"As for how things are today"—to illustrate how the texts of different Classics resemble one another. These are merely coincidental parallels. One wonders whether, when the sages composed the Classics, they truly intended to make them mutually interchangeable and imitative of one another? Is this not rather an overly strained search for connections?

Now, the Way of the Six Classics is one. Ever since these four theories arose, discourse has become convoluted, yet it has done no real harm. As for that which arises in the mind, manifests in words, and brings harm to affairs—is it not found among those who cavil at the Classics, usurp the Classics, or betray the Classics! Thus, Liu Zhiji 劉知幾 doubted the accounts of Boyi 伯益 in the Documents; He Xiu 何休 regarded the Rites of Zhou (Zhouli) as a book of sinister plots from the Six States; and Wang …

title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
安石以春秋爲斷爛朝報議者如此然以
歐陽脩之賢且疑十翼焉况其他乎楊雄
之擬易白居易之續書束晳之賡華黍僭
者如此然以司馬光之賢且作潜虚焉况
其他乎公孫弘之阿世劉歆之獻符命張
禹以不語怪神欺君叛者如此然杜鎬老
儒乃以圖書爲神道設教不近于叛乎夫
由前觀之析言也偏重也牽合也過求也
似于聖人作經之旨未能渾融然推重專
===
經亦不易之論也豈盡出于尋章摘句者
乎由後觀之議也僭也叛也則于聖人作
經之旨大相乖戾然叛經之害尤大孰非
所謂計功謀利者乎是故窮經者亦惟求
諸心以致之用而已矣何以紛紛辭說爲
哉故能求諸心則雖孔明之獨觀大旨陶
潜之不求甚解君子以爲通經矣能致其
用則雖劉元城守不妄語之一言李沆誦
節用愛人之數語君子亦以爲通經矣然
punctuated: 安石以《春秋》爲斷爛朝報，議者如此，然以歐陽脩之賢，且疑《十翼》焉，况其他乎？楊雄之擬《易》、白居易之續《書》、束晳之賡《華黍》，僭者如此，然以司馬光之賢，且作《潜虚》焉，况其他乎？公孫弘之阿世、劉歆之獻符命、張禹以「不語怪神」欺君，叛者如此，然杜鎬老儒，乃以圖、書爲神道設教，不近于叛乎？夫由前觀之，析言也，偏重也，牽合也，過求也，似于聖人作經之旨未能渾融，然推重專經，亦不易之論也，豈盡出于尋章摘句者乎？由後觀之，議也，僭也，叛也，則于聖人作經之旨大相乖戾，然叛經之害尤大，孰非所謂計功謀利者乎？是故窮經者，亦惟求諸心以致之用而已矣，何以紛紛辭說爲哉？故能求諸心，則雖孔明之獨觀大旨、陶潜之不求甚解，君子以爲通經矣；能致其用，則雖劉元城守「不妄語」之一言、李沆誦「節用愛人」之數語，君子亦以爲通經矣。然
translation_en:
… [Wang] Anshi 王安石 dismissed the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu) as "tattered court gazettes." Such were those who impugned the Classics; yet even a worthy like Ouyang Xiu 歐陽脩 doubted the Ten Wings (Shiyi), so how much more so with others? Yang Xiong's 楊雄 imitation of the Changes (Yi), Bai Juyi's 白居易 continuation of the Documents (Shu), and Shu Xi's 束晳 composition to supply the lost "Millet in Flower" (Huashu) ode—such were those who usurped the Classics; yet even a worthy like Sima Guang 司馬光 composed the Latent Void (Qianxu), so how much more so with others? Gongsun Hong's 公孫弘 pandering to the age, Liu Xin's 劉歆 presentation of auspicious omens, and Zhang Yu's 張禹 deceiving his ruler by citing "not speaking of prodigies and spirits"—such were those who betrayed the Classics; yet when an aged Confucian scholar like Du Hao 杜鎬 claimed that the River Chart and Luo Writing (Tu Shu) were merely devices to establish teaching through the way of the spirits, was this not close to betrayal?

Viewed from the former perspective—splintering words, partiality of emphasis, forced correlations, and excessive searching—these seem not yet fully harmonized with the sages' intent in creating the Classics; yet esteeming the dedicated mastery of a single Classic is also an unalterable principle, so how could they all stem merely from phrase-mongers and pedants? Viewed from the latter perspective—impugning, usurping, and betraying—these are utterly at odds with the sages' intent in creating the Classics; yet the harm of betraying the Classics is greatest of all, for which of those culprits was not someone who calculated personal merit and schemed for profit?

Therefore, those who exhaustively study the Classics should simply seek their meaning within the mind in order to carry it into practical application—what need is there for such a profusion of verbal disputation? Thus, if one can seek it within the mind, then even though Kongming 孔明 [Zhuge Liang 諸葛亮] looked only at the broad purport and Tao Qian 陶潜 did not seek overly literal explanations, the gentleman still considers them to have comprehended the Classics. And if one can carry them into practical application, then even though Liu Yuancheng 劉元城 [Liu Anshi 劉安世] held fast to the single precept of "not speaking falsely," and Li Hang 李沆 constantly recited the few words on "economizing in expenditures and loving the people," the gentleman likewise considers them to have comprehended the Classics. Yet…

title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
則養心之要致用之實豈待于遠求哉雖
然未易言也亦嘗聞王禕之言而有得矣
蓋六經聖人心學以心畫心法心聲心制
與夫史外傳心之要典言也可謂窮經得
其本矣六經聖人之用以趨吉避凶圖治
立政别勸懲辨上下象功德明道義言也
可謂窮經知其實矣是故取諸心焉則知
六經之理無一非吾之所固有而拘于章
句祗見其蔽也已致諸用焉則知六經之
===
道無一非吾之所當為而溺于功利祗見
其舛也已然則窮經者何居以心驗之以
身體之從容默會于幽閒靜一之中超然
自得于意言象數之表一念之發一息之
存必涵泳乎六經焉由是持之恒久而所
謂時也中也正也變也敬與和也一以貫
之矣是之謂有本之學將有言也將有行
也必準則于六經焉由是措諸事業所謂
考吉凶也達政事也辨淑慝也公是非也
punctuated: 則養心之要、致用之實，豈待于遠求哉？雖然，未易言也。亦嘗聞王禕之言而有得矣。蓋「六經，聖人心學」，以心畫、心法、心聲、心制，與夫史外傳心之要典言也，可謂窮經得其本矣。「六經，聖人之用」，以趨吉避凶、圖治立政、别勸懲、辨上下、象功德、明道義言也，可謂窮經知其實矣。是故取諸心焉，則知六經之理無一非吾之所固有，而拘于章句，祗見其蔽也已；致諸用焉，則知六經之道無一非吾之所當為，而溺于功利，祗見其舛也已。然則窮經者何居？以心驗之，以身體之，從容默會于幽閒靜一之中，超然自得于意言象數之表。一念之發，一息之存，必涵泳乎六經焉。由是持之恒久，而所謂時也、中也、正也、變也、敬與和也，一以貫之矣。是之謂有本之學。將有言也，將有行也，必準則于六經焉。由是措諸事業，所謂考吉凶也、達政事也、辨淑慝也、公是非也、
translation_en: … then why should one need to seek far afield for the essentials of nourishing the mind and the substance of practical application? Even so, this is not easy to speak of. I have also heard the words of Wang Yi 王禕 and gained insight from them. When he says, "The Six Classics are the learning of the mind of the sages," he is speaking in terms of the drawings of the mind [the Changes], the method of the mind [the Documents], the voice of the mind [the Odes], the regulations of the mind [the Rites], and the essential canons that transmit the mind beyond mere history [the Spring and Autumn Annals]; this may be called exhausting the Classics and grasping their root. When he says, "The Six Classics are the practical application of the sages," he is speaking in terms of pursuing good fortune and avoiding calamity, planning governance and establishing administration, distinguishing encouragement and warning, differentiating superior and inferior, symbolizing merit and virtue, and clarifying the Way and righteousness; this may be called exhausting the Classics and knowing their substance. Therefore, if one draws them from the mind, one knows that not a single principle of the Six Classics is not inherently one's own, and that being bound to chapter and phrase merely reveals one's blindness; if one carries them into practical application, one knows that not a single way of the Six Classics is not what one ought to do, and that being mired in功利 (merit and profit) merely reveals one's perversity. This being so, where should one who exhausts the Classics abide? Verify them with the mind, embody them in the person,comprehend them calmly and silently in quietude and unity, and attain them transcendently for oneself beyond ideas, words, images, and numbers. In the arising of a single thought, in the preservation of a single breath, one must immerse oneself in the Six Classics. Holding to this with constancy over a long time, what are called timeliness, centrality, correctness, change, reverence, and harmony are threaded together as one. This is called learning that has a root. When one is about to speak, or when one is about to act, one must take the Six Classics as the standard. Putting this into practice in one's undertakings, what are called examining good fortune and calamity,comprehending governance and affairs, distinguishing the good and the evil, making impartial judgments of right and wrong, …

title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
莊敬和樂也一以貫之矣是之謂務實之
學由是德以立道以行倫以篤物以化文
以成業以著由是性盡命至而教彰六經
不于是而會通耶雖然經未易窮也苟不
得其要則求諸心而或淪于空虛致諸用
而未免于駁雜何以立本而務實乎朱子
曰爲學莫先於窮理窮理惟在於讀書讀
書之法貴循序而致精其本又在居敬而
持志噫此固承學之所勉焉而未逮者也
===
第三問
劉業成
同考試官教諭李 批 敷對詳而趨向正蓋留心於君
子儒者
考試官教授蔡 批 發明純儒之道而推本於躬行
關係世教不尠取之
考試官教授朱 批 發揮儒道一貫之旨詳盡
天下之道一而已矣二之非道也儒者之
學亦一而已矣二之非學也夫道非他也
punctuated:
莊敬、和樂也，一以貫之矣。是之謂務實之學。由是德以立、道以行、倫以篤、物以化、文以成、業以著；由是性盡、命至而教彰，六經不于是而會通耶？雖然，經未易窮也。苟不得其要，則求諸心而或淪于空虛，致諸用而未免于駁雜，何以立本而務實乎？朱子曰：「爲學莫先於窮理，窮理惟在於讀書。讀書之法，貴循序而致精；其本又在居敬而持志。」噫！此固承學之所勉焉而未逮者也。

第三問
劉業成
同考試官教諭李批：敷對詳而趨向正，蓋留心於君子儒者。
考試官教授蔡批：發明純儒之道，而推本於躬行，關係世教不尠。取之。
考試官教授朱批：發揮儒道一貫之旨，詳盡。

天下之道，一而已矣，二之非道也；儒者之學，亦一而已矣，二之非學也。夫道非他也，
translation_en:
…and solemn reverence and harmonious joy—all are bound together by a single thread. This is what is called learning devoted to substantial reality. From this, virtue is established, the Way is practiced, human relations are made earnest, things are transformed, cultural refinement is achieved, and accomplishments are made manifest; from this, human nature is fully realized, heaven's decree is attained, and moral teaching shines forth. Are the Six Classics not thereby brought into comprehensive unity? Even so, the Classics are not easily mastered. If one fails to grasp their essentials, then seeking them in the mind may sink into emptiness, while applying them in practice may not escape being impure and mixed. How then could one establish the root and devote oneself to substantial reality? Master Zhu [Zhu Xi 朱熹] said: "In pursuing learning, nothing comes before fathoming principle, and fathoming principle lies solely in reading books. In the method of reading books, one values following the proper sequence and achieving precision; its root, moreover, lies in abiding in reverence and holding fast to one's determination." Alas! This is indeed what I, as a student, strive after yet have not yet attained.

Third Policy Question
Liu Yecheng 劉業成
Comment by Associate Examiner Instructor Li 李: The exposition and response are detailed and the orientation is orthodox; he is evidently one who sets his mind on being a Confucian of the noble man's sort.
Comment by Examiner Professor Cai 蔡: He elucidates the Way of the pure Confucian and traces its root back to personal practice, which is of no small consequence to public moral teaching. Selected.
Comment by Examiner Professor Zhu 朱: He develops the purport of the single thread of the Confucian Way thoroughly and exhaustively.

The Way under heaven is one and no more; to divide it into two is not the Way. The learning of the Confucian is likewise one and no more; to divide it into two is not learning. Now the Way is nothing other than…

title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
原於天地散於民物流行於古今待人而
行者也儒者之學非他也統天地之心握
民物之紀貫古今之緒以待後學者也是
故明此以立本則盡性而至命焉明此以
達用則政立而敎彰焉明此而得位則爲
君爲相焉明此而不得位則爲師爲弟子
焉以脩於家則宗族鄉黨孚化焉以行於
天下則中外遠邇歸心焉是豈有二道亦
豈有二學也哉故主之者心也辨之者志
===
也考之者經也運之者才也驗之者功化
也故擬之弗精者其失也雜與之弗慎者
其失也輕析之過詳者其失也支而儒者
之學晦矣執事發策以儒道爲問豈以諸
生列儒林將以究其志乎愚非其人也敢
誦所聞以對且儒之名何始也昔唐虞三
代之際以君則曰皇曰帝曰王以臣則曰
聖曰賢曰俊乂曰忠良而儒之名不少槩
見何哉蓋是時明良交會世運方隆非無
punctuated:
原於天地，散於民物，流行於古今，待人而行者也。儒者之學，非他也，統天地之心，握民物之紀，貫古今之緒，以待後學者也。是故明此以立本，則盡性而至命焉；明此以達用，則政立而敎彰焉；明此而得位，則爲君爲相焉；明此而不得位，則爲師爲弟子焉；以脩於家，則宗族鄉黨孚化焉；以行於天下，則中外遠邇歸心焉。是豈有二道，亦豈有二學也哉！故主之者心也，辨之者志也，考之者經也，運之者才也，驗之者功化也。故擬之弗精者，其失也雜；與之弗慎者，其失也輕；析之過詳者，其失也支，而儒者之學晦矣。
執事發策，以儒道爲問，豈以諸生列儒林，將以究其志乎？愚非其人也，敢誦所聞以對。且儒之名何始也？昔唐、虞、三代之際，以君則曰皇、曰帝、曰王，以臣則曰聖、曰賢、曰俊乂、曰忠良，而儒之名不少槩見，何哉？蓋是時明良交會，世運方隆，非無…
translation_en:
…originates in Heaven and Earth, is dispersed among the people and things, flows through antiquity and the present, and awaits human beings in order to be put into practice. The learning of the Confucian scholar (ru) is nothing other than this: it unites the mind of Heaven and Earth, grasps the ordering principles of the people and things, and threads together the continuity of antiquity and the present so as to await later learners. Therefore, when one illuminates this to establish the fundamental root, one fully realizes one's nature and reaches the decree of Heaven; when one illuminates this to achieve practical application, governance is established and moral instruction becomes manifest; when one illuminates this and attains office, one acts as sovereign or as minister; when one illuminates this and does not attain office, one acts as teacher or as disciple; when one cultivates it within the family, clansmen and neighbors are inspired and transformed in trust; when one puts it into practice throughout the realm, those within and without, far and near, turn their hearts in allegiance. How could there be two Ways in this, and how could there be two kinds of learning! Thus, that which presides over it is the mind; that which discerns it is the will; that by which it is examined is the Classics; that by which it is put into operation is talent; and that by which it is verified is meritorious transformation. Therefore, when those who model it lack precision, their failing is eclecticism; when those who grant recognition to it lack caution, their failing is superficiality; when those who analyze it are overly minute, their failing is fragmentation—and thus the learning of the Confucian scholar becomes obscured.

Your Reverence has posed this policy question inquiring into the Way of the Confucian scholar; is it not because we students are ranked in the forest of scholars and you wish to probe our aspirations? Though I am not worthy of being such a person, I venture to recite what I have heard by way of reply. Moreover, where did the name "Confucian scholar" (ru) begin? In antiquity, during the eras of Tang, Yu, and the Three Dynasties, with respect to rulers men spoke of August Ones, Emperors, and Kings, and with respect to subjects they spoke of Sages, Worthies, men of eminence and ability, and the loyal and good; yet the name "Confucian scholar" is not seen at all—why is this? Indeed, at that time enlightened rulers and worthy ministers met in harmony and the fortune of the age was flourishing; it was not that there were no…

title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
儒也夫人而爲儒也迨周公以文德致太
平而太宰之九兩大司徒之本俗始有儒
之名焉孔子以君子小人定趨向始分儒
之品焉儒行一篇詞繁意複固非聖筆也
然讀其篇章彬彬馴雅不詭于道亦聖門
之流裔爾可盡廢乎是故通天地人舉其
全也魯國之儒一人昭其實也乃或岐而
爲四爲五爲七不亦言愈詳而道愈晦乎
彼大儒小儒雅儒俗儒竝列者荀卿子之
===
言也然大與雅君子之謂也小與俗小人
之謂也奚四之云乎淳于髠荀卿愼到騶
奭與孟子同傳馬遷之史也自今觀之博
聞强記迂大閎衍果與述唐虞三代之德
者若是班乎田仲王孟游俠之儒遷固文
史之儒莊列曠達之儒良平智數之儒毛
萇鄭玄章句之儒管晏事功之儒孔孟道
德之儒此宋濂之七儒解也自今觀之游
俠曠達謬也智數事功譎也文史章句淺
punctuated: 儒也，夫人而爲儒也。迨周公以文德致太平，而太宰之「九兩」、大司徒之「本俗」，始有儒之名焉；孔子以「君子」、「小人」定趨向，始分儒之品焉。《儒行》一篇，詞繁意複，固非聖筆也；然讀其篇章，彬彬馴雅，不詭于道，亦聖門之流裔爾，可盡廢乎？是故「通天地人」，舉其全也；「魯國之儒一人」，昭其實也。乃或岐而爲四、爲五、爲七，不亦言愈詳而道愈晦乎？彼大儒、小儒、雅儒、俗儒竝列者，荀卿子之言也。然大與雅，君子之謂也；小與俗，小人之謂也，奚四之云乎？淳于髠、荀卿、愼到、騶奭與孟子同傳，馬遷之史也。自今觀之，博聞强記、迂大閎衍，果與「述唐虞三代之德」者若是班乎？田仲、王孟，游俠之儒；遷、固，文史之儒；莊、列，曠達之儒；良、平，智數之儒；毛萇、鄭玄，章句之儒；管、晏，事功之儒；孔、孟，道德之儒：此宋濂之《七儒解》也。自今觀之，游俠、曠達，謬也；智數、事功，譎也；文史、章句，淺
translation_en: …Confucian scholars (ru); rather, every person was a Confucian scholar. Only when the Duke of Zhou brought about great peace through civil virtue did the name "Confucian scholar" (ru) first appear in the "Nine Bonds" (jiuliang) of the Grand Councillor (taizai) and the "Fundamental Customs" (bensu) of the Grand Minister of Education (da situ). And when Confucius determined men's orientation by distinguishing the "gentleman-scholar" (junzi) from the "petty scholar" (xiaoren), the grades of Confucian scholars were first divided. As for the chapter "Conduct of the Scholar" (Ruxing), its wording is prolix and its ideas repetitive—it certainly did not come from the brush of the Sage. Yet when one reads its passages, they are refined, tractable, and elegant, not at variance with the Way; they too come from the later followers of the Sage's school—how could they be entirely discarded? Therefore, "penetrating the principles of Heaven, Earth, and Man" captures the whole of it; and the saying that "in the state of Lu there is but one Confucian scholar" illuminates its reality. When later thinkers branched it out into four, five, or seven types, did the Way not grow ever more obscure the more detailed their words became? Setting "great Confucians" (daru), "petty Confucians" (xiaoru), "refined Confucians" (yaru), and "vulgar Confucians" (suru) side by side was the teaching of Master Xun Qing (Xunzi). Yet "great" and "refined" are what is meant by the gentleman, while "petty" and "vulgar" are what is meant by the petty man—why speak of four? Placing Chunyu Kun, Xun Qing, Shen Dao, and Zou Shi in the same biography alongside Mencius (Mengzi)—reducing them to a group of five—was the history of Sima Qian. Viewed from today, can those characterized by "broad learning and strong memory" or by "circuitous, grandiose, and sprawling discourse" truly be ranked on a par with one who "transmitted the virtue of Tang, Yu, and the Three Dynasties"? Taking Tian Zhong and Wang Meng as "Confucians of wandering knight-errantry," Sima Qian and Ban Gu as "Confucians of literature and history," Zhuangzi and Liezi as "Confucians of untrammeled detachment," Zhang Liang and Chen Ping as "Confucians of strategic calculation," Mao Chang and Zheng Xuan as "Confucians of chapter-and-verse exegesis," Guan Zhong and Yan Ying as "Confucians of practical achievement," and Confucius and Mencius as "Confucians of the Way and virtue"—this is Song Lian's Explication of the Seven Types of Confucians (Qiru jie).
