Viewed from today, knight-errantry and untrammeled detachment are aberrant; strategic calculation and practical achievement are crafty; literature, history, and chapter-and-verse exegesis are shallow…

title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
也豈道全德備者可竝論乎然司馬談敘
六家指要列儒于道法之後遷史蓋有所
受矣韓愈論二家相用援墨于儒道之中
宋氏亦囿于見矣若是者皆不知儒道之
大也豈不失之雜乎自是而後此義益微
當漢之時六學殘缺則尚訓詁故儒林傳
所載丁寬施讎劉昆洼丹輩爾而賢如董
仲舒下帷發憤潛心大業先儒謂有儒者
氣象乃別為傳述豈以繁露諸篇非專門
===
===
訓詁者比耶則漢之所謂儒可知巳唐之
時正學晦蝕則尚疏義故儒學傳所載顏
師古孔穎達輩爾賢如韓愈文本六經心
存仁義論者謂起八代之衰乃亦別為傳
述豈以原道諸篇非專經討論者比耶則
唐之所謂儒可知巳宋承五季之後聖學
日雜故尚理學作史者乃以胡瑗蔡元定
陸九淵眞德秀列諸儒林而周敦頤程顥
兄弟張載朱熹而下又別為道學豈以周
punctuated: 也，豈道全德備者可竝論乎？然司馬談敘六家指要，列儒于道、法之後，遷史蓋有所受矣；韓愈論二家相用，援墨于儒道之中，宋氏亦囿于見矣。若是者，皆不知儒道之大也，豈不失之雜乎？自是而後，此義益微。當漢之時，六學殘缺，則尚訓詁，故《儒林傳》所載丁寬、施讎、劉昆、洼丹輩爾；而賢如董仲舒，下帷發憤，潛心大業，先儒謂有儒者氣象，乃別為傳述，豈以《繁露》諸篇非專門訓詁者比耶？則漢之所謂儒可知巳。唐之時，正學晦蝕，則尚疏義，故《儒學傳》所載顏師古、孔穎達輩爾；賢如韓愈，文本六經，心存仁義，論者謂起八代之衰，乃亦別為傳述，豈以《原道》諸篇非專經討論者比耶？則唐之所謂儒可知巳。宋承五季之後，聖學日雜，故尚理學，作史者乃以胡瑗、蔡元定、陸九淵、眞德秀列諸《儒林》，而周敦頤、程顥兄弟、張載、朱熹而下又別為《道學》，豈以周、
translation_en:
… How could they be discussed on an equal footing with those whose Way is complete and whose virtue is fully realized? Yet Sima Tan 司馬談, in his account of the essential ideas of the Six Schools (Liujia zhiyao 六家指要), ranked the Confucians after the Daoists and Legalists, so Sima Qian's 司馬遷 history doubtless inherited this view; and Han Yu 韓愈, in discussing how the two schools drew upon each other, pulled Mozi 墨子 into the fold of the Confucian Way, so Master Song [Song Lian 宋濂] was likewise blinkered by precedent. All such cases failed to understand the greatness of the Confucian Way; did they not err on the side of promiscuous admixture?

From that time onward, this true meaning grew ever more obscure. During the Han dynasty, the Six Arts were fragmented and incomplete, so scholars prized philological glossing (xungu 訓詁). Thus the "Biographies of Confucian Scholars" (Rulin zhuan 儒林傳) recorded only the likes of Ding Kuan 丁寬, Shi Chou 施讎, Liu Kun 劉昆, and Gui Dan 洼丹. Meanwhile, a worthy such as Dong Zhongshu 董仲舒—who lowered his curtain and applied himself with fervent determination, immersing his mind in the great enterprise, and whom earlier Confucians described as possessing the true bearing of a Confucian—was instead given a separate biography. Was this not because the chapters of his Luxuriant Gems of the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu fanlu 春秋繁露) were not comparable to the work of specialists in philological glossing? From this, what the Han meant by "Confucian" can readily be known.

During the Tang dynasty, orthodox learning was eclipsed and obscured, so scholars prized subcommentaries and exegesis (shuyi 疏義). Thus the "Biographies of Confucian Scholars" (Ruxue zhuan 儒學傳) recorded only the likes of Yan Shigu 顏師古 and Kong Yingda 孔穎達. A worthy such as Han Yu—whose writings were rooted in the Six Classics, whose mind abided in humanity and righteousness, and whom critics credited with revitalizing literature from the decline of eight dynasties—was likewise given a separate biography. Was this not because essays such as his "Essentials of the Moral Way" (Yuan Dao 原道) were not comparable to the specialized textual discussions of a single classic? From this, what the Tang meant by "Confucian" can readily be known.

After the Song succeeded the Five Dynasties, sage learning had grown daily more eclectic, so scholars prized the learning of principle (lixue 理學). The compilers of the dynastic history accordingly placed Hu Yuan 胡瑗, Cai Yuanding 蔡元定, Lu Jiuyuan 陸九淵, and Zhen Dexiu 眞德秀 in the "Biographies of Confucian Scholars" (Rulin 儒林), while setting up a separate section on "Learning of the Way" (Daoxue 道學) for Zhou Dunyi 周敦頤, Cheng Hao 程顥 and his brother [Cheng Yi 程頤], Zhang Zai 張載, Zhu Xi 朱熹, and their followers. Was this not because Zhou…

title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
程諸子者得孔孟之正傳而非儒林可槩
乎夫道不行百世無善治學不傳千載無
眞儒未有道而非儒亦未有儒而不本于
道者也今乃分傳焉何其視儒之輕而岐
道于二乎竊意宋史旣創道學傳則儒林
不當復見周程張朱固爲正宗矣其餘諸
子或同時或生乎前後其聲應氣求獨非
羽翼斯道者乎而胡可別也然考漢人論
序惟錄通經名家之徒唐人紀載祗取誦
===
習傳授之學則宋史別儒林於道學亦因
陋承誤爾若是者亦不知儒道之大也其
不失之輕乎元儒劉因又爲之說曰周至
精邵至大程至正朱子極大盡精而貫之
以正蓋于圖書之旨見其精也于經世之
書見其大也于辨異端闢邪說見其正也
于居敬窮理反躬見其集諸儒之大成也
初讀之未甞不快其言之當徐而察之大
非淪于粗也正非局于器也毋亦言之詳
punctuated: 程諸子者，得孔、孟之正傳，而非儒林可槩乎？夫道不行，百世無善治；學不傳，千載無眞儒。未有道而非儒，亦未有儒而不本于道者也。今乃分傳焉，何其視儒之輕而岐道于二乎？竊意《宋史》旣創〈道學傳〉，則〈儒林〉不當復見。周、程、張、朱固爲正宗矣，其餘諸子，或同時，或生乎前後，其聲應氣求，獨非羽翼斯道者乎？而胡可別也！然考漢人論序，惟錄通經名家之徒；唐人紀載，祗取誦習傳授之學。則《宋史》別〈儒林〉於〈道學〉，亦因陋承誤爾。若是者，亦不知儒道之大也，其不失之輕乎？元儒劉因又爲之說曰：「周至精，邵至大，程至正，朱子極大盡精而貫之以正。」蓋于圖書之旨見其精也，于《經世》之書見其大也，于辨異端、闢邪說見其正也，于居敬、窮理、反躬見其集諸儒之大成也。初讀之，未甞不快其言之當；徐而察之，大非淪于粗也，正非局于器也，毋亦言之詳
translation_en:
…and Master Cheng [Cheng Hao 程顥 and Cheng Yi 程頤], and the other masters obtained the orthodox transmission of Confucius and Mencius, and thus could not simply be grouped under the "Forest of Confucians" (Rulin 儒林)? Now, if the Way is not practiced, for a hundred generations there will be no good governance; if learning is not transmitted, for a thousand years there will be no true Confucians. There has never been the Way that is not Confucian, nor has there ever been a Confucian who is not rooted in the Way. Yet now they are given separate biographies—how lightly does this regard "Confucians," and how does it bifurcate the Way into two! In my humble opinion, since the History of the Song (Songshi 宋史) already established the "Biographies of the Learning of the Way" (Daoxue zhuan 道學傳), the "Forest of Confucians" should no longer have appeared. Zhou [Zhou Dunyi 周敦頤], the Cheng brothers, Zhang [Zhang Zai 張載], and Zhu [Zhu Xi 朱熹] were assuredly the orthodox lineage; as for the remaining masters, whether contemporaries or born before or after them, responding to one another in voice and seeking one another in spirit, were they not also wings aiding this Way? How then could they be separated? Yet when we examine the discussions and prefaces of the Han historians, they recorded only famous specialists well-versed in the Classics; and the records of the Tang writers selected merely the learning of recitation, practice, and textual transmission. Thus, for the History of the Song to separate the "Forest of Confucians" from the "Learning of the Way" was merely following narrow conventions and inheriting past errors. To act like this is also to fail to understand the greatness of the Confucian Way; does it not err in taking it too lightly?

The Yuan Confucian Liu Yin 劉因 further formulated a theory about them, saying: "Zhou was most subtle, Shao [Shao Yong 邵雍] was most vast, the Chengs were most correct, and Master Zhu reached the utmost vastness and exhausted the utmost subtlety, threading them together with correctness." This is because he saw Zhou's subtlety in the purport of the Diagram [Taijitu 太極圖] and the Book [Tongshu 通書]; he saw Shao's vastness in the Book of Supreme World-Ordering (Huangji jingshi shu 皇極經世書); he saw the Chengs' correctness in their distinguishing of heterodoxies and refuting of perverse doctrines; and he saw Master Zhu's great synthesis of all the Confucians in his abiding in reverence, exhausting principle, and self-reflection. When one first reads this, one cannot help but be pleased by the aptness of his words. Yet when one examines it unhurriedly, vastness does not mean sinking into coarseness, and correctness does not mean being confined to concrete vessels; is his statement not perhaps so detailed…

title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
而過于析歟宋濂又復舉宋諸儒之學而
竝論之曰永嘉曰永康曰金谿曰橫浦則
各有所評焉若金華若廣漢若武夷則獨
有所取焉是其微意要自有在以愚言之
摘其微而議之者方人之事取其長而師
之者爲己之功況諸君子入道之途雖有
異同非判然黑白若前之五儒七儒之辨
也豈暇雌黃于其間哉嗚呼道一也儒者
之學亦一也一則精精則不可雜陳矣一
===
===
則大大則不可輕與矣一則全全則不可
過析矣而諸說紛紛何以明道於天下也
哉洪惟
聖祖開天崇儒重道經書傳註頒布學宮
列聖紹統聿申
謨訓教一文同天下士皆知崇正學廸正道
不以異說參之故今人才輩出光輔
盛治儒者之効昭著一時矣董仲舒所謂百
家殊方指意不同者非今所患也韓愈所
punctuated: 而過于析歟？宋濂又復舉宋諸儒之學而竝論之，曰永嘉、曰永康、曰金谿、曰橫浦，則各有所評焉；若金華、若廣漢、若武夷，則獨有所取焉，是其微意要自有在。以愚言之，摘其微而議之者，方人之事；取其長而師之者，爲己之功。況諸君子入道之途雖有異同，非判然黑白若前之五儒、七儒之辨也，豈暇雌黃于其間哉！嗚呼！道一也，儒者之學亦一也。一則精，精則不可雜陳矣；一則大，大則不可輕與矣；一則全，全則不可過析矣。而諸說紛紛，何以明道於天下也哉！洪惟聖祖開天，崇儒重道，經書傳註，頒布學宮；列聖紹統，聿申謨訓，教一文同，天下士皆知崇正學、廸正道，不以異說參之。故今人才輩出，光輔盛治，儒者之効，昭著一時矣。董仲舒所謂「百家殊方，指意不同」者，非今所患也；韓愈所
translation_en:
… and yet overly analytical? Song Lian 宋濂 furthermore brought together the learning of the various Song-dynasty Confucians and discussed them side by side. Regarding the schools of Yongjia 永嘉, Yongkang 永康, Jinxi 金谿, and Hengpu 橫浦, he had criticisms for each; whereas regarding those of Jinhua 金華 [Lü Zuqian], Guanghan 廣漢 [Zhang Shi], and Wuyi 武夷 [Zhu Xi], he singled them out for approval. In this, his subtle intent certainly had its own point. In my humble opinion, picking out subtle flaws to criticize them is the business of comparing others, whereas taking their strengths to emulate them is the work of self-cultivation. Moreover, although the paths by which these gentlemen entered the Way had their differences and similarities, they are not as starkly black-and-white as the aforementioned distinctions among the "five types of Confucians" or "seven types of Confucians." How could one have the leisure to sit in arbitrary judgment over them?

Alas! The Way is one, and the learning of Confucians is also one. Being one, it is pure, and being pure, it cannot be set forth in a motley manner; being one, it is great, and being great, it cannot be lightly granted; being one, it is complete, and being complete, it cannot be overly dissected. Yet with all these theories proliferating in confusion, how can the Way be made clear to the world?

We reverently reflect how our Sacred Progenitor founded the dynasty, honoring Confucians and revering the Way, and promulgated the Classics and their commentaries to the schools; and how the successive Sacred Emperors inherited the line, reiterating the grand instructions, so that education is unified and writing standardized, and scholars throughout the realm all know to revere orthodox learning and follow the orthodox Way without adulterating it with heterodox theories. Therefore, talents now emerge in succession to gloriously assist our flourishing rule, and the efficacy of Confucians is brilliantly manifest in our time. What Dong Zhongshu 董仲舒 called "the hundred schools pursuing different directions with diverging aims" is not what we need to worry about today; what Han Yu 韓愈…

title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
謂入主出奴入附出汙者非今所憂也程
氏所謂彌近理而大亂眞者非今所慮也
愚謂今之急者其責士以實行乎蓋論儒
於聖學未明之前擇之不可不精論儒於
聖學旣明之後行之不可不力今天下士
日盛矣文日昌矣乃或闊議論而缺反躬
貴詞華而略名檢析玄奧而忽切近駕成
說而炫已見儒云儒云豈是之謂哉夫道
非難行也孔子曰道不遠人孟子曰人人
===
親其親長其長而天下平歸而求之有餘
師是豈待辨說者哉誠使今之爲儒者於
家庭倫理之間食息起居之際辭受取與
之節謹而不踰是卽所謂君子儒而孔孟
程朱之徒也雖議論微有不同吾且將師
之而况粹然出于正者乎若越禮義之閑
忽孝弟之義蔑存省之功弛廉靖之防卽
使日誦虞廷危微精一之言孔門博約一
貫之旨祇爲口耳之學爾吾何取焉故曰
punctuated: 謂「入主出奴，入附出汙」者，非今所憂也；程氏所謂「彌近理而大亂眞」者，非今所慮也。愚謂今之急者，其責士以實行乎！蓋論儒於聖學未明之前，擇之不可不精；論儒於聖學旣明之後，行之不可不力。今天下士日盛矣，文日昌矣，乃或闊議論而缺反躬，貴詞華而略名檢，析玄奧而忽切近，駕成說而炫已見，「儒云儒云」，豈是之謂哉！夫道非難行也。孔子曰：「道不遠人。」孟子曰：「人人親其親，長其長，而天下平。」「歸而求之，有餘師。」是豈待辨說者哉？誠使今之爲儒者，於家庭倫理之間、食息起居之際、辭受取與之節，謹而不踰，是卽所謂君子儒，而孔、孟、程、朱之徒也。雖議論微有不同，吾且將師之，而况粹然出于正者乎！若越禮義之閑，忽孝弟之義，蔑存省之功，弛廉靖之防，卽使日誦虞廷「危微精一」之言、孔門「博約一貫」之旨，祇爲口耳之學爾，吾何取焉！故曰：
translation_en: … called "treating one's own school as master and others as slaves, clinging to those inside and slandering those outside," is not what we worry about today; what the Cheng brothers (Cheng Yi 程頤 and Cheng Hao 程顥) called "coming ever closer to principle while greatly confounding the truth," is not what we are concerned about today. In my humble opinion, what is urgent today is surely holding scholars accountable for their actual conduct! For when discussing Confucians before the Sagely Learning had been clarified, one's selection among teachings could not but be precise; when discussing Confucians after the Sagely Learning has been clarified, one's practice of it cannot but be vigorous. Today, scholars throughout the realm grow ever more numerous by the day, and literary culture flourishes ever more brightly by the day. Yet some indulge in grandiose discourse while lacking self-reflection, prize华丽 rhetoric while neglecting moral integrity, dissect abstruse mysteries while overlooking what is close at hand, and override established doctrines to show off their own views. "A Confucian, a Confucian, they say"—is this what is meant by the term?! Now, the Way is not difficult to practice. Confucius (Kongzi 孔子) said, "The Way is not far from man." Mencius (Mengzi 孟子) said, "If everyone would love his parents and treat his elders as elders, the whole realm would be at peace," and "Go home and seek it, and you will have more than enough teachers." Does this require disputation and theorizing? Truly, if those who act as Confucians today are careful and do not transgress amidst family human relations, in moments of eating, resting, and daily life, and in the integrity of declining or accepting, giving or taking—this is precisely what is called a "gentleman Confucian" (junzi ru), and a follower of Confucius, Mencius, the Cheng brothers, and Zhu Xi 朱熹. Even if their discussions differ slightly, I would still take them as my teachers—how much more so if they issue purely from orthodoxy! If, however, one oversteps the bounds of ritual and righteousness, neglects the principles of filial piety and brotherly respect, scorns the effort of preserving the mind and self-examination, and relaxes the defenses of integrity and quietude, then even if one daily recites the words of the Yu court on the "precarious and subtle, refined and single-minded," or the doctrines of the Confucian school on "broad learning, restraint through ritual, and a single thread," it is merely learning of the mouth and ear—what use do I have for it?! Therefore it is said: …

title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
與其行不足而言有餘也不若言不足而
行有餘也又曰天下有道則行有枝葉為
儒者豈必他求哉于己取之而已矣是故
知儒道之出于一則不可以輕擬知儒道
之貴于行則不在於繁言謹對
第四問
李敷華
同考試官教諭劉批將家者流材品靡一此作摭采悉
評隲當而以天下之將屬之郭中令是千古確論至陳選任將
===
帥之道尤鑿鑿可行非經生漫語也敬羡敬羡
考試官教授蔡批天下未甞無將顧所以選任之者
何如爾子能亹亹談之謂子碩俊士非邪
考試官教授朱批該而中腴而不浮
執事發策承學而以將材下詢因及所以
選將之道愚生鉛槧士也不習介胄之技
安足奉條對哉顧詮伏草莽甞聽鼓鼙而
思將帥久矣敢誦所聞以復執事試垂聽
焉夫將者國之輔也輔周則國强輔隙則
punctuated:
「與其行不足而言有餘也，不若言不足而行有餘也。」又曰：「天下有道，則行有枝葉。」為儒者豈必他求哉？于己取之而已矣。是故知儒道之出于一，則不可以輕擬；知儒道之貴于行，則不在於繁言。謹對。

第四問
李敷華
同考試官教諭劉批：將家者流，材品靡一。此作摭采悉，評隲當，而以天下之將屬之郭中令，是千古確論。至陳選任將帥之道，尤鑿鑿可行，非經生漫語也。敬羡，敬羡！
考試官教授蔡批：天下未甞無將，顧所以選任之者何如爾。子能亹亹談之，謂子碩俊士，非邪？
考試官教授朱批：該而中，腴而不浮。

執事發策承學，而以將材下詢，因及所以選將之道。愚生鉛槧士也，不習介胄之技，安足奉條對哉？顧詮伏草莽，甞聽鼓鼙而思將帥久矣，敢誦所聞以復，執事試垂聽焉。夫將者，國之輔也；輔周則國强，輔隙則
translation_en:
… "Rather than one's conduct being insufficient while one's words are in excess, it is better for one's words to be insufficient while one's conduct is in excess." And it is also said: "When the Way prevails in the world, conduct puts forth branches and leaves." Why must one who acts as a Confucian scholar seek elsewhere? One simply draws it from oneself and nothing more. Therefore, knowing that the Way of the Confucian issues from unity, one must not lightly make comparisons; knowing that the Way of the Confucian places value on conduct, it does not lie in prolix words. Respectfully replied.

Fourth Policy Question
Li Fuhua 李敷華
Comment by Associate Examiner Instructor Liu 劉: Among those of the school of military commanders, talents and qualities are far from uniform. This essay gathers its materials thoroughly and evaluates them aptly, and in assigning the title of commander for the whole realm to Secretariat Director Guo 郭 [Guo Ziyi 郭子儀], it states an indisputable judgment for all ages. As for setting forth the way of selecting and appointing commanders, it is especially concrete and practicable, not the idle talk of a mere student of the classics. Truly admirable, truly admirable!
Comment by Examiner Confucian School Professor Cai 蔡: The world has never lacked commanders; it is only a question of how they are selected and appointed. You are able to discourse on this tirelessly—would it be wrong to call you a great and outstanding scholar?
Comment by Examiner Confucian School Professor Zhu 朱: Comprehensive yet hitting the mark; rich yet not superficial.

Your Honor has posed a policy question to us junior scholars, inquiring of us regarding military talent, and thereby touching upon the way of selecting commanders. I, a foolish student, am a scholar of writing tablets and brushes, unpracticed in the skills of armor and helmet; how could I be worthy of offering a point-by-point reply? Yet while living in obscurity among the weeds and brush, I have long heard the war drums and thought of great commanders; I venture to recite what I have heard by way of reply, if Your Honor would deign to listen. Now, the commander is the bulwark of the state: when the bulwark is complete, the state is strong; when the bulwark is flawed, …

title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
國弱將之有繫于人國也厥惟重矣粤自
鷹揚奮于八百尚父流聲車徒陳于六月
元戎茂績三傑當逐鹿之秋肆翼炎祚雲
臺繪功臣之像庸顯中興故有一代之明
君則必有一代之良將應運而生佐命而
起謀臣猛士雲合風從或讚帷幄之算或
奉疆場之任皆能建鉅勛于當年垂鴻名
于來禩曷甞借材于異代哉然將之材未
易言也不知古今乃匹夫之勇而徒讀父
===
書者適足以僨師臨難決疑非一劔之任
而謀定後戰者始可以揚伐甞觀孔子論
行軍之道則曰臨事而懼好謀而成剛勇
罔謀者不得與焉噫斯言也其萬世為將
者之矩矱乎夫將一也有一軍之將有一
國之將有天下之將一軍之將茭敵搴旗
以力勝者也將之下也一國之將折衝夷
難以智勝者也將之次也所謂天下之將
則勳庸在社稷精忠貫日月以德勝者也
punctuated: 國弱。將之有繫于人國也，厥惟重矣！粤自鷹揚奮于八百，尚父流聲；車徒陳于六月，元戎茂績。三傑當逐鹿之秋，肆翼炎祚；雲臺繪功臣之像，庸顯中興。故有一代之明君，則必有一代之良將，應運而生，佐命而起。謀臣猛士，雲合風從，或讚帷幄之算，或奉疆場之任，皆能建鉅勛于當年，垂鴻名于來禩，曷甞借材于異代哉？然將之材未易言也。不知古今，乃匹夫之勇，而徒讀父書者，適足以僨師；臨難決疑，非一劔之任，而謀定後戰者，始可以揚伐。甞觀孔子論行軍之道，則曰：「臨事而懼，好謀而成。」剛勇罔謀者，不得與焉。噫！斯言也，其萬世為將者之矩矱乎！夫將一也，有一軍之將，有一國之將，有天下之將。一軍之將，茭敵搴旗，以力勝者也，將之下也；一國之將，折衝夷難，以智勝者也，將之次也；所謂天下之將，則勳庸在社稷，精忠貫日月，以德勝者也，
translation_en:
… then the state is weak. The bearing that a general has upon a state is weighty indeed! Ever since the eagle-like soaring roused the eight hundred諸侯, Grand Father [Lü Shang 呂尚] left behind a lasting reputation; and when chariots and foot soldiers were arrayed in the sixth month, the Supreme Commander [Yin Jifu 尹吉甫] achieved splendid merit. The Three Heroes [Xiao He 蕭何, Zhang Liang 張良, and Han Xin 韓信], in the season of chasing the deer of empire, exerted themselves to assist the fiery fortune of Han; and the Cloud Terrace, painted with portraits of meritorious ministers, thereby manifested the dynastic restoration. Therefore, whenever there is an enlightened ruler of an age, there are certain to be fine generals of that age, born in response to the turn of destiny and rising up to aid the Mandate. Counseling ministers and fierce warriors gather like clouds and follow like the wind; whether assisting with calculations within the command tent or receiving charges on the frontier battlefields, all are able to establish great merit in their own time and hand down illustrious names to future generations. When did one ever have to borrow talent from another era?

Yet the talent required of a general is not easy to speak of. One who does not know antiquity and the present possesses merely the bravery of a common fellow, while one who merely reads his father's books [like Zhao Kuo 趙括] is just sufficient to ruin an army. Facing crisis and resolving doubts is not the task of a single swordsman; only one who settles upon a strategy before going to battle can display martial prowess in punitive campaigns. I have observed how Confucius discussed the Way of conducting an army, saying: "Approach affairs with reverent caution, andbe fond of planning so as to bring them to completion." Those who are fiercely brave but lack strategy are not permitted to take part. Alas! Are not these words the standard and rule for generals for ten thousand generations?

Now, while the title of "general" is one, there is the general of a single army, the general of a single state, and the general of All-under-Heaven. The general of a single army mows down [?] the enemy and captures flags, conquering through strength; he is the lowest grade of general. The general of a single state repulses enemy assaults and pacifies difficulties, conquering through wisdom; he is the next grade of general. As for what is called the general of All-under-Heaven, his meritorious service rests with the altars of soil and grain, and his pure loyalty pierces the sun and moon; conquering through virtue, …

title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
將之上也德者何敬而已語在蘭陵論將
篇其言由制號政令以及遇敵決戰爲六
術由無欲將惡廢以及慮事用財爲五權
由不受命于主有三爲三至敬謀敬事敬
吏敬衆敬敵爲五無壙愼行六術五權三
至而處之以恭敬無壙夫是之謂天下之
將通于神明矣有味哉其言之也恭敬云
者非孔子所謂臨事之懼乎善將者能由
玆道則孫子之所語爲將五術如曰智曰
===
仁曰信勇嚴皆得其全體蘇明允氏之所
謂賢將亶其人也奚翅稱才將哉愚嘗逖
覽往古名將斌斌史冊未可更僕數也然
求其可居天下將者誰歟試即明問所及
者熟數而細評之文能附衆武能威敵者
穰苴也爲齊捍燕晉之師莊賈監軍後期
而至即斬以徇其申令何嚴矣故穰苴兵
法後世譚兵者必宗焉大將軍衞青擊匈
奴裨將蘇建盡亡其軍于法不宥乃具歸
punctuated:
將之上也。德者何？敬而已。語在蘭陵《論將篇》。其言由制號政令以及遇敵決戰爲「六術」，由無欲將、惡廢以及慮事、用財爲「五權」，由不受命于主有三爲「三至」，敬謀、敬事、敬吏、敬衆、敬敵爲「五無壙」。愼行六術、五權、三至，而處之以恭敬無壙，夫是之謂天下之將，通于神明矣。有味哉，其言之也！恭敬云者，非孔子所謂臨事之懼乎？善將者能由玆道，則孫子之所語爲將五術，如曰智、曰仁、曰信、勇、嚴，皆得其全體。蘇明允氏之所謂賢將，亶其人也，奚翅稱才將哉！
愚嘗逖覽往古，名將斌斌史冊，未可更僕數也，然求其可居天下將者誰歟？試即明問所及者熟數而細評之：文能附衆、武能威敵者，穰苴也。爲齊捍燕、晉之師，莊賈監軍，後期而至，即斬以徇，其申令何嚴矣！故《穰苴兵法》，後世譚兵者必宗焉。大將軍衞青擊匈奴，裨將蘇建盡亡其軍，于法不宥，乃具歸
translation_en:
… This is the highest class of general. And what is this virtue? It is simply reverence. The words are found in the Master of Lanling's [Xunzi's] "Discourse on Generals" (Lun jiang pian). There he speaks of the "Six Arts," ranging from establishing signals and administrative orders to encountering the enemy and fighting a decisive battle; the "Five Prerogatives," ranging from not desiring to appoint or dismiss out of personal preference to deliberating on affairs and expending wealth; the "Three Absolutes," consisting of the three instances in which one does not accept orders from the ruler; and the "Five Unremitting Reverences" [wu wu kuang], namely revering plans, revering affairs, revering officers, revering the multitude, and revering the enemy. Carefully practicing the Six Arts, the Five Prerogatives, and the Three Absolutes, while conducting oneself with unremitting respect and reverence—this is what is called a general of the All-under-Heaven, whose insight communicates with the spirits! How meaningful are these words! Is not what he calls "respect and reverence" precisely what Confucius meant by "approaching affairs with apprehension"? If a good general can follow this Way, then the five qualities of a general spoken of by Master Sun [Sunzi]—namely wisdom, benevolence, trustworthiness, courage, and strictness—will all be realized in their entirety. What Su Mingyun [Su Xun 蘇洵] called a "worthy general" is truly such a person; how could he merely be called a "talented general"!

I have surveyed antiquity from afar: famous generals shine brightly in the historical records, too numerous to count even if one changed attendants, yet if we seek one worthy to occupy the place of a general of the All-under-Heaven, who would it be? Let me take those touched upon in the insightful question, enumerate them thoroughly, and evaluate them in detail. He whose civil virtue could win the attachment of the multitude and whose martial prowess could awe the enemy was Rangju [Sima Rangju 司馬穰苴]. Defending Qi against the armies of Yan and Jin, when the Army Supervisor Zhuang Jia 莊賈 arrived past the appointed time, Rangju immediately beheaded him to make an example to the troops—how strict was his enforcement of orders! Thus the Military Methods of Rangju (Rangju bingfa) was invariably revered as a model by later generations who discussed warfare. When General-in-Chief Wei Qing 衞青 attacked the Xiongnu, his Deputy General Su Jian 蘇建 lost his entire army. Under the law this could not be pardoned, yet Wei Qing sent him back in full custody for…

title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
天子自裁之蓋不敢席肺腑之寵擅專誅
于境外爾史著其以和柔自媚于上天下
靡得而稱述之誠知言哉臥不設席行不
騎乘者吳起也為魏將擊秦親裹餱糧與
士卒最下者同衣食其待下亦仁矣然卒
以刻暴少恩亡其軀仁安在焉驃騎將軍
霍去病封狼居胥禪姑衍厥功不世乃還
軍重車餘梁肉而士有饑者蓋其少而侍
中貴不省士爾然為將尚方略匈奴未滅
===
無心治第又可盡訾耶程李東西衞尉也
廣軍無部伍行陣就善水草屯舍止不擊
刁斗未甞遇害不識正部曲行伍營陣士
吏治軍簿至明軍不休息虜亦不得犯其
時士卒樂從廣之簡而苦不識之煩然廣
之勇氣無雙名震匈奴結髮從軍大小七
十餘戰竟以數奇不侯千載而下猶為扼
腕彼不識廑廑謹于文法惡足軼聲飛將
也李郭齊名一時也光弼嚴毅沈果治師
punctuated: 天子自裁之，蓋不敢席肺腑之寵，擅專誅于境外爾。史著其以和柔自媚于上，天下靡得而稱述之，誠知言哉！臥不設席、行不騎乘者，吳起也。為魏將擊秦，親裹餱糧，與士卒最下者同衣食，其待下亦仁矣。然卒以刻暴少恩亡其軀，仁安在焉？驃騎將軍霍去病封狼居胥、禪姑衍，厥功不世。乃還軍，重車餘梁肉，而士有饑者，蓋其少而侍中，貴不省士爾。然為將尚方略，匈奴未滅，無心治第，又可盡訾耶？程、李，東西衞尉也。廣軍無部伍行陣，就善水草屯舍，止不擊刁斗，未甞遇害；不識正部曲行伍營陣，士吏治軍簿至明，軍不休息，虜亦不得犯。其時士卒樂從廣之簡，而苦不識之煩。然廣之勇氣無雙，名震匈奴，結髮從軍，大小七十餘戰，竟以數奇不侯，千載而下，猶為扼腕。彼不識廑廑謹于文法，惡足軼聲飛將也？李、郭，齊名一時也。光弼嚴毅沈果，治師
translation_en:
… the Son of Heaven to decide the matter himself, for he did not dare presume upon the favor he enjoyed as an intimate relative of the imperial house to arrogate the power of execution beyond the borders. The history notes that he ingratiated himself with his sovereign through compliant gentleness, so that no one in the empire found anything in him to praise—truly discerning words!

He who did not spread a mat when sleeping and did not ride a mount or carriage when marching was Wu Qi 吳起. Serving as a general of Wei 魏 to attack Qin 秦, he personally wrapped up his own dry provisions and shared the same clothing and food as the lowest of his soldiers; his treatment of his subordinates was indeed benevolent. Yet in the end he lost his life through harshness, brutality, and a lack of grace—where, then, was his benevolence?

The General of Agile Cavalry (Piaoji jiangjun 驃騎將軍), Huo Qubing 霍去病, performed the feng sacrifice at Mount Langjuxu 狼居胥 and the shan sacrifice at Guyan 姑衍, achieving merits unmatched in his age. Yet when his army returned, his heavy supply wagons had a surplus of fine grain and meat while some of his soldiers went hungry; this was simply because he had served as a Palace Attendant (Shizhong 侍中) from youth and, being of noble status, was inconsiderate of his troops. Even so, as a general he valued strategic planning, and declaring that so long as the Xiongnu 匈奴 were not yet destroyed he had no heart to tend to a personal residence—how can he be wholly disparaged?

Cheng [Bushi] 程不識 and Li [Guang] 李廣 served as the Commandant of the Guards (Weiwei 衞尉) of the Eastern and Western Palaces. Li Guang's army maintained no fixed divisions or battle formations; it camped wherever there was good water and grass, and at night stops did not strike the watchman's kettle, yet it never met with disaster. Cheng Bushi kept his divisions, ranks, and camp formations strictly aligned; his officers and clerks attended to the military registers until dawn so the army got no rest, yet the northern raiders likewise could not violate his lines. At the time, the soldiers gladly followed Li Guang's simplicity and found Cheng Bushi's繁 [tediousness] burdensome. Moreover, Li Guang's courage was peerless and his renown shook the Xiongnu; from the time he first bound up his hair to join the army, he fought in more than seventy battles large and small, yet because of ill fortune he was never enfeoffed as a marquis—a thousand years later, people still wring their wrists in sighing regret over him. As for Cheng Bushi, who was merely cautious about rules and regulations, how could he suffice to surpass the fame of the "Flying General" (Feijiang 飛將)?

Li [Guangbi] 李光弼 and Guo [Ziyi] 郭子儀 enjoyed equal renown in their time. Li Guangbi was stern, resolute, composed, and decisive, governing his troops…

title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
訓整始至朔方斬張用濟而軍中爲之股
慄子儀恕以御下賞罰必信頤指宿將若
部曲然而寬厚得人過之其時將士樂子
儀之寬而憚光弼之嚴然子儀略平大難
再造王室屢遭讒間聞命就道無纖芥顧
望以身繫天下安危者二十年完名高節
爛然獨著若光弼被搆奄寺遂陷嫌郄而
拙于謀巳君子有遺慨焉合而觀之由數
子致用之異以定數子爲將之品汾陽賢
===
將哉其天下乎臨淮蓋庶幾焉衛霍而下
並稱才將矣未可一律論也雖然之數子
者莫不際時遘會而當時之君亦皆能慎
選而善任之以盡其用固宜休烈顯乎無
窮聲稱浹乎千兹也已方
今天下之患北搆于胡南挂于越邇者雲中
上谷黠虜雖款關矣而薊鎮遼左尤滋訌
焉東西兩粵捷書雖交馳矣而山海殘孽
日蠢蠢也
punctuated: 訓整，始至朔方，斬張用濟，而軍中爲之股慄；子儀恕以御下，賞罰必信，頤指宿將若部曲然，而寬厚得人過之。其時將士樂子儀之寬，而憚光弼之嚴。然子儀略平大難，再造王室，屢遭讒間，聞命就道，無纖芥顧望，以身繫天下安危者二十年，完名高節，爛然獨著；若光弼被搆奄寺，遂陷嫌郄，而拙于謀巳，君子有遺慨焉。合而觀之，由數子致用之異，以定數子爲將之品，汾陽賢將哉！其天下乎！臨淮蓋庶幾焉，衛、霍而下，並稱才將矣，未可一律論也。雖然，之數子者，莫不際時遘會，而當時之君，亦皆能慎選而善任之，以盡其用，固宜休烈顯乎無窮，聲稱浹乎千兹也已。方今天下之患，北搆于胡，南挂于越。邇者雲中、上谷，黠虜雖款關矣，而薊鎮、遼左，尤滋訌焉；東西兩粵，捷書雖交馳矣，而山海殘孽，日蠢蠢也。
translation_en: … was disciplined and orderly. When he first arrived in Shuofang, he executed Zhang Yongji 張用濟, causing the entire army to tremble with fear. [Guo] Ziyi 郭子儀 governed his subordinates with magnanimity, yet his rewards and punishments were invariably trustworthy. He directed veteran generals with a nod of his chin as though they were mere rank-and-file soldiers, yet in winning people over through generosity and kindness, he surpassed [Li Guangbi 李光弼]. At that time, the officers and men delighted in Ziyi's leniency and dreaded Guangbi's severity. Moreover, Ziyi pacified the great rebellion and restored the royal house. Though repeatedly subjected to slander and estrangement, the moment he heard an imperial summons he set out on the road without the slightest hesitation or backward glance. For twenty years the safety and peril of the empire rested upon his person, and his unblemished reputation and lofty integrity shone forth uniquely. As for Guangbi, when framed by the eunuchs, he fell into suspicion and estrangement, proving inept at safeguarding himself—something over which gentlemen still feel lingering regret. Viewed together, if we determine the caliber of these several men as generals based on the differences in how they achieved their results: the Prince of Fenyang [Guo Ziyi] was a worthy general indeed—truly a match for the whole empire! The Prince of Linhuai [Li Guangbi] came close to that; while from Wei [Qing 衛青] and Huo [Qubing 霍去病] on down, all may be called talented generals, though they cannot be judged by a single standard. Even so, every one of these several men met with an opportune moment, and the rulers of their times were likewise able to select them with care and employ them well so as to exhaust their usefulness. It is fitting indeed that their glorious achievements shine endlessly and their renown pervades a thousand years [?]! At present, the troubles of the empire are entangled with the northern barbarians in the north and caught up with the Yue peoples in the south. Recently, in Yunzhong and Shanggu, although the crafty caitiffs have submitted at the passes, in Jizhen and Liaodong they are stirring up ever more turmoil; in Eastern and Western Yue [Guangdong and Guangxi], although dispatches of victory have been racing back and forth, the remnant miscreants in the mountains and seas are wriggling about day by day. …

title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
廟堂之上攄計樽俎決筴前箸所以爲剋敵
制勝之筭靡不備至而烽燧未盡熄邊鄙
未盡寧議者謂患在無將且今之握鈐擁
纛仗鉞執綏者豈少也大都溺其職矣巽
愞首鼠者率庸礫而木强奸黠狙獪者多
奧援而竊重又其賈名飾實之流每每習
褒衣之揖讓而騎射罔閑弄墨士之筆端
而措施則悖若而將也
國家安所賴之洪惟
===
聖天子御極兼統覆載乂安區夏德威四訖然
邊境之慮尚廑
宵旰思得桓桓文武之士布列中外
詔下所司廣開薦辟而搜羅將材視文吏益梀
眞虎臣驍帥據鞍躍馬之秋也顧寥寥罕
睹豈以天下之大遂無其人耶毋亦選任
之道尚有可議者歟以言乎選將也非出
世胄之蔭授則由武科之拔遷膏粱紈袴
每闇于韜鈐弓馬記誦未盡乎跅跑以言
punctuated: 廟堂之上，攄計樽俎，決筴前箸，所以爲剋敵制勝之筭靡不備至；而烽燧未盡熄，邊鄙未盡寧，議者謂患在無將。且今之握鈐擁纛、仗鉞執綏者，豈少也？大都溺其職矣。巽愞首鼠者，率庸礫而木强；奸黠狙獪者，多奧援而竊重。又其賈名飾實之流，每每習褒衣之揖讓，而騎射罔閑；弄墨士之筆端，而措施則悖。若而將也，國家安所賴之？洪惟聖天子御極，兼統覆載，乂安區夏，德威四訖。然邊境之慮，尚廑宵旰，思得桓桓文武之士，布列中外。詔下所司，廣開薦辟，而搜羅將材，視文吏益梀，眞虎臣驍帥據鞍躍馬之秋也。顧寥寥罕睹，豈以天下之大，遂無其人耶？毋亦選任之道，尚有可議者歟？以言乎選將也，非出世胄之蔭授，則由武科之拔遷。膏粱紈袴，每闇于韜鈐；弓馬記誦，未盡乎跅跑。以言
translation_en:
At the imperial court, plans are laid out over banquet tables and strategies are decided by pointing with chopsticks before the meal, so that calculations for overcoming the enemy and securing victory are thorough in every respect. Yet the beacon fires are not completely extinguished, and the borderlands are not completely at peace; commentators say that the trouble lies in a lack of generals. Moreover, are there few today who grasp the military tallies and hold the great banners, who wield the battle-axe and hold the chariot reins? For the most part, they neglect their duties. Those who are timid, cowardly, and vacillating are generally mediocre pebbles and woodenly rigid; those who are treacherous,狡猾 (crafty), and deceitful mostly rely on secret patronage at court to usurp weighty positions. Furthermore, the sort who peddle their reputation and dress up their actual abilities constantly practice the bowing and yielding of wide-robed scholars while remaining untrained in horsemanship and archery; they play with the brush-tips of ink-wielding literati while their practical measures go awry. With generals such as these, how can the state rely on them?

Reflecting deeply upon how His Sacred Majesty ascended the throne, encompassing all between Heaven and Earth, bringing order and peace to the Chinese realm, his virtue and majesty reaching to the four quarters—yet concerns over the frontiers still trouble his waking and sleeping hours. He longs to obtain martial and civil men of valor to be deployed inside and outside the court. An imperial edict was sent down to the competent authorities to broadly open up recommendations and special recruitment, and the search for command talent is even more urgent [?] than for civil officials. Truly, this is the season for tiger-like ministers and valiant commanders to mount their saddles and make their horses leap! Yet when one looks about, they are sparse and rarely seen. Can it be that in an empire as vast as this, there are simply no such men? Or is it rather that the methods of selecting and appointing them still leave room for discussion?

To speak of selecting generals: if they do not come from hereditary appointment by family privilege (yin), then they rise through promotion from the military examinations. Yet pampered scions raised on rich food and fine silk are often ignorant of military strategy; and archery, horsemanship, and rote memorization do not exhaust the recruitment of unconventional men of boundless talent. To speak…

title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
乎任將也始于束縛之太嚴繼以功罪之
罔辨威令不行于偏裨徒擁空銜訾譽淆
亂于煩言致令解體天下之所以無將也
職此矣是故選用有二道焉廣搜拔也精
教試也夫芝草無根醴泉無源將相無種
自古記之矣穰苴擢于閭伍李廣起于良
家衛青人奴去病假子昔之用人何無方
也故掄將之法取之門第不若取之行間
求之內服不若求之邊徼宜下各邊筦鑰
===
重臣博采四方山林中謀勇絕倫者疏名
上聞寘之轅門寄以亭障本兵視所成績
而重畀焉武弁之裔武舉之制皆將家進
用之途也光弼襲父封子儀舉異等名碩
將業皆由玆出胡可廢之顧教育不可不
預而試閱不可不嚴其教之也在內責成
于武校在外兼督于憲臣先以諸家兵法
使博觀成敗之迹參以職方圖本使備知
形勢之宜其試之也較騎射必主于穿札
punctuated: 乎任將也，始于束縛之太嚴，繼以功罪之罔辨；威令不行于偏裨，徒擁空銜，訾譽淆亂于煩言，致令解體。天下之所以無將也，職此矣！是故選用有二道焉：廣搜拔也，精教試也。夫芝草無根，醴泉無源，將相無種，自古記之矣。穰苴擢于閭伍，李廣起于良家，衛青人奴，去病假子，昔之用人何無方也！故掄將之法，取之門第不若取之行間，求之內服不若求之邊徼。宜下各邊筦鑰重臣，博采四方山林中謀勇絕倫者，疏名上聞，寘之轅門，寄以亭障，本兵視所成績而重畀焉。武弁之裔、武舉之制，皆將家進用之途也。光弼襲父封，子儀舉異等，名碩將業，皆由玆出，胡可廢之？顧教育不可不預，而試閱不可不嚴。其教之也，在內責成于武校，在外兼督于憲臣；先以諸家兵法，使博觀成敗之迹，參以職方圖本，使備知形勢之宜。其試之也，較騎射必主于穿札，
translation_en:
… [And when it comes] to employing generals, it begins with binding them too strictly, and is followed by failing to distinguish between merit and fault. Their authority and commands do not carry weight among their subordinate commanders, so they merely hold empty titles; blame and praise are confounded by carping talk, causing their resolve to fall apart. The reason the empire has no generals is precisely because of this!

Therefore, in selecting and employing them there are two ways: broadly searching out and promoting talent, and thoroughly training and testing them. Now, "magical fungi have no roots, sweet springs have no source," and generals and ministers have no fixed pedigree—this has been recorded since antiquity. Sima Rangju 司馬穰苴 was promoted from the village ranks, Li Guang 李廣 rose from a respectable commoner family, Wei Qing 衛青 was a household slave, and Huo Q病 霍去病 was an illegitimate son—how unbound by convention was the employment of men in former times! Thus, as for the method of selecting generals, taking them from eminent families is not as good as taking them from the military ranks, and seeking them in the interior territories is not as good as seeking them on the frontiers. Orders should be sent down to the senior ministers who hold the keys to the various frontiers to broadly gather from the mountains and forests of the four quarters men of peerless strategy and bravery, memorialize their names to the throne, place them at military headquarters, and entrust them with frontier forts and outposts; the Ministry of War (benbing) should then observe their achievements and bestow heavy responsibilities upon them.

The descendants of military officers and the system of the Military Examinations are both avenues of advancement for military families. Li Guangbi 李光弼 inherited his father's enfeoffment, and Guo Ziyi 郭子儀 was recommended for exceptional grade; the deeds of famous and great generals have all come forth from these avenues, so how could they be abolished? Yet their education must be prepared beforehand, and their testing and review must be strict. In educating them, in the capital responsibility should be assigned to the Military Schools, and in the provinces supervision should be concurrently exercised by the Surveillance Officials. First give them the military treatises of the various masters so that they may broadly observe the traces of past successes and failures, and supplement these with the maps and records of the Bureau of Operations so that they may thoroughly know the advantages of terrain. In testing them, comparing mounted archery must prioritize piercing armor laminates, …

title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
策方略毋取其文辭力足以挽强引重者
收之而豐軀碩幹者弗與焉智足以運籌
決勝者收之而記錄章句者弗與焉昔歐
陽脩欲于軍伍中求將選其技精而最勇
者百人之中得一人以為隊將合十隊得
一人為裨將合十裨得一人為大將蘇軾
欲試之于治兵觀其顏色和易以見其氣
約束堅明以見其威坐作進退以見其能
斯兩言者最得擇將之意誠能採而行之
===
則進取之途闢拘攣之見越而山林奇傑
之士將杖策而效命矣然選將非難任將
為難既選之矣而任之不專雖選何益是
故其機在於明功罪而其要在於重事權
夫張鵠以行賞罔不射矣立標而使赴罔
不趨矣今將領有功稽覈遷延積歲未敘
而望風折北與夫玩寇養亂之徒或得以
脫於吏議而法不加少則誰為之激勸而
奔走者故必倣古人賞不踰時之制小之
punctuated:
策方略毋取其文辭。力足以挽强引重者收之，而豐軀碩幹者弗與焉；智足以運籌決勝者收之，而記錄章句者弗與焉。昔歐陽脩欲于軍伍中求將，選其技精而最勇者，百人之中得一人以為隊將，合十隊得一人為裨將，合十裨得一人為大將。蘇軾欲試之于治兵，觀其顏色和易以見其氣，約束堅明以見其威，坐作進退以見其能。斯兩言者，最得擇將之意，誠能採而行之，則進取之途闢，拘攣之見越，而山林奇傑之士，將杖策而效命矣。
然選將非難，任將為難。既選之矣，而任之不專，雖選何益？是故其機在於明功罪，而其要在於重事權。夫張鵠以行賞，罔不射矣；立標而使赴，罔不趨矣。今將領有功，稽覈遷延，積歲未敘；而望風折北，與夫玩寇養亂之徒，或得以脫於吏議，而法不加少，則誰為之激勸而奔走者？故必倣古人賞不踰時之制，小之
translation_en:
…and in testing them with policy questions on strategic plans, do not select them merely for their literary phrasing. Accept those whose strength suffices to draw stiff bows and lift heavy weights, while excluding those who merely have corpulent bodies and tall frames; accept those whose wisdom suffices to devise strategies and secure victory, while excluding those who merely memorize texts and parse sentences. In the past, Ouyang Xiu 歐陽脩 wished to seek commanders from within the military ranks by selecting those most skilled in martial arts and most courageous: obtaining one man out of a hundred to serve as a Squad Commander (duijiang 隊將), combining ten squads to obtain one man as a Deputy Commander (pijiang 裨將), and combining ten deputies to obtain one man as a Grand Commander (dajiang 大將). Su Shi 蘇軾 wished to test them in drilling troops: observing whether their countenance was calm and composed in order to see their spirit, whether their discipline was firm and clear in order to see their authority, and whether their maneuvers in halting, rising, advancing, and retreating were well-ordered in order to see their capability. These two proposals best capture the true principle of selecting commanders. If we can truly adopt and put them into practice, the paths for advancement will be opened wide, narrow and rigid views will be transcended, and extraordinary heroes from the mountains and forests will lean on their riding crops and come forward to offer their lives in service.

Yet selecting commanders is not what is difficult; entrusting commanders with responsibility is what is difficult. Once they have been selected, if they are not entrusted with undivided authority, of what benefit is their selection? Therefore, the pivotal mechanism lies in clarifying merits and offenses, and the essential point lies in giving weight to their operational authority. When a target is set up and rewards are offered, there is no one who will not shoot; when a marker is erected and men are ordered to reach it, there is no one who will not hasten toward it. Nowadays, when commanders achieve merit, verification and review drag on, and for years on end they are not advanced in rank or rewarded; meanwhile, those who flee at the mere wind of the enemy and suffer defeat, as well as those who trifle with bandits and foster rebellion, sometimes manage to escape the deliberations of the judicial officials without the law being applied to them in the slightest. Under such circumstances, who would be roused to encouragement and exert themselves in service? Therefore, we must model ourselves on the ancients' system of bestowing rewards without letting the moment pass: in minor cases,…

title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
金帛之賚大之爵秩之增叙勳錄勱毋嫌
隆渥而縮朒無能撓敗多方者亟議罰焉
是惟無賞賞之必當而果是惟無罰罰之
必當而嚴庶幾人知勸阻乎則功罪安得
而不明也夫孟賁力雄萬夫縶其手則豎
子易之矣騏驥日騁千里維其足則駑馬
先之矣今出師命將權從中制事多掣肘
而又董之以監軍拘之以文法是維騏驥
之足而縶孟賁之手也是故勿以機宜從
===
中遙制使得迅耳目策應可也勿以文法
繩之使得游刃其間無所顧避可也勿以
監軍統之使得昂首信眉不萎薾喪氣可
也有信可結則如秦武之盟甘茂而不嫌
于瀆有權可假則如漢文之按轡亞夫而
不病于屈有法可任則如宋祖之歸訴於
郭進而不害于專何者彼足以集天下事
而吾亦信其能集也則亦遑恤乎其他故
陸贄有云運機遙制則多變戎帥稟命則
punctuated: 金帛之賚，大之爵秩之增，叙勳錄勱，毋嫌隆渥；而縮朒無能、撓敗多方者，亟議罰焉。是惟無賞，賞之必當而果；是惟無罰，罰之必當而嚴。庶幾人知勸阻乎，則功罪安得而不明也！夫孟賁力雄萬夫，縶其手則豎子易之矣；騏驥日騁千里，維其足則駑馬先之矣。今出師命將，權從中制，事多掣肘，而又董之以監軍，拘之以文法，是維騏驥之足而縶孟賁之手也。是故勿以機宜從中遙制，使得迅耳目、策應可也；勿以文法繩之，使得游刃其間、無所顧避可也；勿以監軍統之，使得昂首信眉、不萎薾喪氣可也。有信可結，則如秦武之盟甘茂而不嫌于瀆；有權可假，則如漢文之按轡亞夫而不病于屈；有法可任，則如宋祖之歸訴於郭進而不害于專。何者？彼足以集天下事，而吾亦信其能集也，則亦遑恤乎其他！故陸贄有云：「運機遙制則多變，戎帥稟命則
translation_en:
…with rewards of gold and silk, and for major ones, with increases in noble rank and official grade. In evaluating merit and recording exertions, do not shrink from generous munificence; meanwhile, as for those who are timid and incompetent, or who suffer defeat in multiple ways, promptly deliberate their punishment. In this way, either there is no reward, or when rewarded it is sure to be fitting and decisive; either there is no punishment, or when punished it is sure to be fitting and severe. Then perhaps men will know what encourages and what deters—how then could merit and guilt fail to be made clear!

Now, Meng Ben (孟賁) had strength surpassing ten thousand men, yet if his hands are bound, even a mere boy can take him lightly; a thoroughbred steed can gallop a thousand li in a day, yet if its feet are tethered, even a worn-out nag can outrun it. Nowadays, when troops are sent forth and generals are appointed, authority is controlled from the center, actions are frequently hamstrung, and moreover they are overseen by Army Supervisors and constrained by legalistic regulations—this is tethering the feet of a thoroughbred steed and binding the hands of Meng Ben. Therefore, do not direct tactical opportunities by remote control from the center, so that they may swiftly use their own eyes and ears and respond with timely stratagems; do not bind them with legalistic regulations, so that they may have ample room to maneuver without hesitation or evasion; do not subordinate them to Army Supervisors, so that they may hold their heads high and unknit their brows without becoming dispirited or losing heart.

Where trust can be sealed, let it be like King Wu of Qin (秦武王) swearing a covenant with Gan Mao (甘茂) without scrupling at familiarity; where authority can be delegated, let it be like Emperor Wen of Han (漢文帝) reining in his horse for Zhou Yafu (周亞夫) without fretting over the condescension; where discipline can be entrusted, let it be like Taizu of Song (宋太祖) sending complainants back to Guo Jin (郭進) without worrying about his autonomous power. Why is this? Because the general is capable of accomplishing the empire's affairs, and the ruler likewise trusts that he can accomplish them—what leisure is there to worry about anything else! Thus Lu Zhi (陸贄) once said: "When tactical operations are controlled from afar, situations change too much; when military commanders must await orders, they…

title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
不威迺欲人君敦以付授之義固以親信
之恩假以便宜之權待以殊常之賞使大
小咸極其分賢愚各適其懷斯言也最得
任將之意誠能採而行之則浮議不奪精
神自奮定計於胷臆之中而制勝於千里
之外決策於毫芒之際而收功於指顧之
間吾之幕下將馳孫吳而走頗牧也事權
又安得而不重哉選任有道則才賢之將
輩出効用由是北掃匈奴可以奏凱於龍
===
城由是南翦兇酋可以勒勳于銅柱而奠
南北赤子于衽席之安者端在是矣書生
之論如此不識執事以為何如
第五問
張孫繼
同考試官教諭劉 批 兵食二事正今日粵西急務子能洞
晰弊源計處詳盡非有先憂之畧不能吾將天下事屬子矣勉之
考試官教授蔡 批 地方重務若燭照數計然有志經濟者
考試官教授朱 批 明達時務而文足以發之宜錄以式
punctuated:
不威，迺欲人君敦以付授之義，固以親信之恩，假以便宜之權，待以殊常之賞，使大小咸極其分，賢愚各適其懷。斯言也，最得任將之意。誠能採而行之，則浮議不奪，精神自奮，定計於胷臆之中，而制勝於千里之外；決策於毫芒之際，而收功於指顧之間。吾之幕下，將馳孫、吳而走頗、牧也，事權又安得而不重哉？選任有道，則才賢之將輩出効用。由是北掃匈奴，可以奏凱於龍城；由是南翦兇酋，可以勒勳于銅柱；而奠南北赤子于衽席之安者，端在是矣。書生之論如此，不識執事以為何如？

第五問
張孫繼
〔同考試官教諭劉 批：兵食二事，正今日粵西急務。子能洞晰弊源，計處詳盡，非有先憂之畧不能。吾將天下事屬子矣，勉之。〕
〔考試官教授蔡 批：地方重務，若燭照數計然，有志經濟者。〕
〔考試官教授朱 批：明達時務，而文足以發之，宜錄以式。〕
translation_en:
… lacks authority." Thus, he wished the ruler of men to earnestly uphold the principle of delegation, strengthen the bond of personal trust and grace, grant the authority to act at discretion, and await them with extraordinary rewards, so that great and small alike fulfill their proper roles and the worthy and foolish each find satisfaction in their hearts. These words best capture the true meaning of employing generals. If one can truly adopt and put them into practice, then baseless criticisms will not sway their resolve, their spirit will naturally be roused, and they will formulate plans within their own breasts while commanding victory a thousand li away; they will decide strategies upon the finest subtleties and reap success in the pointing of a finger or the turn of a head. Those in our command tents will outrun Sun Wu 孫武 and Wu Qi 吳起 and outpace Lian Po 廉頗 and Li Mu 李牧—how then could their authority and responsibility fail to be weighty? When selection and appointment follow the proper way, talented and worthy generals will emerge in succession to render service. Thereby, sweeping away the Xiongnu in the north, one can play the music of triumph at Longcheng 龍城; thereby, cutting down the fierce chieftains in the south, one can engrave merits upon the Bronze Pillars; and placing the common people of both north and south upon a secure mat of peace lies precisely in this. Such is the discourse of a mere student; I do not know what Your Excellency thinks of it.

Fifth Policy Question
Zhang Sunji 張孫繼
[Comment by Associate Examiner, Instructor Liu 劉: Military affairs and food supplies are precisely the urgent tasks in Guangxi today. You are able to thoroughly discern the roots of the abuses and plan arrangements in exhaustive detail—something impossible without the strategic foresight of one who worries before the world worries. I would entrust the affairs of the realm to you; strive on!]
[Comment by Examiner, Instructor Cai 蔡: On the weighty affairs of the region, it is as if illuminating them with a candle and calculating them by numbers—one who aspires to statecraft.]
[Comment by Examiner, Instructor Zhu 朱: Clear and conversant with current affairs, with writing sufficient to express them; it should be recorded as a model.]

title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
執事發策諸生欲議兵馭夷興屯清賦爲
地方計良厚書生習父老之傳聞抱桑梓
之一得欲借筯而前籌無繇也兹承明問
敢布其愚語曰按調而移柱者善曲者也
酌俗而制事者善治者也惟執事垂聽焉
夫粤西交廣上游
宗藩世守郡縣星羅環四方而與吾民錯居
者極目皆夷獠也故會省屯重兵爲根本
計也乃狼兵歲更十冒六七班軍借名于
鄰省輪番靡常兵款應募于市民老稚參
半尺籍空存而緩急一無所恃于是始議
撤狼兵召練客兵矣夫以狼制獞猶以虎
制羊百粤長技恃此乆矣而可遽撤焉哉
營堡分戍兵爲剽掠防也乃戍卒單疲聞
警輒潰里排通賊劫掠表裏爲奸豪勢包
食賊田彼此兩利城社有托而狐鼠日以
縱橫于是始議專招撫量輸煙竈矣夫以
撫娛賊猶以餅啖兒百粤積習相沿乆矣
punctuated:
執事發策諸生，欲議兵馭夷、興屯清賦，爲地方計良厚。書生習父老之傳聞，抱桑梓之一得，欲借筯而前籌，無繇也。兹承明問，敢布其愚。語曰：「按調而移柱者，善曲者也；酌俗而制事者，善治者也。」惟執事垂聽焉。
夫粤西，交、廣上游，宗藩世守，郡縣星羅，環四方而與吾民錯居者，極目皆夷獠也。故會省屯重兵，爲根本計也。乃狼兵歲更，十冒六七；班軍借名于鄰省，輪番靡常；兵款應募于市民，老稚參半。尺籍空存，而緩急一無所恃，于是始議撤狼兵、召練客兵矣。夫以狼制獞，猶以虎制羊，百粤長技恃此乆矣，而可遽撤焉哉？營堡分戍兵，爲剽掠防也。乃戍卒單疲，聞警輒潰；里排通賊劫掠，表裏爲奸；豪勢包食賊田，彼此兩利。城社有托，而狐鼠日以縱橫，于是始議專招撫、量輸煙竈矣。夫以撫娛賊，猶以餅啖兒，百粤積習相沿乆矣，
translation_en:
Your Reverence has put a policy question to the candidates, wishing to deliberate on troops to control the non-Chinese tribes and on promoting military agricultural colonies and clearing up tax assessments—a plan of great generosity on behalf of this region. I, a mere student, am familiar with the accounts passed down by the elders and hold a humble insight regarding my native place; I have wished to borrow Your Reverence's chopsticks to lay out my calculations before you, yet have had no means to do so. Now, having received your enlightened inquiry, I venture to set forth my foolish thoughts. The saying goes: "He who shifts the bridges on the lute in accordance with the tune is skilled at music; he who regulates affairs by weighing local customs is skilled at governance." May Your Reverence condescend to listen.

Now Guangxi is the upper reaches above Jiaozhi and Guangdong, where an imperial princely fief is hereditarily guarded and prefectures and counties are arrayed like stars; yet surrounding us on all four sides and living intermingled with our people, as far as the eye can see, are the Man and Liao tribes. Therefore, stationing heavy forces at the provincial capital is a plan for the fundamental base. Yet the wolf-pack troops (langbing) are rotated annually, and six or seven out of ten are fraudulent substitutes; the shift soldiers borrow the name from neighboring provinces, rotating without regularity; and the categories of troops recruited from among the townspeople are half old men and children. The military registers exist in name only, and in an emergency there is nothing at all to rely upon; thereupon people have begun proposing to withdraw the wolf-pack troops and recruit and train guest troops (kebing) instead. Now, using the wolf-pack troops to control the Zhuang tribesmen is like using a tiger to control sheep—the special strength of the Hundred Yue has relied on this for a long time; how can they be suddenly withdrawn?

Dividing garrison troops among camps and forts is a defense against plundering raids. Yet the garrison soldiers are thin and exhausted, routing as soon as they hear an alarm; the hundred-household heads (lipai) collude with bandits in plundering, acting as traitors from within and without; and powerful magnates engross and live off the bandits' fields, to the mutual profit of both sides. With city walls and altars of the soil to shelter them, these foxes and rats grow more rampant by the day; thereupon people have begun proposing to rely exclusively on pacification and to have them pay a modest levy by household hearth. Now, amusing bandits with pacification is like feeding cakes to a child—this inveterate habit of the Hundred Yue has been followed for a long time, …

title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
而可覆蹈焉哉戶口稅額半為夷侵乘兵
威而丈勘非多事也顧借口賊占逋負為
常駕言抛荒影射得計細民稅浮于田則
喜輕豪右田浮于稅則懼重轉相構煽妄
騰加賦之名而阻撓有司牢不可破夫禹
貢則壤周禮辨方食土之毛而忘其報獨
非王民耶子粒屯田半為官占奉部檄而
清查非生擾也顧倔强武弁日肆侵漁占
據豪强久紊經界軍樂于脫伍而棄之若
===
遺官利于營私而視為已有轉相蒙蔽倡
為年遠之說而粉飾文具弊不可詰夫屯
田湟中積穀塞下因地之利而且耕守寧
非往事耶嘗觀漢韓安國之說曰利不什
不易業功不百不變常故懲噎而廢食者
愚也逆緒而理棼者亂也今所以處廣右
者寧有他哉要不過通權變酌要機無改
絃易轍之名而得補偏救弊之術爾夫平
時人自為耕不費尺帛斗粟之養而有事
punctuated: 而可覆蹈焉哉？戶口稅額，半為夷侵，乘兵威而丈勘，非多事也。顧借口賊占，逋負為常；駕言抛荒，影射得計。細民稅浮于田，則喜輕；豪右田浮于稅，則懼重。轉相構煽，妄騰加賦之名，而阻撓有司，牢不可破。夫《禹貢》則壤，《周禮》辨方，食土之毛而忘其報，獨非王民耶？子粒屯田，半為官占，奉部檄而清查，非生擾也。顧倔强武弁，日肆侵漁；占據豪强，久紊經界。軍樂于脫伍，而棄之若遺；官利于營私，而視為已有。轉相蒙蔽，倡為年遠之說，而粉飾文具，弊不可詰。夫屯田湟中，積穀塞下，因地之利而且耕守，寧非往事耶？嘗觀漢韓安國之說曰：「利不什，不易業；功不百，不變常。」故懲噎而廢食者，愚也；逆緒而理棼者，亂也。今所以處廣右者，寧有他哉？要不過通權變、酌要機，無改絃易轍之名，而得補偏救弊之術爾。夫平時人自為耕，不費尺帛斗粟之養，而有事
translation_en: …and how could one tread that path again? Half of the registered households and tax quotas have been encroached upon by the native tribes; taking advantage of military prestige to survey and verify the land is not making unnecessary trouble. Yet people use bandit occupation as a pretext to make tax delinquency the norm, and falsely claim that land lies abandoned so their schemes of tax evasion through false registration succeed. When petty commoners have taxes exceeding their actual land, they rejoice at having them lightened; when powerful families have land exceeding their taxes, they fear having them made heavier. They collude to stir up agitation, falsely spreading claims of tax increases to obstruct the authorities in a way that is utterly unbreakable. Now, the Tribute of Yu (Yu gong) graded the soils for taxation, and the Rites of Zhou (Zhou li) distinguished the regions. To eat the produce of the land while forgetting one's obligation to repay—are they alone not the King's subjects? Half of the grain-yielding military colony lands (tuntian) have been seized by officers; carrying out a thorough investigation pursuant to a directive from the Ministry is not creating disturbance. Yet recalcitrant military officers daily indulge in encroachment and predation, and powerful local magnates who occupy the land have long confounded the boundary lines. Soldiers are happy to abscond from the ranks and cast the land aside as if it were nothing; officers profit from pursuing private gain and regard the land as their own property. They cover up for one another, putting forward the excuse that too many years have passed, and window-dress with mere paperwork so that the abuses cannot be investigated. Yet establishing military colonies in Huangzhong and stockpiling grain along the frontier—relying on the advantages of the terrain to both farm and defend—are these not precedents from the past? I have observed the words of Han Anguo of the Han dynasty: "If the benefit is not tenfold, one does not change the occupation; if the achievement is not a hundredfold, one does not alter the norm." Therefore, to give up eating for fear of choking is foolish; to untangle a skein by pulling against the thread only creates worse confusion. In managing Guangxi today, what else is needed? In essence, it is nothing more than adapting to circumstances and weighing the critical mechanisms—incurring no reputation for restringing the lute or changing the tracks, yet attaining the art of remedying imbalances and rescuing from abuses. Now, those who farm for themselves in peacetime without costing a foot of silk or a peck of grain for their upkeep, and yet in times of crisis…

title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
坐得其力可當衝鋒冒鏑之能者粤之狼
兵是矣往者朝下三尺之紙夕報數千之
集非我抗也邇來稍稍驕蹇一二奉法不
前者何哉連歲疲于征調精壯困于傷殘
有功則賞多踰時出征則漢將朘削欲以
服其心而得其力難矣故戍守會省者先
務軍聲而已誠得一良將領之時其敎習
申之軍令戒戢將校毋事漁獵班軍兵款
汰冗覈實恩可以結則分甘損滋法可以
===
伸則徇師釁鼓果得勝兵三千大舉則大
創小戰則小勝縱橫闔闢惟吾所指較之
召集無賴人鮮固志杼軸坐耗帑藏日虛
而一有不給則脫巾呼道如往歲者功相
千萬也故土兵不可不練也兵臨則有禽
奔獸駭之恐兵退則有蜂屯蟻聚之虞者
粤之夷獠是矣往者兩江勾劫無虛日古
田蠶食無寧歲患非細也邇來大事掃蕩
一二時復跳梁者何哉蛇虺志在吞噬窟
punctuated:
坐得其力，可當衝鋒冒鏑之能者，粤之狼兵是矣。往者朝下三尺之紙，夕報數千之集，非我抗也。邇來稍稍驕蹇，一二奉法不前者，何哉？連歲疲于征調，精壯困于傷殘；有功則賞多踰時，出征則漢將朘削。欲以服其心而得其力，難矣。故戍守會省者，先務軍聲而已。誠得一良將領之，時其敎習，申之軍令，戒戢將校，毋事漁獵，班軍兵款，汰冗覈實，恩可以結則分甘損滋，法可以伸則徇師釁鼓。果得勝兵三千，大舉則大創，小戰則小勝，縱橫闔闢，惟吾所指。較之召集無賴，人鮮固志，杼軸坐耗，帑藏日虛，而一有不給，則脫巾呼道如往歲者，功相千萬也。故土兵不可不練也。

兵臨則有禽奔獸駭之恐，兵退則有蜂屯蟻聚之虞者，粤之夷獠是矣。往者兩江勾劫無虛日，古田蠶食無寧歲，患非細也。邇來大事掃蕩，一二時復跳梁者，何哉？蛇虺志在吞噬，窟…
translation_en:
… effortlessly avail ourselves of their strength, and who are capable of charging the vanguard and braving arrows, are none other than the native "Wolf Troops" (langbing) of Guangxi. In the past, when a three-foot slip of paper was sent down in the morning, thousands would report as assembled by evening; they did not defy us. Why is it that recently they have grown somewhat arrogant and recalcitrant, with a few failing to obey the law and advance? For successive years they have been exhausted by requisitions and deployments, and their able-bodied men have suffered from wounds and maiming; when they achieve merit, rewards are often delayed past their due time, and when they go on campaign, Chinese commanders exploit and fleece them. Wishing under such conditions to win their hearts and obtain their strength is difficult indeed. Therefore, as for garrisoning the provincial capital, the first priority is simply to build up our own military prestige. If we truly obtain a capable commander to lead them, conduct their training at the proper seasons, reiterate military orders to them, restrain the officers from engaging in predatory extortion, regulate the rotated troops and military funds, weed out the superfluous and verify the actual rosters—when grace can bind them, sharing delicacies and sparing our own abundance; when the law must be enforced, parading offenders before the army and anointing the war drums with blood—then if we truly obtain three thousand victorious soldiers, in a major campaign they will inflict a major blow, and in a minor engagement they will win a minor victory, maneuvering and deploying entirely as we direct. Compared to recruiting shiftless riffraff who rarely have a steadfast will—where the looms are idly exhausted, the treasuries are depleted day by day, and as soon as provisions fall short they cast off their headcloths and clamor in the roads as happened in past years—the achievement is ten thousand times greater. Therefore, the local troops must not go untrained.

Those who scatter in panic like fleeing birds and startled beasts when our troops arrive, yet give cause for worry that they will swarm like bees and gather like ants as soon as our troops withdraw, are none other than the non-Chinese tribes (Yiliao) of Guangxi. In the past, in the Two Rivers (Liangjiang) region there was scarcely a day without collusion and plundering, and in Gutian there was not a peaceful year free from their piecemeal encroachment; the affliction was no small matter. Recently we have carried out a great campaign of sweeping eradication, yet why is it that one or two of them from time to time again leap out in defiance? Like vipers and adders, their intent lies in吞 devouring and biting, and their lairs…

title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
穴易以依憑而奸滑從中鼓之恐官則曰
糾黨復聚恐賊則曰大兵將臨欲以安漢
法而制其命難矣故分戍營堡者先禁交
通而已誠得各將領嚴守信地杜絕私交
里排籍名官府毋容反復誘煽聽撫則量
輸煙竈出劫則先事報聞一切包食庇賊
如柳慶諸郡廉得其狀盡為釐正大舉則
集各堡以為防小入則時鵰勦以示武或
撫或勦勝算在我較之豺狼當道日煩公
===
家膏腴厚利盡歸私室而簸弄得計戕官
據邑如懷遠者利相什百也故交通不可
不嚴也丈地均糧立法本善銖稱寸度弊
孔實多近日
明詔停止深為擾民爾顧二三郡邑
詔書以前已經丈量者欲援而盡罷之過矣蓋
粵之田非江南比也江南有水患田之高
下患在不均粵西有夷患糧之失額患在
不明卽興全灌臨諸州邑或舊額什九而
punctuated:
穴易以依憑，而奸滑從中鼓之。恐官則曰糾黨復聚，恐賊則曰大兵將臨，欲以安漢法而制其命，難矣。故分戍營堡者，先禁交通而已。誠得各將領嚴守信地，杜絕私交，里排籍名官府，毋容反復誘煽。聽撫則量輸煙竈，出劫則先事報聞。一切包食庇賊如柳、慶諸郡，廉得其狀，盡為釐正。大舉則集各堡以為防，小入則時鵰勦以示武。或撫或勦，勝算在我，較之豺狼當道，日煩公家，膏腴厚利，盡歸私室，而簸弄得計，戕官據邑如懷遠者，利相什百也。故交通不可不嚴也。

丈地均糧，立法本善，銖稱寸度，弊孔實多。近日明詔停止，深為擾民爾。顧二三郡邑詔書以前已經丈量者，欲援而盡罷之，過矣。蓋粵之田，非江南比也。江南有水患，田之高下患在不均；粵西有夷患，糧之失額患在不明。卽興、全、灌、臨諸州邑，或舊額什九而
translation_en:
…lairs are easy for them to rely upon for shelter, while treacherous rogues stir them up from within. To intimidate the officials, they say that [the bandits] are gathering their bands again; to intimidate the bandits, they say that a great army is about to arrive. If we wish for them to rest peacefully under Chinese law and hold their fates in our hands, it is difficult indeed! Therefore, in dividing garrisons among camps and forts, the priority is simply to prohibit illicit collusion. If only we can get the various commanders to strictly guard their assigned sectors and cut off private dealings, and have the tithing-heads (lipai 里排) register names with the authorities without allowing repeated enticement and incitement; if [the natives] submit to pacification, let them pay a measured levy by hearth and household, and if they go out to raid, let word be reported beforehand. As for all the practices of monopolizing extortion [?] (baoshi 包食) and sheltering bandits, as found in prefectures such as Liuzhou 柳州 and Qingyuan 慶遠, once their circumstances are investigated and uncovered, they should all be thoroughly rectified. When [the bandits] launch a major incursion, we should assemble the various forts to mount a defense; when they make minor raids, we should carry out swift, hawk-like strikes from time to time to display our martial might. Whether pacifying or suppressing, the winning strategy remains in our hands. Compared to having ravenous wolves blocking the roads, daily troubling the state, while fertile lands and rich profits all go to private households—and manipulators succeed in their schemes, murdering officials and seizing district seats as in Huaiyuan 懷遠—the advantage is ten- or a hundred-fold. Therefore, the prohibition of illicit collusion must be strictly enforced.

Surveying the land to equalize the grain tax was originally a well-intentioned law, but in weighing every grain and measuring every inch, the loopholes for abuse were truly numerous. Recently, a clear imperial edict ordered a halt to it, simply because it deeply disturbed the people. However, for those two or three prefectures and districts where the land survey had already been completed prior to the imperial edict, to cite [the edict] and completely abolish what was done is going too far. Indeed, the fields of Guangxi are not comparable to those of Jiangnan 江南. Jiangnan suffers from floods, so the trouble with high- and low-lying fields lies in inequality; western Guangdong and Guangxi (Yuexi 粵西) suffer from native uprisings, so the trouble with lost tax quotas lies in lack of clarity. Even in departments and districts such as Xing'an 興安, Quanzhou 全州, Guanyang 灌陽, and Lingui 臨桂, where the old quota was perhaps nine parts in ten, yet…

title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
實徵不滿什一者寧能置不問哉往歲承
委者地里有遠近任事有勤惰未能一一
沿坵履畝减故增新勢所必至要于處之
而已一曰令民自首以得頃畝之多寡二
曰官為覆量以質報數之虛實三曰官民
一則毋以飛洒容奸四曰量復舊額毋以
新增作課其借口賊占妄援近徵以撓官
府者必置之法不少貸如此而謂糧額不
清未之信也衞所珠聯官舍坐食屯種失
===
額行伍空虛近日勘合清查本為足兵爾
顧數十衞所經年委官無一報完者欲援
詔而幷寢之謬矣且粤之屯與關隴一也耕以
十之三服農畝而因夫授田為自食之制
獲以十二計抵口分而歲徵六石待不時
之需俾兵得自食其力官得歲收其餘屯
日增而兵日充焉古法寧不善哉乃今正
軍勞于征調正糧歸于餘丁豪民利無差
而包佃武弁利無糧而侵漁屯政日壞勢
punctuated:
實徵不滿什一者，寧能置不問哉？往歲承委者，地里有遠近，任事有勤惰，未能一一沿坵履畝，减故增新，勢所必至，要于處之而已。一曰：令民自首，以得頃畝之多寡；二曰：官為覆量，以質報數之虛實；三曰：官民一則，毋以飛洒容奸；四曰：量復舊額，毋以新增作課。其借口賊占、妄援近徵以撓官府者，必置之法，不少貸。如此而謂糧額不清，未之信也。

衞所珠聯，官舍坐食，屯種失額，行伍空虛。近日勘合清查，本為足兵爾。顧數十衞所，經年委官無一報完者，欲援詔而幷寢之，謬矣！且粤之屯，與關隴一也。耕以十之三服農畝，而因夫授田，為自食之制；獲以十二計抵口分，而歲徵六石，待不時之需。俾兵得自食其力，官得歲收其餘，屯日增而兵日充焉，古法寧不善哉？乃今正軍勞于征調，正糧歸于餘丁，豪民利無差而包佃，武弁利無糧而侵漁，屯政日壞，勢
translation_en:
…actual collections do not reach even one-tenth—how could we leave this uninvestigated? Among those commissioned in recent years, the distances to the localities varied, and their diligence in handling affairs differed. When they could not personally walk every plot and tread every mu one by one, reducing old assessments and adding new ones was an inevitable result; the key lies simply in how we manage it. First, order the people to report their holdings voluntarily so as to ascertain the amount of land in qing and mu. Second, have officials conduct verification surveys to check the truth or falsity of the reported figures. Third, apply a single tax rate to both official and private lands, so as not to harbor fraud through fraudulent tax redistribution (feisa). Fourth, restore the old quotas according to measured capacity, without treating newly added assessments as extra performance quotas. As for those who use rebel occupation as a pretext or falsely cite recent examples to obstruct the authorities, they must be subjected to the law without the slightest leniency. If this is done and someone says the grain quotas are still not clarified, I would not believe it.

The Guards and Battalions (weisuo) are strung together like pearls, yet officers and their housemen sit idle and eat, military farm (tuntian) cultivation has lost its quotas, and the ranks are depleted. Recently, verification tallies were issued for a thorough audit, which was fundamentally intended to ensure sufficient troops. Yet across dozens of Guards and Battalions, deputies have been commissioned for years without a single one reporting completion; to wish to cite the imperial decree to shelve this audit as well is a grave error! Moreover, the military farms of Guangxi are one and the same in principle as those of Guanlong. Assigning three-tenths of the soldiers to work the agricultural fields, granting land according to the individual man as a system of self-support; calculating twelve shi of the harvest to offset their personal rations, while annually collecting six shi of surplus grain to await unforeseen needs—this allowed the soldiers to support themselves by their own strength and the state to annually collect the surplus, so that military farms increased daily and the troops grew daily more full. How could the ancient method not be good? Yet nowadays, the regular soldiers toil in campaign mobilizations while the regular grain goes to the supernumerary adult males (yuding); powerful civilians profit from the absence of corvée labor to monopolize tenancies, and military officers profit from the absence of land tax to encroach upon and appropriate the fields. That the administration of military farms deteriorates daily is an inevitable trend…

title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
所必至要在清之而已一曰稽原額以覈
見存之田二曰課餘丁以查買閒之役三
曰節優免以稽隱漏之差四曰嚴營屯以
杜侵欺之弊其借口民侵妄稱埋沒以阻
官府者必重法繩之不少惜如此而謂屯
政不脩未之信也雖然愚猶有說焉孫子
論兵以選將爲急大學理財以用人爲先
蓋將者三軍之司命君受之制而無所制
于人者也守令者百姓之司命承君之令
===
而致之民者也練土著任偏裨禁侵削勤
憂恤調之卽至無敢後時驅之卽行無敢
違令威足以懾其氣廉足以服其心此將
之事也而鼓唇吻恃胸臆微勞則竊爲己
功有事則委之將校者非所與矣巡行阡
陌徧歷郊丘均原隰量肥瘠輕徭薄賦視
官如家信足以結其心而明足以照其隱
此守令之事也而飾眉睫獵虛聲應文以
逃責飾偽以邀名者非所與矣牧帥旣得
punctuated: 所必至，要在清之而已。一曰稽原額以覈見存之田，二曰課餘丁以查買閒之役，三曰節優免以稽隱漏之差，四曰嚴營屯以杜侵欺之弊。其借口民侵、妄稱埋沒以阻官府者，必重法繩之，不少惜。如此而謂屯政不脩，未之信也。雖然，愚猶有說焉。《孫子》論兵，以選將爲急；《大學》理財，以用人爲先。蓋將者，三軍之司命，君受之制而無所制于人者也；守令者，百姓之司命，承君之令而致之民者也。練土著，任偏裨，禁侵削，勤憂恤，調之卽至，無敢後時，驅之卽行，無敢違令，威足以懾其氣，廉足以服其心，此將之事也；而鼓唇吻，恃胸臆，微勞則竊爲己功，有事則委之將校者，非所與矣。巡行阡陌，徧歷郊丘，均原隰，量肥瘠，輕徭薄賦，視官如家，信足以結其心，而明足以照其隱，此守令之事也；而飾眉睫，獵虛聲，應文以逃責，飾偽以邀名者，非所與矣。牧帥旣得
translation_en:
…is an inevitable outcome; the key lies simply in clearing them up. First, audit the original quotas in order to verify the fields currently in existence; second, assess the supernumerary adult males in order to investigate corvée exemptions bought for idleness; third, curtail privilege exemptions in order to audit concealed and evaded labor services; fourth, strictly regulate the military colonies in order to stop the abuses of encroachment and fraud. As for those who use civilian encroachment as a pretext or falsely claim that lands have been lost to registry in order to obstruct the authorities, they must be restrained with heavy penalties without the slightest leniency. That the administration of military colonies would remain unrectified under such measures is something I do not believe.

Even so, I still have more to say. When Master Sun (Sunzi) discusses warfare, he takes selecting generals as the urgent priority; when the Great Learning (Daxue) discusses fiscal administration, it puts employing the right men first. For the general is the arbiter of fate for the Three Armies, one who receives his mandate from the ruler and is not controlled by others; the prefects and magistrates are the arbiters of fate for the common people, those who receive the ruler's commands and carry them out among the people. To train local troops, delegate to deputy and assistant commanders, prohibit extortion and exploitation, diligently show care and compassion, so that when mobilized they arrive at once without daring to be late, and when ordered forward they march at once without daring to disobey commands—his authority sufficient to overawe their spirit and his integrity sufficient to win their hearts—this is the business of a general. Those who merely flap their lips and rely on subjective whims, claiming petty efforts as their own merit and shifting the blame onto subordinate officers whenever trouble arises, have no part in this. To tour the field paths, travel throughout the rural districts and hills, equalize high plains and low marshes, measure fertility and barrenness, lighten corvée and reduce taxes, and regard office as one's own home—his trustworthiness sufficient to bind their hearts and his discernment sufficient to illuminate their hidden plight—this is the business of prefects and magistrates. Those who merely put on superficial displays right before people's eyes, hunt for empty reputations, go through the motions of paperwork to evade responsibility, and practice deceit to court fame, have no part in this. Once civil governors and military commanders have been…

title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
其人以之練兵馭夷隱然韓白之望以之
查屯清賦藹然龔卓之風故曰牧帥不可
以不慎也夫多指亂視多言亂聽今事之
難任凡以議論之多爾一人稱便則朝而
攘臂一人以爲不便則夕而投杼十羊九
牧誰其聽之故議事之始必根究弊源熟
思其便定議之後必詢謀僉同委任責成
不惑于羣議不阻于邪謀不怵于勢要雖
毁言日至而不以爲疑雖人心稍拂而不
===
以爲懼如此則練兵也制夷也丈勘也興
屯也皆次第舉矣故曰議論不可不一也
粤西僻遠禁網疎闊習俗獷悍易動難安
吏玆土者一切姑息因仍務爲寬大人心
玩愒非一日矣故大將之令必伸于偏裨
偏裨之令必伸于士卒監司之令必行于
守令守令之法必行于豪强大將令肅則
土官之虚冒里排之交通可按法而治也
文臣令行則奸豪之阻撓武弁之頑梗可
punctuated: 其人，以之練兵馭夷，隱然韓、白之望；以之查屯清賦，藹然龔、卓之風。故曰牧帥不可以不慎也。夫多指亂視，多言亂聽，今事之難任，凡以議論之多爾。一人稱便，則朝而攘臂；一人以爲不便，則夕而投杼。十羊九牧，誰其聽之？故議事之始，必根究弊源，熟思其便；定議之後，必詢謀僉同，委任責成。不惑于羣議，不阻于邪謀，不怵于勢要，雖毁言日至而不以爲疑，雖人心稍拂而不以爲懼。如此則練兵也、制夷也、丈勘也、興屯也，皆次第舉矣。故曰議論不可不一也。粤西僻遠，禁網疎闊，習俗獷悍，易動難安。吏玆土者，一切姑息因仍，務爲寬大，人心玩愒，非一日矣。故大將之令，必伸于偏裨；偏裨之令，必伸于士卒；監司之令，必行于守令；守令之法，必行于豪强。大將令肅，則土官之虚冒、里排之交通，可按法而治也；文臣令行，則奸豪之阻撓、武弁之頑梗，可
translation_en:
… the right men, then when employed to train troops and control the non-Chinese tribes, they will command an imposing prestige like that of Han Xin 韓信 and Bai Qi 白起; when employed to inspect military colonies and clear up tax registers, they will exude the benevolent air of Gong Sui 龔遂 and Zhuo Mao 卓茂. Therefore it is said that one cannot but be careful in selecting civil administrators and military commanders.

Now, too many pointing fingers confuse the sight, and too many words confuse the hearing. Today, the difficulty in taking on responsibilities lies entirely in the multiplicity of competing opinions. If one person declares a measure convenient, people roll up their sleeves in enthusiasm in the morning; if another deems it inconvenient, they drop the shuttle in doubt by evening. With nine herdsmen for ten sheep, whom should they obey? Therefore, at the beginning of deliberating on a matter, one must thoroughly investigate the root of the abuses and carefully ponder what is advantageous; after a policy is decided, one must ensure that consultations yield unanimous agreement, and then delegate authority and demand results. One must not be swayed by the chatter of the crowd, nor obstructed by perverse schemes, nor intimidated by the powerful and influential. Even if slanderous words arrive daily, one should not harbor doubts; even if popular sentiment is slightly ruffled, one should not be afraid. In this way, training troops, controlling the tribes, surveying land, and promoting military colonies will all be carried out in due order. Therefore it is said that deliberations cannot but be unified.

Guangxi is remote and isolated, the net of prohibitions is loose and wide-meshed, and local customs are fierce and unruly—easy to stir up and hard to pacify. Those who serve as officials in this territory have uniformly practiced indulgence and routine continuance, striving for leniency and magnanimity, so that people's minds have grown lax and negligent for longer than a single day. Therefore, the orders of the grand general must be enforced among the deputy and assistant commanders; the orders of the deputy and assistant commanders must be enforced among the rank-and-file soldiers; the orders of the surveillance and circuit officials must be carried out by the prefects and magistrates; and the laws of the prefects and magistrates must be carried out against local bullies and powerful families. When the grand general's orders are strictly observed, false claims by native officials (tuguan) and illicit collusion by tithing-rotation heads (lipai) can be punished according to the law; when the orders of civil officials are carried out, obstruction by unscrupulous magnates and stubborn defiance by military officers can be …

title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
執吏而議也冠履之分既嚴則澆風丕變
夷夏之防既飭則邪沴潛消如是而地方
諸因革皆可爲矣故曰紀綱不可不振也
夫委任專矣議論一矣紀綱振矣至于斟
酌時宜鼓舞羣動選賢馭將挈領提綱自
有當事者石畫在愚生何敢容喙焉
punctuated: 執吏而議也。冠履之分既嚴，則澆風丕變；夷夏之防既飭，則邪沴潛消。如是，而地方諸因革皆可爲矣。故曰：紀綱不可不振也。夫委任專矣，議論一矣，紀綱振矣，至于斟酌時宜，鼓舞羣動，選賢馭將，挈領提綱，自有當事者石畫在，愚生何敢容喙焉。
translation_en:
…be handed over to the law officers for deliberation. Once the distinction between cap and shoe—between superior and inferior—is strictly maintained, degenerate customs will be thoroughly transformed; once the boundary between non-Chinese and Chinese is firmly enforced, pernicious influences will quietly vanish. In this way, all local measures of continuity and reform can be carried out. Therefore it is said: discipline and order must be invigorated.

Now, when the delegation of authority has been made exclusive, deliberations have been unified, and discipline and order have been invigorated—as for weighing what suits the occasion, inspiring collective action, selecting worthy men and commanding generals, and grasping the collar and main cord of governance, there are naturally the rock-solid plans of the officials in charge; how would this foolish student dare to interject a word?

title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
廣西鄉試錄後序
今天子統承丕丕基握符紀元聿
新
鴻猷濬哲徇齊神資首出
聖學日蒸彰聞中外寤寐賢雋賓
興海宇爰自畿甸達于侯綏
江介嶺海之間甌脫斗辟之
內士有章縫而呫嗶者咸忻
聖作而快先覩于時巡按御史唐
錬監臨廣西試事錄成存省
以職事宜敘諸末簡存省聞
之重華南巡警蹕賁于衡湘
聲敎達于梧野西粤固古帝
之流化區也秦漢以戈船載
punctuated:
廣西鄉試錄後序
今天子統承丕丕基，握符紀元，聿新鴻猷，濬哲徇齊，神資首出，聖學日蒸，彰聞中外。寤寐賢雋，賓興海宇，爰自畿甸，達于侯綏。江介嶺海之間，甌脫斗辟之內，士有章縫而呫嗶者，咸忻聖作而快先覩。于時巡按御史唐錬監臨廣西試事，錄成，存省以職事宜敘諸末簡。存省聞之：重華南巡，警蹕賁于衡湘，聲敎達于梧野，西粤固古帝之流化區也。秦、漢以戈船載
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Guangxi Provincial Examination

The reigning Son of Heaven, having succeeded to the vast foundation, holds the imperial tally and inaugurates a new reign era, thereby renewing the grand design. Profoundly wise and swiftly discerning, of preeminent divine endowment, his sagely learning advances daily and is manifestly known at court and abroad. Yearning waking and sleeping for worthy and outstanding talents, he has summoned them as guests from throughout the realm, extending from the imperial domain all the way to the outer pacified zones. Between the borders of the Yangzi and the ridges and seas of the south, and within the frontier outposts and remote corners, every scholar who wears ceremonial attire and drones over his texts rejoices at the rise of a sage and is thrilled to be among the first to behold it.

At this time, the Regional Investigating Censor Tang Lian 唐錬 served as Supervising Official for the examination affairs of Guangxi. Once the record was completed, by virtue of my official duties I, Cunxing 存省, ought to write a postface for its final pages.

I, Cunxing, have heard that when Chonghua 重華 [Shun 舜] made his southern tour of inspection, his imperial cortege graced Heng 衡 and Xiang 湘, and his prestige and teachings reached the wilds of Cangwu 蒼梧; western Yue [Guangxi] is indeed a region where the transforming influence of the ancient emperors flowed. When the Qin and Han dynasties, with their戈-warships, repeatedly…

title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
闢桂林象郡歷唐彌顯奇人
墨士往往與桂蠹翠翮文犀
馴象並貢稱珍
明興樹藩設學材賢彙征名卿碩
輔勛猷代著下至酋長莫不
慕義趨風解結投弩競列纓
緌之林猗其盛哉然存省甞
===
涉湘浮灕攬結西粵之勝海
陽中峙支嶂萬分攢戟列珪
翥鶙翔駕岧嶢崔嵬玲瓏崒
嵂雲譎波詭不可狀陳而其
間二三巍巒赤立乎漢表若
偉丈人儒長者高踞俯視羣
子弟蒲伏趨走聽指授之不
punctuated: 闢桂林、象郡，歷唐彌顯，奇人墨士，往往與桂蠹、翠翮、文犀、馴象並貢稱珍。明興，樹藩設學，材賢彙征，名卿碩輔，勛猷代著；下至酋長，莫不慕義趨風，解結投弩，競列纓緌之林。猗其盛哉！然存省甞涉湘浮灕，攬結西粵之勝。海陽中峙，支嶂萬分，攢戟列珪，翥鶙翔駕，岧嶢崔嵬，玲瓏崒嵂，雲譎波詭，不可狀陳。而其間二三巍巒，赤立乎漢表，若偉丈人、儒長者高踞俯視，羣子弟蒲伏趨走，聽指授之不
translation_en:
…opened up the commanderies of Guilin and Xiang. Passing through the Tang dynasty, the region grew ever more illustrious, and its extraordinary individuals and men of letters were often presented as tribute and praised as treasures right alongside cassia grubs, kingfisher feathers, patterned rhinoceros horns, and tamed elephants.

With the rise of the Ming, provincial administrations were established and schools were founded. Men of talent and worth advanced together in great numbers, and renowned ministers and great statesmen made their meritorious plans manifest from generation to generation. Down to the native chieftains, there were none who did not admire righteousness and hasten toward our civilizing influence, untying their topknots and casting aside their crossbows to vie for a place in the forest of capped and tasseled officials. Oh, how flourishing it is!

Yet I, Cunxing, once crossed the Xiang River and floated down the Li River, taking in the scenic wonders of Western Yue (Guangxi). Mount Haiyang stands towering in the center, while branching peaks divide in ten thousand directions—clustered like halberds, arrayed like jade tablets, soaring like hawks and wheeling like wild geese [? 駕 for 鵝], lofty and precipitous, exquisitely pierced and jaggedly towering, as wondrously shifting as clouds and waves, beyond all power to describe. And among them, two or three巍然 lofty peaks stand stark against the sky beyond the Milky Way, like a magnificent patriarch or a Confucian elder seated on high and looking down, while a crowd of younger disciples crawl and hasten about, listening to his instructions without…

title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
皇也又若元戎搴旗連百萬
熊羆追垓下戰昆陽虎臣驍
騎角力之恐後也斯其山川
奇勝雖秦蜀莫之甲也蓋蹶
然嘆曰西粤材賢之衆多其
間名公卿之勛猷以揆之今
日其方權輿而未可津涯者
===
歟何則昆侖之氣鼓行域內
自北徂南而西粤固南國之
極壤精華之尤萃也以彼其
山川而值精華之萃則自今
蒸蒸奮豈可量哉曩又聞莅
玆土者唯固守簡闊舊畫多
未嘗事事曰吾無攖也巳而
punctuated: 皇也；又若元戎搴旗，連百萬熊羆，追垓下、戰昆陽，虎臣驍騎角力之恐後也。斯其山川奇勝，雖秦、蜀莫之甲也。蓋蹶然嘆曰：「西粤材賢之衆多，其間名公卿之勛猷，以揆之今日，其方權輿而未可津涯者歟！」何則？昆侖之氣，鼓行域內，自北徂南，而西粤固南國之極壤，精華之尤萃也。以彼其山川，而值精華之萃，則自今蒸蒸奮，豈可量哉！曩又聞莅玆土者，唯固守簡闊舊畫，多未嘗事事，曰：「吾無攖也。」巳而
translation_en: …no time to spare; and again they are like a supreme commander capturing enemy banners, leading a million bear-like warriors to pursue the foe at Gaixia or battle at Kunyang, with tiger-like vassals and valiant horsemen vying in strength for fear of falling behind. Such is the wondrous splendour of its mountains and rivers that not even Qin or Shu can surpass it. Thus I was moved to exclaim with a sigh: "Given the abundance of talented and worthy men in Western Yue [Guangxi], and the meritorious achievements and grand plans of its renowned high ministers, if we measure them by what we see today, are they not just at their beginning and boundlessly vast without limit?" Why is this so? The vital pneuma of the Kunlun Mountains surges across the realm, moving from north to south; and Western Yue is truly the farthest territory of the southern lands, where the finest essence especially gathers. With mountains and rivers such as those, coinciding with this gathering of the finest essence, how could their flourishing and vigorous rise from this day forth possibly be measured! In the past, I also heard that those who came to govern this land merely clung fast to simple and loose old policies, mostly refraining from taking active charge of affairs, saying, "Let us not stir things up." Before long, …

title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
虺穴木樵𧴀跣之餘孽卵育
日繁豪噬我民其極至侵疆
奪邑戕官剚吏歲罔虚日襟
喉爲之鬲塞諸司猶然視曰
吾無攖也頃得節鉞大吏繡
斧使臣毅然議征於是古田
先復府江繼通刋除棼鬱旁
===
鬯日南之遐談者則曰西粤
之人事又何其與天運地靈
相協應也然則西粤材賢駿
發而鴻宣引長而勿替斯又
非其時歟玆者大比賓興羅
蒐卓犖諸士乗
昌運遘
punctuated: 虺穴木樵𧴀跣之餘孽，卵育日繁，豪噬我民。其極至侵疆奪邑，戕官剚吏，歲罔虚日，襟喉爲之鬲塞。諸司猶然視曰：「吾無攖也。」頃得節鉞大吏、繡斧使臣毅然議征，於是古田先復，府江繼通，刋除棼鬱，旁鬯日南之遐。談者則曰：「西粤之人事，又何其與天運地靈相協應也！」然則西粤材賢駿發而鴻宣，引長而勿替，斯又非其時歟？玆者大比賓興，羅蒐卓犖，諸士乗昌運、遘
translation_en: …the remnant miscreants—dwelling in viper dens, gathering firewood in the forests, and going barefoot—spawned and multiplied day by day, violently devouring our people. At its worst, they went so far as to encroach upon boundaries and seize district towns, murdering officials and stabbing clerks, with scarcely a day passing in the year without incident, so that the strategic chokepoints of the region were blocked off. Yet the various authorities still looked on and said, "We shall not provoke them." Recently, however, high commanders bearing axes of authority and imperial commissioners clad in embroidered robes resolutely deliberated on a punitive campaign. Thereupon, Gutian 古田 was first recovered, and the Fu River (Fujiang 府江) was subsequently opened to traffic; the tangled, overgrown thickets were cleared away, and order spread far and wide even to the remote reaches of the far south (Rinan 日南). Commentators thus remark: "How remarkably the human affairs of Western Yue (Guangxi 廣西) harmonize and correspond with the cycle of Heaven and the numinous power of the Earth!" This being so, for the men of talent and worth in Western Yue to burst forth swiftly and shine broadly, extending their legacy far into the future without decline—is this not indeed the very time for it? Now, on the occasion of the triennial examination and the ceremonial recommendation of worthy guests, we have cast our net to gather preeminent talents. As the gentlemen ride upon this prosperous destiny and encounter…

title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
盛時而適際
聖作之期則三試之所揮霍有司
之所鑑遴歔詞奧義鏗耳溢
眥纚纚藝林固足以進叩南
宫矣不知其翼
運應時仰對
聖人求賢之實詎止斯藝已乎夫
===
士之為藝談儒行則宗聖脩
而詆老佛論治法則尊王道
而卑五伯籌國計則上商周
而下管桑非不章章著也然
一朝布之中外較其行事與
曩所言者若兩人焉何哉則
以未達
punctuated: 盛時，而適際聖作之期。則三試之所揮霍，有司之所鑑遴，歔詞奧義，鏗耳溢眥，纚纚藝林，固足以進叩南宫矣。不知其翼運應時，仰對聖人求賢之實，詎止斯藝已乎？夫士之為藝，談儒行則宗聖脩而詆老佛，論治法則尊王道而卑五伯，籌國計則上商周而下管桑，非不章章著也。然一朝布之中外，較其行事，與曩所言者若兩人焉。何哉？則以未達
translation_en:
… a flourishing era, and have just coincided with the moment of the sage's rise. Thus, what they have brandished with flair across the three examination sessions and what the authorities have appraised and selected—breathing forth fine diction and profound meaning that ring in the ears and brim before the eyes, flowing continuously in the forest of letters—is indeed sufficient for them to advance and knock at the gates of the Southern Palace [for the Metropolitan Examination]. Yet I wonder: in assisting the dynastic destiny, responding to the times, and looking up to fulfill the true substance of the Sage's quest for the worthy, how could it merely end with such literary arts?

Now, when scholars practice the literary arts, in discussing Confucian conduct they revere sage self-cultivation and disparage Laozi and the Buddha; in debating methods of governance they exalt the Kingly Way and belittle the Five Hegemons; in planning state finances they place the Shang and Zhou dynasties above and Guan Zhong and Sang Hongyang below. It is not that these arguments are not brilliantly manifest! Yet once they are appointed to posts at court and in the provinces, if one compares their actual deeds with what they previously spoke of, it is as though they were two different people. Why is this? It is because they have not yet comprehended …

title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
國家求賢之實者也詩曰濟濟
多士維周之楨士胡以克楨
哉書曰不惟逸豫唯以亂民
詩又曰百辟卿士媚于天子
不解于位民之攸暨是則
國家自養士布列有位冀爲國
楨非斯世斯民無爲也士自
===
始學至列有位爰楨乃國非
斯世斯民無事也此
國家求賢之實亦士之自靖也
士既不知其實而脩之方其
