學操翰輒私心卜曰吾得繇
是飽刀泉華閭里足矣他吾
奚有有晉是者曰吾得繇是
punctuated: 國家求賢之實者也。《詩》曰：「濟濟多士，維周之楨。」士胡以克楨哉？《書》曰：「不惟逸豫，唯以亂民。」《詩》又曰：「百辟卿士，媚于天子，不解于位，民之攸暨。」是則國家自養士、布列有位，冀爲國楨，非斯世斯民無爲也；士自始學至列有位，爰楨乃國，非斯世斯民無事也。此國家求賢之實，亦士之自靖也。士既不知其實而脩之，方其學操翰，輒私心卜曰：「吾得繇是飽刀泉、華閭里，足矣，他吾奚有？」有晉是者曰：「吾得繇是
translation_en: … the reality of the state's search for worthies. The Classic of Odes (Shijing) says: "Dignified are the many scholars; they are the pillars of Zhou." How are scholars able to serve as pillars? The Classic of Documents (Shujing) says: "Not for idle pleasure, but solely to govern the people." The Classic of Odes also says: "All the princes and ministers show devotion to the Son of Heaven; never lax in their positions, in them the people find rest." Thus, from nurturing scholars to appointing them to official positions, the state hopes they will become pillars of the state—there is no purpose other than this world and these people. And for scholars, from the beginning of their studies to taking their place in official positions and thereby serving as pillars of the state, there is no business other than this world and these people. This is the reality of the state's search for worthies, and also how scholars dedicate themselves to their duty. Since scholars do not understand this reality and cultivate themselves accordingly, as soon as they learn to wield the brush, they privately calculate in their hearts, saying: "If by this means I can fill myself with wealth and bring glory to my native village, that is enough; what else does it matter to me?" Those who advance beyond this say: "If by this means I can…

title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
樹名檢階顯融則身名兼之
矣他吾奚有又有晉者則又
曰吾得繇是抒猷悃垂後世
可也是非無世與民之事也
而其實非也旣非其實則士
雖日日操翰而宗聖脩是竊
言聖脩也其行有老佛覆詆
===
之者矣雖日日操翰而陳王
道是竊言王道也其政有五
伯覆卑之者矣日日操翰而
偉商周是竊言商周也其計
有管桑覆下之者矣夫
國家求賢之實若此而士固如
彼則世與民將焉賴
punctuated: 樹名檢、階顯融，則身名兼之矣，他吾奚有！」又有晉者則又曰：「吾得繇是抒猷悃、垂後世可也。」是非無世與民之事也，而其實非也。旣非其實，則士雖日日操翰而宗聖脩，是竊言聖脩也，其行有老、佛覆詆之者矣；雖日日操翰而陳王道，是竊言王道也，其政有五伯覆卑之者矣；日日操翰而偉商、周，是竊言商、周也，其計有管、桑覆下之者矣。夫國家求賢之實若此，而士固如彼，則世與民將焉賴，
translation_en: … establish a reputation for personal integrity and ascend to prominence and glory, I will thereby possess both status and fame—what else is any concern of mine!” And those who advance even further say in turn: “If by this means I get to give expression to my plans and sincere convictions and hand them down to posterity, that will do.” Now, this is not devoid of concern for the age and the people, yet in reality it is not the true substance. Since it lacks the true substance, then even though a scholar wields his brush day after day to revere the self-cultivation of the sages, this is merely stealing the words of sage self-cultivation; in his conduct, there is that which even Laozi and the Buddha would in turn disparage! Even though day after day he wields his brush to set forth the Kingly Way, this is merely stealing the words of the Kingly Way; in his governance, there is that which even the Five Hegemons would in turn despise as base! Day after day he wields his brush to extol the Shang and Zhou dynasties, yet this is merely stealing the words of the Shang and Zhou; in his calculations, there is that which even Guan Zhong and Sang Hongyang would in turn look down upon as inferior! Now, when the true substance of the State’s search for the worthy is like this, while the scholars stubbornly remain like that, then upon what shall the age and the people rely, and…

title: 萬曆元年廣西鄉試錄
text:
國家亦焉用三試士為也是必
有古之已饑已溺一夫引辜
者作夫乃可以幹世而膏澤
斯民則士於
國家允楨之矣藝云乎哉嗟乎
今西粵士欲以翼
運應時仰對
===
聖人求賢之實安知不有若而人
者繩繩繼繼贊
睿德而鬯
鴻化也存省滋望矣故曰今日未
可以津涯也
浙江杭州府儒學教授蔡存
省謹序
punctuated:
國家亦焉用三試士為也？是必有古之已饑已溺、一夫引辜者作，夫乃可以幹世而膏澤斯民，則士於國家允楨之矣，藝云乎哉！嗟乎！今西粵士欲以翼運應時，仰對聖人求賢之實，安知不有若而人者，繩繩繼繼，贊睿德而鬯鴻化也？存省滋望矣，故曰：「今日未可以津涯也。」
浙江杭州府儒學教授蔡存省謹序。
translation_en:
…and what use would the Dynasty have for examining scholars through three sessions? There must arise men like those of antiquity who felt that if anyone went hungry or drowned it was their own doing, and who took the blame upon themselves if even a single commoner was left out of place; only then can they serve as the framework of the age and shower rich blessings upon the people. Then scholars will truly be the pillars of the Dynasty—how could it be a mere matter of literary skill!

Alas! As the scholars of Guangxi today seek to assist the imperial destiny and respond to the times, looking up to answer the reality of the Sage Emperor's search for the worthy, how can we know that there will not be men such as these coming forth in continuous succession to aid the Emperor's sagely virtue and spread far and wide his grand transformation? I, Cunxing, place ever greater hopes in this; therefore I say: "What begins today cannot be bounded or measured."

Respectfully prefaced by Cai Cunxing 蔡存省, Instructor in the Confucian School of Hangzhou Prefecture in Zhejiang.
